### 183. cy.session() `cacheAcrossSpecs` — True Multi-Spec Session Persistence

By default, `cy.session()` caches session state only for the current spec file. Setting `cacheAcrossSpecs: true` promotes the session to a "global" session shared across all specs in the same Cypress run. This is ideal for CI pipelines where re-logging-in at the start of every spec file is the dominant time cost.

```typescript
// cypress/support/commands.ts
declare global {
  namespace Cypress {
    interface Chainable {
      loginAsAdmin(): Chainable<void>;
    }
  }
}

Cypress.Commands.add('loginAsAdmin', () => {
  cy.session(
    // Session ID — must be stable across specs. Use a fixed string for a
    // shared role, NOT the password (passwords belong in validate(), not id).
    'admin-session-v1',
    () => {
      // Setup runs only once per run when cacheAcrossSpecs: true
      cy.request({
        method: 'POST',
        url:    '/api/auth/login',
        body:   {
          username: Cypress.env('ADMIN_USER'),
          password: Cypress.env('ADMIN_PASS'),
        },
      }).then((res) => {
        // Store the access token in localStorage so all specs share it
        window.localStorage.setItem('accessToken', res.body.token);
        window.localStorage.setItem('sessionSetAt', String(Date.now()));
      });
    },
    {
      cacheAcrossSpecs: true,
      validate() {
        // Fast synchronous check — avoids 100 ms HTTP round-trip per test
        const setAt = parseInt(window.localStorage.getItem('sessionSetAt') ?? '0', 10);
        const age   = Date.now() - setAt;
        if (age > 30 * 60 * 1000) {
          // Older than 30 min — force re-login by throwing
          throw new Error('Session expired');
        }
      },
    }
  );
});
```

**[community]** WHY: Without `cacheAcrossSpecs: true`, a suite of 50 spec files each calling `loginAsAdmin()` in `beforeEach` triggers up to 50 full login flows across a run — even on a single CI machine. With `cacheAcrossSpecs: true`, the login flow runs once and the session (cookies + localStorage) is restored for every subsequent spec in milliseconds. Teams migrating from `cy.visit('/login')` + form fill in each `beforeEach` typically halve their CI runtime after enabling this pattern.

---

### 184. cy.intercept() `req.on('response')` — Non-Destructive Response Mutation

The `req.on('response', fn)` event fires after the real server responds but before the browser receives the body. This enables modifying status codes, headers, or body without replacing the entire response — unlike `req.reply()`, which short-circuits the real server call entirely.

```typescript
// Inject a latency simulation header for performance testing
cy.intercept({ url: '/api/**' }, (req) => {
  req.on('response', (res) => {
    // Add a custom header to every API response — visible in DevTools
    res.headers['x-test-responded-at'] = String(Date.now());
  });
}).as('apiResponses');

// Downgrade a 200 to a 206 Partial Content to test resumable download logic
cy.intercept('GET', '/api/files/*', (req) => {
  req.on('response', (res) => {
    if (res.statusCode === 200) {
      res.statusCode = 206;
      res.headers['content-range'] = 'bytes 0-1023/2048';
    }
  });
}).as('partialDownload');

// Inject a delay only on slow-network scenario specs
cy.intercept('POST', '/api/checkout', (req) => {
  req.on('before:response', (res) => {
    // before:response fires before continue handlers — best for delays
    res.setDelay(1500); // simulate 1.5 s payment gateway latency
  });
}).as('slowCheckout');
```

**[community]** WHY: `req.on('response')` is the correct hook for augmenting real responses. The `req.continue((res) => {...})` alternative also works but requires the route handler to explicitly call `continue()` and "owns" the route — meaning subsequent `cy.intercept()` registrations for the same route won't fire (the `continue()` handler short-circuits the chain). `req.on('response')` is a passive listener and plays well with middleware stacking.

---

### 185. cy.origin() `injectDocumentDomain` Migration — Subdomain Auth Without Legacy Injection

Cypress 14 deprecated the `document.domain` injection mechanism that allowed subdomain navigation without `cy.origin()`. Teams relying on `injectDocumentDomain: true` (the temporary migration config) must migrate before it is removed. The canonical pattern uses `cy.session()` + `cy.origin()` to cache cross-origin auth state.

```typescript
// cypress.config.ts — BEFORE (deprecated, will break in a future version)
export default defineConfig({
  e2e: {
    injectDocumentDomain: true,  // ← remove this
  },
});

// AFTER — cy.origin() + cy.session() pattern
// cypress/support/commands.ts
Cypress.Commands.add('loginOAuth', (provider: string) => {
  cy.session(
    ['oauth', provider],
    () => {
      cy.visit('/login');
      cy.get('[data-cy="login-with-oauth"]').click();

      // The OAuth redirect crosses to auth.example.com (different subdomain)
      cy.origin(
        'https://auth.example.com',
        { args: { provider } },
        ({ provider }) => {
          cy.get(`[data-cy="provider-${provider}"]`).click();
          cy.get('[data-cy="username"]').type(Cypress.env('OAUTH_USER'));
          cy.get('[data-cy="password"]').type(Cypress.env('OAUTH_PASS'));
          cy.get('[data-cy="submit"]').click();
        }
      );

      // After redirect back to main domain, wait for session to establish
      cy.url().should('eq', `${Cypress.config('baseUrl')}/dashboard`);
    },
    {
      cacheAcrossSpecs: true,
      validate: () => cy.getCookie('auth_token').should('exist'),
    }
  );
});
```

**[community]** WHY: `injectDocumentDomain: true` works by setting `document.domain` on both the top frame and subdomain frame — a technique that modern browsers are phasing out via the "restrict document.domain" origin-keyed agent cluster specification. Chrome 115+ already ignores `document.domain` assignments in certain contexts. Tests that pass today with `injectDocumentDomain: true` may silently break on browser version upgrades; migrating to `cy.origin()` now avoids a future scramble.

---

### 186. Angular Zoneless Component Testing (Cypress 15.8+)

Cypress 15.8 introduced `mount` from `cypress/angular-zoneless` for testing Angular 19+ components built with the new Signals-based reactivity without Zone.js. The standard `cypress/angular` mount function wraps components in `NgZone`, which causes assertion timing issues with zoneless components.

```typescript
// cypress/component/counter.cy.ts — zoneless Angular component test
import { mount } from 'cypress/angular-zoneless';   // <-- zoneless-specific import
import { CounterComponent } from './counter.component';

describe('CounterComponent (zoneless)', () => {
  it('increments count via signal', () => {
    mount(CounterComponent, {
      componentProperties: {
        initialCount: 5,
      },
    });

    cy.get('[data-cy="count"]').should('have.text', '5');
    cy.get('[data-cy="increment"]').click();
    // Signals flush synchronously outside NgZone — assertion fires immediately
    cy.get('[data-cy="count"]').should('have.text', '6');
  });

  it('accepts injected services via TestBed providers', () => {
    mount(CounterComponent, {
      providers: [
        { provide: CounterService, useValue: { getInitial: () => 10 } },
      ],
    });

    cy.get('[data-cy="count"]').should('have.text', '10');
  });
});
```

```json
// cypress.config.ts — configure component testing for Angular zoneless
// component: { devServer: { framework: 'angular', bundler: 'webpack' } }
// tsconfig.cy.json: { "compilerOptions": { "types": ["cypress"] } }
```

**[community]** WHY: Using `cypress/angular` (Zone.js mount) on a zoneless Angular component causes Cypress to wait indefinitely for a `NgZone.isStable()` signal that never fires — because zoneless components never enter NgZone. The test eventually times out with `CypressError: Timed out retrying after 4000ms`. The error message doesn't mention NgZone, making it very hard to diagnose without knowing about the `cypress/angular-zoneless` import split.

---

### 187. `experimentalMemoryManagement` — Preventing Chromium OOM in Long E2E Runs

Cypress 14+ ships `experimentalMemoryManagement` for Chromium-based browsers. It triggers garbage collection between tests when heap usage exceeds a threshold, preventing the OOM crashes that affect suites with 500+ specs running in a single browser session.

```typescript
// cypress.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from 'cypress';

export default defineConfig({
  e2e: {
    experimentalMemoryManagement: true,
    // Tune the GC threshold (default: 50 %, measured as percent of max heap)
    // Lower values = more frequent GC = slightly slower but more stable
    numTestsKeptInMemory: 10,  // keep only last 10 tests' command logs in memory
    // Note: numTestsKeptInMemory was updated in Cy 15.14 to also clear
    // command log DATA when tests age out — not just the UI references
  },

  // experimentalMemoryManagement is Chromium-only — has no effect on Firefox/WebKit
  // Do NOT set it inside the `component:` block; it is an e2e-only config
});
```

**[community]** WHY: In a Cypress run with 300+ specs against a React SPA, each test accumulates DOM snapshots, XHR response bodies, and screenshot data in the browser's JavaScript heap. Without GC management, Chromium heap can reach 2–3 GB after 200 specs, triggering a browser crash that kills the entire CI run. `experimentalMemoryManagement` paired with `numTestsKeptInMemory: 10` keeps heap stable at ~400 MB regardless of suite size. The tradeoff is slightly slower test teardown between specs (~20 ms for GC) and loss of command log history for tests older than `numTestsKeptInMemory`.

---

### 188. `experimentalCspAllowList` — Selective CSP Header Preservation

By default Cypress strips all `Content-Security-Policy` headers to prevent CSP from blocking Cypress's own injected scripts. `experimentalCspAllowList` lets you pass specific CSP directives through, enabling tests against a realistic CSP environment without completely disabling security policies.

```typescript
// cypress.config.ts — allow specific CSP directives through
import { defineConfig } from 'cypress';

export default defineConfig({
  e2e: {
    experimentalCspAllowList: [
      'default-src',    // base policy
      'img-src',        // test that image sources are properly whitelisted
      'font-src',       // verify font CDN is in policy
      'connect-src',    // validate that API origins are allowed
      // Do NOT include 'script-src' — it blocks Cypress's injected runner script
      // Do NOT include 'frame-src' — blocks the spec-bridge iframe for cy.origin()
    ],
  },
});

// In tests — assert CSP compliance without Cypress stripping the header
it('serves images only from approved CDN', () => {
  cy.visit('/');
  // If img-src is preserved and the page loads, the CDN is in the policy
  cy.get('[data-cy="hero-image"]').should('be.visible');
  // Verify the CSP header is present in the navigation response
  cy.intercept('GET', '/', (req) => {
    req.on('response', (res) => {
      expect(res.headers['content-security-policy']).to.include('img-src');
    });
  });
});
```

**[community]** WHY: `experimentalCspAllowList: true` (boolean, allow all non-Cypress-breaking directives) is a footgun — it passes through `frame-src` which blocks the `cy.origin()` spec-bridge iframe, causing all cross-origin tests to fail with `SecurityError: Blocked a frame from accessing a cross-origin frame`. The array form is always safer: explicitly list only the directives you need to test, excluding `script-src`, `frame-src`, and `worker-src`.

---

### 189. Accessibility Testing with `cypress-axe` — Scoped and Configured Checks

`cypress-axe` integrates Deque's axe-core engine into Cypress tests. The key to useful a11y testing is scoping checks to meaningful page areas and configuring which WCAG rules to enforce, rather than running a blanket full-page scan on every spec.

```typescript
// cypress/support/e2e.ts — inject axe in beforeEach for all E2E tests
import 'cypress-axe';

// cypress/component/accessibility.cy.tsx
describe('Checkout form accessibility', () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    cy.visit('/checkout');
    // Inject axe AFTER the page is interactive — not before hydration completes
    cy.get('[data-cy="checkout-form"]').should('be.visible');
    cy.injectAxe();
  });

  it('passes WCAG 2.1 AA for the checkout form', () => {
    cy.checkA11y(
      '[data-cy="checkout-form"]',   // scope to specific element
      {
        runOnly: {
          type:   'tag',
          values: ['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa'],  // only check AA rules
        },
        rules: {
          // Disable rules that are known false-positives for your design system
          'color-contrast': { enabled: false },  // custom design token — reviewed separately
        },
      },
      // Custom violation reporter for CI — writes structured output
      (violations) => {
        const messages = violations.map((v) =>
          `[${v.impact}] ${v.id}: ${v.description}\n  ${
            v.nodes.map((n) => n.target.join(', ')).join('\n  ')
          }`
        );
        cy.task('log', messages.join('\n\n'));
        throw new Error(`${violations.length} accessibility violation(s) found`);
      }
    );
  });

  it('supports keyboard-only navigation through form fields', () => {
    cy.get('[data-cy="card-number"]').focus();
    cy.press('Tab');
    cy.focused().should('have.attr', 'data-cy', 'expiry-date');
    cy.press('Tab');
    cy.focused().should('have.attr', 'data-cy', 'cvv');
    cy.press('Tab');
    cy.focused().should('have.attr', 'data-cy', 'submit-order');
  });
});
```

**[community]** WHY: Running `cy.checkA11y()` on `document` (no scope argument) in `beforeEach` on every test produces hundreds of noise violations from third-party widgets, analytics scripts, and CSS-in-JS hydration artifacts that your team doesn't own. Scope checks to the component under test and run them in a dedicated accessibility spec rather than scattered across functional tests. This keeps failure signal clean — a failing a11y check in a scoped spec means something in your component broke, not a third-party widget.

---

### 190. cy.press('Escape') — Modal Dismiss and Focus-Return Testing (Cypress 15.1+)

`cy.press('Escape')` dispatches a native `keydown` event for the Escape key, enabling tests for modal dialogs, dropdowns, and drawer panels that dismiss on Escape without JavaScript simulation hacks.

```typescript
describe('Modal keyboard dismissal', () => {
  it('dismisses the dialog and returns focus to the trigger', () => {
    cy.visit('/products');
    cy.get('[data-cy="open-filter-modal"]').click();
    cy.get('[data-cy="filter-modal"]').should('be.visible');

    // Escape should close the modal
    cy.press('Escape');
    cy.get('[data-cy="filter-modal"]').should('not.exist');

    // Focus must return to the trigger element (WCAG 2.1 SC 2.1.2)
    cy.focused().should('have.attr', 'data-cy', 'open-filter-modal');
  });

  it('does not close modal when Escape is pressed inside a select', () => {
    cy.get('[data-cy="open-filter-modal"]').click();
    // Open a native <select> inside the modal
    cy.get('[data-cy="category-select"]').focus().select('Electronics', { force: true });

    // Browser handles Escape to close the select — NOT the modal
    cy.press('Escape');
    // Modal must remain open because Escape was consumed by the select
    cy.get('[data-cy="filter-modal"]').should('be.visible');
  });
});
```

**[community]** WHY: Before `cy.press('Escape')`, the standard approach was `cy.get('body').type('{esc}')`. This works, but `cy.type()` dispatches `keydown`, `keypress`, `keyup` AND `input` events — the extra `input` event fires on whatever element has focus, potentially triggering form validation and corrupting test state for the assertion that follows. `cy.press('Escape')` dispatches only the native keyboard events without `input`, matching the browser's actual behavior for non-printable keys.

---

### 191. `Cypress.Commands.overwrite()` — Masked Logging for Sensitive Inputs

`Cypress.Commands.overwrite()` intercepts calls to existing Cypress commands, enabling security-hardened logging for commands that handle credentials. This prevents passwords and tokens from appearing in Cypress Cloud recordings, screenshots, and test reports.

```typescript
// cypress/support/commands.ts — mask type() calls when log:false is set
Cypress.Commands.overwrite(
  'type',
  function (originalFn, element, text, options: Cypress.TypeOptions = {}) {
    // If the caller set log: false, mask the text in the log instead of
    // completely suppressing logging (preserving the command chain timeline)
    if (options.log === false) {
      options.log = true;
      Cypress.log({
        name:    'type',
        message: '****',   // mask the actual value
        $el:     element as JQuery<HTMLElement>,
      });
      options.log = false;  // disable the built-in log now that we've logged manually
    }
    return originalFn(element, text, options);
  }
);

// Usage: passwords are masked in recordings but command chain is visible
cy.get('[data-cy="password"]').type(Cypress.env('PASSWORD'), { log: false });
// Command Log shows: type (****)  — not: type (myS3cr3tP@ss!)
```

**[community]** WHY: By default, `cy.type(value, { log: false })` completely hides the type command from the Command Log and from Cypress Cloud Test Replay. This makes debugging auth failures difficult because the log shows a gap in the command sequence. The overwrite pattern preserves the command in the log as `****` — you can see that a type occurred, see the element, see the timing, but not the value. This is the pattern used by the Cypress Real-World App for credential handling.

---

### 192. `cy.wrap()` Circular Reference Guard (Cypress 15.7+)

Cypress 15.7 fixed a crash where `cy.wrap()` on an object containing circular references caused infinite recursion during serialization for the Command Log. Before 15.7, any object with a `parent` or `this` property pointing back to itself would crash the test runner.

```typescript
// Pattern: safe wrap of complex store objects with circular references
// This was a crash in Cypress < 15.7 — now works correctly

class StoreNode {
  public parent: StoreNode | null = null;
  public children: StoreNode[]   = [];
  constructor(public name: string) {}
  addChild(child: StoreNode) {
    child.parent = this;  // circular reference: child.parent → this
    this.children.push(child);
  }
}

it('processes store tree without circular-reference crash', () => {
  const root  = new StoreNode('root');
  const child = new StoreNode('child');
  root.addChild(child);

  // Cypress 15.7+: safe; <15.7: `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded`
  cy.wrap(root).its('name').should('eq', 'root');
  cy.wrap(child).its('parent.name').should('eq', 'root');
});

// Guard pattern for projects that need to support Cypress < 15.7
function safeWrap<T extends object>(obj: T): Cypress.Chainable<T> {
  // Strip circular references before wrapping on older Cypress versions
  const safe = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(obj, (_key, val) =>
    typeof val === 'object' && val !== null && val === obj ? '[Circular]' : val
  ));
  return cy.wrap(safe as T);
}
```

**[community]** WHY: The crash was silent on the CI log — the runner process exited with a non-zero code but left no useful error message pointing at circular references. Teams debugging this spent hours thinking it was a memory leak in their application. If you're on Cypress < 15.7 and wrapping store/state objects, always serialize through `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(...))` before wrapping. After 15.7, the fix is built in and no workaround is needed.

---

### 193. `cy.request()` Multipart Form Data Upload

`cy.request()` supports `multipart/form-data` uploads via the `form: true` option combined with a `FormData`-compatible body. This is the correct approach for testing file upload API endpoints without triggering the browser's file dialog.

```typescript
// cypress/support/api-helpers.ts
export function uploadProfileImage(
  userId: string,
  imagePath: string
): Cypress.Chainable<{ avatarUrl: string }> {
  // Read the fixture file as binary
  return cy.fixture(imagePath, 'binary').then((imageData: string) => {
    // Convert to a Blob via Cypress.Blob helper
    const blob = Cypress.Blob.binaryStringToBlob(imageData, 'image/png');

    // Build FormData manually — cy.request() serializes it with proper boundary
    const formData = new FormData();
    formData.append('userId', userId);
    formData.append('avatar', blob, 'avatar.png');

    return cy.request<{ avatarUrl: string }>({
      method:      'POST',
      url:         '/api/profile/avatar',
      body:        formData,
      // Do NOT set Content-Type manually — the browser must set it with
      // the boundary parameter: "multipart/form-data; boundary=----..."
    });
  }).then((res) => res.body);
}

// In spec:
it('updates user avatar via API', () => {
  uploadProfileImage('user-123', 'test-avatar.png').then(({ avatarUrl }) => {
    expect(avatarUrl).to.match(/^https:\/\/cdn\.example\.com\//);
  });
});
```

**[community]** WHY: Setting `headers: { 'Content-Type': 'multipart/form-data' }` manually in `cy.request()` breaks the upload because the `Content-Type` header must include the `boundary` parameter (e.g., `multipart/form-data; boundary=----WebKitFormBoundaryXXX`) that the browser generates when it serializes the `FormData` object. Explicitly setting the header overrides the auto-generated boundary, and the server receives malformed data. Always omit the `Content-Type` header when sending `FormData` — `cy.request()` will set it correctly.

---

### 194. cy.intercept() `times: 1` + `forceNetworkError` — Transient Failure Resilience Testing

Combining `times: 1` with `forceNetworkError: true` (or a `statusCode: 503`) tests how the application recovers from a single transient failure before succeeding on retry. This is the correct pattern for testing exponential backoff, retry logic, and error boundary recovery.

```typescript
describe('Cart API resilience', () => {
  it('retries the add-to-cart request after a transient 503', () => {
    // First request fails with 503
    cy.intercept('POST', '/api/cart/items', {
      statusCode: 503,
      body:       { error: 'Service temporarily unavailable' },
      times:      1,  // match once, then unregister this route
    }).as('cartFail');

    // Second request (retry) succeeds — real server responds
    cy.intercept('POST', '/api/cart/items').as('cartSuccess');

    cy.visit('/products/123');
    cy.get('[data-cy="add-to-cart"]').click();

    // First attempt returns 503
    cy.wait('@cartFail').its('response.statusCode').should('eq', 503);

    // App should show retry indicator, then succeed
    cy.get('[data-cy="cart-retry-indicator"]').should('be.visible');
    cy.wait('@cartSuccess').its('response.statusCode').should('eq', 201);

    cy.get('[data-cy="cart-count"]').should('contain', '1');
  });

  it('shows error boundary after 3 consecutive network failures', () => {
    // Fail 3 times with a hard network error
    cy.intercept('POST', '/api/cart/items', { forceNetworkError: true, times: 3 }).as('cartError');

    cy.visit('/products/123');
    cy.get('[data-cy="add-to-cart"]').click();

    cy.wait(['@cartError', '@cartError', '@cartError']);
    cy.get('[data-cy="error-boundary"]').should('contain', 'Unable to add item');
  });
});
```

**[community]** WHY: A common mistake is to not set `times: 1` on the error intercept, causing the real retry request to also match the error route and producing an infinite retry loop in the test. Without `times`, Cypress keeps matching the same error route for every subsequent request to the URL. `times: 1` correctly unregisters the error route after the first match, letting subsequent requests reach either the real server or a success stub.

---

### 195. TypeScript 6 `const` Object Literal Migration for Cypress Config

TypeScript 6 `isolatedModules: true` (now the default in many frameworks) treats `const enum` as an error because it requires full type information to erase. Cypress config files and custom command type definitions that used `const enum` must migrate to plain object literals with `as const`.

```typescript
// BEFORE — breaks with TypeScript 6 isolatedModules (used in cypress.config.ts)
const enum TestRole {
  Admin    = 'admin',
  ReadOnly = 'readonly',
  Guest    = 'guest',
}

// AFTER — TypeScript 6 safe, fully erasable syntax
const TestRole = {
  Admin:    'admin',
  ReadOnly: 'readonly',
  Guest:    'guest',
} as const;

type TestRole = (typeof TestRole)[keyof typeof TestRole];
// Usage: TestRole.Admin === 'admin' — same behavior, no const enum

// cypress/support/commands.ts — type-safe login helper
declare global {
  namespace Cypress {
    interface Chainable {
      loginAs(role: TestRole): Chainable<void>;
    }
  }
}

Cypress.Commands.add('loginAs', (role: TestRole) => {
  cy.session(
    ['login', role],
    () => {
      cy.request('POST', '/api/auth/test-login', { role })
        .its('body.token')
        .then((token) => window.localStorage.setItem('token', token));
    },
    { cacheAcrossSpecs: true }
  );
});

// In spec
cy.loginAs(TestRole.Admin);
```

**[community]** WHY: Cypress 15.0 replaced `ts-node` with `tsx` for config parsing. `tsx` compiles TypeScript with `isolatedModules: true` semantics, which means `const enum` references in `cypress.config.ts` or any file imported into the config throw `Error: const enum member initializers can only be used with string literals`. The error appears during Cypress startup, not during the TypeScript compile step, making it confusing to debug — the TypeScript compiler (`tsc`) may not flag it if your project's `tsconfig.json` doesn't have `isolatedModules: true`.

---

### 196. Cypress Cloud Branch Review Integration — Blocking Merges on Test Failures

Cypress Cloud's Branch Review feature connects to GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket via webhook to post test results as commit status checks, blocking PR merges until the full Cypress run passes. This requires a properly configured `projectId` and record key in CI.

```yaml
# .github/workflows/cypress.yml — full Branch Review setup
name: Cypress E2E

on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  push:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  cypress:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        container: [1, 2, 3, 4]  # 4 parallel machines
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: npm

      - run: npm ci

      - name: Cypress run (recorded)
        uses: cypress-io/github-action@v6
        with:
          record:   true
          parallel: true
          group:    'E2E — PR'
          # ci-build-id ties parallel machines to the same Cloud run
          ci-build-id: ${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          start: npm run dev
          wait-on: 'http://localhost:3000'
        env:
          CYPRESS_RECORD_KEY: ${{ secrets.CYPRESS_RECORD_KEY }}
          # Required for Branch Review status check posting
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        if: failure()
        with:
          name: cypress-screenshots-${{ matrix.container }}
          path: cypress/screenshots
          if-no-files-found: ignore
```

**[community]** WHY: Without `GITHUB_TOKEN` in the env, Cypress Cloud cannot post the commit status check to GitHub — the Branch Review widget shows "Pending" indefinitely even after the run completes. The token is needed for Cypress Cloud to call the GitHub Checks API on behalf of the repository. The `ci-build-id` parameter is equally critical for parallel runs — without it, each parallel machine creates a separate Cloud run rather than contributing results to a single run, and Branch Review reports 4 partial runs instead of 1 complete run.

---

### 197. Cypress Flakiness Detection Strategy — `detect-flake-but-always-fail` for Pre-Merge Gates

The `detect-flake-but-always-fail` retry strategy reruns failing tests up to `maxRetries` times and marks the test as "flaky" if it passes on any retry — but crucially still fails the suite. This is the correct strategy for pre-merge CI where flaky = broken.

```typescript
// cypress.config.ts — fail-fast flakiness detection for CI
import { defineConfig } from 'cypress';

export default defineConfig({
  e2e: {
    retries: {
      // detect-flake-but-always-fail: retry up to 2 times, always fail if any retry passes
      runMode: {
        strategy:   'detect-flake-but-always-fail',
        maxRetries: 2,
        // passesRequired is NOT used with detect-flake-but-always-fail — it applies
        // only to detect-flake-and-pass-on-threshold
      },
      // In open mode, use the simpler retry strategy for local development
      openMode: 1,
    },
  },
});

// cypress/e2e/flake-demo.cy.ts — example of a genuinely flaky test
let callCount = 0;

it('demonstrates flakiness detection', () => {
  // This test fails on attempt 1, passes on attempt 2 — Cypress marks it "Flaky"
  callCount++;
  if (callCount === 1) {
    cy.visit('/dashboard');
    // Intentional race condition — remove this in prod
    cy.get('[data-cy="widget"]').should('be.visible');
  }
});
// Result: test is marked "Flaky" AND fails the CI run
// Without detect-flake-but-always-fail, a simple retry: 2 would PASS this test
```

**[community]** WHY: The default Cypress retry behavior (`retries: 2`) silently passes a flaky test if it succeeds on any retry. This produces a "green" CI run for code that is non-deterministically broken — a form of technical debt that accumulates until the flakiness rate becomes so high that merges start being blocked randomly. `detect-flake-but-always-fail` makes flakiness visible immediately in CI and surfaces it in Cypress Cloud's Flaky Test dashboard. The tradeoff is that the strategy requires a `openMode`/`runMode` object syntax — setting `retries: { strategy: '...' }` without specifying `openMode`/`runMode` separately throws a config validation error.

---

## Additional Real-World Gotchas (Cycle 24) [community]

178. **`injectDocumentDomain: true` will be removed in a future Cypress major version — it is not a permanent escape hatch** [community] — Cypress 14.0 added `injectDocumentDomain: true` as a temporary migration config to give teams time to rewrite cross-subdomain tests using `cy.origin()`. The documentation explicitly states this option "will be removed in a future release." Teams that set it and forget it are accumulating migration debt. The removal will be a silent breaking change — existing subdomain tests will stop working with no deprecation warning in test output, only in the Cypress startup log.

179. **`req.on('response')` cannot change the `statusCode` — use `req.continue((res) => { res.statusCode = ... })` instead** [community] — The `response` event fired on `req.on('response', fn)` exposes a read-only view of the status code for observation. Attempting to assign `res.statusCode = 206` inside a `req.on('response')` handler silently fails — the browser receives the original status code. To mutate the status code, you must use `req.continue((res) => { res.statusCode = 206; })`. This is an asymmetry between the observation API (`req.on`) and the mutation API (`req.continue`) that is not clearly documented.

180. **`cy.origin()` `args` uses the structured clone algorithm — functions, class instances, and Symbols are silently dropped** [community] — The `args` object passed to `cy.origin()` is serialized via the HTML spec's structured clone algorithm before being sent to the secondary origin. Structured clone supports plain objects, arrays, `Date`, `RegExp`, `Map`, `Set`, and typed arrays — but silently drops `function` values, class instances with prototype methods, and `Symbol` properties. Teams that pass a helper object like `{ formatDate: (d: Date) => d.toISOString() }` will receive `{}` inside the callback with no error. Pass only primitive values and plain serializable data through `args`.

181. **Angular zoneless mount from `cypress/angular` (not `cypress/angular-zoneless`) causes infinite timeout with Signals-based components** [community] — Using the wrong mount import is a silent failure. The component mounts successfully, interactions fire, but all `cy.get()` assertions hang for 4 seconds before timing out. This is because the standard Angular mount wraps the fixture in `NgZone` and waits for zone stability before resolving assertions — but a zoneless component never stabilizes the zone. The fix is a single import line change: `import { mount } from 'cypress/angular-zoneless'`.

182. **`experimentalMemoryManagement` is Chromium-only and has no effect on Firefox or WebKit** [community] — Setting `experimentalMemoryManagement: true` in `cypress.config.ts` on a Firefox CI run produces no warning and appears to work, but GC is never triggered between tests. Firefox has its own memory management that Cypress cannot control via the Chromium DevTools Protocol. If your CI matrix includes Firefox, you must set `numTestsKeptInMemory` low (e.g., 5) to limit Command Log memory retention — this is the only cross-browser memory control available.

183. **`experimentalCspAllowList` with `frame-src` breaks `cy.origin()` — the spec-bridge iframe is blocked by the app's own CSP** [community] — `cy.origin()` works by loading a spec-bridge iframe at the secondary origin URL. If `frame-src` is in the allow list, the app's CSP `frame-src` directive is enforced — and if the Cypress runner is not an allowed frame source, the iframe is blocked with a `Refused to display in a frame because an ancestor violates the following Content Security Policy directive` error. Never include `frame-src` in `experimentalCspAllowList` unless your CSP explicitly allows `self` or wildcard frame sources.

184. **`cy.injectAxe()` called before the page is fully interactive produces false-negative a11y results** [community] — `cy.injectAxe()` executes immediately when called and runs axe against the DOM as it exists at that moment. If the app uses progressive hydration (React Server Components, Next.js streaming SSR, or async image loading), the DOM at `cy.injectAxe()` time may be incomplete — missing alt text on images that haven't loaded, missing ARIA roles on components that hydrate lazily. Always `cy.get('[data-cy="main-content"]').should('be.visible')` before `cy.injectAxe()` to ensure the DOM is stable.

185. **`cy.press('Escape')` is a no-op if no element has focus — Escape events must be dispatched to a focused element** [community] — `cy.press()` dispatches the key event to `document.activeElement`. If the active element is `document.body` (which has no keyboard event handlers), the Escape key press is dispatched but ignored by the browser. Modal and dropdown close handlers typically listen on a focused overlay element, the modal container itself, or the document with `event.target` checks. Before calling `cy.press('Escape')`, always ensure the modal's close button, the modal container, or a focusable element inside the modal has focus: `cy.get('[data-cy="modal"]').focus()` or `cy.get('[data-cy="close-modal"]').focus()`.

186. **`Cypress.Commands.overwrite()` cannot call the overwritten command by name — it must call `originalFn` or it will recurse infinitely** [community] — Inside an overwrite handler, calling `cy.type(...)` (the same command being overwritten) causes infinite recursion and a `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded`. The only way to invoke the original implementation is via the `originalFn` argument injected by Cypress. Teams that refactor an overwrite to delegate to another command via `cy.[commandName]()` must ensure they're not calling the overwritten command itself, even indirectly through a helper that ultimately calls `cy.type()`.

187. **`cy.wrap()` with circular references crashes Cypress versions before 15.7 with `Maximum call stack size exceeded`** [community] — Cypress 15.7 fixed the circular reference serialization bug. If your project pins Cypress to an older version, wrapping any object where `obj.x.parent === obj` will crash the test runner with a stack overflow during Command Log serialization. The error appears as a generic JavaScript stack overflow, not as a Cypress-specific error, making root-cause analysis difficult. Check `cy.wrap()` calls when debugging stack overflow crashes in older Cypress versions.

188. **`cy.request()` multipart upload breaks when `Content-Type` is set manually — the boundary is overwritten** [community] — When using `cy.request()` with a `FormData` body, Cypress automatically sets `Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary=<generated>`. Passing `headers: { 'Content-Type': 'multipart/form-data' }` explicitly overwrites this header without a boundary parameter, causing the server to reject the upload with `400 Bad Request: Could not read multipart request body`. The fix: never set `Content-Type` for `FormData` requests — omit it entirely and let Cypress set it automatically.

189. **`cy.intercept()` with `times: 1` and `forceNetworkError` still increments the alias hit count — `cy.wait('@alias')` only needs to be called once even though two requests are made** [community] — After a `times: 1` error route fires and is unregistered, Cypress creates a new alias for the next matching intercept (the success route registered after the error one). The error route alias (`@cartFail`) is matched exactly once. The success alias (`@cartSuccess`) is matched by the second request. `cy.wait(['@cartFail', '@cartSuccess'])` correctly awaits both. Teams mistakenly call `cy.wait('@cartFail')` twice (expecting two error responses) and time out on the second wait because the alias was only matched once.

190. **TypeScript 6 `const enum` in files imported by `cypress.config.ts` causes startup failure — even if the enum is not used in config** [community] — Cypress uses `tsx` to transpile `cypress.config.ts` with `isolatedModules: true` semantics. If `cypress.config.ts` imports (directly or transitively) any file containing a `const enum`, `tsx` throws at startup even if the `const enum` is not used in the config itself. This is a transitive dependency problem — renaming enums in deeply imported utility files requires careful auditing. Use `npx tsx --check cypress.config.ts` locally to detect the issue before pushing to CI.

191. **Cypress Cloud Branch Review requires `GITHUB_TOKEN` in CI env — without it, the commit status check is never posted and PRs show "Pending" forever** [community] — The `GITHUB_TOKEN` must be exposed as an environment variable (`env: GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}`) in the GitHub Actions step that runs Cypress. Without it, the Cypress Cloud API cannot post the commit check. The workflow will still run and results will appear in the Cloud dashboard, but the GitHub PR will show the status check as "Pending" indefinitely, effectively disabling the Branch Review merge gate.

192. **`detect-flake-but-always-fail` requires `runMode`/`openMode` sub-keys — setting `strategy` directly under `retries:` throws a config validation error** [community] — The correct syntax is `retries: { runMode: { strategy: 'detect-flake-but-always-fail', maxRetries: 2 }, openMode: 1 }`. Setting `retries: { strategy: '...', maxRetries: 2 }` without the `runMode`/`openMode` wrapper throws `ConfigValidationError: Invalid retry configuration`. The error message mentions "invalid schema" but doesn't show the correct nested structure, causing teams to spend time guessing the shape.

## Cycle 26 — 2026-05-13

### 198. Cypress Cloud MCP Integration — AI Agents Querying Live Test Data

The Cypress Cloud MCP (Model Context Protocol) exposes 11 read-only tools via `https://mcp.cypress.io/mcp`, allowing AI coding assistants (Cursor, Claude, VS Code Copilot) to query real-time test health, flaky test lists, failed test stack traces, and UI coverage analysis directly from the IDE.

```typescript
// .cursor/mcp.json — configure MCP client to point at Cypress Cloud
// (analogous config for Claude Desktop, VS Code)
// {
//   "servers": {
//     "cypress": {
//       "url": "https://mcp.cypress.io/mcp",
//       "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer <YOUR_CYPRESS_CLOUD_PAT>" }
//     }
//   }
// }

// cypress/support/e2e.ts — task that emits a run URL for the MCP tool to follow up on
Cypress.on('after:run', (results) => {
  if (results && 'runUrl' in results) {
    // In Cloud-recorded runs, results.runUrl points to the dashboard entry
    // Your AI assistant can paste this URL to the MCP tool for instant analysis
    cy.task('log', { message: 'Cloud run:', url: (results as { runUrl?: string }).runUrl });
  }
});

// Example: ask your AI assistant (Claude, Copilot) after a CI failure:
// "Use the Cypress Cloud MCP to show me failed tests from the last run on branch 'feat/checkout'"
// The AI calls get_run_summary → get_failed_tests → summarises root-cause without you
// switching to the browser dashboard.

// cypress.config.ts — ensure projectId is set so MCP can resolve your project
import { defineConfig } from 'cypress';

export default defineConfig({
  projectId: process.env.CYPRESS_PROJECT_ID ?? 'xxxxxxxx',
  e2e: {
    baseUrl: process.env.BASE_URL ?? 'http://localhost:3000',
  },
});
```

**Tradeoff / When to use:** Use MCP when your team already uses an AI coding assistant and wants to avoid context-switching to the Cypress Cloud dashboard. MCP is read-only (cannot write or delete), rate-limited to 100 tool requests per hour across all plans, and requires the run to have been recorded to Cloud — local `cypress run` without `--record` produces no data. When-NOT-to-use: offline/air-gapped CI environments where outbound HTTPS to `mcp.cypress.io` is blocked.

**[official]** The integration is available free on all Cypress Cloud plans with no minimum app version requirement.

### 199. Svelte 5 Component Testing (Alpha) — Runes and Snippet Props

Cypress 15.x introduced alpha support for Svelte 5 component testing with both Vite 5+ and Webpack 5 bundlers. Svelte 5's runes (`$state`, `$derived`, `$effect`) work inside mounted components but require the correct Svelte adapter import.

```typescript
// cypress/component/Counter.cy.ts — Svelte 5 runes-based component test
import { mount } from 'cypress/svelte';
import Counter from '../../src/Counter.svelte';

describe('Counter (Svelte 5 runes)', () => {
  it('increments via $state rune', () => {
    // Mount with initial props
    mount(Counter, {
      props: { initialCount: 0, step: 2 },
    });

    cy.get('[data-cy="count"]').should('have.text', '0');
    cy.get('[data-cy="increment"]').click();
    cy.get('[data-cy="count"]').should('have.text', '2');
  });

  it('exposes snippet props for slot-like content in Svelte 5', () => {
    // Svelte 5 replaces slots with "snippets" — pass them as props
    mount(Counter, {
      props: {
        initialCount: 10,
        // Snippets are passed via the `children` prop in Svelte 5 CT
        // (actual snippet objects are framework-internal; use slots API via mount options)
      },
    });

    cy.get('[data-cy="count"]').should('have.text', '10');
  });

  afterEach(() => {
    // Svelte 5 CT alpha: components must be explicitly unmounted to avoid
    // $effect cleanup leaks across tests
    cy.get('[data-cy="app-root"]').then(($el) => {
      // Cypress handles unmount automatically; this is a defensive check
      expect($el).to.exist;
    });
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff / When to use:** Use Svelte 5 CT when your project uses runes-based state management and you want fast, browser-native component tests without a full E2E stack. The alpha label means the mount API may change before GA — pin Cypress patch versions in lock files and review the CHANGELOG before upgrading. When-NOT-to-use: production test suites where stability is paramount; wait for beta/stable release.

**[official]** Svelte CT is marked alpha with support for Svelte 5 in Cypress 15.x. Breaking mount API changes are possible before GA.

### 200. `cy.intercept()` Browser Cache Bypass — Preventing Intercepts from Being Silently Skipped

If the browser returns a response from its HTTP cache, `cy.intercept()` never fires — the request never reaches the network layer. This is a silent failure: no error is thrown, the test continues, and your intercept alias is never matched, causing `cy.wait('@alias')` to timeout.

```typescript
// cypress/support/e2e.ts — global cache-busting middleware for all specs
// Adds Cache-Control: no-store to every outgoing request to prevent browser caching
Cypress.on('window:before:load', (win) => {
  // Prevent fetch/XHR from ever reading from cache
  const originalFetch = win.fetch;
  win.fetch = (input: RequestInfo | URL, init?: RequestInit) => {
    return originalFetch(input, {
      ...init,
      cache: 'no-store',
    });
  };
});

// cypress/e2e/product-api.cy.ts — explicit per-test cache bypass pattern
describe('Product API intercepts', () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    // Force-clear browser cache before each test so intercepts always fire
    cy.clearAllCookies();
    cy.clearAllLocalStorage();
    cy.clearAllSessionStorage();

    // Intercept + force no-cache on the response so the NEXT test also misses cache
    cy.intercept('GET', '/api/products*', (req) => {
      req.continue((res) => {
        // Strip caching headers from the response
        res.headers['cache-control'] = 'no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate';
        res.headers['pragma'] = 'no-cache';
        delete res.headers['etag'];
        delete res.headers['last-modified'];
      });
    }).as('getProducts');
  });

  it('intercepts are reliably matched', () => {
    cy.visit('/products');
    cy.wait('@getProducts').its('response.statusCode').should('eq', 200);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff / When to use:** Add the response header-stripping intercept in `beforeEach` for any spec that stubs or waits on network requests. The global `fetch` override is appropriate for apps where XHR isn't used. When-NOT-to-use: if you explicitly want to test caching behaviour (e.g., ETag-based conditional requests), do not strip cache headers — disable this middleware for those tests via a custom `cy.intercept()` override.

**[community]** WHY: Teams encounter this when running the same spec twice in a session — the first run populates the browser cache, and the second run's intercepts silently never fire. The test appears to pass (because the cached response delivers valid data) but the intercept alias is unmatched, so any `cy.wait('@alias')` times out on the second run. The root cause is the browser cache layer sitting below Cypress's network proxy.

### 201. `cy.session()` TTL Sentinel — Proactive Session Expiry Before the App Expires It

`cy.session()` cached sessions do not expire on their own during a run — but your app's server-side token may expire if a test suite runs longer than the session TTL. Adding a custom TTL sentinel in localStorage lets the `validate()` callback proactively refresh the session before the server rejects requests.

```typescript
// cypress/support/auth.ts — session with TTL sentinel
const SESSION_TTL_MS = 20 * 60 * 1000; // 20 minutes

export function loginWithTtl(email: string, password: string): void {
  cy.session(
    ['ttl-session', email],
    () => {
      cy.request('POST', '/api/auth/login', { email, password })
        .its('body')
        .then((body: { token: string }) => {
          window.localStorage.setItem('token', body.token);
          // Store epoch expiry so validate() can check it without a network request
          window.localStorage.setItem(
            'session_expires_at',
            String(Date.now() + SESSION_TTL_MS)
          );
        });
    },
    {
      validate() {
        // Read the sentinel — re-login if < 60 s left
        cy.window().then((win) => {
          const expiresAt = Number(win.localStorage.getItem('session_expires_at') ?? '0');
          const remainingMs = expiresAt - Date.now();
          if (remainingMs < 60_000) {
            // Throwing from validate() forces setup() to re-run
            throw new Error(`Session expires in ${remainingMs}ms — refreshing`);
          }
        });
      },
      cacheAcrossSpecs: true,
    }
  );
}
```

**Tradeoff / When to use:** Use this pattern when your auth token TTL is shorter than your full test suite runtime (e.g., 30-minute JWT in a 45-minute CI run). It prevents `401 Unauthorized` mid-suite failures that are hard to debug without knowing the session age. When-NOT-to-use: if `validate()` calls the network (`/api/me`), it adds latency to every test's setup phase; the localStorage sentinel avoids that overhead but requires clock accuracy. Do not rely on this for OAuth flows where refresh tokens are involved — those require the full token-refresh round-trip.

**[community]** WHY: A common misunderstanding is that `cacheAcrossSpecs: true` implies the session stays valid indefinitely. It does not — it only means Cypress reuses the cached cookies/localStorage across spec files; it does not know or enforce your app's token TTL. Without a TTL sentinel, a long CI run silently transitions from authenticated to `401` mid-suite, making the failing spec appear to have a selector bug rather than an auth problem.

### 202. Cypress `--posix-exit-codes` CLI Flag — Standardising Exit Codes for CI Pipelines

Cypress historically used non-standard exit codes. The `--posix-exit-codes` flag (added in Cypress 15.x) normalises exit codes to POSIX conventions so CI pipelines can distinguish pass (0) from test-failure (1) from infrastructure-error (2+).

```yaml
# .github/workflows/cypress.yml — posix-exit-codes for reliable pipeline branching
name: Cypress E2E

on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  cypress:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version: '22', cache: npm }

      - run: npm ci

      - name: Run Cypress with posix exit codes
        run: |
          npx cypress run \
            --record \
            --posix-exit-codes \
            --pass-with-no-tests \
            --ci-build-id "${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}"
        env:
          CYPRESS_RECORD_KEY: ${{ secrets.CYPRESS_RECORD_KEY }}
```

```typescript
// cypress/e2e/exit-code-check.cy.ts — verify exit code semantics in local CI scripts
// Use this to validate your pipeline branching before promoting to production
describe('Exit code contract', () => {
  it('passes cleanly — exit code 0 expected', () => {
    cy.visit('/');
    cy.get('body').should('exist');
  });

  // To test exit code 1 (test failure), uncomment:
  // it('fails — exit code 1 expected', () => {
  //   cy.get('[data-cy="nonexistent"]').should('be.visible');
  // });
});
```

**Tradeoff / When to use:** Use `--posix-exit-codes` whenever your CI pipeline scripts branch on exit codes (shell `if [ $? -eq 1 ]`, GitHub Actions exit-code inspection, or scripted Slack notifications). When-NOT-to-use: if your CI system only inspects pass/fail without caring about the specific exit code, the flag adds no value.

**[official]** `--posix-exit-codes` was added alongside `--pass-with-no-tests` in Cypress 15.x to improve CI integration ergonomics.

### 203. `cy.prompt()` Placeholder Caching for Dynamic Test Loops

`cy.prompt()` caches AI-generated selector mappings keyed on the prompt text. Using dynamic string interpolation instead of static prompt strings busts the cache on every run — defeating the performance optimization and burning rate-limit quota.

```typescript
// cypress/e2e/checkout.cy.ts — WRONG: dynamic prompt string busts selector cache
// DON'T DO THIS
const itemName = 'Widget Pro 3000';
cy.prompt(`Add the product "${itemName}" to the cart`);
// Each unique product name = unique prompt string = new AI round-trip = rate limit consumed

// CORRECT: use placeholders to keep prompt static, pass values as data
cy.prompt(
  'Add the product "{{productName}}" to the cart then proceed to checkout',
  { productName: 'Widget Pro 3000' }
  // placeholder substitution — prompt text stays constant → cache hits every time
);

// cypress/e2e/multi-product-checkout.cy.ts — loop with cached prompts
const products: Array<{ productName: string; qty: number }> = [
  { productName: 'Widget Pro', qty: 2 },
  { productName: 'Gadget Plus', qty: 1 },
  { productName: 'Nano Gizmo', qty: 3 },
];

for (const { productName, qty } of products) {
  cy.prompt(
    'Add {{qty}} units of "{{productName}}" to the cart',
    { productName, qty: String(qty) }
  );
  // Only the first iteration performs an AI round-trip;
  // iterations 2+ hit the cached selector mapping
}

// After the loop — assert the cart total
cy.get('[data-cy="cart-item-count"]').should('have.text', '6');
```

**Tradeoff / When to use:** Use placeholders whenever prompt text contains test-specific values (user names, product IDs, dollar amounts). Static prompt text is the cache key — keep it invariant across parameterised runs. When-NOT-to-use: `cy.prompt()` is E2E only (no component testing), Chromium-only, English-optimized, and has a hard 50-step limit per call plus a rate limit of 600 prompts/hour (paid) / 100 prompts/hour (free). Do not use in air-gapped CI.

**[official]** Placeholder syntax `{{key}}` is documented in the `cy.prompt()` API as the correct way to inject dynamic values while preserving cache efficiency.

**[community]** WHY: Teams discover the caching gotcha when they see their CI rate-limit counter climbing faster than expected. Each unique prompt string is treated as a separate cacheable entity — parameterised loops without placeholders call the AI API N times (once per iteration) instead of 1 time.

### 204. Svelte 5 CT Alpha — Verifying `$effect` Cleanup with Stub-at-Window Pattern

Svelte 5's `$effect` rune runs cleanup functions when the component unmounts. In Cypress CT, `$effect` cleanup callbacks may run asynchronously relative to the next `cy.mount()` call, causing resource leaks between tests.

```typescript
// cypress/component/WebSocketWidget.cy.ts — verify $effect cleanup fires on unmount
import { mount } from 'cypress/svelte';
import WebSocketWidget from '../../src/WebSocketWidget.svelte';

describe('WebSocketWidget — Svelte 5 $effect cleanup', () => {
  let wsConnectSpy: sinon.SinonStub;
  let wsCloseSpy: sinon.SinonStub;

  beforeEach(() => {
    // Stub the WebSocket constructor at the window level before mounting
    cy.window().then((win) => {
      wsConnectSpy = cy.stub();
      wsCloseSpy  = cy.stub();

      class MockWebSocket {
        constructor(url: string) { wsConnectSpy(url); }
        close()                  { wsCloseSpy();      }
        addEventListener()       {}
        removeEventListener()    {}
      }
      // @ts-expect-error — intentional override for testing
      win.WebSocket = MockWebSocket;
    });
  });

  it('opens WebSocket on mount', () => {
    mount(WebSocketWidget, { props: { endpoint: 'wss://api.example.com/events' } });
    cy.wrap(wsConnectSpy).should('have.been.calledOnceWith', 'wss://api.example.com/events');
  });

  it('closes WebSocket on unmount ($effect cleanup)', () => {
    mount(WebSocketWidget, { props: { endpoint: 'wss://api.example.com/events' } });

    // Re-mounting unmounts the previous component → triggers $effect cleanup
    mount(WebSocketWidget, { props: { endpoint: 'wss://api.example.com/v2/events' } });

    // Yield the event loop so async cleanup can complete before asserting
    cy.wait(0);

    // wsCloseSpy should have been called exactly once (cleanup from first mount)
    cy.wrap(wsCloseSpy).should('have.been.calledOnce');
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff / When to use:** Use this pattern for any Svelte 5 component that registers external resources in `$effect`. The stub-at-window approach is the only reliable way to intercept browser globals inside Cypress CT. When-NOT-to-use: if the component does not use `$effect` for resource management, cleanup verification is unnecessary.

**[community]** WHY: Svelte 5 CT is in alpha and the Cypress adapter does not guarantee synchronous `$effect` cleanup before the next `cy.mount()` call. Resource leaks (open WebSockets, timers, ResizeObservers) cause subsequent tests to fail with errors that point to the wrong test, making the root cause invisible in the test output. The `cy.wait(0)` pattern yields the JavaScript event loop and gives Svelte's effect scheduler time to run pending cleanups.

---

### 205. `experimentalFastVisibility` — When Point-Sampling Breaks Shadow DOM Tests

`experimentalFastVisibility: true` replaces the legacy visibility algorithm with a faster point-sampling approach that checks whether the element's centre point is visible in the viewport. The tradeoff: it does not pierce Shadow DOM trees and treats elements outside the viewport differently from the legacy algorithm.

```typescript
// cypress.config.ts — conditionally enable experimentalFastVisibility
import { defineConfig } from 'cypress';

export default defineConfig({
  e2e: {
    // WARNING: do NOT enable if your app uses Shadow DOM web components
    // cy.get('[data-cy="shadow-host"]').shadow().find('button').should('be.visible')
    // will FAIL with experimentalFastVisibility — point-sampling cannot pierce shadow roots
    experimentalFastVisibility: false, // leave OFF for apps using <custom-element> with shadow DOM
  },
  component: {
    // Safe to enable for React/Vue/Svelte CT — those frameworks don't use Shadow DOM by default
    experimentalFastVisibility: true,
    devServer: { framework: 'react', bundler: 'vite' },
  },
});

// cypress/e2e/web-components.cy.ts — guard pattern for shadow DOM visibility tests
const FAST_VIS = Cypress.config('experimentalFastVisibility' as keyof Cypress.Config);

it('shadow DOM button responds to interaction', function () {
  cy.visit('/component-demo');

  if (FAST_VIS) {
    // Visibility assertion inside shadow root unreliable with fast visibility;
    // assert existence + interactability instead
    cy.get('[data-cy="shadow-host"]')
      .shadow()
      .find('[data-cy="action-btn"]')
      .should('exist')
      .click();
  } else {
    cy.get('[data-cy="shadow-host"]')
      .shadow()
      .find('[data-cy="action-btn"]')
      .should('be.visible')
      .click();
  }

  cy.get('[data-cy="result"]').should('have.text', 'clicked');
});
```

**Tradeoff / When to use:** Enable `experimentalFastVisibility` for test suites targeting standard React/Vue/Angular apps (no Shadow DOM) — expect 10-30% speedup on assertion-heavy specs due to reduced layout recalculation. When-NOT-to-use: any spec targeting custom elements with shadow roots, apps with translucent overlays (cookie banners, loading veils), or tests relying on off-viewport visibility semantics.

**[official]** `experimentalFastVisibility` explicitly does not support Shadow DOM — this is documented as a known limitation of the point-sampling approach.

**[community]** WHY: Teams enabling `experimentalFastVisibility` globally start seeing intermittent failures on web-component-heavy pages with no obvious cause. The assertion fails with the generic `expected to be visible` message — it does not mention shadow DOM — leading teams to suspect a selector issue or timing problem and waste hours debugging the wrong thing.
