### 191. Typed cy.intercept() Generics for Request and Response Body Safety  [official]

Cypress TypeScript definitions support generics on `cy.intercept()` for compile-time safety on intercepted request/response body shapes, preventing shape drift between test stubs and API contracts.

```typescript
// Define typed API shapes (can be shared with the app's OpenAPI-generated types)
interface CreateOrderRequest {
  productId: string;
  quantity: number;
  shippingAddress: { street: string; city: string; country: string };
}

interface CreateOrderResponse {
  orderId: string;
  status: 'pending' | 'confirmed';
  estimatedDelivery: string;
}

it('places an order and validates request/response shape', () => {
  cy.intercept<CreateOrderRequest, CreateOrderResponse>(
    'POST',
    '/api/orders',
    (req) => {
      // req.body is typed as CreateOrderRequest
      const body = req.body as CreateOrderRequest;
      expect(body.productId).to.be.a('string');
      expect(body.quantity).to.be.gte(1);
      expect(body.shippingAddress.country).to.match(/^[A-Z]{2}$/);

      req.reply({
        statusCode: 201,
        body: {
          orderId: 'ord_test_001',
          status: 'confirmed',
          estimatedDelivery: '2026-05-21',
        } satisfies CreateOrderResponse, // compile-time check on stub shape
      });
    }
  ).as('createOrder');

  cy.visit('/checkout');
  cy.get('[data-cy="place-order"]').click();

  cy.wait('@createOrder').then(({ request, response }) => {
    const reqBody = request.body as CreateOrderRequest;
    const resBody = response?.body as CreateOrderResponse;
    expect(reqBody.quantity).to.be.gte(1);
    expect(resBody.orderId).to.match(/^ord_/);
  });

  cy.get('[data-cy="order-confirmed"]').should('be.visible');
});
```

**Tradeoff / When to use:** Use typed intercept generics for core API contracts (order creation, payment, auth) where shape regressions carry high business risk. The types serve as executable documentation of the contract. When NOT to use: don't bother for simple GET stubs where only the presence of a response matters — the type definition overhead is not justified. Named alternative: `cy.request()` with a generic return type for pure API contract testing without UI.

**[official]** The `cy.intercept<Req, Res>()` generic signature is in the official Cypress TypeScript definitions from Cypress 12+.

---

### 192. cy.press() for Global Keyboard Shortcut and Focus Trap Testing  [official]

`cy.press()` (Cypress 14+) fires keyboard events at the document level without requiring a focused element, making it the correct tool for global shortcuts and modal focus trap validation.

```typescript
// cypress/e2e/keyboard-shortcuts.cy.ts
describe('Global keyboard shortcuts', () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    loginAsRole('user');
    cy.visit('/dashboard');
    cy.window().focus(); // required in headless CI — ensures window has focus
  });

  it('/ shortcut opens global search modal', () => {
    cy.get('body').click(); // deselect any focused element
    cy.press(Cypress.Keyboard.Keys.SLASH);
    cy.get('[data-cy="search-modal"]').should('be.visible');
    cy.focused().should('have.attr', 'data-cy', 'search-input');
  });

  it('Escape closes modal and returns focus to trigger element', () => {
    cy.get('[data-cy="open-settings"]').click();
    cy.get('[data-cy="settings-modal"]').should('be.visible');
    cy.press(Cypress.Keyboard.Keys.ESCAPE);
    cy.get('[data-cy="settings-modal"]').should('not.exist');
    cy.focused().should('have.attr', 'data-cy', 'open-settings');
  });

  it('Tab key cycles focus within an open dialog (focus trap)', () => {
    cy.get('[data-cy="open-dialog"]').click();
    cy.get('[data-cy="dialog"]').should('be.visible');

    const trapOrder = ['dialog-name', 'dialog-email', 'dialog-cancel', 'dialog-confirm'];

    trapOrder.forEach((testId) => {
      cy.focused().should('have.attr', 'data-cy', testId);
      cy.press(Cypress.Keyboard.Keys.TAB);
    });

    // Tab from last item wraps to first — confirming the focus trap
    cy.focused().should('have.attr', 'data-cy', 'dialog-name');
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff / When to use:** Use `cy.press()` for document-level keyboard events and focus-trap validation. When NOT to use: don't use `cy.press()` when typing into a specific element — use `cy.get(...).type('{key}')` which targets the element directly. Note: `cy.press()` yields `null`, so you cannot chain `.should()` directly off it (see gotcha #199 in this file). Named alternative: `cy.get('body').type('{esc}', { force: true })` works for Escape key but requires `force: true` which bypasses visibility checks.

**[official]** `cy.press()` requires the browser window to have OS-level focus. Add `cy.window().focus()` in `beforeEach` for reliable headless CI execution.

---

### 193. experimentalFastVisibility — Accurate Visibility via checkVisibility()  [official]

`experimentalFastVisibility` (Cypress 14+) replaces jQuery's `:visible` check with the browser-native `checkVisibility()` API, fixing false-positives from CSS `opacity: 0` and `content-visibility: auto`.

```typescript
// cypress.config.ts — enable fast visibility checking
import { defineConfig } from 'cypress';

export default defineConfig({
  e2e: {
    experimentalFastVisibility: true,
  },
  component: {
    devServer: { framework: 'react', bundler: 'vite' },
    experimentalFastVisibility: true,
  },
});
```

```typescript
// Migration checklist — test assertions affected by the flag change:

// Case 1: opacity:0 elements
// BEFORE: cy.get('[data-cy="fade-out-tooltip"]').should('not.be.visible') → FAILS
//   jQuery `:visible` considers opacity:0 VISIBLE
// AFTER: cy.get('[data-cy="fade-out-tooltip"]').should('not.be.visible') → PASSES
//   checkVisibility() correctly treats opacity:0 as NOT visible

// Case 2: content-visibility:auto (virtual scroll rows)
// cy.get('[data-cy="virtual-row"]').should('be.visible') may fail for off-screen rows
// Fix: assert only on rows within the visible viewport range

// Guard: detect the flag at runtime for conditional test logic
it('tooltip hidden via opacity is correctly detected as not visible', () => {
  cy.visit('/product-card');
  cy.get('[data-cy="tooltip"]').should('not.be.visible');
  cy.get('[data-cy="tooltip-trigger"]').trigger('mouseenter');
  // After mouseenter, opacity transitions to 1 — checkVisibility() returns true
  cy.get('[data-cy="tooltip"]').should('be.visible');
  cy.get('[data-cy="tooltip-trigger"]').trigger('mouseleave');
  cy.get('[data-cy="tooltip"]').should('not.be.visible');
});
```

**Tradeoff / When to use:** Enable in new projects or after a suite baseline comparison. The flag produces more correct visibility semantics than jQuery's legacy behaviour. When NOT to use: hold off enabling if your suite has assertions that rely on jQuery's lenient `:visible` semantics (e.g., asserting `should('be.visible')` on an `opacity: 0` loading spinner to check for its DOM presence, not its actual visibility). Named alternative: explicitly assert on `have.css, 'opacity', '0'` when you need to distinguish between "hidden via opacity" and "not in the DOM" without relying on visibility semantics.

**[official]** `experimentalFastVisibility` is documented in the Cypress 14+ changelog. Shadow DOM visibility through nested shadow roots has known inconsistencies in some browser versions when using `checkVisibility()`.

---

### 194. Cross-Spec localStorage Auditing with cy.getAllLocalStorage()  [official]

`cy.getAllLocalStorage()` (Cypress 12+) returns all localStorage per origin. Use it to audit cross-test state residue without per-key assertions and to detect isolation violations early.

```typescript
// cypress/support/storage-audit.ts — localStorage isolation auditor
const SENSITIVE_KEYS = ['auth_token', 'user_id', 'session', 'cart', 'feature_flags'] as const;

// Audit after each test — logs residual keys, does not fail (audit mode)
afterEach(function () {
  if (this.currentTest?.state !== 'passed') return; // only audit passing tests

  cy.getAllLocalStorage().then((storageByOrigin) => {
    const origin = Cypress.config('baseUrl') ?? '';
    const currentStorage = storageByOrigin[origin] ?? {};

    const residual = SENSITIVE_KEYS.filter((k) => k in currentStorage);
    if (residual.length > 0) {
      cy.log(`Storage residue in "${this.currentTest?.title}": ${residual.join(', ')}`);
    }
  });
});

// Direct use in a spec — assert that logout clears all auth state
it('logout removes all auth-related localStorage keys', () => {
  loginAsRole('user');
  cy.visit('/dashboard');

  // Verify auth state exists before logout
  cy.getAllLocalStorage().then((storage) => {
    const origin = Cypress.config('baseUrl')!;
    expect(storage[origin]).to.have.property('auth_token');
  });

  cy.get('[data-cy="nav-logout"]').click();
  cy.url().should('include', '/login');

  // Verify all auth keys are cleared
  cy.getAllLocalStorage().then((storage) => {
    const origin = Cypress.config('baseUrl')!;
    const keys = Object.keys(storage[origin] ?? {});
    const authKeys = keys.filter((k) => SENSITIVE_KEYS.includes(k as typeof SENSITIVE_KEYS[number]));
    expect(authKeys).to.have.length(0);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff / When to use:** Use `cy.getAllLocalStorage()` for isolation auditing and explicit before/after state comparison. When NOT to use: don't use it to share test data between specs — cross-spec localStorage sharing creates order-dependent tests. For shared setup state use `cy.session()` with `cacheAcrossSpecs: true`. Named alternative: `cy.window().its('localStorage')` accesses the current origin synchronously but doesn't support multi-origin inspection.

**[official]** In `testIsolation: true` mode (Cypress 12+ default), localStorage is cleared between tests — `cy.getAllLocalStorage()` comparisons across test boundaries are only valid within the same test body.

---

### 195. Cypress Module API with TypeScript and Pre/Post DB Lifecycle  [official]

The Cypress Module API lets you orchestrate test runs programmatically from Node.js — essential for monorepo runners and DB lifecycle management outside `setupNodeEvents`.

```typescript
// scripts/run-e2e.ts — typed Module API runner with full DB lifecycle
import cypress from 'cypress';
import type { CypressRunResult, CypressFailedRunResult } from 'cypress';

interface SuiteConfig {
  spec: string;
  dbScenario: string;
  env?: Record<string, string>;
}

async function runSuite(config: SuiteConfig): Promise<void> {
  // Import DB helpers directly — avoids setupNodeEvents CJS/ESM boundary issues
  const { seedDatabase, teardownDatabase } = await import('../src/db/test-helpers.js');

  console.log(`[runner] Seeding DB: ${config.dbScenario}`);
  await seedDatabase(config.dbScenario);

  let result: CypressRunResult | CypressFailedRunResult;
  try {
    result = await cypress.run({
      browser: 'chrome',
      headless: true,
      spec: config.spec,
      config: {
        baseUrl: process.env.CYPRESS_BASE_URL ?? 'http://localhost:3000',
        video: process.env.CI === 'true',
        retries: { runMode: 2, openMode: 0 },
        screenshotOnRunFailure: true,
      },
      env: {
        PAYMENT_MODE: 'test',
        ...config.env,
      },
    });
  } finally {
    console.log('[runner] Tearing down DB');
    await teardownDatabase(); // always runs, even if cypress.run() throws
  }

  if (result.status === 'failed') {
    console.error('[runner] Cypress binary failed to launch');
    process.exit(1);
  }

  const run = result as CypressRunResult;
  const passRate = ((run.totalPassed / run.totalTests) * 100).toFixed(1);
  console.log(`[runner] ${run.totalPassed}/${run.totalTests} passed (${passRate}%)`);

  if (run.totalFailed > 0) process.exit(1);
}

runSuite({
  spec: 'cypress/e2e/checkout/**/*.cy.ts',
  dbScenario: 'checkout-e2e',
}).catch((err) => { console.error(err); process.exit(1); });
```

**Tradeoff / When to use:** Use the Module API when the DB seed library has ESM-only exports incompatible with `setupNodeEvents`'s CommonJS context, or when you need multiple sequential Cypress invocations with different configurations. When NOT to use: for standard single-run CI pipelines, the CLI is simpler and produces better default output formatting. Named alternative: `cypress-io/github-action` with multiple `run` steps handles sequential spec group runs declaratively without custom Node.js scripts.

**[official]** `cypress.run()` returns `Promise<CypressRunResult | CypressFailedRunResult>`. Always check `result.status === 'failed'` first before casting to `CypressRunResult` — the two types are discriminated unions.

---

### 196. Comprehensive Accessibility Testing Across All UI States  [official]

`cypress-axe` must be called after every meaningful state change — modal opens, form errors, tab changes — not only on page load. This pattern encapsulates that workflow.

```typescript
// cypress/support/a11y.ts — wrapper that formats violations as readable errors
import 'cypress-axe';

export interface A11yOptions {
  context?: string | null;
  skipRules?: string[];
  impactsToFail?: ('minor' | 'moderate' | 'serious' | 'critical')[];
}

export function checkA11y(opts: A11yOptions = {}): void {
  const { context, skipRules = [], impactsToFail = ['serious', 'critical'] } = opts;
  const disabledRules = Object.fromEntries(skipRules.map((r) => [r, { enabled: false }]));

  cy.checkA11y(
    context ?? undefined,
    {
      runOnly: { type: 'tag', values: ['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21aa'] },
      includedImpacts: impactsToFail,
      rules: disabledRules,
    },
    (violations) => {
      const msgs = violations.map(
        (v) => `[${v.impact}] ${v.id}: ${v.description}\n  → ${v.nodes[0]?.target.join(', ')}`
      );
      throw new Error(`${violations.length} a11y violation(s):\n${msgs.join('\n')}`);
    },
    true, // failSilently — violations thrown by handler above
  );
}

// In a spec — check every meaningful UI state
describe('Checkout a11y', () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    cy.visit('/checkout');
    cy.injectAxe();
  });

  it('initial form is WCAG 2.1 AA compliant', () => { checkA11y(); });

  it('error state has accessible violation messages', () => {
    cy.get('[data-cy="submit-order"]').click(); // submit empty to trigger errors
    cy.get('[data-cy="field-errors"]').should('be.visible');
    checkA11y({ context: '[data-cy="checkout-form"]' });
  });

  it('confirmation modal is accessible', () => {
    cy.get('[data-cy="fill-form"]').click(); // helper fills valid data
    cy.get('[data-cy="confirm-purchase"]').click();
    cy.get('[data-cy="confirmation-modal"]').should('be.visible');
    checkA11y({
      context: '[data-cy="confirmation-modal"]',
      skipRules: ['color-contrast'], // tracked in separate dark-mode ticket
    });
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff / When to use:** Use for all customer-facing flows with WCAG compliance requirements. Scope `context` to specific components to reduce noise from shared layouts tested elsewhere. When NOT to use: don't run `checkA11y()` on every test — it adds ~200ms per call. Consider a dedicated nightly a11y spec if CI time is tight. Named alternative: `@axe-core/playwright` offers the same axe-core integration for teams on Playwright.

**[official]** `cypress-axe` is listed in the Cypress plugin directory and wraps `axe-core`. Inject axe once per test with `cy.injectAxe()` and call `cy.checkA11y()` after each state change.

### 197. Server-Sent Events (SSE) Testing via EventSource Stubbing  [community]

`cy.intercept()` cannot intercept `text/event-stream` SSE connections. The solution is to stub the `EventSource` constructor and push synthetic events from the test.

```typescript
// cypress/support/sse-stub.ts — reusable EventSource stub
declare global {
  namespace Cypress {
    interface Chainable {
      /** Replace EventSource for the given URL pattern; yields a controller to push events */
      stubSSE(urlPattern: string | RegExp): Chainable<{
        emit(type: string, data: unknown): void;
      }>;
    }
  }
}

Cypress.Commands.add('stubSSE', (urlPattern: string | RegExp) => {
  return cy.window().then((win) => {
    type EventMap = Record<string, Array<(e: MessageEvent) => void>>;
    let pushEvent: ((type: string, data: unknown) => void) | null = null;

    cy.stub(win, 'EventSource').callsFake((src: string) => {
      const pattern = typeof urlPattern === 'string' ? new RegExp(urlPattern) : urlPattern;
      const fakeES = {
        readyState: 1,
        _map: {} as EventMap,
        addEventListener(type: string, fn: (e: MessageEvent) => void) {
          (this._map[type] ??= []).push(fn);
        },
        removeEventListener(type: string, fn: (e: MessageEvent) => void) {
          this._map[type] = (this._map[type] ?? []).filter((h) => h !== fn);
        },
        close() { this.readyState = 2; },
        onmessage: null as ((e: MessageEvent) => void) | null,
      };

      if (pattern.test(src)) {
        pushEvent = (type, data) => {
          const event = new win.MessageEvent(type, {
            data: typeof data === 'string' ? data : JSON.stringify(data),
          });
          (fakeES._map[type] ?? []).forEach((h) => h(event));
          if (type === 'message' && fakeES.onmessage) fakeES.onmessage(event);
        };
      }
      return fakeES;
    }).as('EventSource');

    return cy.wrap(
      new Cypress.Promise<{ emit: (type: string, data: unknown) => void }>((resolve) => {
        const id = setInterval(() => {
          if (pushEvent) { clearInterval(id); resolve({ emit: pushEvent }); }
        }, 20);
      })
    );
  });
});

// In a spec — simulate real-time price updates
it('live price ticker updates when SSE events arrive', () => {
  cy.visit('/live-prices', {
    onBeforeLoad(win) {
      // Must stub before mount — SSE connection is opened in useEffect on mount
      cy.stub(win, 'EventSource').as('esConstructor');
    },
  });

  cy.stubSSE('/api/prices/stream').then((sse) => {
    cy.get('[data-cy="price-btc"]').should('contain.text', '$');

    sse.emit('priceUpdate', { symbol: 'BTC', price: 69420.0 });
    cy.get('[data-cy="price-btc"]').should('contain.text', '69,420');

    sse.emit('priceUpdate', { symbol: 'BTC', price: 70000.0 });
    cy.get('[data-cy="price-btc"]').should('contain.text', '70,000');
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff / When to use:** Use this pattern when your app uses SSE for real-time data (dashboards, live feeds, notification streams). When NOT to use: if the SSE server exposes a test-only `POST /api/test/emit` endpoint, trigger events via `cy.request()` and use the real SSE connection — this tests the full stack. Named alternative: WebSocket stubs use the same pattern with `win.WebSocket` instead of `win.EventSource`.

**[community]** WHY: The EventSource stub contains the entire mock inside the Cypress test process — no extra server process required. Teams that run a dedicated mock SSE server in CI add a process lifecycle dependency that causes flaky "server not ready" failures on slow CI agents.

---

## Additional Real-World Gotchas (Cycle 28) [community]

204. **`experimentalFastVisibility` fails tests that assert `should('be.visible')` on `opacity: 0` elements** [community] — jQuery's `:visible` (default) returns `true` for `opacity: 0` elements; the native `checkVisibility()` used by `experimentalFastVisibility` correctly returns `false`. Tests that relied on asserting existence via `should('be.visible')` on a spinner with `opacity: 0` will fail after enabling the flag. WHY: Teams often write `should('be.visible')` to check that an element is in the DOM, not that it is actually perceptible to users. `experimentalFastVisibility` forces the correct semantic — if you want to check DOM presence, use `should('exist')` instead. Run a full suite comparison job before enabling in CI.

205. **`cy.stubSSE()` — `EventSource` must be stubbed in `onBeforeLoad`, not after `cy.visit()`** [community] — If the app opens the SSE connection in a `useEffect`/`ngOnInit` that fires during page mount, calling `cy.stub(win, 'EventSource')` after `cy.visit()` is too late — the real connection is already open. WHY: Cypress's `cy.visit()` resolves after the page load event, which is after all synchronous `useEffect` hooks have run. Always pass the stub setup as `{ onBeforeLoad: (win) => { win.EventSource = FakeES; } }` to guarantee the stub is in place before the first script executes.

206. **`cy.getAllLocalStorage()` returns `{}` when called before `cy.visit()`** [community] — `cy.getAllLocalStorage()` reads storage from the currently loaded page's browser context. Before `cy.visit()`, the browser is on `about:blank`, which has no real origin. WHY: Teams use `cy.getAllLocalStorage()` in a `before()` hook to assert a clean initial state. But `{}` from `about:blank` doesn't mean the app origin's storage is empty — it means nothing has been visited yet. Assert clean state by calling `cy.getAllLocalStorage()` after `cy.visit()`.

207. **Angular Signals `effect()` with HTTP calls requires `provideExperimentalZonelessChangeDetection()` in CT for synchronous assertions** [community] — Angular Signals' `effect()` runs outside `NgZone`. When an `effect()` triggers an `HttpClient` call and updates a signal on response, Angular's change detection is not automatically scheduled in CT (which doesn't patch `zone.js` the way the full Angular app does). WHY: The DOM update from the signal is queued but not flushed until the next change detection cycle. Workaround: mount with `providers: [provideExperimentalZonelessChangeDetection()]` (Angular 18+), which makes change detection fully signal-driven and synchronous in CT contexts.

208. **`cy.press()` requires `cy.window().focus()` in headless CI for Tab navigation to work** [community] — `cy.press(Cypress.Keyboard.Keys.TAB)` dispatches a key event at the document level. In headless Chrome on CI agents that don't have a display (X11/Wayland not running), the browser window is not granted OS focus, and Tab key events are silently ignored — no focus movement occurs. WHY: Focus movement in response to Tab requires the browser window to be the OS focus target. Calling `cy.window().focus()` before `cy.press()` forces Cypress to assert and grant window focus via CDP before dispatching the key. Without it, focus trap tests pass locally but fail non-deterministically in headless CI.

209. **CTRF report file is absent when Cypress crashes before `after:run` fires** [community] — `cypress-ctrf-json-reporter` writes its output in the `after:run` event. If Cypress exits abnormally (OOM kill, binary launch failure, unhandled rejection in `setupNodeEvents`), `after:run` never fires and no CTRF file is produced. WHY: CI steps that depend on the CTRF file (upload artifact, publish summary) then silently succeed with an empty or missing file, producing a dashboard with a gap that looks like a clean run instead of a crash. Guard all CTRF-dependent steps with `if: always()` and add a file existence check: `test -f ctrf/ctrf-report.json || (echo "CTRF missing — possible Cypress crash" && exit 1)`.
