## Cycle 29 — 2026-05-14

### 198. `cy.intercept()` Request Body Inspection with Schema Validation  [community]

Validate outgoing request payloads against a JSON schema directly inside an intercept handler. This catches regressions in payload shape at the moment the request fires, before the response arrives — turning a network monitor into a contract test.

```typescript
// npm install --save-dev ajv
import Ajv from 'ajv';

const ajv = new Ajv({ strict: true });

const loginSchema = {
  type: 'object',
  required: ['email', 'password', 'rememberMe'],
  properties: {
    email:      { type: 'string', format: 'email' },
    password:   { type: 'string', minLength: 8 },
    rememberMe: { type: 'boolean' },
  },
  additionalProperties: false,
};

const validateLogin = ajv.compile(loginSchema);

it('login form sends a valid request payload', () => {
  cy.intercept('POST', '/api/auth/login', (req) => {
    const valid = validateLogin(req.body);
    if (!valid) {
      throw new Error(
        `Login request body failed schema validation:\n${ajv.errorsText(validateLogin.errors)}`
      );
    }
    req.reply({ statusCode: 200, body: { token: 'tok_test' } });
  }).as('login');

  cy.visit('/login');
  cy.get('[data-cy="email"]').type('alice@example.com');
  cy.get('[data-cy="password"]').type('hunter2!!');
  cy.get('[data-cy="remember-me"]').check();
  cy.get('[data-cy="submit"]').click();
  cy.wait('@login');
});
```

**Tradeoff / When to use:** Use for form submissions, checkout flows, and any POST/PATCH that carries structured data where a payload shape regression would be silent on the UI. Particularly valuable when the frontend and backend are developed independently (different squads or microservices). When NOT to use: for simple GET requests or when your team already has comprehensive API contract tests with Pact or similar tools — AJV validation in intercept handlers adds overhead that duplicates existing coverage. Named alternative: `cy.intercept()` with a typed generic (`cy.intercept<LoginBody>(...)`) catches TypeScript-level errors at compile time but cannot validate runtime values like string format or `additionalProperties`.

**[community]** WHY: AJV is synchronous and has zero async overhead in the intercept handler — unlike calling a remote validator service. Teams that skip request body validation discover payload regressions only when the backend rejects the request and returns a 400, which may be obscured behind a generic "Something went wrong" UI error with no diagnostic detail.

---

### 199. Svelte 5 Runes Component Testing — `$state` and `$derived`  [official]

Svelte 5's runes API (`$state`, `$derived`, `$effect`) is reactive without a compiler intermediary in Cypress CT. Mount Svelte 5 rune-based components directly; assertions on derived state work synchronously because rune reactivity is microtask-level.

```typescript
// src/components/Cart.svelte (Svelte 5 runes syntax)
// <script lang="ts">
//   let items = $state<string[]>([]);
//   const count = $derived(items.length);
//   function add(item: string) { items = [...items, item]; }
// </script>
// <span data-cy="count">{count}</span>
// <button data-cy="add" onclick={() => add('Widget')}>Add</button>
// <ul>{ #each items as item }<li data-cy="item">{item}</li>{/each}</ul>

// cart.cy.ts
import Cart from '../../src/components/Cart.svelte';

describe('Cart — Svelte 5 runes', () => {
  it('derived count updates when items are added', () => {
    cy.mount(Cart);
    cy.get('[data-cy="count"]').should('have.text', '0');

    cy.get('[data-cy="add"]').click();
    cy.get('[data-cy="count"]').should('have.text', '1');
    cy.get('[data-cy="item"]').should('have.length', 1).first().should('have.text', 'Widget');

    cy.get('[data-cy="add"]').click();
    cy.get('[data-cy="count"]').should('have.text', '2');
    cy.get('[data-cy="item"]').should('have.length', 2);
  });

  it('renders empty state correctly on mount', () => {
    cy.mount(Cart);
    cy.get('[data-cy="count"]').should('have.text', '0');
    cy.get('[data-cy="item"]').should('not.exist');
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff / When to use:** Use Cypress CT (over Vitest) for Svelte 5 components when the test needs browser APIs (ResizeObserver, IntersectionObserver, CSS custom properties, canvas). Cypress CT catches visual breakage; Vitest is faster for pure logic tests. When NOT to use: if the component has no DOM interaction, use Vitest with `@testing-library/svelte` — 10x faster per-test startup. Named alternative: Playwright CT also supports Svelte 5 and offers multi-browser matrix testing.

**[official]** Cypress 13+ officially supports Svelte 5 via the `@cypress/svelte` mounting library with Vite as the bundler.

---

### 200. `cy.intercept()` Fixture Factory — Dynamic Fixture Generation  [community]

Instead of static JSON files, generate fixture data programmatically inside `cy.intercept()` using factory functions. This gives you fixture reuse with per-test variation without creating dozens of near-identical JSON files.

```typescript
// cypress/support/factories.ts
export interface Product {
  id:      string;
  name:    string;
  price:   number;
  inStock: boolean;
}

export function makeProduct(overrides: Partial<Product> = {}): Product {
  return {
    id:      `prod_${Math.random().toString(36).slice(2, 9)}`,
    name:    'Generic Widget',
    price:   9.99,
    inStock: true,
    ...overrides,
  };
}

export function makeProductList(count: number, overrides: Partial<Product> = {}): Product[] {
  return Array.from({ length: count }, () => makeProduct(overrides));
}

// In a spec — override specific fields per test
describe('Product catalog', () => {
  it('shows out-of-stock badge when product is unavailable', () => {
    const products = [
      makeProduct({ name: 'Available Item', inStock: true }),
      makeProduct({ name: 'Sold-Out Item',  inStock: false }),
    ];
    cy.intercept('GET', '/api/products', { body: products }).as('getProducts');
    cy.visit('/catalog');
    cy.wait('@getProducts');
    cy.get('[data-cy="product-card"]').eq(1)
      .find('[data-cy="out-of-stock-badge"]').should('be.visible');
  });

  it('paginates a long list correctly', () => {
    cy.intercept('GET', '/api/products?page=1', { body: makeProductList(20) }).as('page1');
    cy.intercept('GET', '/api/products?page=2', { body: makeProductList(5)  }).as('page2');
    cy.visit('/catalog');
    cy.wait('@page1');
    cy.get('[data-cy="next-page"]').click();
    cy.wait('@page2');
    cy.get('[data-cy="product-card"]').should('have.length', 5);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff / When to use:** Use factories when you have more than 3 tests that share the same data shape but need minor variations. Factories eliminate fixture file proliferation (products-out-of-stock.json, products-paginated-p2.json…) and make intent clearer. When NOT to use: for integration tests that must match exact production snapshots (e.g., backend-driven rendering), static fixtures are more reliable — factories can mask real-data edge cases that come from character encodings, null fields, or non-ASCII content. Named alternative: `faker.js` (via `@faker-js/faker`) adds realistic randomization on top of a factory approach but risks test flakiness if factories are non-deterministic and assertions depend on specific values.

**[community]** WHY: Static fixture files silently go stale when the API response shape changes. A factory co-located with the TypeScript type forces a compile error when the interface changes, surfacing contract drift at build time rather than during a CI run hours later.

---

### 201. `cy.session()` with `idleTimeout` and localStorage Expiry Sentinel  [official]

Combine `cy.session()`'s `validate()` callback with a lightweight localStorage sentinel to evict cached sessions that have been idle longer than a configurable threshold — without making a network round-trip in every `validate()` call.

```typescript
// cypress/support/auth.ts
const SESSION_KEY  = 'app_session_expiry';
const IDLE_TTL_MS  = 30 * 60 * 1000; // 30 minutes

export function loginWithExpiry(email: string, password: string): void {
  cy.session(
    [email, 'v2'],                          // bump version suffix to bust cache globally
    () => {
      cy.visit('/login');
      cy.get('[data-cy="email"]').type(email);
      cy.get('[data-cy="password"]').type(password, { log: false });
      cy.get('[data-cy="submit"]').click();
      cy.url().should('include', '/dashboard');
      // write expiry sentinel to localStorage after successful login
      cy.window().then((win) => {
        win.localStorage.setItem(SESSION_KEY, String(Date.now() + IDLE_TTL_MS));
      });
    },
    {
      validate() {
        cy.window().then((win) => {
          const expiry = Number(win.localStorage.getItem(SESSION_KEY) ?? '0');
          if (Date.now() > expiry) {
            // Throwing inside validate() forces re-login without a network call
            throw new Error('Session sentinel expired — re-running login setup');
          }
        });
      },
      cacheAcrossSpecs: true,
    }
  );
}
```

**Tradeoff / When to use:** Use when your CI pipeline takes longer than the application's session TTL (e.g., a 15-minute JWT expiry on a 30-minute CI run) and `validate()` HTTP calls are too slow or noisy. When NOT to use: if session expiry is not a real risk in your CI (short pipelines, long-lived tokens), the sentinel is extra complexity for no gain. Named alternative: simply omit `validate()` entirely and use `cacheAcrossSpecs: false` — this re-authenticates per spec file, which is slower but simpler.

**[official]** The `validate()` function may throw or return a Promise that rejects; both forms cause Cypress to evict the cached session and re-run the setup function.

---

### 202. Multi-Tab / `window.open()` Testing via `cy.stub()`  [community]

Cypress runs in a single browser tab. Stub `window.open` to capture opened URLs rather than attempting cross-tab navigation, then assert on the intended destination.

```typescript
it('external link opens in a new tab', () => {
  cy.visit('/resources');

  // Stub window.open BEFORE clicking — it fires synchronously on click
  cy.window().then((win) => {
    cy.stub(win, 'open').as('windowOpen');
  });

  cy.get('[data-cy="docs-link"]').click();

  cy.get('@windowOpen').should(
    'have.been.calledWithMatch',
    Cypress.sinon.match(/^https:\/\/docs\.example\.com/),
    '_blank'
  );
});

it('PDF download uses correct filename via window.open', () => {
  cy.window().then((win) => {
    cy.stub(win, 'open').as('openPdf');
  });

  cy.visit('/reports');
  cy.get('[data-cy="download-report"]').click();

  cy.get('@openPdf')
    .should('have.been.calledOnce')
    .its('firstCall.args.0')
    .should('match', /\/api\/reports\/\d+\.pdf/);
});
```

**Tradeoff / When to use:** Use this pattern for any link or button that calls `window.open()`, `window.location.href` redirects to external URLs, or anchor tags with `target="_blank"`. It validates intent without needing multi-tab automation. When NOT to use: if the new tab contains content that must be functionally tested (e.g., an OAuth consent screen that returns a token), use `cy.origin()` with a single-tab OAuth redirect flow instead — the stub approach cannot test the opened content. Named alternative: Playwright natively supports multi-page/multi-tab testing via the `Page` object — prefer Playwright if multi-tab flows are a core feature requirement.

**[community]** WHY: Cypress intentionally blocks `window.open()` to prevent multi-tab states that break the Cypress runner's iframe architecture. Without a stub, the click either opens a tab that Cypress cannot control, or silently does nothing in headless mode — both masking the actual behavior.

---

### 203. `cy.intercept()` + `cy.clock()` for Polling / Auto-Refresh Tests  [official]

Combine `cy.clock()` (to freeze and advance time) with `cy.intercept()` (to control responses) to test components that poll an endpoint on an interval without adding real wall-clock delays.

```typescript
it('dashboard auto-refreshes metrics every 30 seconds', () => {
  // First response — initial render
  cy.intercept('GET', '/api/metrics', { fixture: 'metrics-initial.json' }).as('metricsLoad');

  cy.clock(); // freeze Date and setInterval
  cy.visit('/dashboard');
  cy.wait('@metricsLoad');

  cy.get('[data-cy="active-users"]').should('have.text', '42');

  // Re-intercept with updated data BEFORE advancing the clock
  cy.intercept('GET', '/api/metrics', { fixture: 'metrics-updated.json' }).as('metricsRefresh');

  // Advance the clock by 30 seconds to trigger the polling interval
  cy.tick(30_000);
  cy.wait('@metricsRefresh');

  cy.get('[data-cy="active-users"]').should('have.text', '87');
});

it('shows stale data indicator when polling request fails', () => {
  cy.intercept('GET', '/api/metrics', { fixture: 'metrics-initial.json' }).as('metricsLoad');
  cy.clock();
  cy.visit('/dashboard');
  cy.wait('@metricsLoad');

  cy.intercept('GET', '/api/metrics', { forceNetworkError: true }).as('metricsFail');
  cy.tick(30_000);
  cy.wait('@metricsFail');

  cy.get('[data-cy="stale-data-warning"]').should('be.visible');
});
```

**Tradeoff / When to use:** Use this for any component with `setInterval`, `setTimeout`-based refresh loops, or auto-save features. The combination eliminates real-time waiting entirely. When NOT to use: `cy.clock()` freezes ALL browser timers including Cypress's own internal retry clock — very deep clock advances (more than 5 minutes) can cause Cypress's own timeout assertions to misbehave. In that case, use `cy.intercept()` with `times: 1` and real waits with a short polling interval in the test build. Named alternative: configure the polling interval via `Cypress.env('POLL_INTERVAL_MS')` and set it to `100` in tests — this avoids needing `cy.clock()` altogether at the cost of coupling the app to a test-only env var.

**[official]** `cy.clock()` stubs `Date`, `setTimeout`, `clearTimeout`, `setInterval`, `clearInterval`, `requestAnimationFrame`, and `cancelAnimationFrame`. `cy.tick(ms)` advances all of them synchronously.

---

### 204. Svelte 4 Store Testing in Cypress CT via `get()`  [community]

Svelte 4 stores are plain JavaScript objects. In CT, import and read the store directly with Svelte's `get()` helper to assert on internal state without exposing it through the DOM — useful for complex state machines where the DOM only shows a subset of state.

```typescript
// src/stores/cart.ts — Svelte 4 writable store
import { writable, derived } from 'svelte/store';
export const cartItems = writable<string[]>([]);
export const cartTotal = derived(cartItems, ($items) => $items.length * 9.99);

// CartSummary.svelte — reads from store, renders summary
// <script>import { cartItems, cartTotal } from '../stores/cart';</script>
// <span data-cy="item-count">{$cartItems.length}</span>
// <span data-cy="total">${$cartTotal.toFixed(2)}</span>

// cart-summary.cy.ts
import { get }         from 'svelte/store';
import { cartItems }   from '../../src/stores/cart';
import CartSummary     from '../../src/components/CartSummary.svelte';

describe('CartSummary', () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    cartItems.set([]);   // reset store before each test
  });

  it('reflects store changes in the DOM immediately', () => {
    cy.mount(CartSummary);
    cy.get('[data-cy="item-count"]').should('have.text', '0');

    cartItems.set(['Widget A', 'Widget B']);

    cy.get('[data-cy="item-count"]').should('have.text', '2');
    cy.get('[data-cy="total"]').should('have.text', '$19.98');
  });

  it('store state can be asserted directly without DOM intermediary', () => {
    cartItems.set(['X', 'Y', 'Z']);
    const items = get(cartItems);
    expect(items).to.deep.equal(['X', 'Y', 'Z']);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff / When to use:** Use direct store access in CT when the DOM renders a summary and you need to assert on precise intermediate state. When NOT to use: for Svelte 5 runes — rune state is not exported as an importable store; use `cy.get()` DOM assertions or `$state.snapshot()` instead. Named alternative: trigger store mutations through user interactions (`cy.get('[data-cy="add"]').click()`) rather than calling `cartItems.set()` directly in tests — this tests the full interaction path rather than the store in isolation.

**[community]** WHY: Svelte stores mutated in `beforeEach` carry over between CT specs because the module is imported once per CT runner session and the store is a singleton in that module scope. Always reset stores explicitly in `beforeEach` — a missing reset causes the most confusing inter-test ordering bugs because the store mutation happens outside the DOM, making it invisible in the Cypress command log.

---

### 205. `cy.task()` with File System Fixtures — Reading/Writing Generated Files  [official]

Use `cy.task()` to perform file system operations in Node.js: read generated files, write synthetic input files, or verify that the app produced expected output files during a test.

```typescript
// cypress/plugins/fs-tasks.ts
import fs   from 'fs';
import path from 'path';

export const fsTasks = {
  readGeneratedFile(filename: string): string {
    const filePath = path.join(process.cwd(), 'test-output', filename);
    if (!fs.existsSync(filePath)) {
      throw new Error(`File not found: ${filePath}`);
    }
    return fs.readFileSync(filePath, 'utf8');
  },
  writeInputFile({ filename, content }: { filename: string; content: string }): null {
    const filePath = path.join(process.cwd(), 'test-input', filename);
    fs.mkdirSync(path.dirname(filePath), { recursive: true });
    fs.writeFileSync(filePath, content, 'utf8');
    return null; // cy.task must return null (not undefined) for a void result
  },
  cleanupTestOutput(): null {
    const dir = path.join(process.cwd(), 'test-output');
    if (fs.existsSync(dir)) fs.rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true });
    return null;
  },
};

// cypress.config.ts — register tasks inside setupNodeEvents:
// on('task', fsTasks);

// In a spec — assert that export produced the correct CSV
it('exports filtered orders to CSV', () => {
  cy.task('cleanupTestOutput');
  cy.visit('/orders?status=shipped');
  cy.get('[data-cy="export-csv"]').click();
  cy.get('[data-cy="export-success"]').should('be.visible');

  cy.task<string>('readGeneratedFile', 'orders-export.csv').then((csv) => {
    const lines = csv.trim().split('\n');
    expect(lines[0]).to.include('Order ID,Status,Amount');
    expect(lines.length).to.be.gte(2); // header + at least one row
    expect(lines.every((l) => l.includes('shipped') || l === lines[0])).to.be.true;
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff / When to use:** Use for testing file export/import features (CSV, JSON, PDF generation), upload workflows that need a pre-built file, or any assertion on server-side file side effects. When NOT to use: for simple in-browser downloads that can be verified with `cy.readFile()` (which reads from the Cypress downloads folder) — `cy.readFile()` requires no `cy.task()` setup. Named alternative: `cy.readFile()` handles download verification directly without a task for file types Cypress supports reading natively (text, JSON, binary via ArrayBuffer).

**[official]** `cy.task()` must return a value serialisable to JSON. Returning `undefined` causes Cypress to throw "cy.task('x') failed because the task did not return anything". Always return `null` for void operations.

---

### 206. `cy.intercept()` WebSocket Upgrade Detection  [community]

Cypress cannot intercept WebSocket frames directly, but it can intercept the HTTP Upgrade handshake to assert that a WebSocket connection was initiated with the correct URL, headers, and query parameters — without needing to stub the full WS protocol.

```typescript
it('connects to the correct WebSocket endpoint with auth token', () => {
  // The browser sends a GET request with Upgrade: websocket before the WS protocol starts
  cy.intercept({
    method:  'GET',
    url:     '/ws/notifications*',
    headers: { Upgrade: 'websocket' },
  }, (req) => {
    // Validate auth is present on the upgrade request
    expect(req.headers['sec-websocket-protocol']).to.include('bearer');
    req.continue(); // spy — don't stub the response
  }).as('wsUpgrade');

  cy.loginAsRole('user');
  cy.visit('/notifications');

  cy.wait('@wsUpgrade').then(({ request }) => {
    // Confirm the correct room ID was requested via query param
    expect(request.url).to.match(/userId=\d+/);
  });
});

it('reconnects after a dropped connection', () => {
  let upgradeCount = 0;
  cy.intercept({ method: 'GET', url: '/ws/**', headers: { Upgrade: 'websocket' } }, (req) => {
    upgradeCount += 1;
    req.continue();
  }).as('wsUpgrade');

  cy.visit('/chat');
  cy.wait('@wsUpgrade'); // first connection

  cy.reload();
  cy.wait('@wsUpgrade'); // reconnect

  cy.wrap(null).should(() => {
    expect(upgradeCount).to.gte(2);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff / When to use:** Use to assert WebSocket connection parameters (URL, protocol headers, auth tokens) and reconnect behavior without stubbing the full WS frame protocol. When NOT to use: if you need to test the content of WebSocket messages (the actual frames), use `cy.stub(win, 'WebSocket')` to intercept the constructor and wrap send/onmessage, or use a dedicated WS testing library. Named alternative: `msw` (Mock Service Worker) v2 supports `ws()` handler mocking at the service-worker level — works in both Cypress and Vitest and intercepts actual frames, not just the upgrade handshake.

**[community]** WHY: Teams assume `cy.intercept('/ws/path')` will catch WebSocket traffic and wonder why the alias never fires. Cypress uses `cy.intercept()` on the HTTP layer; the WebSocket *upgrade* is an HTTP GET, but subsequent WS frames are not HTTP — they bypass `cy.intercept()` entirely. The upgrade-only intercept is the only supported approach without full WS stubbing.

---

### 207. Scroll-Driven Animation Testing with `IntersectionObserver` Stub  [community]

When components trigger animations or lazy-loading via `IntersectionObserver`, stub the observer to imperatively control which elements are "visible" — removing the need to scroll pixel-perfectly in a test environment where viewport size varies.

```typescript
// cypress/support/intersection-observer-stub.ts
declare global {
  namespace Cypress {
    interface Chainable {
      stubIntersectionObserver(): Chainable<{
        triggerIntersection(selector: string, isIntersecting?: boolean): void;
      }>;
    }
  }
}

Cypress.Commands.add('stubIntersectionObserver', () => {
  return cy.window().then((win) => {
    const observedCallbacks = new Map<Element, IntersectionObserverCallback>();

    class MockIO {
      constructor(private cb: IntersectionObserverCallback) {}
      observe(el: Element)    { observedCallbacks.set(el, this.cb); }
      unobserve(el: Element)  { observedCallbacks.delete(el); }
      disconnect()            { observedCallbacks.clear(); }
      takeRecords()           { return []; }
    }

    cy.stub(win, 'IntersectionObserver').callsFake(
      (cb: IntersectionObserverCallback) => new MockIO(cb)
    );

    return {
      triggerIntersection(selector: string, isIntersecting = true) {
        cy.get(selector).then(($el) => {
          const el = $el[0];
          const cb = observedCallbacks.get(el);
          if (!cb) throw new Error(`No observer registered for ${selector}`);
          cb(
            [{ target: el, isIntersecting } as IntersectionObserverEntry],
            {} as IntersectionObserver
          );
        });
      },
    };
  });
});

// In a spec — test lazy-loaded section reveals
it('section heading animates in when scrolled into view', () => {
  cy.visit('/landing');
  cy.stubIntersectionObserver().then((io) => {
    cy.get('[data-cy="features-section"]').should('have.class', 'hidden');
    io.triggerIntersection('[data-cy="features-section"]', true);
    cy.get('[data-cy="features-section"]').should('have.class', 'visible');
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff / When to use:** Use when the app uses IntersectionObserver for scroll-triggered animations, lazy image loading, or infinite scroll sentinel detection. The stub makes tests deterministic and viewport-independent. When NOT to use: if testing the real scroll behaviour (i.e., whether the threshold pixel value is correct), use `cy.scrollTo()` with specific scroll amounts and a known viewport size — stubbing defeats the purpose of a pixel-accuracy test. Named alternative: `cypress-real-events` with `cy.realScroll()` can trigger real scroll events and let the real IO fire, at the cost of requiring a headed Chromium session.

**[community]** WHY: IntersectionObserver callbacks fire asynchronously in the browser's rendering pipeline, not immediately when `scrollTo()` completes. Tests that assert on scroll-triggered class changes after `cy.scrollTo('bottom')` are among the most common sources of flake in component-heavy SPAs — the callback simply hasn't fired yet when the assertion runs.

---

### 208. `cypress-axe` with Custom Rules — Enforcing Design System Token Compliance  [community]

Extend `cypress-axe` with custom Axe rules to catch design-system-specific violations (e.g., colour tokens from a non-approved palette) as part of the accessibility audit. This couples visual consistency checking to a11y testing without a separate linting pass.

```typescript
// cypress/support/custom-axe-rules.ts
import type { Rule } from 'axe-core';

export const brandColorRule: Rule = {
  id:          'brand-color-only',
  description: 'Elements must use approved brand colour tokens, not raw hex values',
  help:        'Use CSS custom properties (--color-*) instead of raw hex/rgb values',
  helpUrl:     'https://design.example.com/tokens/color',
  selector:    '*',
  any: [
    {
      id: 'check-brand-colors',
      evaluate(node: Element): boolean {
        const style  = window.getComputedStyle(node);
        const rawHex = /^#[0-9a-f]{3,8}$/i;
        return !rawHex.test(style.color) && !rawHex.test(style.backgroundColor);
      },
    },
  ],
};

// cypress/support/e2e.ts — register before cy.injectAxe() is called
import axe from 'axe-core';
import { brandColorRule } from './custom-axe-rules';
axe.configure({ rules: [brandColorRule] });

// In a spec — use the custom rule alongside built-in WCAG checks
it('product cards use only approved brand colours', () => {
  cy.visit('/catalog');
  cy.injectAxe();
  cy.checkA11y('[data-cy="product-card"]', {
    rules: { 'brand-color-only': { enabled: true } },
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff / When to use:** Use when your design system mandates token-based theming and visual drift (hard-coded colours sneaking in) is a real regression risk. Custom Axe rules run in every branch pipeline without separate tooling. When NOT to use: custom `evaluate` functions that call `window.getComputedStyle` on every node in the DOM will slow down large pages significantly — scope with `cy.checkA11y('[data-cy="content"]', ...)` rather than the full document. Named alternative: `stylelint` with a custom rule catches token violations at CSS authoring time — faster feedback but doesn't catch dynamically injected styles from CSS-in-JS libraries or third-party widgets.

**[community]** WHY: Custom Axe rules run in the browser context — they can access computed styles, shadow DOM, and runtime state that static linters cannot. This is the only approach that catches colour token violations introduced by CSS-in-JS libraries, third-party widget themes, or server-rendered style attributes.

---

### 209. `cy.request()` JWT Decode Helper for Token Claim Assertions  [community]

After a login `cy.request()`, decode the returned JWT and assert on its claims without installing a full JWT library — using only `atob()` and JSON.parse, which are available in the browser context.

```typescript
// cypress/support/jwt.ts
export function decodeJwtPayload<T = Record<string, unknown>>(token: string): T {
  const base64Payload = token.split('.')[1];
  if (!base64Payload) throw new Error('Invalid JWT: missing payload segment');
  // URL-safe Base64 uses - and _ instead of + and /; atob() requires standard Base64
  const standardBase64 = base64Payload.replace(/-/g, '+').replace(/_/g, '/');
  const decoded        = atob(standardBase64);
  return JSON.parse(decoded) as T;
}

interface AppTokenClaims {
  sub:   string;
  email: string;
  role:  'admin' | 'user' | 'viewer';
  exp:   number;
  iat:   number;
}

// In a spec — validate role escalation is not possible via normal login
it('admin login produces JWT with admin role claim', () => {
  cy.request<{ token: string }>({
    method: 'POST',
    url:    '/api/auth/login',
    body:   { email: 'admin@example.com', password: Cypress.env('ADMIN_PASS') },
  }).then(({ body }) => {
    const claims = decodeJwtPayload<AppTokenClaims>(body.token);
    expect(claims.role).to.equal('admin');
    expect(claims.email).to.equal('admin@example.com');
    const fiveMinFromNow = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000) + 300;
    expect(claims.exp).to.be.gte(fiveMinFromNow);
  });
});

it('viewer cannot obtain admin claims by injecting role in request body', () => {
  cy.request<{ token: string }>({
    method:           'POST',
    url:              '/api/auth/login',
    body:             { email: 'viewer@example.com', password: Cypress.env('VIEWER_PASS'), role: 'admin' },
    failOnStatusCode: false,
  }).then(({ body, status }) => {
    if (status === 200) {
      const claims = decodeJwtPayload<AppTokenClaims>(body.token);
      expect(claims.role).to.equal('viewer'); // role injection must be ignored by server
    } else {
      expect(status).to.be.oneOf([400, 403]);
    }
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff / When to use:** Use for security-adjacent tests (role injection, claim tampering, expiry window checks) in auth regression suites. The helper is zero-dependency and runs inside the Cypress browser context. When NOT to use: do not use this to validate JWT *signatures* — `atob` only decodes the payload and you cannot verify the signature in a browser test context. For signature verification, use `cy.task()` to call `jsonwebtoken.verify()` in Node.js with the secret from env vars. Named alternative: `cy.task('verifyJwt', token)` with the `jsonwebtoken` npm package provides full signature and expiry verification in Node.js.

**[community]** WHY: URL-safe Base64 JWT payloads use `-` and `_` instead of `+` and `/`. Calling `atob()` on a raw JWT segment without the character substitution throws `InvalidCharacterError` in roughly 25% of tokens, making the bug appear intermittent and token-content-dependent.

---

### 210. Responsive Design Testing with Multiple Viewport Presets  [community]

Parameterise viewport dimensions across a matrix of device presets to catch responsive breakage systematically. Use `cy.viewport()` inside a `describe` block factory to avoid duplicating test bodies.

```typescript
// cypress/support/viewports.ts
export const VIEWPORTS = {
  mobile:       { width: 375,  height: 812,  label: 'iPhone 14 Pro'     },
  mobileLarge:  { width: 430,  height: 932,  label: 'iPhone 14 Pro Max' },
  tablet:       { width: 768,  height: 1024, label: 'iPad'              },
  desktopSmall: { width: 1280, height: 800,  label: '13 inch laptop'    },
  desktopFull:  { width: 1920, height: 1080, label: '1080p desktop'     },
} as const;

type ViewportKey = keyof typeof VIEWPORTS;

// cypress/e2e/nav-responsive.cy.ts
import { VIEWPORTS } from '../support/viewports';

function runNavTests(): void {
  it('primary nav is visible at this viewport', () => {
    cy.get('[data-cy="primary-nav"]').should('be.visible');
  });

  it('hamburger menu is present on mobile and absent on desktop', () => {
    cy.window().its('innerWidth').then((width) => {
      if (width < 768) {
        cy.get('[data-cy="hamburger"]').should('be.visible');
      } else {
        cy.get('[data-cy="hamburger"]').should('not.exist');
      }
    });
  });
}

(Object.keys(VIEWPORTS) as ViewportKey[]).forEach((key) => {
  const { width, height, label } = VIEWPORTS[key];
  describe(`Navigation — ${label} (${width}x${height})`, () => {
    beforeEach(() => {
      cy.viewport(width, height); // use beforeEach, not before — test isolation resets viewport
      cy.visit('/');
    });
    runNavTests();
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff / When to use:** Use this pattern when responsive layout regressions are a regular occurrence. Running 5 viewports × N tests multiplies suite time — gate the full matrix behind a `@responsive` tag with `@cypress/grep` and run only desktop in the default pipeline. When NOT to use: do not test pixel-perfect layout correctness this way — a 1px margin difference will not cause an assertion to fail. Use visual regression testing (Argos, Percy, Applitools) for pixel-level fidelity. Named alternative: `cy.viewport('iphone-14-pro')` uses Cypress's built-in device presets for common mobile sizes without needing a custom config object.

**[community]** WHY: `cy.viewport()` set in `before()` is reset by Cypress test isolation between tests. Only the first test in the `describe` block runs at the intended viewport size; subsequent tests revert to the default. Always use `beforeEach()` when setting viewport dimensions in a responsive test matrix.

---

### 211. `cy.intercept()` Spy-Mode Request Counting for De-duplication Testing  [community]

Use `cy.intercept()` in spy mode (no stub, just a counter via the alias request log) to assert that components send the expected number of requests — catching double-fetches, polling loop bugs, and missing request de-duplication.

```typescript
it('search input de-duplicates rapid keystrokes via debounce', () => {
  cy.intercept('GET', '/api/search*').as('search');

  cy.visit('/search');
  // Type quickly — debounce should collapse to a single request
  cy.get('[data-cy="search-input"]').type('cypress test patterns', { delay: 30 });

  // Wait for debounce to settle (default 300ms) then assert only one request was made
  // cy.get('@alias.all') returns the array of all intercepted requests for this alias
  cy.get('@search.all').should('have.length', 1);
});

it('does NOT refetch products when sort order changes locally', () => {
  cy.intercept('GET', '/api/products*', { fixture: 'products.json' }).as('getProducts');

  cy.visit('/catalog');
  cy.wait('@getProducts'); // initial load — count is now 1

  // Sorting should be a client-side operation — no re-fetch
  cy.get('[data-cy="sort-select"]').select('price-asc');
  cy.get('[data-cy="sort-select"]').select('price-desc');

  // Assert the alias still has exactly 1 request (no additional fetches fired)
  cy.get('@getProducts.all').should('have.length', 1);
});
```

**Tradeoff / When to use:** Use for verifying debounce, throttle, SWR de-duplication, and React Query stale-while-revalidate behaviour. Catching double-fetches early prevents performance regressions in production. When NOT to use: `cy.get('@alias.all')` only counts requests that matched the intercept pattern — if the URL changes (e.g., page query param added), the alias won't capture it and your length assertion will appear to pass while missing requests. Named alternative: a closure counter variable inside the intercept handler (`let count = 0; cy.intercept('GET', '/api/search*', (req) => { count += 1; req.continue(); })`) gives the same result but must be reset in `beforeEach` to avoid cross-test accumulation.

**[community]** WHY: `cy.get('@alias.all')` is maintained automatically by Cypress for every aliased intercept — it is an array of all matched requests in the current test. This is the canonical approach recommended in Cypress docs. The closure-counter alternative is fragile because `let count = 0` declared at `describe` scope persists across the entire block; declaring it at `it` scope requires restructuring the intercept setup.

---

### 212. `cy.origin()` + `cy.session()` Cached Cross-Origin Authentication  [official]

Cache cross-origin login sessions with `cy.session()` to avoid repeating the OAuth redirect on every test — passing only serialisable arguments through the `cy.origin()` boundary.

```typescript
// cypress/support/auth.ts
export function loginWithOAuth(email: string): void {
  cy.session(
    ['oauth', email],
    () => {
      cy.visit('/login');
      cy.get('[data-cy="sso-login"]').click();

      cy.origin(
        'https://sso.example-idp.com',
        { args: { email, password: Cypress.env('SSO_PASS') as string } },
        ({ email: e, password: p }) => {
          cy.get('#identifier').type(e);
          cy.get('#password').type(p, { log: false });
          cy.get('#sign-in-button').click();
          // cy.origin block ends when navigation leaves this domain
        }
      );

      // Back on app domain — confirm session established
      cy.url().should('include', '/dashboard');
      cy.getCookie('session_id').should('exist');
    },
    {
      validate() {
        cy.request({ url: '/api/me', failOnStatusCode: false })
          .its('status').should('eq', 200);
      },
      cacheAcrossSpecs: true,
    }
  );
}

// In a spec
describe('Admin panel', () => {
  beforeEach(() => loginWithOAuth('admin@example.com'));

  it('shows the user management table', () => {
    cy.visit('/admin/users');
    cy.get('[data-cy="users-table"]').should('be.visible');
  });

  it('can deactivate a user account', () => {
    cy.visit('/admin/users');
    cy.get('[data-cy="user-row"]').first().find('[data-cy="deactivate"]').click();
    cy.get('[data-cy="confirm-deactivate"]').click();
    cy.get('[data-cy="user-row"]').first().should('have.attr', 'data-status', 'inactive');
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff / When to use:** Use when the OAuth/SAML redirect adds more than 3 seconds per test and the total test count is more than 20 — the session cache pays off quickly. When NOT to use: if the IdP rate-limits automated logins (common with Okta and Azure AD trial tenants), the cold login attempt can trigger a CAPTCHA or IP block. In that case, bypass OAuth entirely by seeding a valid session cookie via `cy.task()` that calls the IdP's machine-to-machine token endpoint. Named alternative: direct API login (posting to `/api/auth/token` with `client_credentials`) avoids the browser redirect entirely and is 10-100x faster for non-UI auth flows.

**[official]** `cy.origin()` callbacks are serialised as strings. Functions, class instances, Symbols, and Promises passed via `args` are silently dropped. Only JSON-serialisable values survive the cross-origin boundary.

---

## Additional Real-World Gotchas (Cycle 29) [community]

210. **`cy.clock()` does not stub `performance.now()` — timestamps in `PerformanceObserver` callbacks are wall-clock values** [community] — `cy.clock()` stubs `Date.now()`, `setTimeout`, `setInterval`, and `requestAnimationFrame`, but does NOT stub `performance.now()` or the timestamps returned by `PerformanceObserver` entries (`entry.startTime`, `entry.duration`). Tests that advance `cy.tick(5000)` and then assert `performance.now() > 5000` will fail because `performance.now()` still reads from the real monotonic clock. WHY: `performance.now()` is sourced from the browser's native monotonic timer, which is not patchable from JavaScript without a CDP-level hook. Workaround: inject a `performance.now` stub manually via `cy.window().then((win) => { win.performance = { ...win.performance, now: () => Date.now() }; })` before calling `cy.clock()`.

211. **`cy.intercept()` spy-mode closure counters accumulate across tests when declared at `describe` scope** [community] — Closure counter variables (e.g., `let count = 0`) declared at `describe` scope persist for the entire describe block's lifetime, not per-test. If `cy.intercept()` is called in `beforeEach` and increments a shared counter, the count accumulates across tests within the same `describe`. WHY: Cypress re-uses the JavaScript closure scope for `describe` blocks; only `it` blocks get fresh scope (via Mocha's per-test context). Always declare request counters inside the `it` block, or use `cy.get('@alias.all').its('length')` — Cypress tracks per-alias request arrays automatically and resets them per test.

212. **`cy.viewport()` set in `before()` is reset by test isolation — use `beforeEach()` for viewport dimensions** [community] — Cypress test isolation (enabled by default since Cypress 12) clears the browser context between tests, which includes resetting the viewport to the configured default. A `before()` hook sets the viewport for the first test only; subsequent tests in the same `describe` block revert to the default dimensions (1000x660). WHY: `before()` runs once before the first test, then test isolation fires before the second test and resets the viewport. Responsive test matrices that use `before()` to set viewport produce only the first test at the intended size, with all others running at the wrong viewport silently.

213. **`cy.stub(win, 'WebSocket')` set after `cy.visit()` misses connections opened during `DOMContentLoaded`** [community] — When `cy.visit()` resolves, the page's `DOMContentLoaded` event has already fired. Any WebSocket (or `EventSource`) opened during `DOMContentLoaded` was created before the stub was in place. WHY: Cypress resolves `cy.visit()` after `load`, not `DOMContentLoaded`. Pass the stub via `{ onBeforeLoad: (win) => { win.WebSocket = MockWS; } }` — `onBeforeLoad` runs before any page script executes and is the correct injection point for global constructor stubs.

214. **Svelte 4 stores are module singletons — `beforeEach` must explicitly reset writable stores or state leaks between CT specs** [community] — When Cypress CT bundles and loads a Svelte store module, the module is cached for the entire CT session. `writable([])` initialises the store once at module-load time. Subsequent `beforeEach` hooks that do not call `store.set(initial)` inherit whatever value the previous test left. WHY: ES module caches are not cleared between Cypress CT test runs within the same runner session — only a full page reload would reset module scope, and CT does not do a full reload between `it` blocks. Always call `store.set(defaultValue)` in `beforeEach` for every writable store the component reads from.

215. **`decodeJwtPayload()` with raw `atob()` throws `InvalidCharacterError` for URL-safe Base64 tokens without character substitution** [community] — JWTs use URL-safe Base64 encoding (RFC 4648 §5), which replaces `+` with `-` and `/` with `_` and omits `=` padding. The browser's `atob()` expects standard Base64 with `+`, `/`, and `=` padding. Calling `atob()` directly on a raw JWT payload segment fails for any token whose payload bytes happen to produce `+` or `/` in standard Base64. WHY: Roughly 25% of random byte sequences produce at least one of these characters, making the bug appear intermittent and token-content-dependent. Always apply `token.replace(/-/g, '+').replace(/_/g, '/')` before calling `atob()`, and optionally pad: `payload.padEnd(payload.length + (4 - payload.length % 4) % 4, '=')`.

---

## Cycle 30 — 2026-05-14

<!-- sources: docs.cypress.io changelog 15.x, docs.cypress.io/api, community blogs 2025 -->

### 216. GraphQL Operation Aliasing via Body Inspection  [official]

When the app uses a single `/graphql` endpoint, distinguish operations by inspecting `req.body.operationName` inside the intercept handler. This enables per-operation stubs, aliases, and wait assertions without URL-based matching.

```typescript
// cypress/support/graphql.ts
export function interceptGql(
  operationName: string,
  fixture: string | Record<string, unknown>
): void {
  cy.intercept('POST', '/graphql', (req) => {
    if (req.body?.operationName === operationName) {
      req.alias = `gql${operationName}`;
      if (typeof fixture === 'string') {
        req.reply({ fixture });
      } else {
        req.reply({ body: fixture });
      }
    }
  });
}

// In a spec:
import { interceptGql } from '../support/graphql';

it('renders product list from GraphQL', () => {
  interceptGql('GetProducts', {
    data: { products: [{ id: '1', name: 'Widget', price: 9.99 }] },
  });

  cy.visit('/catalog');
  cy.wait('@gqlGetProducts').its('request.body.operationName').should('eq', 'GetProducts');
  cy.get('[data-cy="product-name"]').should('contain', 'Widget');
});

it('shows error state when GetProducts returns errors', () => {
  interceptGql('GetProducts', {
    errors: [{ message: 'Resolver error' }],
  });

  cy.visit('/catalog');
  cy.wait('@gqlGetProducts');
  cy.get('[data-cy="error-banner"]').should('be.visible');
});
```

**Tradeoff / When to use:** Use whenever the app sends all GraphQL operations to the same endpoint (Apollo, urql, URQL, Relay). Aliasing by operation name gives you the same determinism as REST-style per-URL aliases. When NOT to use: do not inspect `req.body.operationName` for GET-based GraphQL (persisted queries send the operation hash in query params, not in the body). Named alternative: `@graphql-codegen` generates typed query document objects; combining them with `hasOperationName()` helper from the Cypress Real World App is a widely adopted community pattern.

---

### 217. Svelte 5 Runes — Component Testing with `$state` and `$derived`  [community]

Svelte 5's rune-based reactivity (`$state`, `$derived`, `$effect`) requires Cypress CT Svelte support ≥ 15.14. Mount the component with `cy.mount()` from `cypress/svelte` and control props via the returned `component` reference.

```typescript
// src/components/Counter.svelte (Svelte 5 rune syntax)
// <script lang="ts">
//   let count = $state(0);
//   let doubled = $derived(count * 2);
// </script>
// <button data-cy="inc" onclick={() => count++}>+</button>
// <span data-cy="count">{count}</span>
// <span data-cy="doubled">{doubled}</span>

// counter.cy.ts
import { mount } from 'cypress/svelte';
import Counter from '../../src/components/Counter.svelte';

describe('Counter (Svelte 5 runes)', () => {
  it('increments count and updates derived value', () => {
    mount(Counter, {});

    cy.get('[data-cy="count"]').should('have.text', '0');
    cy.get('[data-cy="doubled"]').should('have.text', '0');

    cy.get('[data-cy="inc"]').click().click().click();

    cy.get('[data-cy="count"]').should('have.text', '3');
    cy.get('[data-cy="doubled"]').should('have.text', '6');
  });

  it('reactivity updates on external state mutation via component ref', () => {
    const { component } = mount(Counter, {});
    // Access rune-exported state via component.$set if using compatibility layer,
    // or drive via UI actions — do NOT mutate $state directly from test code
    cy.get('[data-cy="inc"]').click();
    cy.get('[data-cy="count"]').should('have.text', '1');
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff / When to use:** Use for pure component logic tests on Svelte 5 components where rune-based reactivity is the primary behaviour under test. When NOT to use: Svelte 5 Runes CT support is still stabilising as of Cypress 15.x — avoid in CI pipelines where Svelte version is not pinned; a patch upgrade to Svelte 5.x can change rune serialisation and break CT snapshot assertions. Named alternative: Vitest + `@testing-library/svelte` is more mature for Svelte 5 unit tests; use Cypress CT for integration-level interaction tests.

---

### 218. `cy.intercept()` `req.on('before:response')` for Non-Blocking Response Transformation  [official]

The `before:response` event fires after the server responds but before Cypress forwards the response to the browser. Using it (vs `req.continue(res => …)`) avoids blocking the entire request-response cycle in the test runner's proxy thread.

```typescript
it('rewrites API pagination metadata without blocking other requests', () => {
  cy.intercept('GET', '/api/items*', (req) => {
    req.on('before:response', (res) => {
      // Mutate without blocking — Cypress continues forwarding concurrently
      if (res.body && typeof res.body === 'object') {
        (res.body as Record<string, unknown>).totalPages = 99;
        (res.body as Record<string, unknown>).hasMore = true;
      }
    });
  }).as('getItems');

  cy.visit('/items');
  cy.wait('@getItems');
  cy.get('[data-cy="load-more"]').should('be.visible');
  cy.get('[data-cy="page-info"]').should('contain', '99');
});

it('compares before:response vs req.continue() for latency-sensitive tests', () => {
  // req.continue(callback) BLOCKS: Cypress holds the response until the callback returns
  // req.on('before:response') NON-BLOCKING: response is forwarded concurrently with the callback
  cy.intercept('GET', '/api/fast-path*', (req) => {
    req.on('before:response', (res) => {
      res.headers['x-test-injected'] = 'true';
      // No need to call res.send() — it auto-continues
    });
  }).as('fastPath');

  cy.visit('/fast-path');
  cy.wait('@fastPath')
    .its('response.headers.x-test-injected')
    .should('eq', 'true');
});
```

**Tradeoff / When to use:** Prefer `req.on('before:response')` when transforming responses that the browser needs quickly (auth token refresh, pagination metadata, feature flag toggles). Use `req.continue(res => …)` only when you need to fully replace or delay the response body. When NOT to use: `before:response` cannot set `res.statusCode` changes that redirect the browser — use `req.reply()` for complete response replacement. Named alternative: `req.continue((res) => { res.body = …; })` is the blocking equivalent; use it only when the next test action depends on the modified response arriving before another UI event.

---

### 219. Angular Standalone Components in Cypress CT  [official]

Angular 17+ standalone components do not require an `NgModule`. Mount them directly with `cy.mount()` providing `imports` for their dependencies in place of a module declaration.

```typescript
// src/app/components/user-badge/user-badge.component.ts (standalone)
// @Component({ standalone: true, selector: 'app-user-badge',
//   imports: [CommonModule], template: `<span [attr.data-cy]="'badge'">{{user.name}}</span>` })
// export class UserBadgeComponent { @Input() user!: { name: string; role: string }; }

// user-badge.component.cy.ts
import { UserBadgeComponent } from './user-badge.component';
import { CommonModule } from '@angular/common';

describe('UserBadgeComponent (standalone)', () => {
  it('renders the user name', () => {
    cy.mount(UserBadgeComponent, {
      componentProperties: { user: { name: 'Alice', role: 'admin' } },
      imports: [CommonModule],
    });

    cy.get('[data-cy="badge"]').should('have.text', 'Alice');
  });

  it('reflects prop change when input is updated', () => {
    cy.mount('<app-user-badge [user]="user"></app-user-badge>', {
      declarations: [UserBadgeComponent],
      imports: [CommonModule],
      componentProperties: { user: { name: 'Bob', role: 'user' } },
    }).then(({ fixture }) => {
      fixture.componentInstance.user = { name: 'Carol', role: 'viewer' };
      fixture.detectChanges();
    });

    cy.get('[data-cy="badge"]').should('have.text', 'Carol');
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff / When to use:** Use for Angular 17+ projects where standalone components are the default. The `imports` array mirrors the component's own `imports` — you only need to add `TestBed` providers for services not already provided by the component. When NOT to use: avoid mixing module-based and standalone mounting styles in the same spec file; the two approaches use different `cy.mount()` overloads and their TypeScript types diverge. Named alternative: Angular's `TestBed.configureTestingModule()` is more flexible for deep service-level testing; Cypress CT is best for interaction and visual assertions.

---

### 220. `cy.session()` `idleTimeout` — Automatically Expire Cached Sessions  [official]

Pass `idleTimeout` (ms) to `cy.session()` to automatically invalidate the cached session when it has not been used for that interval. This is safer than relying solely on `cacheAcrossSpecs: true` in long-running suites.

```typescript
// cypress/support/auth.ts
export function loginWithIdleTimeout(email: string): void {
  cy.session(
    ['idle-timeout', email],
    () => {
      cy.request('POST', '/api/auth/login', {
        email,
        password: Cypress.env('USER_PASS'),
      }).then(({ body }) => {
        window.localStorage.setItem('auth_token', body.token);
        window.localStorage.setItem('auth_expiry', String(Date.now() + 3_600_000));
      });
    },
    {
      validate() {
        // Re-run setup if the token has expired or is missing
        const expiry = Number(window.localStorage.getItem('auth_expiry') ?? 0);
        if (Date.now() >= expiry) throw new Error('session expired');
        cy.request({ url: '/api/me', failOnStatusCode: false })
          .its('status').should('eq', 200);
      },
      cacheAcrossSpecs: true,
      idleTimeout: 30 * 60 * 1000, // invalidate after 30 min of non-use
    }
  );
}

// In a long suite that runs >30 min across parallel machines:
beforeEach(() => loginWithIdleTimeout('ci@example.com'));
```

**Tradeoff / When to use:** Use when CI suites run longer than your app's session TTL (common for JWT-based auth with 1-hour expiry). `idleTimeout` prevents the cached session from being re-used on a machine that picked up a spec file 45 minutes after the session was first created. When NOT to use: do not set `idleTimeout` shorter than the average test duration — a session that expires mid-spec forces a cold re-login and can cascade failures if the setup step has network latency. Named alternative: a `validate()` callback that checks `Date.now()` against a stored expiry timestamp gives the same protection without a fixed timer, adapting to real token expiry.

---

### 221. Cypress Module API — Programmatic Run with Per-Spec Retry  [official]

The Cypress Module API (`cypress.run()`) lets you drive test execution from a Node.js script. Use it to implement per-spec retry logic: re-run only failing spec files rather than the entire suite.

```typescript
// scripts/run-with-retry.ts
import cypress from 'cypress';

async function runWithRetry(maxRetries = 2): Promise<void> {
  let failedSpecs: string[] = [];

  // First full run
  const firstRun = await cypress.run({ browser: 'chrome' });
  if ('runs' in firstRun) {
    failedSpecs = firstRun.runs
      .filter((r) => r.stats.failures > 0)
      .map((r) => r.spec.absolute);
  }

  if (failedSpecs.length === 0) {
    console.log('All tests passed on first run.');
    process.exit(0);
  }

  for (let attempt = 1; attempt <= maxRetries; attempt++) {
    console.log(`Retry ${attempt}: re-running ${failedSpecs.length} spec(s)`);
    const retryRun = await cypress.run({
      browser: 'chrome',
      spec: failedSpecs.join(','),
    });

    if ('runs' in retryRun) {
      failedSpecs = retryRun.runs
        .filter((r) => r.stats.failures > 0)
        .map((r) => r.spec.absolute);
    }

    if (failedSpecs.length === 0) {
      console.log(`All tests passed on retry ${attempt}.`);
      process.exit(0);
    }
  }

  console.error(`Tests still failing after ${maxRetries} retries:`, failedSpecs);
  process.exit(1);
}

runWithRetry();
```

**Tradeoff / When to use:** Use for expensive E2E suites (>10 min) where 1-2 specs are flaky but re-running the entire suite is cost-prohibitive. Per-spec retry is faster and cheaper than Cypress Cloud's built-in retry because it does not consume Cypress Cloud test credits for the retry runs. When NOT to use: do not use per-spec retry to hide persistently flaky tests — set a flakiness budget and alert when a spec retries more than 3 times in a week. Named alternative: Cypress Cloud's `retries.runMode` in `cypress.config.ts` retries at the test level (not spec level) and integrates with Cypress Cloud's flaky test detection dashboard.

---

### 222. `experimentalFastVisibility` — Opt-In Visibility Check Engine  [official]

`experimentalFastVisibility` (added Cypress 15.8.0) changes how Cypress computes element visibility. It skips CSS `transform`-based off-screen checks and uses a bounding-rect approach instead, which is significantly faster on large DOMs.

```typescript
// cypress.config.ts — opt in to the new visibility engine
import { defineConfig } from 'cypress';

export default defineConfig({
  e2e: {
    experimentalFastVisibility: true,
    setupNodeEvents(on) {
      // No additional setup required
    },
  },
  component: {
    devServer: { framework: 'react', bundler: 'vite' },
    experimentalFastVisibility: true,
  },
});

// No spec changes required — cy.should('be.visible') uses the new engine automatically.
// Verify the flag is active by checking visibility assertions complete faster in large suites:
it('checks many elements visible quickly', () => {
  cy.visit('/dashboard');
  // With experimentalFastVisibility, this loop completes ~40% faster on 1000-node DOMs
  const selectors = ['header', 'main', 'footer', '[data-cy="sidebar"]', '[data-cy="content"]'];
  selectors.forEach((sel) => {
    cy.get(sel).should('be.visible');
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff / When to use:** Use when your test suite has measurable slow visibility checks — the flag typically shaves 10-40% off suites with many `should('be.visible')` / `should('not.be.visible')` assertions on dynamic SPAs. When NOT to use: do not enable on apps that use `transform: translateX(-9999px)` or similar off-screen hiding patterns for modals or drawers — these elements remain technically visible under the bounding-rect algorithm and assertions that expect `not.be.visible` will start failing. Named alternative: refactor hiding patterns to use `display: none` or `visibility: hidden` (which both engines correctly detect) rather than transform-based off-screen placement.

---

### 223. Typed Fixture Factory with `cy.fixture()` and Builder Pattern  [community]

A fixture builder generates strongly-typed test data by starting from a base fixture and allowing per-test overrides via a fluent API. This eliminates duplicated fixture files for minor variations.

```typescript
// cypress/support/fixtures/user-builder.ts
import type { UserFixture } from './types';

const BASE_USER: UserFixture = {
  id: 'usr_test_001',
  name: 'Test User',
  email: 'test@example.com',
  role: 'user',
  createdAt: '2025-01-01T00:00:00Z',
  preferences: { theme: 'light', notifications: true },
};

export class UserBuilder {
  private data: UserFixture = structuredClone(BASE_USER);

  withRole(role: UserFixture['role']): this {
    this.data.role = role;
    return this;
  }

  withEmail(email: string): this {
    this.data.email = email;
    return this;
  }

  withPreferences(prefs: Partial<UserFixture['preferences']>): this {
    Object.assign(this.data.preferences, prefs);
    return this;
  }

  build(): UserFixture {
    return structuredClone(this.data);
  }
}

// In a spec:
import { UserBuilder } from '../support/fixtures/user-builder';

it('admin sees deactivation controls', () => {
  const admin = new UserBuilder().withRole('admin').withEmail('admin@example.com').build();

  cy.intercept('GET', '/api/me', admin).as('getMe');
  cy.visit('/profile');
  cy.wait('@getMe');
  cy.get('[data-cy="deactivate-controls"]').should('be.visible');
});

it('viewer does not see deactivation controls', () => {
  const viewer = new UserBuilder().withRole('viewer').build();

  cy.intercept('GET', '/api/me', viewer).as('getMe');
  cy.visit('/profile');
  cy.wait('@getMe');
  cy.get('[data-cy="deactivate-controls"]').should('not.exist');
});
```

**Tradeoff / When to use:** Use when a data model has many optional variations tested across different specs — the builder centralises default values and eliminates 5-20 near-duplicate fixture JSON files. When NOT to use: for simple one-off test data, a plain object literal is less overhead. Do not share a single `UserBuilder` instance across tests — always call `.build()` to get a fresh copy via `structuredClone`, otherwise mutations from one test affect the next. Named alternative: `@faker-js/faker` generates randomised fixture data; combine it with a builder when you need deterministic seeds (`faker.seed(42)`) for reproducible CI failures.

---

### 224. Accessibility Testing with `cypress-axe` and Custom Rule Configuration  [community]

`cypress-axe` integrates the axe-core engine into Cypress. Use `cy.checkA11y()` with targeted selectors and impact thresholds to enforce accessibility standards without blocking on known third-party violations.

```typescript
// cypress/support/e2e.ts
import 'cypress-axe';

// cypress/e2e/a11y.cy.ts
describe('Accessibility — product listing page', () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    cy.visit('/products');
    cy.injectAxe(); // injects axe-core into the page
  });

  it('has no critical or serious violations on initial load', () => {
    cy.checkA11y(
      undefined,                   // check entire page
      {
        runOnly: {
          type: 'tag',
          values: ['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21aa'],
        },
        rules: {
          // Suppress known third-party widget violation until vendor fixes it
          'color-contrast': { enabled: false },
        },
      },
      (violations) => {
        const critical = violations.filter((v) => v.impact === 'critical' || v.impact === 'serious');
        cy.log(`${critical.length} critical/serious a11y violations`);
        critical.forEach((v) => cy.log(v.description));
      },
      false // do NOT fail test on violation — report only (set to true to enforce)
    );
  });

  it('modal dialog traps focus and is announced to screen readers', () => {
    cy.get('[data-cy="open-detail-modal"]').click();
    cy.get('[role="dialog"]').should('be.visible');

    // Only check the modal for a11y violations
    cy.checkA11y('[role="dialog"]', {
      rules: { 'dialog-name': { enabled: true } },
    });

    // Focus should be trapped inside the dialog
    cy.focused().closest('[role="dialog"]').should('exist');
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff / When to use:** Use as a gating check in your CI pipeline for WCAG 2.1 AA compliance. `cy.checkA11y()` catches ~35% of WCAG violations automatically (those detectable by static DOM analysis). When NOT to use: do not replace manual screen reader testing with `cypress-axe` — automated tools cannot detect content meaning, reading order, or cognitive load issues. Setting `failOnViolations: false` across the board defeats the purpose; only disable specific known rules with documented justification. Named alternative: Cypress's own Accessibility testing feature in Cypress Cloud (Cloud plan required) provides per-run violation trends and suggested AI-generated test coverage.

---

### 225. `cy.stub()` for Browser APIs — `window.fetch`, `localStorage`, and `navigator`  [community]

Stub browser-native APIs directly on the `window` object inside `cy.visit()`'s `onBeforeLoad` callback. This is the only safe injection point — stubs set after `cy.visit()` resolves may miss calls made during page initialisation.

```typescript
it('handles fetch failure gracefully', () => {
  cy.visit('/dashboard', {
    onBeforeLoad(win) {
      // Stub window.fetch to always reject — simulates offline/network error
      cy.stub(win, 'fetch').rejects(new TypeError('Failed to fetch'));
    },
  });

  cy.get('[data-cy="offline-banner"]').should('be.visible');
  cy.get('[data-cy="retry-btn"]').should('be.visible');
});

it('reads persisted preferences from localStorage on mount', () => {
  cy.visit('/settings', {
    onBeforeLoad(win) {
      // Seed localStorage before any app script runs
      win.localStorage.setItem('theme', 'dark');
      win.localStorage.setItem('language', 'de');
    },
  });

  cy.get('[data-cy="theme-toggle"]').should('have.attr', 'data-active', 'dark');
  cy.get('[data-cy="language-select"]').should('have.value', 'de');
});

it('uses geolocation API stub to test location-aware UI', () => {
  cy.visit('/nearby', {
    onBeforeLoad(win) {
      cy.stub(win.navigator.geolocation, 'getCurrentPosition').callsFake((success) => {
        success({ coords: { latitude: 52.52, longitude: 13.405, accuracy: 10 } } as GeolocationPosition);
      });
    },
  });

  cy.get('[data-cy="location-label"]').should('contain', 'Berlin');
});
```

**Tradeoff / When to use:** Use `onBeforeLoad` stubs when testing app behaviour that depends on browser APIs not easily reproducible in a test environment (geolocation, clipboard, notifications, service workers). When NOT to use: do not stub `fetch` globally when you have `cy.intercept()` available — `cy.intercept()` is more granular, composable, and produces better Command Log output. Stubbing `fetch` completely bypasses `cy.intercept()` because intercept hooks into the browser's network layer, which is above the `fetch` implementation. Named alternative: `cy.intercept()` handles 95% of network stubbing scenarios without touching `window.fetch` directly.

---

### 226. Parallel Spec Execution with Cypress Cloud and `--parallel`  [official]

Cypress Cloud's smart orchestration distributes spec files across multiple CI machines. Use `--parallel` with a `--ci-build-id` to let Cypress balance the spec queue based on historical run duration.

```typescript
// cypress.config.ts — configure for parallel execution
import { defineConfig } from 'cypress';

export default defineConfig({
  e2e: {
    baseUrl: 'http://localhost:3000',
    // Enable automatic spec balancing based on previous run history
    // (requires Cypress Cloud project key)
    projectId: process.env.CYPRESS_PROJECT_ID,
  },
});
```

```yaml
# .github/workflows/e2e.yml — 4 parallel machines
jobs:
  e2e:
    strategy:
      matrix:
        machine: [1, 2, 3, 4]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version: '22' }
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm start &
      - run: |
          npx cypress run \
            --record \
            --parallel \
            --ci-build-id "${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}" \
            --group "e2e-parallel"
        env:
          CYPRESS_RECORD_KEY: ${{ secrets.CYPRESS_RECORD_KEY }}
```

**Tradeoff / When to use:** Use when E2E suite wall-clock time exceeds 10 minutes and CI cost is acceptable. `--parallel` with 4 machines typically cuts a 40-minute suite to ~12 minutes. When NOT to use: do not use `--parallel` without `--record` — the parallelisation algorithm requires Cypress Cloud to assign spec files; without it each machine runs the full suite independently. Also avoid `--parallel` for component testing suites that are already fast (<3 min) — the machine spin-up overhead eliminates the benefit. Named alternative: Cypress's `autoCancelAfterFailures` stops the parallel run when N tests fail, preventing credit burn on a fundamentally broken build.

---

### 227. `cy.intercept()` `forceNetworkError` for Resilience Testing  [official]

Pass `{ forceNetworkError: true }` as the response stub to simulate a TCP-level network failure — no HTTP response, no status code, just a connection drop. This is distinct from a 500 error and tests a different application error path.

```typescript
describe('Network resilience', () => {
  it('shows connection error UI when the API endpoint is unreachable', () => {
    cy.intercept('GET', '/api/dashboard/stats', { forceNetworkError: true }).as('statsError');

    cy.visit('/dashboard');
    cy.wait('@statsError');

    // App should show a "connection failed" message, not a generic error
    cy.get('[data-cy="connection-error"]').should('be.visible');
    cy.get('[data-cy="http-error"]').should('not.exist');
  });

  it('auto-retries after a network error and recovers gracefully', () => {
    let callCount = 0;

    cy.intercept('GET', '/api/health', (req) => {
      callCount += 1;
      if (callCount === 1) {
        req.destroy(); // forceNetworkError programmatically on first attempt
      } else {
        req.reply({ statusCode: 200, body: { status: 'ok' } });
      }
    }).as('healthCheck');

    cy.visit('/');
    // Wait for both calls: the failed one and the successful retry
    cy.wait('@healthCheck'); // first call — network error
    cy.wait('@healthCheck'); // second call — success

    cy.get('[data-cy="health-indicator"]').should('have.attr', 'data-status', 'healthy');
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff / When to use:** Use to verify the difference between HTTP error handling (4xx/5xx) and connection-level error handling. Many apps show the same generic error UI for both, which is a UX regression risk. When NOT to use: `forceNetworkError` does not test slow networks — use `req.on('response', (res) => res.setDelay(ms))` for latency simulation. Named alternative: `statusCode: 503` with a `Retry-After` header tests HTTP-level downtime with a specific retry directive, which is more realistic for load-balanced production outages.

---

### 228. `cy.press()` Keyboard Navigation Testing — Tab Order and ARIA Focus Management  [official]

`cy.press()` (Cypress 14.3+) fires native Tab key events through the browser's focus management engine. Use it to verify tab order, focus trap boundaries, and ARIA `aria-activedescendant` patterns that `cy.type('{tab}')` misses.

```typescript
describe('Modal dialog focus management', () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    cy.visit('/components/modal-demo');
    cy.get('[data-cy="open-modal"]').click();
    cy.get('[role="dialog"]').should('be.visible');
  });

  it('focuses the first interactive element on open', () => {
    // Focus must be moved into the dialog automatically on open (WCAG 2.4.3)
    cy.focused().should('be.within', '[role="dialog"]');
    cy.focused().should('have.attr', 'data-cy', 'modal-close');
  });

  it('Tab cycles through modal interactive elements only', () => {
    // Verify focus stays within the dialog (focus trap)
    cy.press('Tab');
    cy.focused().should('have.attr', 'data-cy', 'modal-confirm');

    cy.press('Tab');
    cy.focused().should('have.attr', 'data-cy', 'modal-cancel');

    // Tab from last element should wrap back to first
    cy.press('Tab');
    cy.focused().should('have.attr', 'data-cy', 'modal-close');
  });

  it('Shift+Tab reverses focus order', () => {
    cy.press('Tab'); // move to second element
    cy.press(['Shift', 'Tab']); // back to first
    cy.focused().should('have.attr', 'data-cy', 'modal-close');
  });

  it('Escape closes the dialog and returns focus to trigger', () => {
    cy.press('Escape');
    cy.get('[role="dialog"]').should('not.exist');
    // Focus should return to the element that opened the dialog
    cy.focused().should('have.attr', 'data-cy', 'open-modal');
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff / When to use:** Use `cy.press()` specifically for keyboard navigation and accessibility assertions — it fires through the real browser focus engine, so results match what a keyboard user actually experiences. When NOT to use: `cy.press()` yields `null`, so you cannot chain `.should()` or `.click()` directly after it. Assert on `cy.focused()` in the next command instead. Also, `cy.press()` requires the browser window to have focus — tests that run in a background tab may fail silently. Named alternative: `cy.realPress()` from `cypress-real-events` is more reliable for chord combinations (Shift+Tab) in some browser configurations but requires Chromium and adds a plugin dependency.

---

### 229. `cy.request()` for API Contract Testing — Schema Validation with Zod  [community]

Combine `cy.request()` with `zod` schema validation to assert API response shape at the schema level, not just value level. This catches breaking backend changes that alter field types or make previously required fields optional.

```typescript
// cypress/support/api-schemas.ts
import { z } from 'zod';

export const ProductSchema = z.object({
  id: z.string().uuid(),
  name: z.string().min(1),
  price: z.number().positive(),
  currency: z.enum(['USD', 'EUR', 'GBP']),
  inStock: z.boolean(),
  tags: z.array(z.string()).optional(),
  createdAt: z.string().datetime(),
});

export const ProductListSchema = z.object({
  data: z.array(ProductSchema),
  total: z.number().int().nonnegative(),
  page: z.number().int().positive(),
  pageSize: z.number().int().positive(),
});

export type Product = z.infer<typeof ProductSchema>;

// cypress/e2e/api-contracts.cy.ts
import { ProductListSchema } from '../support/api-schemas';

it('GET /api/products returns valid schema', () => {
  cy.request<unknown>('GET', '/api/products?page=1&pageSize=10')
    .then(({ body, status }) => {
      expect(status).to.eq(200);

      const result = ProductListSchema.safeParse(body);
      if (!result.success) {
        const issues = result.error.issues.map((i) => `${i.path.join('.')}: ${i.message}`);
        throw new Error(`API contract violation:\n${issues.join('\n')}`);
      }

      expect(result.data.data.length).to.be.lte(10);
      expect(result.data.page).to.eq(1);
    });
});
```

**Tradeoff / When to use:** Use schema validation tests as a contract test layer between frontend and backend teams — they catch type regressions (e.g., `price` changing from `number` to `string`) that value-based assertions miss. Run them in a dedicated `api-contracts` suite that fires on every backend deploy. When NOT to use: do not import `zod` into spec files in projects that do not already have it as a dependency — the 12KB bundle size is negligible in Node.js but schema validation in CI is also achievable with `ajv` (JSON Schema) which many projects already have. Named alternative: Pact.io consumer-driven contract testing provides a full contract brokerage workflow for microservice teams; Zod + Cypress is lighter-weight and suitable for monorepo or single-backend apps.

---

### 230. `cy.task()` Email Testing with Mailpit/MailHog — Full E2E Email Flow  [community]

Test transactional email delivery by polling a local SMTP trap (Mailpit or MailHog) via `cy.task()`. This verifies the full email path: backend sends → SMTP trap receives → frontend action triggered by link in email.

```typescript
// cypress/plugins/mailpit.ts
import axios from 'axios';

interface MailpitMessage {
  ID: string;
  Subject: string;
  To: Array<{ Address: string }>;
  HTML: string;
  Text: string;
}

export async function getLatestEmail(toAddress: string): Promise<MailpitMessage | null> {
  const { data } = await axios.get<{ messages: MailpitMessage[] }>(
    'http://localhost:8025/api/v1/messages'
  );
  return data.messages.find((m) => m.To.some((r) => r.Address === toAddress)) ?? null;
}

export async function clearAllEmails(): Promise<void> {
  await axios.delete('http://localhost:8025/api/v1/messages');
}

// cypress.config.ts
import { getLatestEmail, clearAllEmails } from './cypress/plugins/mailpit';

export default defineConfig({
  e2e: {
    setupNodeEvents(on) {
      on('task', {
        'email:get': (address: string) => getLatestEmail(address),
        'email:clear': () => clearAllEmails().then(() => null),
      });
    },
  },
});

// cypress/e2e/email-verification.cy.ts
it('sends welcome email and user can verify account via link', () => {
  cy.task('email:clear');

  cy.request('POST', '/api/users/register', {
    email: 'newuser@example.com',
    password: 'P@ssword123!',
  }).its('status').should('eq', 201);

  // Poll for the email with retryability
  cy.task<{ HTML: string } | null>('email:get', 'newuser@example.com', { timeout: 15_000 })
    .should('not.be.null')
    .then((email) => {
      // Extract verification link from email HTML
      const match = email!.HTML.match(/href="([^"]*verify[^"]*)"/);
      expect(match).to.not.be.null;
      const verificationUrl = new URL(match![1]);
      cy.visit(verificationUrl.pathname + verificationUrl.search);
    });

  cy.get('[data-cy="verification-success"]').should('be.visible');
  cy.get('[data-cy="account-status"]').should('have.text', 'Verified');
});
```

**Tradeoff / When to use:** Use for registration, password reset, and transactional email flows where the email is an integral part of the user journey. Mailpit is lightweight (single binary, ~15MB) and runs in Docker, making it suitable for local dev and CI. When NOT to use: do not use a local SMTP trap if your backend sends emails through a third-party provider (SendGrid, SES) in the test environment — the email will bypass the trap. In that case, use the provider's sandbox/test mode API to poll delivered messages. Named alternative: `mailosaur.com` is a hosted email testing service with a Cypress plugin (`cypress-mailosaur`) that handles email polling without running a local SMTP server.
