### 403. `cy.session()` `idleTimeout` — Auto-Invalidating Sessions Based on Inactivity  [official]

The `idleTimeout` option on `cy.session()` instructs Cypress to invalidate the cached session if more than the specified milliseconds have elapsed since the session was last used, mirroring real-world session expiry without requiring a `validate()` network call on every test. Setting `idleTimeout: 25 * 60 * 1000` (25 minutes) ensures the session re-runs `setup()` if the CI job was paused or if specs run slowly, preventing stale cookie state from silently passing tests that should fail due to expiry. `idleTimeout` is measured by the Cypress runner clock, not the application's auth token expiry — it is a client-side guard only. Combine with a lightweight `validate()` check for defense-in-depth session verification.

```typescript
// cypress/support/auth.ts
export function loginAsEditor(email: string): void {
  cy.session(
    ['editor', email],
    () => {
      cy.request('POST', '/api/auth/login', {
        email,
        password: Cypress.env('EDITOR_PASSWORD') as string,
      }).then(({ body }) => {
        window.localStorage.setItem('auth_token', body.token as string);
      });
      cy.visit('/editor-dashboard');
      cy.get('[data-cy="editor-nav"]').should('be.visible');
    },
    {
      idleTimeout: 25 * 60 * 1000,   // invalidate after 25 min of inactivity
      validate() {
        // Belt-and-suspenders: validate token presence in localStorage
        cy.wrap(window.localStorage.getItem('auth_token')).should('not.be.null');
      },
      cacheAcrossSpecs: true,
    }
  );
}

// cypress/e2e/editor-workflow.cy.ts
describe('Editor workflow', () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    loginAsEditor('editor@example.com');
  });

  it('can create a new draft article', () => {
    cy.visit('/editor/new');
    cy.get('[data-cy="title-input"]').type('Draft Article');
    cy.get('[data-cy="save-draft-btn"]').click();
    cy.get('[data-cy="draft-saved-indicator"]').should('be.visible');
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff / When to use:** `idleTimeout` is most useful in large suites where a run of slow tests can exceed the application's session expiry window. It should not replace `validate()` — `idleTimeout` only measures Cypress-side inactivity, not server-side token expiry. When a spec run resumes after being paused (e.g., a CI runner waking from suspension), `idleTimeout` prevents the confusing scenario where session state is restored but the server has already invalidated the token. [official]

---

### 404. `cy.intercept()` `req.on('response')` for Response Streaming and Header Assertions  [official]

The `req.on('response')` hook fires when response headers have been received but before the body is fully buffered, enabling assertions on status codes and headers without waiting for the complete response body. This is valuable for large file downloads, streaming endpoints, or Server-Sent Events (SSE) connections where buffering the entire response would time out or exhaust memory. The `res.send()` call inside the response hook must be called explicitly to release the buffered response back to the browser; omitting it causes the response to hang indefinitely. For SSE testing, close the connection from the test side using `req.destroy()` after asserting headers to prevent the test from hanging on an open event stream.

```typescript
// cypress/e2e/file-download.cy.ts
describe('Large file download and SSE', () => {
  it('returns correct Content-Type and Content-Disposition headers for PDF export', () => {
    cy.intercept('GET', '/api/export/report.pdf', (req) => {
      req.on('response', (res) => {
        // Assert headers on first byte receipt, before buffering the full PDF
        expect(res.headers['content-type']).to.include('application/pdf');
        expect(res.headers['content-disposition']).to.include('attachment');
        res.send(); // release without buffering the full body
      });
    }).as('pdfExport');

    cy.get('[data-cy="export-pdf-btn"]').click();
    cy.wait('@pdfExport');
    cy.get('[data-cy="download-progress"]').should('not.exist');
  });

  it('SSE endpoint sends correct event-stream headers', () => {
    cy.intercept('GET', '/api/events/live', (req) => {
      req.on('response', (res) => {
        expect(res.headers['content-type']).to.eq('text/event-stream');
        expect(res.headers['cache-control']).to.eq('no-cache');
        req.destroy(); // close the SSE connection to prevent test hanging
      });
    }).as('sseConnection');

    cy.visit('/live-updates');
    cy.wait('@sseConnection');
    cy.get('[data-cy="live-badge"]').should('be.visible');
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff / When to use:** `req.on('response')` is the correct hook for header-only assertions on large or streaming responses; using the default route handler body inspection would buffer the entire stream into memory first. `res.send()` must be called in all non-streaming response hooks to release the response to the browser — forgetting it is the most common cause of post-assertion test hangs. For SSE, prefer `req.destroy()` over waiting for a natural stream close; the event source will reconnect automatically, but the test should assert on the initial connection headers only. [official]

---

### 405. `Cypress.Commands.add()` Overload-Safe Custom Commands with TypeScript Declaration Merging  [official]

TypeScript strict mode requires custom commands added with `Cypress.Commands.add()` to be declared via module augmentation of the `Cypress.Chainable` interface; without the declaration, `cy.myCommand()` fails compilation with "Property 'myCommand' does not exist on type 'Chainable'". Using a dedicated `cypress/support/commands.d.ts` file to house all augmentations keeps declarations co-located with the implementation and prevents them from polluting the global `tsconfig.json` includes. When a custom command accepts an optional second argument with destructured defaults, the TypeScript signature must use `options?: MyOptions` (optional parameter) rather than `options: MyOptions = {}` (default parameter) to satisfy Cypress's overload resolution. The `export {}` line is mandatory to make the file a module rather than a script.

```typescript
// cypress/support/commands.ts
Cypress.Commands.add(
  'loginViaApi',
  (email: string, options?: { role?: 'admin' | 'user'; rememberMe?: boolean }) => {
    const { role = 'user', rememberMe = false } = options ?? {};

    cy.request({
      method: 'POST',
      url: '/api/auth/login',
      body: { email, role, rememberMe },
      log: false,   // suppress credentials from Command Log / Cloud recordings
    }).then(({ body }) => {
      window.localStorage.setItem('auth_token', body.token as string);
    });
  }
);

// cypress/support/commands.d.ts
declare global {
  namespace Cypress {
    interface Chainable {
      /**
       * Login via API, bypassing the UI login flow.
       * @example cy.loginViaApi('admin@example.com', { role: 'admin' })
       */
      loginViaApi(
        email: string,
        options?: { role?: 'admin' | 'user'; rememberMe?: boolean }
      ): Chainable<void>;
    }
  }
}

export {};  // Required: makes this file a module; prevents global declaration pollution
```

**Tradeoff / When to use:** Centralise all `Cypress.Chainable` augmentations in a single `commands.d.ts` — spreading declarations across multiple files causes TypeScript to pick up only the last-imported declaration in some project configurations. The `export {}` line at the bottom of `commands.d.ts` is not optional: without it the file is treated as a script rather than a module and the `declare global` block extends the global type space unpredictably. Use the `log: false` option on auth helper commands to prevent credentials from appearing in Cypress Cloud test recordings. [official]

---

### 406. `cy.intercept()` `times` Option for Precise Request Count Assertions  [official]

The `times` option on `cy.intercept()` limits the number of times a route stub applies, after which the request passes through to the real server. This is ideal for testing retry behaviour: stub the first two requests to fail (with 503) and let the third succeed, confirming the app's retry logic fires and eventually shows the user success feedback. Without `times`, a permanent stub would mask the natural pass-through and prevent testing the recovery path. `times` resets on each test (it is not a cumulative counter across tests), so a `beforeEach` that registers intercepts with `times: 1` works correctly for independent retry tests.

```typescript
// cypress/e2e/retry-logic.cy.ts
describe('API retry behaviour', () => {
  it('retries on 503 and shows success after 3rd attempt', () => {
    let callCount = 0;

    cy.intercept('GET', '/api/recommendations', (req) => {
      callCount++;
      if (callCount < 3) {
        req.reply({ statusCode: 503, body: { error: 'Service unavailable' } });
      }
      // 3rd call and beyond: pass through to real server
    }).as('recommendations');

    cy.visit('/homepage');

    // App retries automatically; wait for 3 calls
    cy.wait('@recommendations');
    cy.wait('@recommendations');
    cy.wait('@recommendations');

    cy.get('[data-cy="recommendations-list"]').should('be.visible');
    cy.wrap(callCount).should('eq', 3);
  });

  it('uses times option to stub exactly once then pass through', () => {
    // First call: stub with error (times: 1 means only one interception)
    cy.intercept(
      'POST',
      '/api/payment',
      { statusCode: 402, body: { error: 'Insufficient funds' } },
      { times: 1 }
    ).as('paymentFirst');

    // Second call: passthrough alias to confirm real server was reached
    cy.intercept('POST', '/api/payment').as('paymentPassthrough');

    cy.get('[data-cy="pay-btn"]').click();
    cy.wait('@paymentFirst');
    cy.get('[data-cy="payment-error"]').should('contain.text', 'Insufficient funds');

    cy.get('[data-cy="retry-payment-btn"]').click();
    cy.wait('@paymentPassthrough');
    cy.get('[data-cy="payment-success"]').should('be.visible');
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff / When to use:** The `times` option is the cleanest way to test recovery scenarios without complex intercept cleanup logic in `afterEach`. Be aware that `cy.wait('@alias')` counts each request invocation separately, so a `times: 2` stub requires two `cy.wait('@alias')` calls to confirm both requests were intercepted. If you mix a `times`-limited stub with a permanent passthrough intercept for the same URL (registered after the limited stub), the registration order matters — register the `times`-limited stub last because Cypress evaluates intercepts in LIFO order. [official]

---

### 407. `Cypress.Buffer` for In-Memory Binary File Generation in `cy.selectFile()`  [official]

`cy.selectFile()` accepts a `Cypress.Buffer` object as the file contents, enabling in-memory binary files to be constructed without writing fixture files to disk. This is the correct approach for testing file upload validation (size limits, MIME type restrictions, corrupt file handling) where the test controls the exact byte content. `Cypress.Buffer.from()` mirrors the Node.js `Buffer.from()` API and supports `'utf8'`, `'base64'`, and `'hex'` encodings. Generating deterministic binary content confirms that the app's file parser handles both valid and malformed binaries without relying on checked-in fixture files that may become stale.

```typescript
// cypress/e2e/file-upload-validation.cy.ts
describe('File upload — validation scenarios', () => {
  it('accepts a valid PNG file constructed in memory', () => {
    // Minimal valid PNG header (8 bytes signature + IHDR chunk stub)
    const pngHeader = Cypress.Buffer.from(
      '89504e470d0a1a0a0000000d49484452',
      'hex'
    );

    cy.visit('/upload');
    cy.get('[data-cy="file-input"]').selectFile({
      contents: pngHeader,
      fileName: 'test-image.png',
      mimeType: 'image/png',
    });

    cy.get('[data-cy="upload-preview"]').should('be.visible');
    cy.get('[data-cy="file-error"]').should('not.exist');
  });

  it('rejects a file exceeding the 5 MB size limit', () => {
    // Generate a 6 MB buffer of zeros
    const oversizedBuffer = Cypress.Buffer.alloc(6 * 1024 * 1024, 0);

    cy.get('[data-cy="file-input"]').selectFile({
      contents: oversizedBuffer,
      fileName: 'large-file.bin',
      mimeType: 'application/octet-stream',
    });

    cy.get('[data-cy="file-error"]')
      .should('be.visible')
      .and('contain.text', 'exceeds 5 MB');
  });

  it('rejects a file with mismatched extension and MIME type', () => {
    const csvContent = Cypress.Buffer.from('id,name\n1,Alice\n2,Bob', 'utf8');

    cy.get('[data-cy="file-input"]').selectFile({
      contents: csvContent,
      fileName: 'data.exe',     // Extension says .exe
      mimeType: 'text/csv',     // MIME type says CSV — intentional mismatch
    });

    cy.get('[data-cy="file-error"]').should('contain.text', 'Invalid file type');
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff / When to use:** In-memory buffer generation is superior to fixture files for validation edge-case tests because the buffer contents are self-documenting and version-controlled inline with the test. For large buffers above ~20 MB, `Cypress.Buffer.alloc()` can exhaust the Cypress proxy serialisation heap on memory-constrained CI runners — write buffers larger than 20 MB to a temp file via `cy.task()` and pass the file path to `cy.selectFile()` instead. The `mimeType` field overrides the MIME type detected from the file extension — this is intentional for mismatch tests but can cause unexpected behaviour if omitted for an extension-agnostic uploader that relies solely on `file.type`. [official]

---

### 408. Svelte 5 Component Testing with `cy.mount()` and Rune Reactivity  [community]

Svelte 5's rune-based reactivity system (`$state`, `$derived`, `$effect`) works correctly with `cy.mount()` but requires adding `cy.wait(0)` between mount and any assertion that depends on a `$derived` or `$effect` value — the signal-based scheduler flushes in a microtask that precedes Cypress's macrotask evaluation tick. For components using only `$state` with no derived computations, `cy.wait(0)` is not needed because `$state` mutation is synchronous. When using `@testing-library/svelte` alongside `cy.mount()`, import and call `cleanup` in `afterEach` to prevent component leaks between tests; `cy.mount()` does not auto-cleanup testing-library registrations.

```typescript
// cypress/component/counter.cy.ts
import { mount } from 'cypress/svelte';
import Counter from './Counter.svelte';

describe('Counter (Svelte 5 runes)', () => {
  it('increments count on button click', () => {
    mount(Counter, { props: { initialCount: 0 } });

    // Wait for $derived initial value to flush through microtask queue
    cy.wait(0);

    cy.get('[data-cy="count-display"]').should('contain.text', '0');

    cy.get('[data-cy="increment-btn"]').click();

    // $derived count updates in microtask after click macro-task
    cy.wait(0);
    cy.get('[data-cy="count-display"]').should('contain.text', '1');
  });

  it('derived formatted label updates after multiple increments', () => {
    mount(Counter, { props: { initialCount: 9 } });
    cy.wait(0);

    cy.get('[data-cy="count-label"]').should('contain.text', 'Count: 9');

    cy.get('[data-cy="increment-btn"]').click().click();
    cy.wait(0);
    cy.get('[data-cy="count-label"]').should('contain.text', 'Count: 11');
  });

  it('$effect cleanup runs on unmount with no memory leak sentinel', () => {
    const component = mount(Counter, { props: { initialCount: 5 } });
    cy.wait(0);

    cy.get('[data-cy="count-display"]').should('contain.text', '5');

    component.then(({ unmount }) => {
      unmount();
    });

    cy.window().its('_counterEffectActive').should('be.undefined');
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff / When to use:** Apply `cy.wait(0)` only for components whose visible state is driven by `$derived` or `$effect` runes — applying it globally in `beforeEach` as a blanket fix masks real flakiness where the UI is genuinely slow to update. The `svelte/internal/client` module must be aliased in the Vite CT config to prevent duplicate Svelte runtime registrations when both the component and a testing-library import from Svelte. When testing Svelte 5 components that receive props from a parent, use `cy.mount()` with `props` rather than creating a wrapper component to keep component tests isolated and readable. [community]

---

### 409. `cy.task()` Polling Pattern for External Service Readiness Gates  [official]

Long-running asynchronous operations triggered by UI actions (email dispatch, PDF generation, background job processing) cannot be asserted directly from the browser — `cy.task()` combined with a polling wrapper provides a reliable gate that waits for an external service to complete without using `cy.wait(ms)` magic numbers. The polling task uses Node.js loop with `setTimeout` within a Promise and resolves when the expected state is detected or rejects after a configurable max wait, producing a deterministic failure message instead of a generic assertion timeout. The task's `maxAttempts` and `intervalMs` should be configurable via task payload to allow per-test tuning without modifying the task implementation.

```typescript
// cypress/tasks/poll-until.ts
export async function pollUntil<T>(
  check: () => Promise<T | null>,
  { maxAttempts = 20, intervalMs = 500 }: { maxAttempts?: number; intervalMs?: number } = {}
): Promise<T> {
  for (let attempt = 0; attempt < maxAttempts; attempt++) {
    const result = await check();
    if (result !== null) return result;
    await new Promise<void>((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, intervalMs));
  }
  throw new Error(
    `pollUntil: condition not met after ${maxAttempts} attempts x ${intervalMs}ms`
  );
}

// cypress/e2e/registration.cy.ts
describe('User registration flow', () => {
  it('sends a verification email after signup', () => {
    cy.visit('/register');
    cy.get('[data-cy="email"]').type('newuser@example.com');
    cy.get('[data-cy="password"]').type('SecurePass123!');
    cy.get('[data-cy="signup-btn"]').click();

    cy.get('[data-cy="check-email-prompt"]').should('be.visible');

    // Poll for email delivery: max 10 sec (20 attempts x 500ms)
    cy.task<{ subject: string; body: string }>('waitForEmail', {
      recipient: 'newuser@example.com',
      subjectContains: 'Verify your account',
      maxAttempts: 20,
      intervalMs: 500,
    }).then(({ subject }) => {
      expect(subject).to.include('Verify your account');
    });
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff / When to use:** The `pollUntil` task is strictly superior to `cy.wait(10000)` because it resolves as soon as the condition is met rather than always waiting the full timeout. The `maxAttempts x intervalMs` product should be tuned to 2-3x the expected real-world operation latency — too tight causes flakiness on slow CI runners; too loose extends the failure wait time unnecessarily. Never use `pollUntil` for DOM state assertions — those belong in `cy.get().should()` retry chains which Cypress handles natively without task overhead. [official]

---

### 410. `cy.origin()` for Cross-Origin iFrame DOM Assertions  [official]

When an application embeds a cross-origin `<iframe>` (e.g., an embedded payment widget, a third-party chat SDK, or an OAuth popup), the Same-Origin Policy prevents direct DOM access via `cy.get('iframe').its('0.contentDocument')`. Using `cy.origin()` with the iframe's origin URL allows test code to execute in that origin's context and perform DOM assertions inside the iframe. The iframe's base origin URL must be passed as the first argument to `cy.origin()`, and all Cypress commands inside the callback run in the iframe's security context rather than the parent page's. `cy.intercept()` routes registered for the iframe origin in the parent context continue to apply inside the `cy.origin()` block — the proxy layer is shared across all origins.

```typescript
// cypress/e2e/payment-widget.cy.ts
describe('Embedded payment widget (cross-origin iframe)', () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    cy.visit('/checkout');
    cy.get('[data-cy="payment-iframe"]').should('be.visible');
  });

  it('renders card number field inside the cross-origin payment iframe', () => {
    cy.origin('https://payments.widget.example.com', () => {
      // All cy.* commands here run inside the iframe context
      cy.get('input[name="cardnumber"]').should('be.visible');
      cy.get('input[name="exp-date"]').should('be.visible');
      cy.get('input[name="cvc"]').should('be.visible');
    });
  });

  it('shows validation error when invalid card number is entered', () => {
    cy.origin('https://payments.widget.example.com', () => {
      cy.get('input[name="cardnumber"]').type('1234 5678 9012 3456');
      cy.get('input[name="cardnumber"]').blur();

      cy.get('[data-cy="card-error"]')
        .should('be.visible')
        .and('contain.text', 'invalid card');
    });
  });

  it('parent page reflects successful payment after iframe postMessage', () => {
    cy.origin('https://payments.widget.example.com', () => {
      cy.get('input[name="cardnumber"]').type('4242 4242 4242 4242');
      cy.get('input[name="exp-date"]').type('12/30');
      cy.get('input[name="cvc"]').type('123');
      cy.get('[data-cy="pay-btn"]').click();
    });

    // Back in parent context: assert postMessage-driven UI update
    cy.get('[data-cy="payment-success-banner"]').should('be.visible');
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff / When to use:** `cy.origin()` for iframe testing requires the Cypress proxy to intercept the iframe's initial request, which means the iframe `src` must route through the Cypress proxy. For third-party iframes loaded from a CDN with strict CSP headers, `experimentalCspAllowList` may need to be configured to permit the iframe's script execution. Each `cy.origin()` call adds approximately 300ms of spec-bridge setup overhead — batch multiple iframe assertions in a single `cy.origin()` callback rather than calling it multiple times in sequence. [official]

---

## Community Gotchas — Cycle 42

296. **`cy.prompt()` consumes its per-run quota even when the step fails or is retried — a single test retry that re-runs `cy.prompt()` calls burns quota a second time, silently exhausting the 100-call run limit mid-suite** [community] — A team configures `retries: 2` globally and has a spec with 10 `cy.prompt()` calls. When three tests fail and retry twice each, the extra 30 prompt calls eat 30% of the run quota. At call 101, Cypress silently skips all subsequent `cy.prompt()` steps, causing tests to reach an unexpected app state and fail with unrelated assertion errors. WHY: `cy.prompt()` quota is counted by the Cypress Cloud inference endpoint per API call, not per unique test; retries are treated as new calls. Fix: tag prompt-assisted specs with `@exploratory` and set `retries: 0` in their describe block; reserve `cy.prompt()` for non-retrying development-mode exploratory runs only.

297. **`cy.intercept()` route handlers that register `req.on('response')` AND call `req.continue()` produce a double-response delivery — the response is sent to the browser twice, causing JSON parse errors or duplicate state updates** [community] — A developer registers a middleware intercept that uses `req.on('response', handler)` to capture headers and then calls `req.continue()` to pass the request through. The `req.on('response')` callback also calls `res.send()` to release the response. Both `req.continue()` and `res.send()` attempt to deliver the response, and for chunked responses the browser receives the body twice. WHY: `req.continue()` implicitly calls `res.send()` for the final delivery; an explicit `res.send()` inside `req.on('response')` causes a double delivery. Fix: when using `req.on('response')` for header mutation only, omit the explicit `res.send()` call and let `req.continue()` handle delivery — or call `req.on('response')` without calling `req.continue()` and use `res.send()` exclusively.

298. **`Cypress.Buffer.alloc()` above approximately 20 MB causes a Cypress proxy serialisation `ENOMEM` crash on memory-constrained CI runners (2 GB RAM) — the proxy serialises the entire buffer for IPC transport to the browser, exhausting the process heap** [community] — A developer uses `Cypress.Buffer.alloc(100 * 1024 * 1024, 0)` to test a 100 MB upload size limit. The test passes locally (16 GB MacBook) but kills the CI runner with "Allocation failed — process out of memory." WHY: `cy.selectFile()` with a `Cypress.Buffer` sends the full buffer through the Cypress proxy IPC channel as a JSON-over-IPC message; large buffers exhaust the serialisation heap. Fix: for buffers larger than 20 MB, write the data to a temp file in a `cy.task()` and pass the file path to `cy.selectFile()` as a fixture path instead of an inline buffer.

299. **`angular-zoneless` harness's `cy.mount()` does not trigger `ngOnChanges()` lifecycle hook when inputs are updated by directly setting `component.someInput = newValue` — the hook is silently skipped because the assignment bypasses Angular's change detection pipeline** [community] — A developer mounts an Angular 21 zoneless component and updates an input via `cy.mount().then(({ component }) => { component.userId = 'new-id' })`. The `ngOnChanges()` hook that should re-fetch user data never fires. WHY: directly setting a property on the component instance bypasses Angular's template binding mechanism; `ngOnChanges()` is only invoked by Angular's internal input-binding system. Fix: use `fixture.componentRef.setInput('userId', 'new-id')` from the mount result object to update inputs through Angular's change detection pipeline, which correctly triggers `ngOnChanges()`.

300. **`cy.clock()` with a `Date` override does not affect `Intl.DateTimeFormat` timezone-aware formatting — tests asserting on locale-formatted date strings fail on UTC CI runners because the system timezone is not overridden by `cy.clock()`** [community] — A developer uses `cy.clock(new Date('2026-05-14T12:00:00-07:00').getTime())` and asserts a dashboard shows `'May 14, 2026'`. The test passes locally (US/Pacific) but fails on the UTC CI runner, which adjusts the timestamp to `May 15, 2026` at UTC midnight. WHY: `cy.clock()` overrides the JavaScript `Date` constructor timestamp but cannot override the OS-level timezone or the Chromium locale used by `Intl.DateTimeFormat`; timezone-sensitive display is determined by the runner's system locale. Fix: pass `{ timeZone: 'UTC' }` to `Intl.DateTimeFormat` in the component and assert the UTC-normalised value, or set `TZ=UTC` in the CI environment to ensure consistent timezone across all runners.

301. **`cy.intercept()` with a `{ hostname }` route matcher performs an exact string match — it does not intercept subdomain traffic such as `api.example.com` when configured with `{ hostname: 'example.com' }`, silently passing through subdomain requests to the real server** [community] — A developer stubs all outbound requests for a domain with `cy.intercept({ hostname: 'example.com' }, { fixture: 'mock.json' })`, expecting it to cover `api.example.com` API calls made by the app. The API calls are not intercepted and the app hits the real back-end. WHY: the `hostname` route matcher performs an exact string match, not a suffix match; subdomain interception requires a glob pattern or a separate intercept per subdomain. Fix: use `cy.intercept({ hostname: '*.example.com' })` (glob wildcard) to match all subdomains, or register explicit intercepts for each subdomain your app calls.

| `cy.prompt()` rate limits | https://docs.cypress.io/api/commands/prompt | 600/hour, 100/run; retries consume quota; tag specs `@exploratory`, disable retries |
| `--posix-exit-codes` CLI flag | https://docs.cypress.io/app/references/command-line | 0=pass, 1=test failure, 2=runner error; required for CI conditional downstream logic |
| `cy.session()` `idleTimeout` | https://docs.cypress.io/api/commands/session | Measured by Cypress runner clock; combine with `validate()` for defence-in-depth |
| `req.on('response')` streaming | https://docs.cypress.io/api/commands/intercept | `res.send()` required to release buffered response; `req.destroy()` for SSE teardown |
| TypeScript `commands.d.ts` merging | https://docs.cypress.io/app/tooling/typescript-support | `export {}` mandatory for module scope; `log: false` on auth commands for Cloud security |
| `cy.intercept()` `times` option | https://docs.cypress.io/api/commands/intercept | LIFO eval order: register `times`-limited stub last; one `cy.wait()` per intercepted call |
| `Cypress.Buffer` upload testing | https://docs.cypress.io/api/utilities/buffer | `alloc()` cap ~20 MB for CI heap; write larger payloads to temp file via `cy.task()` |
| Svelte 5 runes + CT | https://docs.cypress.io/app/component-testing/svelte/overview | `cy.wait(0)` for `$derived`/`$effect`; `cleanup()` in `afterEach` with testing-library |
| `cy.task()` polling pattern | https://docs.cypress.io/api/commands/task | `pollUntil` helper; tune `maxAttempts x intervalMs` to 2-3x expected latency |
| `cy.origin()` iframe assertions | https://docs.cypress.io/api/commands/origin | Batch in single callback; ~300ms setup overhead per call; `experimentalCspAllowList` for strict CSP |

## Cycle 43 — 2026-05-14

### 411. `cy.press()` for Native Keyboard Navigation and Focus Management Testing  [official]

`cy.press()` (introduced in Cypress 14.3.0, expanded through 15.3.0) dispatches actual native keyboard events to the browser rather than simulating input character sequences the way `cy.type()` does. This makes it the correct tool for testing Tab focus order, arrow-key navigation in custom listboxes, Escape key dismissal of modals, and any interaction that depends on the browser's native `keydown`/`keyup` event pipeline rather than value injection. Unlike `cy.type()`, `cy.press()` is called on `cy` directly (not on a subject element), so focus must be established on the intended element before the call. Named keys are accessed via the `Cypress.Keyboard.Keys` enum — attempting to use raw special strings like `'{tab}'` (the `cy.type()` syntax) as the argument will throw a type error.

```typescript
// cypress/e2e/keyboard-nav.cy.ts
describe('Form keyboard navigation', () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    cy.visit('/contact');
  });

  it('Tab moves focus through fields in DOM order', () => {
    cy.get('[data-cy="name-input"]').focus();

    cy.press(Cypress.Keyboard.Keys.TAB);
    cy.get('[data-cy="email-input"]').should('have.focus');

    cy.press(Cypress.Keyboard.Keys.TAB);
    cy.get('[data-cy="message-textarea"]').should('have.focus');

    cy.press(Cypress.Keyboard.Keys.TAB);
    cy.get('[data-cy="submit-btn"]').should('have.focus');
  });

  it('Escape closes the modal and returns focus to the trigger', () => {
    cy.get('[data-cy="open-modal-btn"]').click();
    cy.get('[data-cy="modal"]').should('be.visible');

    cy.press(Cypress.Keyboard.Keys.ESC);

    cy.get('[data-cy="modal"]').should('not.exist');
    cy.get('[data-cy="open-modal-btn"]').should('have.focus');
  });

  it('Arrow keys navigate a custom combobox dropdown', () => {
    cy.get('[data-cy="combobox"]').focus().click();
    cy.get('[data-cy="combobox-option-list"]').should('be.visible');

    cy.press(Cypress.Keyboard.Keys.DOWN);
    cy.get('[data-cy="combobox-option"]').first().should('have.attr', 'aria-selected', 'true');

    cy.press(Cypress.Keyboard.Keys.DOWN);
    cy.get('[data-cy="combobox-option"]').eq(1).should('have.attr', 'aria-selected', 'true');

    cy.press(Cypress.Keyboard.Keys.ENTER);
    cy.get('[data-cy="combobox"]').should('contain.value', 'Option 2');
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff / When to use:** Use `cy.press()` for single-key events that trigger focus transitions, keyboard shortcuts, or ARIA widget navigation patterns — use `cy.type()` for multi-character text input or when you need modifier combos (`{ctrl}a`). `cy.press()` yields `null`, so no subject chain is possible after it; if you need to assert on the focused element, use `cy.focused()` as a new chain. F1–F12 function keys are not supported because Chromium intercepts them as browser-level shortcuts before the page receives the event. [official]

---

### 412. `cy.env()` Secure Environment Variable Access with Async Command Chains  [official]

`cy.env()` (introduced in Cypress 15.10.0) replaces the synchronous `Cypress.env()` API for reading sensitive values like API keys, passwords, or tokens inside test code. Unlike `Cypress.env()`, which hydrated all environment variables into the global `Cypress` object at runner startup — making them visible in the Cypress Cloud replay timeline and serialisable into spec-bridge snapshots — `cy.env()` only fetches the explicitly named variables asynchronously, keeping them out of browser-accessible scope. Variables are requested as an array of keys and resolved via a `.then()` callback, which means they compose naturally into `cy` command chains. The `log: false` option suppresses the variable names from the Cypress Cloud test replay, which is critical when the variable name itself is a hint about the secret's purpose.

```typescript
// cypress/support/commands.ts
Cypress.Commands.add('loginWithApiToken', () => {
  // Fetch only the two vars needed — never hydrate the full env namespace
  cy.env(['API_BASE_URL', 'ADMIN_API_KEY'], { log: false }).then(
    ({ API_BASE_URL, ADMIN_API_KEY }) => {
      cy.request({
        method: 'POST',
        url: `${API_BASE_URL}/auth/token`,
        headers: { 'x-api-key': ADMIN_API_KEY },
        body: { grant_type: 'client_credentials' },
      }).then(({ body }) => {
        cy.setCookie('auth_token', body.access_token, { log: false });
      });
    }
  );
});

// cypress/e2e/admin-panel.cy.ts
describe('Admin panel', () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    cy.loginWithApiToken();
  });

  it('lists all users in the admin table', () => {
    cy.visit('/admin/users');
    cy.get('[data-cy="users-table"] tbody tr').should('have.length.above', 0);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff / When to use:** Migrate to `cy.env()` from `Cypress.env()` for any variable that is a secret — the async model is a minor inconvenience that provides a meaningful security boundary in Cypress Cloud recordings. For non-sensitive public configuration values (feature flag names, API version strings, environment labels), use `Cypress.expose()` instead — it is synchronous and appropriate for values that may be visible in the browser context. Set `allowCypressEnv: false` in `cypress.config.ts` to block the deprecated synchronous API and enforce the migration. [official]

---

### 413. `Cypress.expose()` for Public Configuration Broadcasting Across Spec Files  [official]

`Cypress.expose()` (introduced in Cypress 15.10.0) provides a synchronous API for storing and retrieving non-sensitive public configuration values that need to be accessible across the Cypress runner, the spec context, and — critically — from within application code running in the browser. Values set with `Cypress.expose()` are intentionally browser-accessible, making them suitable for feature flag overrides, environment labels, plugin version strings, or A/B test bucket assignments that the application reads from `window.Cypress`. Setting an object to `Cypress.expose()` performs a shallow merge with existing exposed values rather than replacing them, enabling multiple plugins or `support/` files to contribute configuration without overwriting each other.

```typescript
// cypress/support/e2e.ts — bootstrap public test configuration
import { version } from '../../package.json';

Cypress.expose({
  appEnv: 'test',
  apiVersion: 'v3',
  featureFlags: {
    newCheckoutFlow: true,
    darkModeEnabled: false,
  },
  sdkVersion: version,
});

// cypress/e2e/feature-flags.cy.ts
describe('Feature flag gate: new checkout flow', () => {
  it('shows new checkout UI when flag is enabled', () => {
    // Application reads window.Cypress.featureFlags at runtime
    cy.visit('/checkout');

    // Verify the application consumed the exposed flag
    cy.get('[data-cy="new-checkout-container"]').should('be.visible');
    cy.get('[data-cy="legacy-checkout-container"]').should('not.exist');
  });

  it('can override a single flag for a negative test without clobbering others', () => {
    Cypress.expose('featureFlags', { ...Cypress.expose('featureFlags'), newCheckoutFlow: false });

    cy.visit('/checkout');
    cy.get('[data-cy="legacy-checkout-container"]').should('be.visible');
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff / When to use:** `Cypress.expose()` is the correct tool for configuration that the application code itself needs to read during a test — do not use it for anything a third-party script or browser extension could misuse (no API keys, no auth tokens). Because exposed values persist for the duration of the spec file, mutating them in one `it()` block for a negative test will affect all subsequent tests in the same describe unless you restore the original value in `afterEach`. For values consumed only inside `cy.task()` or Node.js test helpers, skip `Cypress.expose()` entirely and use `cy.env()`. [official]

---

### 414. `cy.prompt()` Placeholders for Dynamic Sensitive Values in AI-Powered Steps  [official]

`cy.prompt()` (Cypress 15.13.0+) converts plain-English test step arrays into executable Cypress commands via an AI inference endpoint. The `options.placeholders` map allows dynamic or sensitive values — passwords, one-time tokens, generated order IDs — to be injected into the step strings at runtime without sending the actual values to the AI model. The `{{placeholder}}` syntax in a step string is replaced with the corresponding `placeholders` map value before the step executes, but the placeholder key (not the value) is what gets transmitted to the inference API, preserving cache efficiency across runs that use different credential sets. Each `cy.prompt()` call counts against the per-user rate limit (100 calls/hour on free plans, 600/hour on paid plans), so prompts should be reserved for exploratory or prototype specs — generated code should be exported and committed as static Cypress commands for regression suites.

```typescript
// cypress/e2e/checkout-prompt.cy.ts
// Exploratory spec: uses cy.prompt() to prototype the flow, then export to static commands
describe('Checkout flow (AI-assisted prototype)', () => {
  it('completes a purchase with a valid credit card', () => {
    cy.session('checkout-user', () => {
      cy.visit('/login');
      cy.prompt(
        [
          'type "testuser@example.com" into the email field',
          'type "{{password}}" into the password field',
          'click the "Sign in" button',
          'wait for the dashboard heading to be visible',
        ],
        { placeholders: { password: Cypress.env('TEST_USER_PASSWORD') } }
      );
    });

    cy.visit('/products/widget-pro');

    cy.prompt([
      'click the "Add to cart" button',
      'click the cart icon in the navigation header',
      'click the "Proceed to checkout" button',
      'type "4242424242424242" into the card number field',
      'type "12/30" into the expiry field',
      'type "123" into the CVC field',
      'click the "Pay now" button',
      'assert "Order confirmed" is visible on the page',
    ]);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff / When to use:** `cy.prompt()` is only available for E2E tests on Chromium-based browsers and requires a Cypress Cloud account or a valid `CYPRESS_RECORD_KEY`. It does not support canvas elements, cross-origin iframes, cookie/session clearing, or direct API requests — use native Cypress commands for those operations. Self-healing selector regeneration consumes an additional AI call each time a cached selector becomes stale, multiplying quota consumption; in high-churn UI codebases, regeneration overhead can exceed the initial generation cost. Always export generated commands to static TypeScript before committing — `cy.prompt()` in committed specs is a liability during CI runs where the inference endpoint may be unavailable or rate-limited. [official]

---

### 415. `justInTimeCompile` for Memory-Efficient Component Test Suites in Monorepos  [official]

Cypress `justInTimeCompile` (promoted from experimental in Cypress 14.0.0 and enabled by default) compiles only the Vite or Webpack resources directly required by the currently executing spec file, rather than pre-compiling the entire component test bundle upfront. In large monorepos where hundreds of component specs share a single Cypress configuration, pre-compilation of all specs before the first test runs can consume 2–4 GB of Vite/Webpack heap and cause OOM crashes on 8 GB CI runners. With `justInTimeCompile: true`, each spec's required modules are compiled in a scoped incremental bundle pass immediately before that spec executes, keeping peak heap usage proportional to the largest single spec rather than the entire suite. The feature is aware of module graph boundaries — shared modules imported by multiple specs are not recompiled per spec; they are cached in the bundler's module resolution cache and only evicted when the `numTestsKeptInMemory` threshold is crossed.

```typescript
// cypress.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from 'cypress';

export default defineConfig({
  component: {
    // justInTimeCompile defaults to true — set explicitly for documentation clarity
    justInTimeCompile: true,
    devServer: {
      framework: 'react',
      bundler: 'vite',
    },
    // Complement with memory management: keep fewer snapshots in CI
    numTestsKeptInMemory: Cypress.env('CI') ? 5 : 50,
  },
});

// cypress/component/product-card.cy.tsx
import React from 'react';
import { mount } from 'cypress/react';
import { ProductCard } from '../../src/components/ProductCard';
import type { Product } from '../../src/types';

const mockProduct: Product = {
  id: 'prod-001',
  name: 'Widget Pro',
  price: 49.99,
  inStock: true,
};

describe('ProductCard', () => {
  it('renders product name and price', () => {
    mount(<ProductCard product={mockProduct} />);
    cy.get('[data-cy="product-name"]').should('contain.text', 'Widget Pro');
    cy.get('[data-cy="product-price"]').should('contain.text', '$49.99');
  });

  it('shows out-of-stock badge when inStock is false', () => {
    mount(<ProductCard product={{ ...mockProduct, inStock: false }} />);
    cy.get('[data-cy="out-of-stock-badge"]').should('be.visible');
    cy.get('[data-cy="add-to-cart-btn"]').should('be.disabled');
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff / When to use:** `justInTimeCompile: true` reduces CI memory consumption significantly for large component test suites at the cost of slightly increased total wall-clock time — each spec pays a short compilation latency (~200–800ms depending on spec size) before its first test executes. For local development, the tradeoff is negligible because Vite's HMR cache warms after the first run. If you observe deterministic test failures that only appear in multi-spec runs, set `justInTimeCompile: false` temporarily to rule out module cache pollution between specs before filing a bug. [official]

---

### 416. React 19 Component Testing — Actions, `use()`, and Concurrent Transitions  [official]

Cypress 14.0.0 unified React 18 and 19 component testing under the `cypress/react` harness, dropping the separate `cypress/react18` import. React 19 introduces `<form>` Actions (server-invoked async form handlers), the `use()` hook for Promise and Context reading during render, and fine-grained concurrent transitions via `useTransition`. Testing these patterns with `cy.mount()` requires awareness that Action-driven form submissions resolve asynchronously via React's Scheduler — `cy.get('[data-cy="success-msg"]')` after a form `action` function will retry until the Scheduler drains the transition queue, which aligns well with Cypress's command retry model. However, testing `use(Promise)` components requires wrapping the component in a `<Suspense>` boundary inside the test; mounting a `use()` component without `<Suspense>` throws a synchronous error before the command log can capture a snapshot.

```typescript
// cypress/component/contact-form.cy.tsx
import React, { Suspense } from 'react';
import { mount } from 'cypress/react';
import { ContactForm } from '../../src/components/ContactForm';

// Stub the server action to avoid real network calls
const mockSubmitAction = cy.stub().as('submitAction').resolves({ success: true });

describe('ContactForm (React 19 Actions)', () => {
  it('shows success message after form Action resolves', () => {
    mount(
      <Suspense fallback={<div data-cy="loading">Loading...</div>}>
        <ContactForm submitAction={mockSubmitAction} />
      </Suspense>
    );

    cy.get('[data-cy="name-input"]').type('Alice');
    cy.get('[data-cy="email-input"]').type('alice@example.com');
    cy.get('[data-cy="message-textarea"]').type('Hello world');

    cy.get('[data-cy="submit-btn"]').click();

    // React 19 Action sets isPending=true during async resolution
    cy.get('[data-cy="submit-btn"]').should('be.disabled');

    // Cypress retries until the Action resolves and isPending clears
    cy.get('[data-cy="success-message"]')
      .should('be.visible')
      .and('contain.text', 'Message sent');

    cy.get('@submitAction').should('have.been.calledOnce');
  });

  it('displays inline field error when Action returns validation failure', () => {
    const failAction = cy.stub().resolves({ success: false, error: 'Email already registered' });

    mount(<ContactForm submitAction={failAction} />);

    cy.get('[data-cy="email-input"]').type('existing@example.com');
    cy.get('[data-cy="submit-btn"]').click();

    cy.get('[data-cy="email-error"]')
      .should('be.visible')
      .and('contain.text', 'Email already registered');
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff / When to use:** Always wrap `use(Promise)`-consuming components in `<Suspense>` in the test — do not rely on the component's internal `<Suspense>` wrapper to catch the test mounting throw, because `cy.mount()` calls React's render synchronously before the Suspense boundary is registered. For components that fire real server Actions (Next.js Server Actions), mock the action prop in component tests and reserve real Action invocation for E2E tests that run against a dev or staging server. React 19 concurrent features (`useOptimistic`, `useFormStatus`) are also fully supported — use `cy.get().should()` retry chains rather than `cy.wait()` for optimistic update assertions. [official]

---

### 417. TypeScript 6 `noUncheckedSideEffectImports` in Cypress Config Files  [official]

Cypress 15.14.0 adds official TypeScript 6 support, and Cypress 15.0.0 switched from `ts-node` to `tsx` for parsing `cypress.config.ts`. TypeScript 6 introduces `noUncheckedSideEffectImports` (enabled under `strict: true` in TS 6), which causes imports that are purely side-effectful (no exports consumed) to be flagged if the imported module has no type definitions. In Cypress configurations, this manifests as a TS error on lines like `import './cypress/support/register-tasks'` — common in `setupNodeEvents`-adjacent utility imports. The fix is to add a `/// <reference types="..." />` triple-slash directive or ensure side-effect-only modules export an empty `{}` to satisfy the checker. The `cypress` folder's dedicated `tsconfig.json` should set `"moduleResolution": "bundler"` when using Vite as the component testing devServer, because TypeScript 6's `"bundler"` resolution mode correctly resolves Vite's virtual module imports.

```json
// cypress/tsconfig.json — TypeScript 6 configuration
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "target": "ES2022",
    "module": "ESNext",
    "moduleResolution": "bundler",
    "lib": ["ES2022", "DOM", "DOM.Iterable"],
    "sourceMap": true,
    "strict": true,
    "types": ["cypress", "node"],
    "paths": {
      "@/*": ["../src/*"]
    }
  },
  "include": ["**/*.ts", "**/*.tsx"],
  "exclude": ["node_modules"]
}
```

```typescript
// cypress/support/e2e.ts — satisfy noUncheckedSideEffectImports
// BAD in TS 6 strict mode: import './custom-commands'; // no exports
// GOOD: explicitly re-export nothing to create a module boundary
export {}; // makes this file a module, not a script
import './custom-commands';
import './auth-helpers';

// cypress/support/custom-commands.ts — always export {} for module scope
export {};

declare global {
  namespace Cypress {
    interface Chainable {
      login(email: string, password: string): Chainable<void>;
      seedDatabase(fixture: string): Chainable<void>;
    }
  }
}

Cypress.Commands.add('login', (email: string, password: string) => {
  cy.env(['AUTH_URL'], { log: false }).then(({ AUTH_URL }) => {
    cy.request('POST', `${AUTH_URL}/login`, { email, password }).then(({ body }) => {
      cy.setCookie('session', body.token, { log: false });
    });
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff / When to use:** Keeping the Cypress `tsconfig.json` separate from the root project `tsconfig.json` is strongly recommended — the Cypress folder needs `"types": ["cypress", "node"]` while the application code should not have `"node"` in its types (to prevent accidental use of Node.js APIs in browser code). If CI reports TypeScript errors only in `cypress.config.ts` after upgrading to TS 6, check that `tsx` (not `ts-node`) is the active config parser — Cypress 15+ bundles `tsx` internally and does not respect a project-level `ts-node` installation for config parsing. [official]

---

### 418. `cy.session()` with `cacheAcrossSpecs` and `validate()` for OAuth PKCE Flows  [official]

`cy.session()` with `cacheAcrossSpecs: true` persists the session cache across all spec files in a run, which is essential for OAuth PKCE flows where the code exchange is a one-time operation that cannot be replayed per spec. Without `cacheAcrossSpecs`, each spec file's `beforeEach` would trigger a full PKCE redirect cycle, inflating test suite time proportionally with spec count. The `validate()` function acts as a guard: if the cached session's access token cookie has expired (common in PKCE flows with short-lived tokens), `validate()` returns `false` and Cypress automatically re-runs the `setup()` function to obtain a fresh token before the test proceeds. The session `id` must capture all parameters that affect the session state — for PKCE flows, include the OAuth scope list so different permission sets produce distinct cached sessions.

```typescript
// cypress/support/auth.ts
export function oauthPkceSession(scopes: string[] = ['openid', 'profile', 'email']) {
  const sessionId = ['oauth-pkce', ...scopes.sort()];

  cy.session(
    sessionId,
    () => {
      // Perform real PKCE OAuth flow once, cache the resulting cookies
      cy.visit('/oauth/authorize?response_type=code&scope=' + scopes.join(' '));
      cy.get('[data-cy="username"]').type('testuser@example.com');
      cy.env(['OAUTH_TEST_PASSWORD'], { log: false }).then(({ OAUTH_TEST_PASSWORD }) => {
        cy.get('[data-cy="password"]').type(OAUTH_TEST_PASSWORD, { log: false });
      });
      cy.get('[data-cy="authorize-btn"]').click();
      // App exchanges code for token and sets access_token cookie
      cy.url().should('include', '/dashboard');
    },
    {
      cacheAcrossSpecs: true,
      validate() {
        // Re-run setup if access_token is expired or absent
        cy.getCookie('access_token').then((cookie) => {
          if (!cookie) return false;
          const expiresMs = (cookie.expiry ?? 0) * 1000;
          return Date.now() < expiresMs - 30_000; // 30s buffer
        });
      },
    }
  );
}

// cypress/e2e/profile.cy.ts
import { oauthPkceSession } from '../support/auth';

describe('User profile', () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    oauthPkceSession(['openid', 'profile']);
    cy.visit('/profile');
  });

  it('displays user avatar and display name', () => {
    cy.get('[data-cy="user-avatar"]').should('be.visible');
    cy.get('[data-cy="display-name"]').should('not.be.empty');
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff / When to use:** `cacheAcrossSpecs: true` introduces a cross-spec dependency — if the session setup fails, every subsequent spec that depends on it will also fail, producing cascading failures that look like unrelated test failures. Add a `before()` hook in a dedicated `auth-gate.cy.ts` spec that runs first to validate the session is obtainable before the rest of the suite starts. The `validate()` function must return a boolean synchronously or resolve a Promise/Cypress command chain — do not mix synchronous `return false` with a `cy.getCookie()` chain (the example above is correct — the `cy.getCookie().then()` chain is the return value). [official]

---

### 419. Brotli-Compressed Response Interception with `cy.intercept()` in Cypress 15.11.0+  [official]

Cypress 15.11.0 added Brotli (`br`) decompression support to the Cypress proxy layer, meaning `cy.intercept()` handlers now receive uncompressed response bodies for Brotli-compressed API responses. Prior to this, an intercept handler reading `res.body` on a Brotli-compressed JSON response would receive a binary `Buffer` instead of a parsed object, causing `expect(res.body).to.have.property('id')` assertions to silently fail. With 15.11.0+, the proxy transparently decompresses `Content-Encoding: br` responses before delivering them to the intercept handler — the body arrives as a plain string or parsed object depending on `Content-Type`, matching the existing behaviour for `gzip` and `deflate` encoding. Downstream, the proxy re-compresses the (potentially modified) response before forwarding it to the browser, so the application continues to receive Brotli-encoded bytes without any code change.

```typescript
// cypress/e2e/products-api.cy.ts
describe('Products API with Brotli compression', () => {
  it('intercepts and asserts Brotli-compressed JSON response body', () => {
    cy.intercept('GET', '/api/v3/products*', (req) => {
      req.on('response', (res) => {
        // In Cypress 15.11.0+, res.body is the decompressed JSON object —
        // no manual Buffer.from(res.body).toString() needed.
        expect(res.body).to.be.an('array');
        expect(res.body[0]).to.have.keys(['id', 'name', 'price', 'inStock']);

        // Modify a field before the browser receives the response
        res.body = res.body.map((p: { id: string; name: string; price: number; inStock: boolean }) => ({
          ...p,
          inStock: true, // Force all products in-stock for this test
        }));
      });
    }).as('getProducts');

    cy.visit('/products');
    cy.wait('@getProducts');

    // Verify the modified response was consumed by the app
    cy.get('[data-cy="product-card"]').each(($card) => {
      cy.wrap($card).find('[data-cy="out-of-stock-badge"]').should('not.exist');
    });
  });

  it('stubs a Brotli endpoint with a static JSON fixture', () => {
    cy.intercept('GET', '/api/v3/products*', { fixture: 'products.json' }).as('stubbedProducts');

    cy.visit('/products');
    cy.wait('@stubbedProducts');
    cy.get('[data-cy="product-card"]').should('have.length', 3);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff / When to use:** The transparent Brotli decompression means existing intercept tests that previously worked around binary body issues (by reading the raw Buffer and decoding manually) now receive double-decoded data if both the workaround and the proxy decompression are active — remove any manual `Buffer.from(res.body).toString()` decodes after upgrading to 15.11.0+. Fixture-based stubs (the second `it()` above) are unaffected by compression: Cypress always serves fixture content with correct headers regardless of the original endpoint's `Content-Encoding`. For performance tests that need to verify the browser receives exactly Brotli-compressed bytes, use `cy.request()` directly rather than `cy.intercept()`, because the proxy always normalises the transport encoding. [official]

---

### 420. Firefox WebDriver BiDi Automation for Cross-Browser Event Fidelity Testing  [official]

Cypress 15.0.0 switched Firefox 135+ from Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP) to WebDriver BiDi for browser automation, improving standards compliance and enabling Cypress to drive Firefox with the same fidelity as Chromium. The practical implication for test authors is that `cy.origin()`, `cy.press()`, and `cy.intercept()` now behave identically in Firefox and Chrome — previously, CDP-over-Firefox adapter limitations caused subtle differences in navigation event ordering and keyboard event dispatching. To run the same test spec against both browsers in CI, configure the `browsers` array in `cypress.config.ts` and use `cy.isBrowser()` guards only for genuinely browser-specific assertions (e.g., CSS rendering differences), not for control flow.

```typescript
// cypress.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from 'cypress';

export default defineConfig({
  e2e: {
    baseUrl: 'http://localhost:3000',
    setupNodeEvents(on, config) {
      // In CI, limit browsers to chrome and firefox for BiDi parity testing
      if (config.env.CI) {
        config.browsers = config.browsers.filter(
          (b) => b.name === 'chrome' || b.name === 'firefox'
        );
      }
      return config;
    },
  },
});

// cypress/e2e/keyboard-cross-browser.cy.ts
describe('Cross-browser keyboard input parity', () => {
  it('Tab focus order is consistent across Chrome and Firefox (BiDi)', () => {
    cy.visit('/form');

    cy.get('[data-cy="first-name"]').focus();
    cy.press(Cypress.Keyboard.Keys.TAB);

    // Both Chrome (CDP) and Firefox (BiDi) now agree on focus target
    cy.focused().should('have.attr', 'data-cy', 'last-name');

    cy.press(Cypress.Keyboard.Keys.TAB);
    cy.focused().should('have.attr', 'data-cy', 'email');
  });

  it('intercept resolves response body identically in both browsers', () => {
    cy.intercept('GET', '/api/user').as('getUser');

    cy.visit('/profile');
    cy.wait('@getUser').then(({ response }) => {
      expect(response!.body).to.have.property('id');
    });

    // Use isBrowser guard only for truly browser-divergent behaviour
    if (Cypress.isBrowser('firefox')) {
      // Firefox renders date inputs as text on some platforms — skip date picker test
      cy.log('Skipping date picker assertion: Firefox renders date as text input');
    } else {
      cy.get('[data-cy="dob-picker"]').should('have.attr', 'type', 'date');
    }
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff / When to use:** WebDriver BiDi for Firefox requires Firefox 135 or later — earlier Firefox versions fall back to CDP automatically. For development teams that do not have Firefox in scope, no configuration change is needed (Cypress handles the protocol selection transparently). The BiDi switch eliminates the most common source of Firefox-specific test flakiness (navigation timing differences between CDP and GeckoDriver), but does not resolve CSS layout differences between Firefox's rendering engine and Blink — browser-visual testing still requires a dedicated screenshot comparison tool rather than `cy.get().should()` assertions on layout properties. [official]

---

### 421. Cypress Studio AI Interaction Recording and Test Extension Workflow  [community]

Cypress Studio (available in Cypress Cloud) records user interactions in the app to generate and extend E2E test files. The Studio AI layer adds automatic assertion recommendations on top of recorded interactions — after a recording session, the AI suggests `cy.should()` assertions based on the DOM state observed at each interaction point, reducing the manual assertion-writing burden for common cases. The generated code is exported directly into the test file and can be reviewed in a diff before committing. For extending existing tests, Studio can append a new `it()` block below an existing spec's `describe`, with the recorded interactions scoped to the page state after the last command in the prior test runs.

```typescript
// Example of Studio AI-generated output (committed after review)
// cypress/e2e/user-registration.cy.ts

// GENERATED BY CYPRESS STUDIO — reviewed and committed 2026-05-14
describe('User registration', () => {
  it('completes sign-up form and reaches onboarding', () => {
    cy.visit('http://localhost:3000/register');

    cy.get('#email').type('studio-test@example.com');
    cy.get('#password').type('StudioPass123!');
    cy.get('#password-confirm').type('StudioPass123!');
    cy.get('[data-cy="terms-checkbox"]').check();
    cy.get('[data-cy="register-btn"]').click();

    // AI-recommended assertions (reviewed before commit)
    cy.url().should('include', '/onboarding');
    cy.get('[data-cy="welcome-heading"]')
      .should('be.visible')
      .and('contain.text', 'Welcome');
    cy.get('[data-cy="step-indicator"]').should('contain.text', 'Step 1 of 3');
  });

  // Studio-extended: recorded from the end state of the prior test
  it('completes onboarding step 1 — profile details', () => {
    cy.visit('http://localhost:3000/register');
    cy.get('#email').type('studio-test-2@example.com');
    cy.get('#password').type('StudioPass456!');
    cy.get('#password-confirm').type('StudioPass456!');
    cy.get('[data-cy="terms-checkbox"]').check();
    cy.get('[data-cy="register-btn"]').click();

    // Recorded from step 1 onboarding page
    cy.get('[data-cy="display-name-input"]').type('Test User');
    cy.get('[data-cy="avatar-upload"]').selectFile('cypress/fixtures/avatar.png');
    cy.get('[data-cy="next-step-btn"]').click();

    cy.get('[data-cy="step-indicator"]').should('contain.text', 'Step 2 of 3');
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff / When to use:** Studio AI-generated tests use absolute `cy.visit()` URLs by default (including hostname) — always replace these with `cy.visit('/path')` relative paths before committing so the `baseUrl` configuration applies correctly across environments. AI assertion recommendations are based on static DOM snapshots and may suggest brittle text-content assertions for elements that carry dynamic content in production — review every suggested `contain.text` assertion before committing. Studio recording is only available for Chrome/Electron in the Cypress App; it cannot be used in headless CI mode or with Firefox. [community]

### 422. `cy.intercept()` Dynamic Alias Assignment via `req.alias` for Conditional Stubs  [official]

Setting `req.alias` inside an intercept handler callback allows the intercept's alias to be determined at request time rather than at registration time, which is essential for GraphQL or REST endpoints that serve multiple operation types over a single URL. Assigning `req.alias` to a computed string (e.g., derived from the GraphQL `operationName` or a query parameter) causes `cy.wait()` to wait for that specific request variant rather than the next request to the URL — enabling per-operation aliasing from a single `cy.intercept()` registration. A route registered without a static alias and with only `req.alias` set dynamically will not appear in the Command Log with a named alias until the request is made, but can still be waited on with `cy.wait('@dynamicAlias')` after the request fires.

```typescript
// cypress/support/graphql.ts
export function interceptGraphQL() {
  cy.intercept('POST', '/graphql', (req) => {
    const { operationName, variables } = req.body ?? {};

    if (!operationName) {
      req.alias = 'unknownGraphQL';
      return;
    }

    // Dynamic alias: one intercept registration covers all operations
    req.alias = `gql_${operationName}`;

    // Stub specific operations; pass others through
    if (operationName === 'GetUserProfile') {
      req.reply({ fixture: `graphql/${operationName}.json` });
    } else if (operationName === 'UpdateUserProfile' && variables?.fail) {
      req.reply({ body: { errors: [{ message: 'Validation failed' }] } });
    }
    // All other operations proceed to the real server
  });
}

// cypress/e2e/profile-edit.cy.ts
import { interceptGraphQL } from '../support/graphql';

describe('Profile edit page', () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    interceptGraphQL();
    cy.visit('/profile/edit');
  });

  it('loads profile data via GetUserProfile query', () => {
    cy.wait('@gql_GetUserProfile').then(({ response }) => {
      expect(response!.body.data.user).to.have.property('displayName');
    });

    cy.get('[data-cy="display-name-input"]').should('not.have.value', '');
  });

  it('shows error message when UpdateUserProfile mutation fails', () => {
    cy.get('[data-cy="display-name-input"]').clear().type('Bad Actor');
    cy.get('[data-cy="save-btn"]').click();

    cy.wait('@gql_UpdateUserProfile');
    cy.get('[data-cy="mutation-error"]')
      .should('be.visible')
      .and('contain.text', 'Validation failed');
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff / When to use:** Dynamic alias assignment is strictly superior to registering a separate `cy.intercept()` per GraphQL operation for suites with many operations, because each intercept registration adds a route to the Cypress router's matching stack and degrades matching performance for stacks with 50+ routes. The dynamic alias approach reduces the router stack to a single entry point per endpoint. However, `req.alias` can only be set once per request — subsequent intercept handlers registered for the same URL that also try to assign `req.alias` will overwrite the first assignment; register only one GraphQL intercept per `describe` block and manage all operation routing within that single handler. [official]

---

### 423. `cy.intercept()` `req.destroy()` for SSE and Long-Poll Connection Teardown Testing  [official]

Server-Sent Events (SSE) and long-poll connections hold the HTTP response open indefinitely, which blocks Cypress's spec completion if the connection is not explicitly closed. `req.destroy()` terminates the intercepted connection at the network layer, causing the browser to receive a connection reset error that the application should handle gracefully. Testing SSE teardown scenarios (reconnection logic, offline state banners, connection health indicators) requires pairing `cy.intercept()` with a stubbed SSE response that streams events and then calls `req.destroy()` after a configurable number of events to simulate a dropped connection. The `req.on('response')` callback receives a streamable response object — send individual SSE frames via `res.send({ body: 'data: ...\n\n', delay: n })` calls before destroying.

```typescript
// cypress/e2e/live-feed.cy.ts
describe('Live feed SSE connection resilience', () => {
  it('shows offline banner and reconnects after SSE connection drops', () => {
    let sseResponse: Cypress.IncomingHttpResponse;

    cy.intercept('GET', '/api/live-feed', (req) => {
      req.on('response', (res) => {
        sseResponse = res;
        // Send two events, then simulate dropped connection
        res.headers['content-type'] = 'text/event-stream';
        res.headers['cache-control'] = 'no-cache';
        res.send({ body: 'data: {"event":"item","id":1}\n\n', delay: 100 });
        res.send({ body: 'data: {"event":"item","id":2}\n\n', delay: 200 });
      });
    }).as('sseFeed');

    cy.visit('/live-feed');
    cy.wait('@sseFeed');

    // Verify initial SSE events rendered
    cy.get('[data-cy="feed-item"]').should('have.length', 2);

    // Destroy the connection to simulate network drop
    cy.then(() => {
      sseResponse.destroy();
    });

    cy.get('[data-cy="offline-banner"]').should('be.visible');
    cy.get('[data-cy="reconnecting-spinner"]').should('be.visible');

    // Stub reconnection with a stable empty feed
    cy.intercept('GET', '/api/live-feed', (req) => {
      req.reply({ statusCode: 200, headers: { 'content-type': 'text/event-stream' }, body: '' });
    }).as('sseFeedReconnect');

    cy.wait('@sseFeedReconnect');
    cy.get('[data-cy="offline-banner"]').should('not.exist');
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff / When to use:** `req.destroy()` causes a hard TCP reset from the Cypress proxy — some applications' SSE client implementations distinguish between a clean server-initiated `close` event and a network-level error; the `destroy()` path tests the error path, not the clean-close path. For testing clean SSE server shutdown (e.g., the server sending a `connection: close` header and flushing the buffer), use `res.send()` with a final empty body followed by `res.setDelay(0)` to flush rather than `req.destroy()`. Never call `req.destroy()` in a `beforeEach` without a guard — if the SSE connection has not yet been established when `destroy()` is called, the call is a no-op that silently skips the teardown test setup. [official]

---

### 424. React 19 `useOptimistic` UI State Testing with Pessimistic Rollback Assertions  [community]

React 19's `useOptimistic` hook applies a temporary UI state immediately on user action and rolls it back to the server-confirmed state after the underlying async operation settles. Testing both the optimistic state (intermediate) and the rollback state (final) in a single `it()` block requires intercepting the network request with an artificial delay — without the delay, the server response settles before Cypress can assert on the optimistic state. The `cy.intercept()` delay option (in milliseconds) holds the response in the Cypress proxy for the specified duration, giving the Cypress command chain time to assert the optimistic state before the real response delivers. For rollback testing (server returns an error), reply with a 4xx status; `useOptimistic` will reverse the optimistic update and the original server state should be restored.

```typescript
// cypress/component/todo-item.cy.tsx
import React from 'react';
import { mount } from 'cypress/react';
import { TodoItem } from '../../src/components/TodoItem';

describe('TodoItem with useOptimistic completion', () => {
  it('shows optimistic checked state then confirms with server response', () => {
    cy.intercept('PATCH', '/api/todos/*', (req) => {
      // Delay response by 600ms to allow optimistic assertion
      req.reply({ delay: 600, statusCode: 200, body: { id: '1', completed: true, title: 'Buy milk' } });
    }).as('toggleTodo');

    mount(<TodoItem id="1" title="Buy milk" completed={false} />);

    cy.get('[data-cy="todo-checkbox"]').click();

    // Optimistic state — UI updates immediately before server confirms
    cy.get('[data-cy="todo-checkbox"]').should('be.checked');
    cy.get('[data-cy="todo-title"]').should('have.class', 'line-through');
    cy.get('[data-cy="pending-indicator"]').should('be.visible');

    // Wait for server confirmation — optimistic state persists as server state
    cy.wait('@toggleTodo');
    cy.get('[data-cy="pending-indicator"]').should('not.exist');
    cy.get('[data-cy="todo-checkbox"]').should('be.checked');
  });

  it('rolls back optimistic state when server returns 422 error', () => {
    cy.intercept('PATCH', '/api/todos/*', {
      delay: 400,
      statusCode: 422,
      body: { error: 'Todo is archived and cannot be modified' },
    }).as('failedToggle');

    mount(<TodoItem id="2" title="Archived task" completed={false} />);

    cy.get('[data-cy="todo-checkbox"]').click();

    // Optimistic state briefly shows checked
    cy.get('[data-cy="todo-checkbox"]').should('be.checked');

    cy.wait('@failedToggle');

    // Rollback: checkbox returns to unchecked, error toast appears
    cy.get('[data-cy="todo-checkbox"]').should('not.be.checked');
    cy.get('[data-cy="error-toast"]')
      .should('be.visible')
      .and('contain.text', 'cannot be modified');
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff / When to use:** The `delay` value in `cy.intercept()` must be long enough for the Cypress command chain to execute between the click and the `cy.wait()` — 400–600ms is usually sufficient for local tests, but CI runners under load may need 800–1200ms. Do not use `cy.clock()`/`cy.tick()` to control the delay window here because React 19's `useOptimistic` uses `startTransition` internally, which defers to the real async scheduler rather than synthetic timers. This pattern is most valuable for rollback testing — optimistic-state-only tests can be simpler synchronous component state assertions without network interception. [community]

---

### 425. `cy.intercept()` `delay` Validation and the 2³¹ Silent Truncation Fix (Cypress 15.13.1)  [official]

Cypress 15.13.1 introduced a validation guard on the `delay` option in `cy.intercept()` reply objects — prior versions silently accepted delay values greater than or equal to 2³¹ milliseconds (~24.8 days) because JavaScript's `setTimeout` truncates values exceeding the 32-bit signed integer maximum to 0, causing the response to be delivered immediately rather than delayed. This silent truncation was a source of confusing test behaviour: developers computing delays as `Date.now() + bigOffsetMs` would occasionally produce values that exceeded the 32-bit limit, resulting in zero-delay responses when a multi-second delay was intended. Cypress 15.13.1+ throws a descriptive `CypressError` at intercept registration time if `delay >= 2**31`, making the miscalculation immediately visible. Always compute delays as relative millisecond offsets (e.g., `1500` for 1.5 seconds) rather than absolute timestamps.

```typescript
// cypress/e2e/delay-validation.cy.ts
describe('cy.intercept() delay validation guard (Cypress 15.13.1+)', () => {
  it('demonstrates correct relative delay usage', () => {
    // CORRECT: relative millisecond delay
    cy.intercept('GET', '/api/slow-endpoint', {
      delay: 1500,
      statusCode: 200,
      body: { result: 'ok' },
    }).as('slowRequest');

    cy.visit('/dashboard');
    cy.wait('@slowRequest', { timeout: 5000 });
    cy.get('[data-cy="dashboard-data"]').should('be.visible');
  });

  it('correctly times out spinner when response is slow', () => {
    cy.intercept('GET', '/api/stats', {
      delay: 800,
      statusCode: 200,
      body: { total: 42 },
    }).as('statsRequest');

    cy.visit('/stats');

    // Loading spinner appears during the 800ms delay
    cy.get('[data-cy="loading-spinner"]').should('be.visible');

    cy.wait('@statsRequest');

    // Spinner dismisses after response
    cy.get('[data-cy="loading-spinner"]').should('not.exist');
    cy.get('[data-cy="stats-total"]').should('contain.text', '42');
  });

  // INCORRECT usage that 15.13.1+ now catches at registration time:
  // cy.intercept('GET', '/api/endpoint', {
  //   delay: Date.now() + 2000, // BUG: produces ~1.7 trillion ms value — throws CypressError
  //   body: {},
  // });
});
```

**Tradeoff / When to use:** The 15.13.1 validation fix is a breaking change for any existing intercept that accidentally passed an absolute timestamp as `delay` — those tests now throw at registration rather than silently passing with a zero-delay response. Audit existing specs for patterns like `{ delay: Date.now() + n }` or `{ delay: performance.now() + n }` and replace with plain relative values. The fix does not affect the computed `delay` in `req.reply()` callbacks (where `delay` is a separate method parameter) — only the object shorthand `{ delay: n }` in route handler config objects is validated. [official]
