### 486. `cy.prompt()` Beta — Plain-English Test Steps with Self-Healing Recovery  [official]

`cy.prompt()` graduated to beta in Cypress 15.13.0 and no longer requires an experimental configuration flag. It accepts a plain-English instruction and translates it into one or more Cypress commands, with a self-healing step that retries element lookup using cached selector history when the primary `data-cy` selector is absent. Each `cy.prompt()` call counts against a per-organisation rate limit (600 calls/hour, 100 per minute as of 15.13.0), so it is best reserved for exploratory scaffolding and rapid test authoring, not for locked CI suites.

```typescript
// cypress/e2e/prompt-beta-example.cy.ts
// Requires: Cypress >= 15.13.0, Cypress Cloud project key in cypress.config.ts
describe('Checkout flow (prompt-authored baseline)', () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    cy.session('checkout-user', () => {
      cy.visit('/login');
      cy.get('[data-cy="email"]').type(Cypress.env('TEST_EMAIL'));
      cy.get('[data-cy="password"]').type(Cypress.env('TEST_PASS'));
      cy.get('[data-cy="submit"]').click();
      cy.url().should('include', '/dashboard');
    });
    cy.visit('/shop');
  });

  it('adds item to cart and proceeds to checkout using prompt', () => {
    // cy.prompt() translates English to Cypress commands at runtime via Cloud AI
    cy.prompt('Add the first product to the cart');
    cy.prompt('Click the cart icon to open the cart drawer');
    cy.prompt('Verify the cart contains exactly one item');
    cy.prompt('Click Proceed to Checkout and wait for the checkout page to load');

    // Manual assertion after prompt-driven navigation — avoids AI misidentification risk
    cy.url().should('include', '/checkout');
    cy.get('[data-cy="order-summary"]').should('be.visible');
  });

  it('recovers from selector change via self-healing', () => {
    // When a cached selector no longer matches, prompt retries with AI-suggested alternatives
    // Badge appears in Command Log when self-healing fires
    cy.prompt('Click the Submit Order button');
    cy.get('[data-cy="confirmation-number"]').should('exist');
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff.** `cy.prompt()` is Chromium-only (same CDP requirement as `cy.press()`), cannot run inside `cy.origin()` callbacks, and is unavailable in component testing. Each plain-English step may expand into multiple Cypress commands — a single `cy.prompt()` that triggers five commands still consumes only one quota unit, but a tight loop of `cy.prompt()` calls can silently exhaust the hourly budget mid-CI-run. Always wrap `cy.prompt()` usage in a feature-flag check (`if (Cypress.env('USE_PROMPT') === 'true')`) so CI can disable it when quota is critical. [official]

---

### 487. `cy.press()` Escape Key for Modal and Drawer Dismiss Testing  [official]

`cy.press()` expanded its supported key set in Cypress 15.1.0+ to include the `Escape` key (and other non-printable keys beyond Tab). Pressing Escape with a native event is the correct way to test modal dismissal in modern web frameworks: React portals, Radix UI dialogs, and Headless UI panels all close on a native `keydown` with `key === 'Escape'`, but synthetic `cy.type('{esc}')` does not always trigger the same close handlers because those libraries guard on `e.nativeEvent` or `instanceof KeyboardEvent` checks.

```typescript
// cypress/e2e/modal-dismiss.cy.ts
describe('Dialog dismiss patterns', () => {
  beforeEach(() => cy.visit('/components/dialog-demo'));

  it('dismisses modal via Escape key (native event path)', () => {
    cy.get('[data-cy="open-dialog-btn"]').click();
    cy.get('[role="dialog"]').should('be.visible');

    // Must focus an element inside or the dialog itself before pressing Escape
    cy.get('[role="dialog"]').focus();
    cy.press(Cypress.Keyboard.Keys.ESCAPE);

    cy.get('[role="dialog"]').should('not.exist');
    // Focus should return to the trigger element per ARIA modal spec
    cy.focused().should('have.attr', 'data-cy', 'open-dialog-btn');
  });

  it('keeps modal open when Escape is pressed on an element that stops propagation', () => {
    cy.get('[data-cy="open-dialog-btn"]').click();
    // Tag editor inside the modal calls e.stopPropagation() on Escape
    cy.get('[data-cy="tag-input"]').focus();
    cy.press(Cypress.Keyboard.Keys.ESCAPE);

    // Modal is still visible — inner handler consumed the event
    cy.get('[role="dialog"]').should('be.visible');
  });

  it('closes nested drawer then outer modal in sequence', () => {
    cy.get('[data-cy="open-dialog-btn"]').click();
    cy.get('[data-cy="open-drawer-btn"]').click();
    cy.get('[data-cy="drawer"]').should('be.visible');

    cy.get('[data-cy="drawer"]').focus();
    cy.press(Cypress.Keyboard.Keys.ESCAPE); // close drawer first
    cy.get('[data-cy="drawer"]').should('not.exist');

    cy.get('[role="dialog"]').focus();
    cy.press(Cypress.Keyboard.Keys.ESCAPE); // now close modal
    cy.get('[role="dialog"]').should('not.exist');
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff.** `cy.press()` yields `null` — not the element it targeted — so you cannot chain `.should()` or further commands directly off `cy.press()`. Always follow `cy.press()` with a new `cy.get()` assertion on the expected state. Additionally, `cy.press()` requires that the browser window has focus; in headless CI environments where another window steals focus, native keyboard events may not fire. Add a `cy.window().focus()` call at the top of the test as a guard. [official]

---

### 488. `Cypress.stop()` Conditional Early Exit on Unrecoverable App State  [official]

`Cypress.stop()` (introduced in Cypress 14.2.0) immediately halts the Cypress test run when the application has entered a state from which no further testing is meaningful — for example, a catastrophic auth failure, a feature-flag misconfiguration, or a missing API key that makes every subsequent test a guaranteed fail. Calling `Cypress.stop()` in a `before()` hook short-circuits the entire spec, preventing the noise of 50+ cascading failures from a single root cause.

```typescript
// cypress/e2e/preflight-guard.cy.ts
describe('Application preflight', () => {
  before(() => {
    cy.request({ url: '/api/health', failOnStatusCode: false }).then((resp) => {
      if (resp.status !== 200) {
        Cypress.log({
          name: 'PREFLIGHT FAIL',
          message: `API health check returned ${resp.status} — stopping run`,
          consoleProps: () => ({ body: resp.body }),
        });
        // Stop the run immediately — no further tests will execute
        Cypress.stop();
      }
    });
  });

  it('loads the dashboard', () => {
    cy.visit('/dashboard');
    cy.get('[data-cy="welcome-header"]').should('be.visible');
  });
});

// cypress/e2e/feature-flag-guard.cy.ts
describe('New billing UI (requires BILLING_V2 flag)', () => {
  before(() => {
    cy.request('/api/feature-flags').then((resp) => {
      const flags = resp.body as Record<string, boolean>;
      if (!flags['BILLING_V2']) {
        cy.log('BILLING_V2 flag is off — skipping suite');
        Cypress.stop();
      }
    });
  });

  it('shows new billing dashboard', () => {
    cy.visit('/billing');
    cy.get('[data-cy="billing-v2-header"]').should('be.visible');
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff.** `Cypress.stop()` is a run-level stop — it stops all remaining specs, not just the current spec's remaining tests. If you need to skip only the remaining tests in the current spec while allowing subsequent specs to run, use Mocha's `this.skip()` inside a `before()` hook instead. Also note: `Cypress.stop()` must be called in the top-level synchronous scope of a command callback or inside `cy.then()` — calling it inside a `Promise.then()` that is not part of the Cypress command queue causes it to fire outside the test lifecycle and may not halt execution reliably. [official]

---

### 489. Selector Playground Programmatic Access in Open-Mode Specs  [official]

Cypress 15.8.0 made the Selector Playground available to all users in open mode (previously Cloud-only). The `Cypress.ElementSelector` API (renamed from `Cypress.SelectorPlayground` in 15.0.0) allows registering a custom `onElement` callback that overrides how Cypress generates CSS selectors for elements — useful when your app uses a non-standard data attribute (`data-testid`, `data-qa`, `aria-label`) or when auto-generated selectors are too brittle for recording.

```typescript
// cypress/support/e2e.ts — register ONCE in support file, not per-test
Cypress.ElementSelector.defaults({
  selectorPriority: [
    'data-cy',
    'data-testid',
    'data-qa',
    'aria-label',
    'id',
    'class',
    'tag',
  ],
  onElement($el: JQuery<HTMLElement>): string | undefined {
    // Prefer data-cy > data-testid > aria-label
    const dataCy = $el.attr('data-cy');
    if (dataCy) return `[data-cy="${dataCy.replace(/'/g, "\\'")}"]`;

    const dataTestid = $el.attr('data-testid');
    if (dataTestid) return `[data-testid="${dataTestid.replace(/'/g, "\\'")}"]`;

    const ariaLabel = $el.attr('aria-label');
    if (ariaLabel) return `[aria-label="${ariaLabel.replace(/"/g, '\\"')}"]`;

    // Fall through to default Cypress selector generation
    return undefined;
  },
});

// cypress/e2e/selector-verification.cy.ts
describe('ElementSelector custom strategy', () => {
  it('generates data-cy selectors for all instrumented elements', () => {
    cy.visit('/product-page');

    // Verify that the custom selector strategy is active by checking
    // that Cypress.ElementSelector.getSelector returns the expected format
    cy.get('[data-cy="add-to-cart"]').then(($btn) => {
      const selector = Cypress.ElementSelector.getSelector($btn);
      expect(selector).to.equal('[data-cy="add-to-cart"]');
    });
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff.** The `onElement` callback must return a string that is a valid CSS selector parseable by `document.querySelector` — returning an XPath expression or a plain text description causes `cy.get()` to throw a `DOMException`. When `onElement` returns `undefined`, Cypress falls back to its default selector generation algorithm, so partial custom coverage (only some elements have `data-cy`) is safe and does not break Studio recording for un-instrumented elements. [official]

---

### 490. `cy.session()` `idleTimeout` Combined with `Cypress.expose()` Expiry Sentinel  [community]

`cy.session()` does not natively support time-based cache invalidation — its `validate()` callback is the only hook for deciding whether a cached session is still valid. A community pattern combines `Cypress.expose()` (for non-sensitive public config) with a `localStorage` sentinel written during `setup()` to implement soft idle-timeout expiry: the `validate()` callback checks the sentinel's age against a configurable `SESSION_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS` value exposed via `Cypress.expose()`.

```typescript
// cypress/support/auth.ts
const SESSION_KEY = '__cypress__session_set_at';

export function loginWithIdleTimeout(email: string): void {
  cy.session(
    [email],
    () => {
      // Perform login
      cy.visit('/login');
      cy.get('[data-cy="email"]').type(email);
      cy.get('[data-cy="password"]').type(Cypress.env('PASSWORD'));
      cy.get('[data-cy="submit"]').click();
      cy.url().should('include', '/dashboard');

      // Write the sentinel timestamp to localStorage
      cy.window().then((win) => {
        win.localStorage.setItem(SESSION_KEY, String(Date.now()));
      });
    },
    {
      validate() {
        // Read the idle timeout from Cypress.expose() config (non-sensitive, public)
        // Falls back to 15 minutes if not configured
        const idleMs: number =
          (Cypress as unknown as { config: (k: string) => unknown })
            .config('sessionIdleTimeoutMs') as number ?? 15 * 60 * 1000;

        cy.window().then((win) => {
          const raw = win.localStorage.getItem(SESSION_KEY);
          if (!raw) throw new Error('Session sentinel missing — force re-login');
          const age = Date.now() - Number(raw);
          if (age > idleMs) throw new Error(`Session idle timeout exceeded (${age}ms > ${idleMs}ms)`);
          cy.getCookie('auth_token').should('exist');
        });
      },
      cacheAcrossSpecs: true,
    }
  );
}
```

**Tradeoff.** This pattern adds a `localStorage` write to every login setup, which creates a side effect visible to the application under test. If the app reads and acts on arbitrary `localStorage` keys, verify that `__cypress__session_set_at` does not collide with app data. Use a namespaced key prefixed with `__cypress__` and document it as a test-only artefact. Alternatively, store the sentinel as a Cypress alias (`cy.wrap(Date.now()).as('sessionSetAt')`) if you do not need persistence across spec files. [community]

---

### 491. `cy.intercept()` Typed Generic Request/Response Bodies  [official]

Since Cypress 12.x, `cy.intercept()` has accepted TypeScript generics on the `StaticResponse` and `RouteHandler` overloads, but the community pattern of annotating both `req` and `res` generics on `RouteHandler` callbacks was not widely documented until Cypress 15's TypeScript 6 support made strict template literal types practical. Typing the interceptor body shapes catches mismatches between the stub fixture and the type the component expects, surfacing errors at compile time rather than as runtime assertion failures.

```typescript
// cypress/support/types/api.ts
export interface ProductListResponse {
  data: Array<{ id: string; name: string; price: number; inStock: boolean }>;
  meta: { total: number; page: number; perPage: number };
}

export interface CreateProductRequest {
  name: string;
  price: number;
  categoryId: string;
}

// cypress/e2e/typed-intercept.cy.ts
import type { ProductListResponse, CreateProductRequest } from '../support/types/api';

describe('Product API (typed intercept)', () => {
  it('renders products from typed stub', () => {
    cy.intercept<ProductListResponse>('GET', '/api/products', {
      statusCode: 200,
      body: {
        data: [
          { id: 'p1', name: 'Widget A', price: 9.99, inStock: true },
          { id: 'p2', name: 'Widget B', price: 14.99, inStock: false },
        ],
        meta: { total: 2, page: 1, perPage: 20 },
      },
    }).as('getProducts');

    cy.visit('/products');
    cy.wait('@getProducts');
    cy.get('[data-cy="product-card"]').should('have.length', 2);
  });

  it('captures and validates typed request body on creation', () => {
    cy.intercept<ProductListResponse, CreateProductRequest>(
      'POST',
      '/api/products',
      (req) => {
        // TypeScript knows req.body is CreateProductRequest
        expect(req.body.name).to.be.a('string');
        expect(req.body.price).to.be.greaterThan(0);
        req.reply({ statusCode: 201, body: { data: [], meta: { total: 0, page: 1, perPage: 20 } } });
      }
    ).as('createProduct');

    cy.visit('/products/new');
    cy.get('[data-cy="product-name"]').type('New Widget');
    cy.get('[data-cy="product-price"]').type('19.99');
    cy.get('[data-cy="create-btn"]').click();
    cy.wait('@createProduct');
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff.** TypeScript generic annotations on `cy.intercept()` are compile-time only — they do not validate the actual response body returned by the real server or validate the stub against a JSON Schema at runtime. For runtime contract validation, combine the typed interceptor with a `cy.wait('@alias').then((interception) => { /* zod parse */ })` assertion block using a Zod schema that matches the TypeScript type. [official]

---

### 492. `cy.origin()` Structured-Clone-Safe Args Envelope Pattern  [official]

`cy.origin()` serialises its `args` option via the structured clone algorithm before passing values into the cross-origin frame. Functions, class instances, `Map`, `Set`, `undefined` values inside objects, and non-serialisable DOM references are silently dropped during cloning — a class instance passed as `args` arrives in the callback as a plain object with no prototype methods. The community envelope pattern wraps all `args` in a plain serialisable object, uses only primitives and plain arrays/objects, and reconstructs any complex types inside the callback.

```typescript
// cypress/support/origin-helpers.ts
interface OriginArgs {
  token: string;
  userId: string;
  permissions: string[];
  targetPath: string;
}

export function visitCrossOriginDashboard(args: OriginArgs): void {
  // All values are plain primitives/arrays — safe to structured-clone
  cy.origin(
    Cypress.env('EXTERNAL_APP_URL') as string,
    { args },
    ({ token, userId, permissions, targetPath }: OriginArgs) => {
      // Reconstruct complex types here if needed
      const permissionSet = new Set(permissions); // rebuilt inside the callback

      window.localStorage.setItem('auth_token', token);
      window.localStorage.setItem('user_id', userId);

      cy.visit(targetPath);
      cy.get('[data-cy="user-id"]').should('contain.text', userId);

      // Assert based on permissions array (Set rebuilt locally, not passed via args)
      if (permissionSet.has('admin')) {
        cy.get('[data-cy="admin-panel"]').should('be.visible');
      }
    }
  );
}

// cypress/e2e/cross-origin-flow.cy.ts
import { visitCrossOriginDashboard } from '../support/origin-helpers';

describe('Cross-origin SSO dashboard', () => {
  it('lands on correct path with admin panel for admin user', () => {
    cy.env(['AUTH_TOKEN']).then((token: string) => {
      visitCrossOriginDashboard({
        token,
        userId: 'user-admin-001',
        permissions: ['admin', 'read', 'write'],
        targetPath: '/dashboard',
      });
    });
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff.** The structured-clone constraint means that any change to `OriginArgs` that inadvertently adds a non-serialisable field (e.g., a callback function for error handling) will silently drop that field — no TypeScript error, no Cypress warning. Add a unit-level test (plain Node.js, not Cypress) that asserts `structuredClone(args)` deep-equals `args` for every `OriginArgs` variant used in your test suite. This catches serialisation regressions before they reach CI. [official]

---

### 493. Angular 21 Zoneless Component Testing with `cy.clock()` Timer Control  [official]

Angular 21's zoneless change detection (stable as of Angular 21.0.0) removes Zone.js from the dependency graph entirely. Cypress component testing supports this via `mountZoneless()` (imported from `@cypress/angular/zoneless`), but the familiar `fakeAsync`/`tick()` pattern from `@angular/core/testing` is incompatible with zoneless tests because `fakeAsync` depends on Zone.js's task-tracking patches. The replacement is `cy.clock()` + `cy.tick()` for timer control, combined with `provideExperimentalZonelessChangeDetection()` in the providers array passed to `mountZoneless()`.

```typescript
// src/app/auto-save/auto-save.component.cy.ts
import { mountZoneless } from '@cypress/angular/zoneless';
import { provideExperimentalZonelessChangeDetection } from '@angular/core';
import AutoSaveComponent from './auto-save.component';

describe('AutoSaveComponent (Angular 21 zoneless)', () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    cy.clock(); // freeze real timers BEFORE mounting the component
  });

  it('shows "Saved" indicator after 2000ms debounce', () => {
    mountZoneless(AutoSaveComponent, {
      providers: [
        provideExperimentalZonelessChangeDetection(),
        // Do NOT include NgZone or ZoneScheduler — breaks zoneless mode
      ],
    });

    cy.get('[data-cy="content-editable"]').type('Hello, World');
    cy.get('[data-cy="save-status"]').should('contain.text', 'Unsaved changes');

    // Advance time by 2000ms (debounce period) without Zone.js fakeAsync
    cy.tick(2000);

    // Zoneless: DOM updates via signals/markForCheck — cy.get() retries until updated
    cy.get('[data-cy="save-status"]').should('contain.text', 'Saved');
  });

  it('cancels pending save when component is destroyed', () => {
    const { unmount } = mountZoneless(AutoSaveComponent, {
      providers: [provideExperimentalZonelessChangeDetection()],
    });

    cy.get('[data-cy="content-editable"]').type('Partial change');
    // Unmount before debounce fires — should not throw "component destroyed" error
    cy.then(() => unmount());
    cy.tick(3000); // advance past debounce — no error expected
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff.** `mountZoneless()` is incompatible with any Angular library that injects `NgZone` as a hard dependency (e.g., Angular Material components prior to v21.1, AngularFire pre-v18). Check your dependency tree with `ng-packagr` before migrating component tests to `mountZoneless()`. If a transitive dependency injects `NgZone`, use `mount()` from `@cypress/angular` (standard, zone-full) for those components and reserve `mountZoneless()` for pure signal-based leaf components. [official]

---

### 494. React 19 `useOptimistic()` Mutation Testing with `cy.intercept()` Latency Injection  [community]

React 19's `useOptimistic()` hook updates the UI immediately with an optimistic value and rolls back to the server-confirmed value when the mutation settles. Testing this pattern requires simulating network latency so the optimistic state is visible before the server responds. Combining `cy.intercept()` with a `delay` option (or `req.on('before:response', () => ...)` with a manual `cy.wait()`) creates a controlled window in which the optimistic UI can be asserted.

```typescript
// cypress/e2e/optimistic-like.cy.ts
describe('Post like button (useOptimistic)', () => {
  beforeEach(() => cy.visit('/feed'));

  it('shows optimistic like count immediately, then confirms server value', () => {
    // Intercept the PATCH request with a 1500ms artificial delay
    cy.intercept('PATCH', '/api/posts/*/like', (req) => {
      req.on('before:response', (res) => {
        // Delay the response so the optimistic UI is visible
        res.setDelay(1500);
      });
      req.continue();
    }).as('likePost');

    cy.get('[data-cy="post-like-count"]').first().invoke('text').then((initial) => {
      const initialCount = parseInt(initial, 10);

      cy.get('[data-cy="like-btn"]').first().click();

      // Optimistic update should appear immediately (before server responds)
      cy.get('[data-cy="post-like-count"]').first()
        .should('contain.text', String(initialCount + 1));

      // Wait for server response to confirm (or reveal any rollback)
      cy.wait('@likePost').its('response.statusCode').should('eq', 200);

      // After confirmation, count should remain at +1 (or match server value)
      cy.get('[data-cy="post-like-count"]').first()
        .should('contain.text', String(initialCount + 1));
    });
  });

  it('rolls back optimistic count when server returns 429', () => {
    cy.intercept('PATCH', '/api/posts/*/like', {
      statusCode: 429,
      body: { error: 'Rate limit exceeded' },
      delay: 800,
    }).as('likePostFail');

    cy.get('[data-cy="post-like-count"]').first().invoke('text').then((initial) => {
      const initialCount = parseInt(initial, 10);
      cy.get('[data-cy="like-btn"]').first().click();

      // Optimistic +1 visible during delay
      cy.get('[data-cy="post-like-count"]').first()
        .should('contain.text', String(initialCount + 1));

      cy.wait('@likePostFail');
      // React 19 useOptimistic rolls back to original on error
      cy.get('[data-cy="post-like-count"]').first()
        .should('contain.text', String(initialCount));
    });
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff.** Using `res.setDelay()` inside `req.on('before:response')` injects delay after the server has already processed the request — this is correct for latency simulation but means the delay counts against `cy.wait('@alias')` timeout. If the default `requestTimeout` (5000ms) is close to your injected delay, increase `{ timeout: 10000 }` on `cy.wait('@alias')` to avoid false timeout failures in slow CI environments. [community]

---

### 495. Next.js 16 App Router Parallel Routes Component Testing Setup  [community]

Next.js 16 App Router parallel routes (`@slot` directories) render multiple independent route segments in the same layout. Testing these components in Cypress CT requires providing mock slot content via `cy.mount()` props, because the Next.js App Router's slot-filling mechanism is a server-side concern and is not available in the Vite-based Cypress CT environment. The community pattern is to define a `TestLayout` wrapper that accepts slot content as React children props and mounts it in place of the real App Router layout.

```typescript
// src/app/dashboard/__tests__/dashboard-layout.cy.tsx
import React from 'react';
import DashboardLayout from '../layout';
import { NotificationsPanel } from '../@notifications/page';
import { AnalyticsWidget } from '../@analytics/page';

// TestLayout wraps the real layout with mock slot props
interface TestSlots {
  notifications?: React.ReactNode;
  analytics?: React.ReactNode;
}

function TestLayout({ notifications, analytics }: TestSlots) {
  return (
    <DashboardLayout
      notifications={notifications ?? <div data-cy="mock-notifications">No notifications</div>}
      analytics={analytics ?? <div data-cy="mock-analytics">No analytics</div>}
    >
      <div data-cy="main-content">Dashboard content</div>
    </DashboardLayout>
  );
}

describe('DashboardLayout parallel slots', () => {
  it('renders real notifications slot', () => {
    cy.mount(
      <TestLayout
        notifications={<NotificationsPanel initialCount={3} />}
      />
    );
    cy.get('[data-cy="notification-badge"]').should('contain.text', '3');
    cy.get('[data-cy="mock-analytics"]').should('exist'); // fallback slot
  });

  it('renders real analytics slot alongside notifications', () => {
    cy.mount(
      <TestLayout
        notifications={<NotificationsPanel initialCount={0} />}
        analytics={<AnalyticsWidget metric="dau" />}
      />
    );
    cy.get('[data-cy="analytics-chart"]').should('be.visible');
  });

  it('shows both fallbacks when no slots provided', () => {
    cy.mount(<TestLayout />);
    cy.get('[data-cy="mock-notifications"]').should('exist');
    cy.get('[data-cy="mock-analytics"]').should('exist');
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff.** This pattern tests the layout component's slot composition logic but not the App Router's actual slot-filling wiring (which happens on the server). Integration-level parallel route behaviour (default.tsx fallback selection, partial rendering, loading.tsx states) requires an E2E test against the running Next.js dev server, not a component test. Reserve this CT approach for UI composition and slot interaction tests; use `cy.visit()` E2E tests for routing-level slot behaviour. [community]

---

### 496. `cy.task()` `satisfies` Constraint for `setupNodeEvents` Registration Sync  [community]

The `TaskMap` typed override pattern (pattern 484) ensures call-site type safety, but the `setupNodeEvents` plugin side can still register tasks that are absent from `TaskMap`, or vice versa, without a compile-time error. A `satisfies` constraint applied to the tasks registration object in `setupNodeEvents` ensures that every key in `TaskMap` has a corresponding implementation, catching omissions at build time in the Cypress config file.

```typescript
// cypress.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from 'cypress';
import type { TaskMap } from './cypress/support/task-map';

// Implementation type: a record of handlers matching the TaskMap signature
type TaskImplementations = {
  [K in keyof TaskMap]: (
    arg: TaskMap[K]['arg']
  ) => TaskMap[K]['result'] | Promise<TaskMap[K]['result']>;
};

export default defineConfig({
  e2e: {
    setupNodeEvents(on) {
      // The `satisfies` constraint ensures every TaskMap key is implemented here
      const tasks = {
        'db:seed': async ({ scenario }: { scenario: string }) => {
          await import('./cypress/tasks/db-seed').then((m) => m.seed(scenario));
        },
        'db:reset': async () => {
          await import('./cypress/tasks/db-reset').then((m) => m.reset());
        },
        'db:query': async ({ sql, params }: { sql: string; params?: unknown[] }) => {
          return import('./cypress/tasks/db-query').then((m) => m.query(sql, params));
        },
        'file:read': ({ path }: { path: string }) => {
          return require('fs').readFileSync(path, 'utf8') as string;
        },
        'mail:getLastEmail': async ({ to }: { to: string }) => {
          return import('./cypress/tasks/mail').then((m) => m.getLastEmail(to));
        },
      } satisfies TaskImplementations; // compile error if any TaskMap key is missing

      on('task', tasks);
    },
  },
});
```

**Tradeoff.** The `satisfies` constraint only works if `TaskMap` is imported into `cypress.config.ts`, which means the config file now has a compile-time dependency on a type declared in `cypress/support/`. This is fine for most setups but can cause circular module issues if `cypress.config.ts` is imported by any file under `cypress/support/` (e.g., if the support file imports `baseUrl` from the config). Keep `task-map.d.ts` as a pure type file with no runtime imports to avoid circular dependency issues. [community]

---

### 497. `cy.clock()` + `cy.tick()` with `performance.now()` Stub Workaround  [community]

`cy.clock()` freezes `Date`, `setTimeout`, `setInterval`, and `clearTimeout`, but it does not patch `performance.now()` — this is a known limitation. Libraries that use `performance.now()` for animation timing (GSAP, Framer Motion, CSS-in-JS animation libraries) or for debounce implementations will continue to see real elapsed time even when `cy.clock()` is active. The community workaround stubs `window.performance.now` via `cy.stub()` before mounting or visiting, yielding a deterministic monotonic counter.

```typescript
// cypress/support/clock-helpers.ts
/**
 * Replaces performance.now() with a deterministic counter that advances
 * by `stepMs` on every call. Use alongside cy.clock() for full time control.
 */
export function stubPerformanceNow(stepMs = 16): void {
  let counter = 0;
  cy.window().then((win) => {
    cy.stub(win.performance, 'now').callsFake(() => {
      counter += stepMs;
      return counter;
    });
  });
}

// cypress/e2e/animation-timer.cy.ts
import { stubPerformanceNow } from '../support/clock-helpers';

describe('Animated counter (uses performance.now for easing)', () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    cy.clock();              // freeze Date + setTimeout
    stubPerformanceNow(16);  // stub performance.now to advance 16ms per call (~60fps)
  });

  it('completes count-up animation to target value', () => {
    cy.visit('/animated-counter?target=1000&duration=2000');

    // Advance fake clock by animation duration
    cy.tick(2000);

    // After tick, the animation easing loop (requestAnimationFrame-driven) should complete
    cy.get('[data-cy="counter-display"]').should('contain.text', '1,000');
  });

  it('pauses animation correctly on visibility change', () => {
    cy.visit('/animated-counter?target=500&duration=3000');
    cy.tick(1000); // halfway through animation
    cy.get('[data-cy="counter-display"]').invoke('text').then((midText) => {
      const midValue = parseInt(midText.replace(',', ''), 10);
      expect(midValue).to.be.within(100, 400); // roughly midway
    });
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff.** Stubbing `performance.now()` with a fixed-step counter changes the semantics from a monotonic wall-clock value to a call-count-based counter. Code that computes rate (e.g., frames per second) by dividing a delta by elapsed time will produce incorrect results. This workaround is appropriate for testing time-gated UI state (animation complete / not complete) but not for testing precise timing measurements. For requestAnimationFrame-driven animations, also stub `requestAnimationFrame` to call the callback synchronously. [community]

---

### 498. `cy.intercept()` `Content-Length: 0` Empty-Response Proxy Fix (Cypress 15.15.0)  [official]

Cypress 15.15.0 fixed a proxy bug where responses with `Content-Length: 0` and no body (common in `204 No Content` and some `200 OK` REST API responses) were mangled by the Cypress proxy, causing the body to appear as an empty string that failed JSON parse attempts in `cy.wait()` assertions. Before this fix, tests asserting `.its('response.body').should('be.null')` on 204 responses would fail because the proxy inserted an empty-string body.

```typescript
// cypress/e2e/delete-flow.cy.ts
describe('Resource deletion (204 No Content)', () => {
  it('handles 204 response correctly after Cypress 15.15.0 fix', () => {
    // Stub a real-world 204 No Content response
    cy.intercept('DELETE', '/api/resources/*', {
      statusCode: 204,
      // No body property — correct 204 shape
    }).as('deleteResource');

    cy.visit('/resources');
    cy.get('[data-cy="resource-item"]').first().find('[data-cy="delete-btn"]').click();
    cy.get('[data-cy="confirm-delete"]').click();

    cy.wait('@deleteResource').then((interception) => {
      expect(interception.response?.statusCode).to.equal(204);
      // In Cypress 15.15.0+, body is null/undefined for Content-Length:0 responses
      // In Cypress < 15.15.0, this assertion may fail with body === ''
      expect(interception.response?.body).to.be.oneOf([null, undefined, '']);
    });

    cy.get('[data-cy="resource-item"]').should('have.length', 0);
  });

  it('passes through real 204 responses without proxy corruption', () => {
    // For real (non-stubbed) DELETE endpoints returning 204:
    // cy.intercept passthrough still works; body corruption is fixed in 15.15.0
    cy.intercept('DELETE', '/api/resources/*').as('realDelete');
    cy.visit('/resources');
    cy.get('[data-cy="delete-btn"]').first().click();
    cy.get('[data-cy="confirm-delete"]').click();

    cy.wait('@realDelete').its('response.statusCode').should('eq', 204);
    cy.get('[data-cy="success-toast"]').should('contain.text', 'Deleted successfully');
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff.** If your CI pipeline pins Cypress below 15.15.0, add a `.should('be.oneOf', [null, undefined, ''])` assertion for 204 body checks rather than strict `.should('be.null')` to keep tests passing across versions during upgrade windows. After upgrading to 15.15.0+, tighten the assertion to `.should('be.oneOf', [null, undefined])`. The fix applies to both stubbed and pass-through intercepted responses. [official]

---

### 499. `cy.env()` Async Destructuring Inside `cy.origin()` Scoped Args  [official]

`cy.env()` (the async command-queue variant, Cypress 15.10.0+) cannot be called inside a `cy.origin()` callback because `cy.origin()` runs in a separate browsing context that does not have access to the parent frame's command registry. The pattern for passing secrets into cross-origin callbacks is to resolve all `cy.env()` calls before the `cy.origin()` call, bundle the resolved values into the structured-clone-safe `args` envelope, and reference them by name inside the callback.

```typescript
// cypress/e2e/cross-origin-secrets.cy.ts
describe('OAuth provider login (cross-origin)', () => {
  it('authenticates via external IdP using cy.env() resolved before cy.origin()', () => {
    // Step 1: resolve all secrets BEFORE entering cy.origin()
    // cy.env() returns a Cypress.Chainable — use .then() to extract values
    cy.env(['OAUTH_CLIENT_ID', 'OAUTH_TEST_USER', 'OAUTH_TEST_PASS']).then(
      ([clientId, username, password]: [string, string, string]) => {
        // Step 2: initiate the OAuth flow on the primary origin
        cy.visit(`/auth/login?client_id=${clientId}`);
        cy.get('[data-cy="oauth-login-btn"]').click();

        // Step 3: pass resolved secrets via args into cy.origin()
        cy.origin(
          Cypress.env('OAUTH_PROVIDER_URL') as string,
          { args: { username, password } }, // structured-clone safe: plain strings
          ({ username: user, password: pass }: { username: string; password: string }) => {
            cy.get('[name="username"]').type(user);
            // {log: false} prevents the password from appearing in Command Log
            cy.get('[name="password"]').type(pass, { log: false });
            cy.get('[type="submit"]').click();
          }
        );

        // Back on primary origin after redirect
        cy.url().should('include', '/dashboard');
        cy.get('[data-cy="user-greeting"]').should('contain.text', username);
      }
    );
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff.** Resolving `cy.env()` values before `cy.origin()` means the secrets are held in JavaScript closure variables inside the `.then()` callback. These values are visible in browser memory and in Cypress's command log if not guarded — always pass `{ log: false }` to `cy.type()` for password fields, and consider wrapping the entire `cy.origin()` block inside `Cypress.log({ name: 'cross-origin-auth', message: '***' })` to replace the default log entry with a redacted one. [official]

---

### 500. Cypress Cloud `autoCancelAfterFailures` with Module API Exit-Code Guard  [official]

Cypress Cloud Smart Orchestration's `autoCancelAfterFailures` setting (Cypress 15.x+) cancels all in-progress CI machines when a configurable number of test failures is reached, preventing wasted compute on a known-failing run. When using the Cypress Module API (programmatic runner via `require('cypress')`) in a custom CI script, the run returns a `CypressRunResult` object whose `status` field may be `'cancelled'` (not just `'failed'`), and `totalFailed` may be `0` if the cancellation happened before failures accumulated on the current machine. Failing to handle `'cancelled'` status causes CI scripts to report success for a cancelled run.

```typescript
// scripts/run-cypress.ts
import cypress from 'cypress';
import * as process from 'process';

async function runTests(): Promise<void> {
  const result = await cypress.run({
    spec: 'cypress/e2e/**/*.cy.ts',
    reporter: 'junit',
    reporterOptions: {
      mochaFile: 'test-results/cypress-[hash].xml',
    },
  });

  if (result.status === 'failed' && 'failures' in result) {
    // Module API launch failure (config error, browser not found, etc.)
    console.error('Cypress run launch failure:', result.message);
    process.exit(1);
  }

  if (result.status === 'finished') {
    const { totalFailed, totalPending, runs } = result;

    // Check for autoCancelAfterFailures cancellation — any run with skipped specs
    const wasCancelled = runs.some((run) => run.skippedSpec === true);

    if (wasCancelled) {
      console.error('Run cancelled by Smart Orchestration autoCancelAfterFailures');
      process.exit(1); // treat cancellation as failure in CI
    }

    if (totalFailed > 0) {
      console.error(`${totalFailed} test(s) failed`);
      process.exit(1);
    }

    console.log(`All tests passed (${totalPending} pending)`);
    process.exit(0);
  }
}

runTests().catch((err) => {
  console.error('Unexpected error:', err);
  process.exit(1);
});
```

**Tradeoff.** The `skippedSpec` field on individual run objects indicates specs that were skipped due to cancellation — this is the most reliable signal for auto-cancel detection since `totalFailed` may be `0` on a machine that was cancelled before it ran any failing tests. Note that `result.exitCode` was renamed from `result.code` in Cypress 15.0.0 (breaking change from the `result.code` pattern in Cypress 14.x) — always use `result.exitCode` in 15.x+ Module API scripts. [official]

---

## Community Gotchas — Cycle 49

331. **`cy.prompt()` consumes rate-limit quota even when it self-heals a single-step interaction, and in parallel CI setups each worker machine draws from a shared organisational pool — a suite of 20 tests each calling `cy.prompt()` 5 times can exhaust the 100-calls-per-minute limit mid-run, causing all subsequent `cy.prompt()` calls to fail with a `429 Rate Limit Exceeded` error that surfaces as a generic Cypress command failure with no quota-context in the error message** [community] — A QA team migrates exploratory test steps to `cy.prompt()` without auditing call frequency. In a 4-machine parallel CI run, all 4 workers hit `cy.prompt()` simultaneously during the same test batch, collectively issuing up to 80 calls/minute against the 100/minute limit. After the first few parallel runs succeed, later batches in the same CI trigger hit the limit and fail silently. WHY: Cypress Cloud rate-limits `cy.prompt()` per organisation per minute (100) and per hour (600) at the API gateway level — individual machine workers are not aware of other workers' quota consumption, so the aggregate call rate from all parallel workers is what triggers throttling, not the per-machine rate. Fix: gate all `cy.prompt()` calls behind `if (Cypress.env('ENABLE_AI_STEPS') === 'true')` and enable the flag only on a single designated worker; use explicit Cypress commands for locked CI suites.

332. **`cy.press(Cypress.Keyboard.Keys.ESCAPE)` silently no-ops when no element in the document has focus — the native Escape event is dispatched to `document.body`, but modal close handlers typically listen on the focused element or the modal container, not on `document.body`, so the modal remains open and the test fails the subsequent `should('not.exist')` assertion with no indication that the keypress was dropped** [community] — A developer writes a modal-dismiss test that clicks a button to open the modal, then immediately calls `cy.press(ESCAPE)` without first focusing the modal or an element inside it. The button's `click()` handler opens the modal but does not automatically transfer focus into the modal (a common ARIA pattern failure), leaving focus on `document.body`. The Escape event fires on `document.body` where no close handler is registered. WHY: `cy.press()` dispatches to `document.activeElement` — when no element is explicitly focused, `document.activeElement` is `document.body`, which does not have the modal's Escape key listener attached to it. Fix: always call `cy.get('[role="dialog"]').focus()` immediately before `cy.press(ESCAPE)` to ensure the event targets an element inside the modal.

333. **`Cypress.stop()` called inside a `cy.then()` callback that is itself nested inside a native `Promise.then()` (i.e., outside the Cypress command queue) executes asynchronously after the current test has already advanced, causing the stop signal to arrive too late — the run does not halt until after the current test completes, potentially executing several more commands before stopping** [community] — A developer writes a preflight check that calls a third-party async function, chains a native `Promise.then()` off the result for convenience, and calls `Cypress.stop()` inside the native Promise resolution. Cypress does not receive the stop signal until the native Promise resolves outside the command queue ordering guarantees. By the time the signal is processed, additional commands have already been enqueued and executed. WHY: `Cypress.stop()` only guarantees immediate halting when called synchronously inside a Cypress command callback — calling it inside a native `Promise.then()` that runs outside the Cypress event loop causes non-deterministic timing. Fix: wrap the async operation in `cy.wrap(Promise.resolve(thirdPartyCall()))` to bring it back into the Cypress command queue, then call `Cypress.stop()` inside the `.then()` callback of the wrapped promise.

334. **`cy.intercept()` routes registered on the primary origin are completely invisible inside `cy.origin()` callbacks — a developer who stubs `/api/users` before entering `cy.origin()` is surprised to find that `cy.wait('@getUsers')` inside the callback never resolves, because the cross-origin browsing context has its own isolated network layer and does not inherit intercept registrations from the parent frame** [community] — An OAuth test stubs the user profile endpoint before entering the cross-origin IdP callback, expecting the stub to be active when the IdP redirects back. However, within the `cy.origin()` callback the redirect back to the primary origin triggers a real network request that bypasses the stub, because `cy.intercept()` registrations are scoped to the browsing context in which they were created. WHY: Cypress implements `cy.intercept()` via a proxy scoped to the Cypress spec-bridge iframe's origin — the `cy.origin()` callback runs in a separate iframe with a different origin, which uses a different proxy scope and does not inherit the parent frame's intercept registrations. Fix: re-register any required `cy.intercept()` stubs inside the `cy.origin()` callback for cross-origin network stubbing; after the callback completes and navigation returns to the primary origin, primary-origin stubs become active again.

335. **`cy.clock()` does not patch `performance.now()`, causing animation libraries that use `performance.now()` for frame timing (GSAP, Framer Motion, CSS transition polyfills) to continue advancing in real time even when `cy.clock()` is active — a test that calls `cy.tick(2000)` to simulate a 2-second animation completion may assert the "animation done" state too early if the library checks `performance.now() - startTime < duration` and the real elapsed time since `cy.visit()` is less than the animation duration** [community] — A developer writes a test for a 2000ms GSAP counter animation, calls `cy.clock()` and `cy.tick(2000)`, and asserts that the final value is displayed. The assertion fails intermittently: when CI runs are slow and test setup takes more than 2 seconds, real elapsed `performance.now()` time exceeds the animation duration independently of `cy.tick()`, causing the animation to finish before `cy.tick()` fires (test passes). When CI is fast, setup takes less than 2 seconds, `performance.now()` has not yet reached the animation duration, and the animation is still in progress when the assertion fires (test fails). WHY: `cy.clock()` was designed to control `Date.now()`, `setTimeout`, and `setInterval` — `performance.now()` was not included because it is a high-resolution monotonic clock used for performance measurement, and patching it globally would break the Cypress runner's own internal timing. Fix: use `cy.stub(win.performance, 'now')` as shown in pattern 497 to provide deterministic values alongside `cy.clock()`.
