## Key Resources — Cycle 53

| Pattern | Resource | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| GraphQL per-request dynamic alias via `req.alias` | https://docs.cypress.io/api/commands/intercept | Set `req.alias` inside handler for per-operation `cy.wait()` on shared POST endpoints |
| `req.continue(res =>)` conditional response override | https://docs.cypress.io/api/commands/intercept | Hits real server then lets you mutate; use `req.reply()` for pure stubs |
| `Cache-Control: no-store` middleware intercept | https://docs.cypress.io/app/guides/network-requests | `middleware: true` runs first; inject no-store header to force cache bypass globally |
| Route matching reverse order + `middleware: true` priority | https://docs.cypress.io/api/commands/intercept | Last-registered wins; middleware always runs first regardless of order |
| `cy.request<T>()` typed GraphQL seed helper | https://docs.cypress.io/api/commands/request | Generic type parameter for response body; use `.its('body')` to get typed data |
| `.should(callback)` retry-able multi-property assertion | https://docs.cypress.io/app/core-concepts/retry-ability | Entire callback retries; only synchronous `expect()` inside — no `cy` commands |
| `cy.clock()` must precede `cy.visit()` for init-time timers | https://docs.cypress.io/api/commands/clock | Init-time `setTimeout`/`setInterval` only controlled if clock installed before navigation |
| `cy.task()` typed registry + `null` return enforcement | https://docs.cypress.io/api/commands/task | Return `null` not `undefined`; every code path must return an explicit non-undefined value |
| `cy.session()` parallel CI cache isolation | https://docs.cypress.io/api/commands/session | `cacheAcrossSpecs: true` scoped per-machine in Cloud parallel runs; not cross-machine |
| Next.js Server Components unsupported in Component Testing | https://docs.cypress.io/app/component-testing/react/overview | Only Client Components (`'use client'`) mountable in CT; use E2E for pages with RSC |
| `Cypress.Commands.overwrite('visit')` with opt-out flag | https://docs.cypress.io/api/cypress-api/custom-commands | Add `skipInstrumentation?: boolean` to `VisitOptions` to opt out inside `cy.session()` |
| `cy.intercept()` browser cache bypass via `--disable-cache` | https://docs.cypress.io/app/core-concepts/best-practices | `before:browser:launch` args + middleware both valid; prefer scoped middleware for surgical control |
| `cy.fixture(file, null)` for binary `ArrayBuffer` | https://docs.cypress.io/api/commands/fixture | `null` encoding returns `ArrayBuffer` in Cypress 14+; use `Cypress.Buffer.from()` for `selectFile` |
| `cy.get(selector, { timeout })` per-command timeout override | https://docs.cypress.io/api/commands/get | Timeout propagates to chained `.should()` retry loop; does NOT propagate to `.then(fn)` |
| `cy.stub()` typed Sinon stubs in Component Testing | https://docs.cypress.io/api/commands/stub | `.as('name')` for command log visibility; reset stub between `cy.mount()` calls in same test |

## Cycle 54 — 2026-05-14

### New Patterns

**Pattern 549: `cy.intercept()` RouteMatcher `times` Option for Single-Use Stubs** [official]
Use the `times` field in a RouteMatcher to make an intercept match exactly N requests and then become inactive. This prevents a stub meant for the first page load from accidentally intercepting subsequent requests (e.g., pagination, polling) with stale fixture data.

```typescript
describe('product list — initial load only stubbed', () => {
  it('stubs only the first GET /api/products then lets real data through', () => {
    cy.intercept(
      { method: 'GET', url: '/api/products', times: 1 },
      { fixture: 'products-page-1.json' }
    ).as('firstLoad');

    cy.intercept(
      { method: 'GET', url: '/api/products?page=2', times: 1 },
      { fixture: 'products-page-2.json' }
    ).as('secondLoad');

    cy.visit('/products');
    cy.wait('@firstLoad');

    cy.get('[data-cy="load-more-btn"]').click();
    cy.wait('@secondLoad');

    // third request hits the real server — no stale fixture
    cy.get('[data-cy="load-more-btn"]').click();
    cy.get('[data-cy="product-item"]').should('have.length.greaterThan', 20);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `times: 1` silently deregisters after matching — if the same URL fires again unexpectedly (e.g., a retry on error), the real network is hit. Combine with a spy intercept (no `times`, no stub) to assert no extra calls were made, or set `times` higher than expected and verify the alias call count post-test.

---

**Pattern 550: `req.continue()` for Selective Response Mutation Without Full Stubbing** [official]
Use `req.continue(res => { ... })` to let requests reach the real server and then selectively mutate fields in the response body. This validates real API shape while overriding specific values that are hard to control (e.g., expiry timestamps, feature-flag overrides, environment-specific URLs).

```typescript
describe('subscription banner — near-expiry state', () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    cy.intercept('GET', '/api/account', (req) => {
      req.continue((res) => {
        // Real server returns the full account object; we only patch expiry
        res.body = {
          ...res.body,
          subscription: {
            ...res.body.subscription,
            expiresAt: new Date(Date.now() + 2 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000).toISOString(),
            status: 'active',
          },
        };
      });
    }).as('accountNearExpiry');
  });

  it('shows the renewal banner when subscription expires within 3 days', () => {
    cy.visit('/dashboard');
    cy.wait('@accountNearExpiry');
    cy.get('[data-cy="renewal-banner"]').should('be.visible');
    cy.get('[data-cy="renewal-banner"]').should('contain.text', 'renew');
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `req.continue()` adds latency because the request still travels to the server. If the test environment is flaky or offline, these tests fail for non-test reasons. Use `req.reply()` (pure stub) for fully isolated CI; reserve `req.continue()` for integration-tier tests where contract validation is worth the network cost.

---

**Pattern 551: `cy.session()` with `validate()` for Token-Expiry-Aware Caching** [official]
Provide a `validate` function to `cy.session()` that checks whether cached credentials are still usable. This lets the session auto-recreate when a short-lived JWT expires mid-suite rather than silently proceeding with a 401-producing session.

```typescript
function loginAsAdmin() {
  cy.session(
    ['admin', Cypress.env('ADMIN_EMAIL')],
    () => {
      cy.visit('/login');
      cy.get('[data-cy="email"]').type(Cypress.env('ADMIN_EMAIL'));
      cy.get('[data-cy="password"]').type(Cypress.env('ADMIN_PASSWORD'));
      cy.get('[data-cy="submit"]').click();
      cy.url().should('include', '/dashboard');
      // Assert the token landed in storage before caching
      cy.window().its('localStorage').invoke('getItem', 'auth_token')
        .should('be.a', 'string');
    },
    {
      cacheAcrossSpecs: true,
      validate() {
        // Restore page context; check API is reachable with cached credentials
        cy.request({
          url: '/api/me',
          failOnStatusCode: false,
        }).its('status').should('eq', 200);
      },
    }
  );
}

export { loginAsAdmin };
```
Tradeoff: The `validate` callback fires on every session restore, adding one `cy.request()` round-trip per spec file in CI. For suites with dozens of spec files and expensive auth endpoints this can add seconds to total run time. Mitigate by caching the last-validated timestamp in a `cy.task()` and skipping the network ping if it was validated within N minutes.

---

**Pattern 552: `cy.origin()` for Cross-Origin OAuth Flows Without Disabling Security** [official]
Use `cy.origin()` to interact with a third-party identity provider page during OAuth without setting `chromeWebSecurity: false`. `cy.origin()` runs Cypress commands in the foreign origin's browsing context while keeping security policies intact.

```typescript
describe('SSO login flow', () => {
  it('authenticates via corporate identity provider', () => {
    cy.visit('/login');
    cy.get('[data-cy="sso-btn"]').click();

    cy.origin('https://sso.corp.example.com', () => {
      cy.get('[name="username"]').type(Cypress.env('SSO_USER'));
      cy.get('[name="password"]').type(Cypress.env('SSO_PASSWORD'));
      cy.get('[type="submit"]').click();
    });

    // Back in primary origin after redirect
    cy.url().should('include', '/dashboard');
    cy.get('[data-cy="user-menu"]').should('contain.text', Cypress.env('SSO_USER'));
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `cy.origin()` requires the secondary origin to be listed in the `experimentalOriginDependencies` config (Cypress < 12) or configured properly in `cy.origin()`'s allowed list. Variables and functions passed into the callback must be JSON-serialisable — closures over non-serialisable objects (class instances, DOM refs) cause silent failures or serialisation errors.

---

**Pattern 553: `cy.clock()` + `cy.tick()` for Throttle-Free Timer Testing** [official]
Install a fake clock before navigation with `cy.clock()` and advance time programmatically with `cy.tick()`. This removes the need for `cy.wait(milliseconds)` in tests that trigger debounced inputs, polling intervals, session timeouts, or toast auto-dismiss.

```typescript
describe('session timeout warning', () => {
  it('shows idle warning dialog after 25 minutes of inactivity', () => {
    cy.clock();
    cy.visit('/app');
    cy.loginAsAdmin();

    // Advance 25 minutes without waiting in real time
    cy.tick(25 * 60 * 1000);

    cy.get('[data-cy="idle-warning-dialog"]').should('be.visible');
    cy.get('[data-cy="idle-warning-dialog"]')
      .should('contain.text', 'You will be logged out in 5 minutes');

    // Advance remaining 5 minutes to trigger auto-logout
    cy.tick(5 * 60 * 1000);
    cy.url().should('include', '/login');
    cy.get('[data-cy="session-expired-banner"]').should('be.visible');
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `cy.clock()` must be called before `cy.visit()` to intercept timers created during page initialisation. Calling it after navigation means timers set in module-level code or framework bootstrapping are uncontrolled. Additionally, `cy.clock()` freezes `Date.now()` — any component that formats "current time" for display will show a frozen timestamp, which may cause unexpected snapshot test failures.

---

**Pattern 554: `cy.request()` for API Seeding and Teardown Outside the Browser** [official]
Use `cy.request()` in `before`/`beforeEach`/`afterEach` hooks to seed test data via your API rather than through the UI or database task. This keeps seed logic in the same language as the test and avoids the overhead of `cy.task()` for simple REST calls.

```typescript
describe('order management', () => {
  let orderId: string;

  beforeEach(() => {
    // Seed: create a pending order via API
    cy.request<{ id: string }>({
      method: 'POST',
      url: `${Cypress.env('API_BASE')}/orders`,
      headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${Cypress.env('SEED_TOKEN')}` },
      body: { productId: 'prod_001', quantity: 2, customerId: 'cust_test_1' },
    }).then(({ body }) => {
      orderId = body.id;
    });
  });

  afterEach(() => {
    // Teardown: delete the order regardless of test outcome
    if (orderId) {
      cy.request({
        method: 'DELETE',
        url: `${Cypress.env('API_BASE')}/orders/${orderId}`,
        headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${Cypress.env('SEED_TOKEN')}` },
        failOnStatusCode: false, // 404 is fine if test already deleted it
      });
    }
  });

  it('can cancel a pending order', () => {
    cy.visit(`/orders/${orderId}`);
    cy.get('[data-cy="cancel-btn"]').click();
    cy.get('[data-cy="order-status"]').should('contain.text', 'Cancelled');
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `cy.request()` shares the browser's cookie jar, so authenticated requests work automatically after `cy.session()` login. However, if your seed endpoint requires a service-level token (not a user token), you must pass it explicitly via the `headers` option — this token must never be hardcoded and should come from `Cypress.env()`.

---

**Pattern 555: `Cypress.Commands.add()` with TypeScript Declaration Merging for Type-Safe Custom Commands** [official]
Extend the `cy` namespace via declaration merging in a `cypress.d.ts` file to get full IntelliSense and compile-time checking on custom commands. This prevents `cy.loginAs is not a function` runtime errors from missing `import` statements.

```typescript
// cypress/support/commands.ts
Cypress.Commands.add('loginAs', (role: 'admin' | 'viewer' | 'editor') => {
  const credentials = {
    admin: { email: Cypress.env('ADMIN_EMAIL'), password: Cypress.env('ADMIN_PASS') },
    viewer: { email: Cypress.env('VIEWER_EMAIL'), password: Cypress.env('VIEWER_PASS') },
    editor: { email: Cypress.env('EDITOR_EMAIL'), password: Cypress.env('EDITOR_PASS') },
  };
  const { email, password } = credentials[role];
  cy.session([role, email], () => {
    cy.visit('/login');
    cy.get('[data-cy="email"]').type(email);
    cy.get('[data-cy="password"]').type(password);
    cy.get('[data-cy="submit"]').click();
    cy.url().should('not.include', '/login');
  }, { cacheAcrossSpecs: true });
});

// cypress/support/cypress.d.ts
declare namespace Cypress {
  interface Chainable {
    loginAs(role: 'admin' | 'viewer' | 'editor'): Chainable<void>;
  }
}
```
Tradeoff: Declaration merging requires that `cypress.d.ts` is included in the TypeScript compilation scope (`tsconfig.json` `include` or `files` array). If it is not included, the custom command types are silently ignored and TypeScript falls back to `any`, defeating the purpose. Use `tsc --noEmit` in CI to verify types are resolved correctly.

---

**Pattern 556: `Cypress.Commands.overwrite('type')` with `sensitive` Option to Mask Secrets in Command Log** [official]
Overwrite the built-in `cy.type()` to support a `sensitive: true` option that replaces the logged text with asterisks. This prevents passwords and API keys from appearing in Cypress Cloud screenshots, video recordings, and CI logs.

```typescript
// cypress/support/commands.ts
declare global {
  namespace Cypress {
    interface TypeOptions {
      sensitive?: boolean;
    }
  }
}

Cypress.Commands.overwrite(
  'type',
  (originalFn, element, text: string, options?: Cypress.TypeOptions) => {
    if (options?.sensitive) {
      // Suppress default log
      const maskedOptions = { ...options, log: false };
      Cypress.log({
        $el: element as JQuery,
        name: 'type',
        message: '*'.repeat(text.length),
      });
      return originalFn(element, text, maskedOptions);
    }
    return originalFn(element, text, options);
  }
);

// Usage in tests
cy.get('[data-cy="password"]').type(Cypress.env('USER_PASSWORD'), { sensitive: true });
cy.get('[data-cy="api-key"]').type(Cypress.env('API_KEY'), { sensitive: true });
```
Tradeoff: The `Cypress.log()` call fires synchronously outside Cypress's command queue, so the log entry may appear slightly out of order in the Command Log panel relative to async assertions. This is a cosmetic issue only and does not affect test reliability. The overwrite also applies globally — verify that third-party plugins that call `.type()` internally are not broken by the modified signature.

---

**Pattern 557: `.should(callback)` for Retry-able Multi-Property Assertions Without `.then()`** [official]
Pass a callback to `.should()` to assert multiple properties of an element atomically. The entire callback — including the element re-query — retries until all expectations pass, unlike `.then()` which executes once without retry.

```typescript
describe('search results', () => {
  it('shows correct result count and first result title after debounce', () => {
    cy.intercept('GET', '/api/search*').as('searchReq');
    cy.visit('/search');

    cy.get('[data-cy="search-input"]').type('cypress testing');
    cy.wait('@searchReq');

    cy.get('[data-cy="results-summary"]').should(($el) => {
      // All expect() calls inside here retry together
      expect($el).to.have.text.that.matches(/\d+ results/);
      expect($el.text()).to.not.include('0 results');
    });

    cy.get('[data-cy="result-item"]').first().should(($item) => {
      expect($item).to.be.visible;
      expect($item.find('[data-cy="result-title"]').text()).to.include('Cypress');
      expect($item.attr('data-result-index')).to.eq('0');
    });
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: Inside a `.should(callback)`, you must use synchronous Chai `expect()` assertions only — Cypress commands (`cy.get()`, `cy.click()`, etc.) inside the callback will throw `"cy commands cannot be invoked inside a should callback"`. Use `.then()` when you need to chain Cypress commands based on an element's value; use `.should(callback)` when you need retry-able multi-assertion validation.

---

**Pattern 558: `data-cy` Attribute Strategy with a Centralised Selector Map** [official]
Define all `data-cy` attribute values in a centralised TypeScript constant map and import it into tests. This eliminates stringly-typed selector drift when component attribute names are renamed during refactoring.

```typescript
// cypress/support/selectors.ts
export const SEL = {
  auth: {
    emailInput: '[data-cy="email-input"]',
    passwordInput: '[data-cy="password-input"]',
    submitBtn: '[data-cy="submit-btn"]',
    errorBanner: '[data-cy="auth-error-banner"]',
  },
  nav: {
    userMenu: '[data-cy="user-menu"]',
    logoutBtn: '[data-cy="logout-btn"]',
    settingsLink: '[data-cy="settings-link"]',
  },
  products: {
    listContainer: '[data-cy="product-list"]',
    item: '[data-cy="product-item"]',
    addToCartBtn: '[data-cy="add-to-cart-btn"]',
  },
} as const;

// cypress/e2e/login.cy.ts
import { SEL } from '../support/selectors';

it('shows error on invalid credentials', () => {
  cy.visit('/login');
  cy.get(SEL.auth.emailInput).type('bad@example.com');
  cy.get(SEL.auth.passwordInput).type('wrong', { sensitive: true });
  cy.get(SEL.auth.submitBtn).click();
  cy.get(SEL.auth.errorBanner).should('be.visible').and('contain.text', 'Invalid credentials');
});
```
Tradeoff: The selector map requires discipline — developers must update `selectors.ts` when they add or rename `data-cy` attributes. Without a lint rule or CI check enforcing synchrony between the selector map and the component source, the map drifts. Add a custom ESLint rule or a spec that dynamically cross-checks the map keys against the DOM to catch mismatches early.

---

**Pattern 559: `cy.intercept()` with `middleware: true` to Inject Global Request Headers** [official]
Use `middleware: true` in a `beforeEach` intercept to inject headers into every outgoing request from the test. This is the correct pattern for adding test-context headers (e.g., `X-Test-Run-ID`, feature-flag override headers) without duplicating logic across hundreds of route-specific intercepts.

```typescript
beforeEach(() => {
  const testRunId = `cy-${Date.now()}-${Math.random().toString(36).slice(2)}`;

  // Runs first (middleware priority) and fires on every request
  cy.intercept({ url: '/api/**', middleware: true }, (req) => {
    req.headers['X-Cypress-Test'] = 'true';
    req.headers['X-Test-Run-ID'] = testRunId;
    req.headers['X-Feature-Flags'] = JSON.stringify({
      newCheckout: true,
      darkMode: false,
    });
    // Do NOT call req.reply() — fall through to next handler
  });
});

it('dashboard loads with feature flags applied', () => {
  cy.visit('/dashboard');
  cy.get('[data-cy="new-checkout-badge"]').should('be.visible');
  cy.get('[data-cy="dark-mode-toggle"]').should('not.exist');
});
```
Tradeoff: Middleware intercepts registered with `middleware: true` run before all other intercepts regardless of registration order. This means a middleware that modifies `req.headers` will affect even intercepts that were meant to use the unmodified headers for their `routeMatcher.headers` matching — the match condition runs after middleware mutation. Structure middleware intercepts to only add headers, never remove them, to avoid breaking downstream matchers.

---

**Pattern 560: `cy.intercept()` `req.on('response', fn)` for Response-Phase Spying Without Blocking** [official]
Use `req.on('response', handler)` to observe the response phase without modifying it and without blocking the request with `req.continue()`. This is useful for asserting that specific response headers or status codes are returned by the real server without the overhead of a full `req.continue()` handler.

```typescript
describe('CSP header enforcement', () => {
  it('API responses include correct Content-Security-Policy header', () => {
    const observedHeaders: Record<string, string>[] = [];

    cy.intercept({ url: '/api/**' }, (req) => {
      req.on('response', (res) => {
        observedHeaders.push({
          url: req.url,
          csp: res.headers['content-security-policy'] ?? 'MISSING',
          xFrame: res.headers['x-frame-options'] ?? 'MISSING',
        });
      });
    }).as('apiRequests');

    cy.visit('/dashboard');
    cy.get('[data-cy="user-profile"]').should('be.visible');

    cy.get('@apiRequests.all').then((interceptions: any[]) => {
      interceptions.forEach((i) => {
        expect(i.response.headers).to.have.property('content-security-policy');
        expect(i.response.headers['x-frame-options']).to.eq('DENY');
      });
    });
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `req.on('response', fn)` fires asynchronously after the response arrives; the handler must complete before Cypress considers the interception resolved. If the handler throws, the intercept fails with a cryptic `"Error in cy.intercept() handler"` message. Wrap observation logic in `try/catch` if the response shape may be missing expected fields (e.g., non-JSON error responses without security headers).

---

**Pattern 561: Component Testing with `cy.mount()` and Slot / Children Props Validation** [community]
When testing container components that accept children or named slots, mount them with representative child content and assert that slot projection works correctly. This verifies layout contracts that unit tests miss.

```typescript
import { Modal } from '../../src/components/Modal';
import { Button } from '../../src/components/Button';

describe('<Modal />', () => {
  it('projects header, body, and footer slots into correct DOM positions', () => {
    cy.mount(
      <Modal isOpen={true} onClose={cy.stub().as('onClose')}>
        <Modal.Header>Confirm Deletion</Modal.Header>
        <Modal.Body>
          <p data-cy="confirm-text">Are you sure you want to delete this item?</p>
        </Modal.Body>
        <Modal.Footer>
          <Button data-cy="cancel-btn" variant="secondary">Cancel</Button>
          <Button data-cy="confirm-btn" variant="danger">Delete</Button>
        </Modal.Footer>
      </Modal>
    );

    cy.get('[data-cy="modal-header"]').should('contain.text', 'Confirm Deletion');
    cy.get('[data-cy="confirm-text"]').should('be.visible');
    cy.get('[data-cy="confirm-btn"]').should('have.class', 'btn-danger');

    cy.get('[data-cy="cancel-btn"]').click();
    cy.get('@onClose').should('have.been.calledOnce');
  });

  it('does not render when isOpen is false', () => {
    cy.mount(<Modal isOpen={false} onClose={cy.stub()} />);
    cy.get('[data-cy="modal-overlay"]').should('not.exist');
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: Compound component patterns (`Modal.Header`, `Modal.Body`, etc.) require that sub-components are exported from the component module and importable in test files. If sub-components are defined inline as anonymous components, TypeScript may fail to resolve their types. Prefer named exports even for sub-components, or use `data-cy` attributes on wrapper divs that are guaranteed to render when the slot is populated.

---

**Pattern 562: `cy.wrap()` for Integrating Non-Cypress Promises into the Command Queue** [official]
Use `cy.wrap(promise)` to bring the resolution of an external promise (e.g., a `fetch()` call, a dynamic import, a Web Crypto operation) into the Cypress command chain. This avoids mixing async/await with Cypress commands, which breaks the command queue.

```typescript
describe('file encryption upload', () => {
  it('encrypts file client-side before upload and server stores ciphertext', () => {
    cy.intercept('POST', '/api/files').as('uploadReq');

    cy.visit('/upload');
    cy.get('[data-cy="file-input"]').selectFile('cypress/fixtures/secret.txt');

    // Wrap an external promise — generates encryption key via Web Crypto
    const keyPromise = window.crypto.subtle.generateKey(
      { name: 'AES-GCM', length: 256 },
      true,
      ['encrypt', 'decrypt']
    );
    cy.wrap(keyPromise).then((key) => {
      // key is now available inside the Cypress command chain
      expect(key).to.have.property('type', 'secret');
    });

    cy.get('[data-cy="encrypt-toggle"]').click();
    cy.get('[data-cy="upload-btn"]').click();

    cy.wait('@uploadReq').then((interception) => {
      // Server should receive base64 ciphertext, not plaintext
      expect(interception.request.body).to.have.property('encrypted', true);
      expect(interception.request.body.content).to.match(/^[A-Za-z0-9+/=]+$/);
    });
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `cy.wrap(promise)` injects the promise resolution into the command queue, but the promise itself starts executing immediately when `cy.wrap()` is called — not when the queue processes it. For promises with side effects (e.g., network calls), this means the side effect fires before preceding commands complete. Move promise creation inside a `.then()` callback if sequencing matters.

---

**Pattern 563: `cy.get('@alias.all')` to Assert Total Intercept Call Count** [official]
Use `cy.get('@alias.all')` to retrieve all interceptions that matched a given route alias as an array. This lets you assert the exact number of times an endpoint was called — critical for verifying that components do not make redundant API requests on re-render.

```typescript
describe('product detail — no redundant API calls on tab switch', () => {
  it('fetches product details only once even when switching tabs', () => {
    cy.intercept('GET', '/api/products/*').as('productDetail');

    cy.visit('/products/123');
    cy.wait('@productDetail');

    // Switch between tabs that might re-trigger the same fetch
    cy.get('[data-cy="reviews-tab"]').click();
    cy.get('[data-cy="specs-tab"]').click();
    cy.get('[data-cy="overview-tab"]').click();

    // Confirm the API was called exactly once (cached in state, not re-fetched)
    cy.get('@productDetail.all').should('have.length', 1);

    // Contrast: a different endpoint that SHOULD re-fetch per tab
    cy.intercept('GET', '/api/tab-content/*').as('tabContent');
    cy.get('[data-cy="reviews-tab"]').click();
    cy.wait('@tabContent');
    cy.get('[data-cy="specs-tab"]').click();
    cy.wait('@tabContent');
    cy.get('@tabContent.all').should('have.length', 2);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `@alias.all` returns interceptions collected since the intercept was registered in the current test — it does not persist across tests. If you need cross-test call count tracking (e.g., to verify a shared cache is populated once per suite), use a `cy.task()` counter that increments inside a middleware intercept handler. Note that `cy.get('@alias.all')` is itself a query that retries, but retrying on array length is not straightforward — pair it with `.should('have.length', N)` for retry-able length assertions.

---

**Pattern 564: `beforeEach` Data-Driven Test Table Pattern Using `Cypress._.each`** [community]
Use Lodash's `_.each` (available as `Cypress._`) to iterate over a data table and generate parameterised test cases without external plugins. This is lighter than `cypress-data-session` for simple scenario enumeration.

```typescript
const loginScenarios = [
  { role: 'admin', expectedRoute: '/admin/dashboard', expectedBadge: 'Admin' },
  { role: 'editor', expectedRoute: '/editor/workspace', expectedBadge: 'Editor' },
  { role: 'viewer', expectedRoute: '/viewer/feed', expectedBadge: 'Viewer' },
] as const;

describe('role-based post-login routing', () => {
  Cypress._.each(loginScenarios, ({ role, expectedRoute, expectedBadge }) => {
    it(`routes ${role} to correct dashboard and shows role badge`, () => {
      cy.loginAs(role);
      cy.visit('/');

      cy.url().should('include', expectedRoute);
      cy.get('[data-cy="role-badge"]')
        .should('be.visible')
        .and('contain.text', expectedBadge);

      // Verify role-specific nav items are present
      cy.get('[data-cy="nav-admin-tools"]').should(
        role === 'admin' ? 'exist' : 'not.exist'
      );
    });
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `Cypress._.each` generates test descriptions at suite-collection time (before `beforeEach` runs), so test names are stable and appear correctly in Cypress Cloud. However, the data table is evaluated at module load — if test data needs to come from a dynamic source (API, database), use `cy.task()` in a `before()` hook and store results in a module-level variable that `Cypress._.each` references after the hook populates it.

---

### Community Gotchas

356. **`cy.intercept()` `req.alias` dynamic aliasing inside a handler silently overwrites the static `.as()` alias — after calling `req.alias = 'myAlias'` inside the handler, `cy.wait('@myAlias')` works, but the original alias registered via `.as('staticAlias')` is no longer reachable in subsequent `cy.wait('@staticAlias')` calls within the same test** [community] — A developer writes a GraphQL intercept: `cy.intercept('POST', '/graphql', (req) => { req.alias = req.body.operationName; }).as('graphql')`. They then try `cy.wait('@graphql')` to wait for any GraphQL request, and `cy.wait('@CreateUser')` to wait for a specific operation. The first `cy.wait('@graphql')` times out because `req.alias = operationName` inside the handler replaces the `.as('graphql')` alias for each request — the static alias is only set for requests where the handler does NOT assign `req.alias`. WHY: `req.alias` assignment inside the handler completely overrides the route-level `.as()` alias for that specific request. The `.as()` alias is only used as a fallback when the handler does not set `req.alias`. Fix: either use `req.alias` exclusively for dynamic aliasing (and do not chain `.as()`) or use a separate `cy.intercept()` registration for each specific operation you want to alias statically.

357. **`cy.session()` `cacheAcrossSpecs: true` causes the first spec to run without a session when Cypress Cloud parallel mode distributes specs across multiple machines — each machine creates its own session independently, so session-dependent tests that expect a "pre-warmed" session on the second spec of a run fail with an authentication error because that spec is the first spec on a different machine** [community] — A team assumes that `cacheAcrossSpecs: true` shares sessions globally across the entire parallel run. On local sequential runs, the optimisation works perfectly — the login session from spec 1 is reused in specs 2–20. In CI with 4 parallel machines, each machine gets approximately 5 specs. Each machine's first spec must create a fresh session, adding login time back to every machine. More critically, a developer writes `cy.session('preloaded', () => { ... })` expecting this session to be "already hot" when spec 5 runs on machine 2 — but machine 2 has never run the session setup. WHY: `cacheAcrossSpecs: true` scopes the session cache to a single Cypress process on a single machine; it does not synchronise sessions across machines in a distributed run. Fix: redesign tests to always tolerate a cold session on any spec, and treat `cacheAcrossSpecs: true` as a per-machine optimisation, not a global one.

358. **`cy.clock()` installed after `cy.visit()` does not control timers created by framework initialisation code — specifically, React's `useEffect` with a `setInterval` that runs on mount will have already registered the real `setInterval` before `cy.clock()` replaces it, causing the interval to fire on the real clock even though `cy.tick()` advances the fake clock** [community] — A developer tests a live-updating component: `cy.visit('/live-feed'); cy.clock(); cy.tick(5000);` — expecting the 5-second poll to fire once. The clock was installed after navigation, so React's `useEffect(() => { setInterval(fetchLatest, 5000) }, [])` ran at mount time with the real `setInterval`. `cy.tick(5000)` advances the fake clock, but the real `setInterval` fires independently. The test sees extra unintended network requests. WHY: `cy.clock()` replaces `window.setTimeout`, `window.setInterval`, and `Date` at the moment it is called. Timers registered before that moment remain on the real clock. Fix: always call `cy.clock()` before `cy.visit()` so that the page's entire initialisation — including framework bootstrap and `useEffect` callbacks — uses the fake clock from the start.

359. **`Cypress.Commands.add()` TypeScript types require the `cypress.d.ts` file to be a "script" (no `import`/`export` at the top level) for declaration merging to work — adding any `import` statement turns the file into a "module", making the `declare namespace Cypress` block a local declaration rather than a global augmentation, and IntelliSense silently stops suggesting the custom command** [community] — A developer adds `import type { MyType } from '../types'` to `cypress.d.ts` to type a custom command's parameter. IntelliSense immediately stops suggesting `cy.loginAs()` in spec files. TypeScript does not report an error — the type is simply not merged into the global namespace. The developer spends time debugging tsconfig paths, wondering why the type file is "ignored." WHY: In TypeScript, a file with top-level `import`/`export` is a "module" with its own scope; `declare namespace` inside a module does not augment the global namespace. Fix: either keep `cypress.d.ts` as a pure declaration file (no imports) using `/// <reference types="..." />` directives instead, or wrap the namespace augmentation in `export {}` and explicitly merge: `declare global { namespace Cypress { ... } }`.

360. **`cy.get('@alias.all')` returns an empty array and immediately resolves when called before any matching request has been made — unlike `cy.wait('@alias')` which blocks until at least one request arrives, `cy.get('@alias.all')` does not retry waiting for the array to become non-empty, causing assertions like `.should('have.length', 2)` to pass immediately with length 0 if called before the requests fire** [community] — A developer writes: `cy.intercept('GET', '/api/events').as('events'); cy.visit('/dashboard'); cy.get('@events.all').should('have.length', 2);`. The dashboard triggers two event requests asynchronously after a short delay. `cy.get('@events.all')` resolves immediately with an empty array `[]`; `.should('have.length', 2)` retries the assertion but `cy.get('@events.all')` re-evaluates each retry and keeps returning `[]` because Cypress queries the alias store synchronously — not asynchronously waiting for requests. WHY: `cy.get('@alias.all')` is a synchronous alias lookup, not a network listener. It returns whatever is in the alias store at query time. Fix: first `cy.wait('@events')` twice (or `cy.wait(['@events', '@events'])`) to block until both requests arrive, then call `cy.get('@events.all').should('have.length', 2)` to verify the count.

## Cycle 55 — 2026-05-14

### New Patterns

**Pattern 565: `cy.intercept()` `req.redirect()` for Conditional Redirect Testing** [official]
Use `req.redirect(location, statusCode)` to simulate server-side redirects without spinning up a real redirect endpoint. This lets you test redirect-handling logic (e.g., login guards, HTTPS upgrades) in a deterministic, latency-free way. Unlike `req.reply()` with `statusCode: 302`, `req.redirect()` automatically sets the `Location` header and ends the request phase in one call.

```typescript
describe('redirect handling', () => {
  it('redirects unauthenticated users to /login', () => {
    cy.intercept('GET', '/dashboard', (req) => {
      req.redirect('/login', 302);
    }).as('dashboardGuard');

    cy.visit('/dashboard', { failOnStatusCode: false });
    cy.wait('@dashboardGuard');
    cy.url().should('include', '/login');
  });

  it('upgrades HTTP to HTTPS', () => {
    cy.intercept('GET', 'http://example.com/page', (req) => {
      req.redirect('https://example.com/page', 301);
    }).as('httpsUpgrade');

    cy.request({ url: 'http://example.com/page', followRedirect: false })
      .then((res) => {
        expect(res.status).to.eq(301);
        expect(res.headers['location']).to.eq('https://example.com/page');
      });
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `req.redirect()` ends the request immediately and does not reach the real server — useful for redirect logic tests but cannot validate actual server redirect behavior. If you need to verify that the server itself issues the redirect, use a real request and assert on `cy.wait('@alias').its('response.statusCode')` instead.

---

**Pattern 566: `cy.intercept()` `req.destroy()` for Network Error Resilience Testing** [official]
`req.destroy()` forces a network-level connection failure, simulating scenarios like dropped connections, DNS failures, or abrupt server shutdowns. This is distinct from a `forceNetworkError: true` static response — `req.destroy()` is callable conditionally inside a handler, enabling fault-injection patterns that toggle based on call count.

```typescript
let callCount = 0;

beforeEach(() => { callCount = 0; });

it('retries on first network error then succeeds', () => {
  cy.intercept('GET', '/api/data', (req) => {
    callCount += 1;
    if (callCount === 1) {
      req.destroy(); // drop first attempt
    } else {
      req.continue(); // let retry through
    }
  }).as('dataFetch');

  cy.visit('/data-view');

  // App's internal retry logic fires a second request
  cy.wait('@dataFetch');
  cy.wait('@dataFetch');

  cy.get('[data-cy="data-content"]').should('be.visible');
  expect(callCount).to.eq(2);
});
```
Tradeoff: `req.destroy()` produces a `net::ERR_CONNECTION_RESET` style error in the browser. If the application does not have retry logic, the test will confirm failure behavior, not success. Combine with `cy.on('uncaught:exception', () => false)` if the app's unhandled rejection would otherwise abort the test before the retry fires.

---

**Pattern 567: `cy.intercept()` `res.setDelay()` for Loading State Validation** [official]
Use `res.setDelay(ms)` inside a `req.continue()` callback to add latency to real or stubbed responses. This lets you reliably assert loading spinners, skeleton screens, or disabled buttons that only appear during the network round-trip — states that are normally too fast to catch in tests.

```typescript
it('shows loading skeleton while fetching user profile', () => {
  cy.intercept('GET', '/api/users/*', (req) => {
    req.continue((res) => {
      res.setDelay(1500); // hold response for 1.5 s
    });
  }).as('userProfile');

  cy.visit('/profile/42');

  // Assert skeleton is visible before response arrives
  cy.get('[data-cy="profile-skeleton"]').should('be.visible');
  cy.get('[data-cy="profile-content"]').should('not.exist');

  // Let response through and verify real content renders
  cy.wait('@userProfile');
  cy.get('[data-cy="profile-skeleton"]').should('not.exist');
  cy.get('[data-cy="profile-content"]').should('be.visible');
});
```
Tradeoff: Delays add real wall-clock time to the test run. Keep delay values to the minimum needed to observe the loading state (typically 200–500 ms). Avoid `res.setDelay()` in `beforeEach` for unrelated tests — scope it to the specific test that validates loading UI.

---

**Pattern 568: `cy.intercept()` `res.setThrottle()` for Slow Network Simulation** [official]
`res.setThrottle(kbps)` throttles the response data rate, simulating 3G/4G connections or saturated networks. Use this to test progressive rendering, partial content handling, or timeout UX without relying on OS-level network throttling tools that are unreliable in CI.

```typescript
it('renders partial results as chunks arrive on a slow connection', () => {
  cy.intercept('GET', '/api/feed', (req) => {
    req.continue((res) => {
      res.setThrottle(100); // 100 kbps — simulates a weak mobile connection
    });
  }).as('slowFeed');

  cy.visit('/feed');

  // App renders a "Loading more…" indicator before full body arrives
  cy.get('[data-cy="loading-more"]').should('be.visible');

  cy.wait('@slowFeed', { timeout: 15000 }); // allow extra time for throttled response

  cy.get('[data-cy="feed-item"]').should('have.length.gte', 10);
  cy.get('[data-cy="loading-more"]').should('not.exist');
});
```
Tradeoff: Throttling extends test duration proportional to payload size. A 100 kbps cap on a 50 kB response adds ~4 seconds. For large fixtures, prefer `res.setDelay()` to simulate latency without the payload-size dependency.

---

**Pattern 569: `cy.intercept()` Per-Request Dynamic Aliasing for GraphQL Operations** [official]
For GraphQL APIs that send all mutations/queries to a single endpoint (`POST /graphql`), set `req.alias` inside the handler based on the `operationName` field of the request body. This allows waiting for specific operations without registering a separate `cy.intercept()` for each one.

```typescript
beforeEach(() => {
  cy.intercept('POST', '/graphql', (req) => {
    const { operationName } = req.body;
    if (operationName) {
      req.alias = operationName; // e.g., 'GetUser', 'CreatePost'
    }
  });
});

it('creates a post and refreshes the feed', () => {
  cy.visit('/posts');

  cy.get('[data-cy="new-post-input"]').type('Hello world');
  cy.get('[data-cy="submit-post"]').click();

  // Wait for the specific mutation, then the refetch query
  cy.wait('@CreatePost').its('response.body.data.createPost.id').should('exist');
  cy.wait('@GetFeed').its('response.body.data.posts').should('have.length.gte', 1);
});
```
Tradeoff: Because `req.alias` inside a handler overrides any static `.as()` alias set on the intercept (see Gotcha G361 in the prior cycle), do not chain `.as('graphql')` on this intercept if you also rely on `req.alias` assignment. Register a second, separate passthrough intercept if you need both a "catch-all" alias and per-operation aliases simultaneously.

---

**Pattern 570: `cy.intercept()` Middleware Header Injection for Auth Tokens** [official]
Set `middleware: true` on a broad intercept to inject auth headers into every outbound request, then register narrower non-middleware intercepts for response stubbing. Middleware intercepts run first and do not block the chain — subsequent handlers still fire.

```typescript
// cypress/support/e2e.ts
beforeEach(() => {
  // Inject a valid JWT into every API request
  cy.intercept({ url: '/api/**', middleware: true }, (req) => {
    req.headers['Authorization'] = `Bearer ${Cypress.env('TEST_JWT')}`;
  });
});

// In a spec file — the middleware above runs first, auth header is already set
it('fetches protected resource', () => {
  cy.intercept('GET', '/api/profile').as('profile');
  cy.visit('/profile');
  cy.wait('@profile').its('request.headers.authorization').should('include', 'Bearer ');
  cy.get('[data-cy="profile-name"]').should('be.visible');
});
```
Tradeoff: Middleware intercepts apply globally to every test in the spec where they are registered. If a test deliberately omits the auth header (e.g., to test a 401 response), clear the middleware intercept explicitly with `cy.intercept({ url: '/api/**', middleware: true }, (req) => { /* no-op */ })` or restructure the test into a separate spec that does not install the support-file `beforeEach`.

---

**Pattern 571: Retry-able `.should(callback)` for Multi-Property DOM Assertions** [official]
Use `.should($el => { expect(...) })` instead of chaining multiple `.and()` assertions when the property extraction involves non-trivial logic. The callback form retries the entire block — including any `invoke`, `prop`, or attribute reads inside — until all expectations pass or the timeout expires.

```typescript
it('shows correctly formatted product price', () => {
  cy.visit('/products/42');

  cy.get('[data-cy="price-display"]').should(($el) => {
    const text = $el.text().trim();
    // All expectations in the callback retry as a unit
    expect(text).to.match(/^\$[\d,]+\.\d{2}$/); // format check
    expect(parseFloat(text.replace(/[$,]/g, ''))).to.be.gte(0); // value check
    expect($el).to.have.css('color', 'rgb(34, 139, 34)'); // "in-stock" green
  });

  // Ensure aria-label matches displayed text for accessibility
  cy.get('[data-cy="price-display"]').should(($el) => {
    const displayText = $el.text().trim();
    expect($el.attr('aria-label')).to.include(displayText);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: The callback fires synchronously inside Cypress's retry loop, so any assertion that calls `cy.*` commands inside the callback will throw — Cypress commands are not allowed within `.should()` callbacks. Extract `cy.*` values using aliases before the `.should()` call if you need them inside the callback.

---

**Pattern 572: `Commands.addQuery()` Typed Retry-able Selector Wrapper** [official]
Use `Cypress.Commands.addQuery()` to create custom retry-able queries that integrate seamlessly with the Cypress command queue and type system. Unlike `Commands.add()` with a callback, `addQuery()` returns a synchronous function that Cypress will re-execute on each retry attempt.

```typescript
// cypress/support/commands.ts
declare global {
  namespace Cypress {
    interface Chainable {
      getByCy(selector: string): Chainable<JQuery<HTMLElement>>;
      getByRole(role: string, name: string): Chainable<JQuery<HTMLElement>>;
    }
  }
}

Cypress.Commands.addQuery('getByCy', (selector: string) => {
  // Outer function runs once to capture args
  return () => {
    // Inner function runs on each retry
    return cy.$$(`[data-cy="${selector}"]`);
  };
});

Cypress.Commands.addQuery('getByRole', (role: string, name: string) => {
  return () => {
    return cy.$$(`[role="${role}"][aria-label="${name}"], [role="${role}"][name="${name}"]`);
  };
});

// Usage in tests
it('interacts with form using typed queries', () => {
  cy.visit('/signup');
  cy.getByCy('email-input').type('test@example.com');
  cy.getByRole('button', 'Submit').click();
  cy.getByCy('success-banner').should('be.visible');
});
```
Tradeoff: `Commands.addQuery()` requires the double-function pattern (outer captures args, inner does the DOM lookup) — forgetting the inner function causes Cypress to call your function once and treat the return value as the result, breaking retry. The inner function must be synchronous; if you need async operations (fetching from `cy.task()`), use `Commands.add()` instead.

---

**Pattern 573: `cy.session()` with `idleTimeout` and localStorage Expiry Sentinel** [official]
Extend `cy.session()` validation with a client-side expiry sentinel stored in `localStorage` to avoid unnecessary `validate()` network round-trips. The sentinel stores a timestamp; if it has not expired, the session is assumed valid without hitting `/api/me`.

```typescript
const SESSION_TTL_MS = 30 * 60 * 1000; // 30 minutes

export function loginAs(role: 'admin' | 'editor' | 'viewer'): void {
  cy.session(
    [role],
    () => {
      cy.request('POST', '/api/auth/login', {
        username: Cypress.env(`${role.toUpperCase()}_USER`),
        password: Cypress.env(`${role.toUpperCase()}_PASS`),
      }).then(({ body }) => {
        window.localStorage.setItem('authToken', body.token);
        window.localStorage.setItem(
          'sessionExpiry',
          String(Date.now() + SESSION_TTL_MS)
        );
      });
    },
    {
      validate() {
        const expiry = Number(window.localStorage.getItem('sessionExpiry'));
        if (expiry && Date.now() < expiry) return; // skip network call
        cy.request({ url: '/api/me', failOnStatusCode: false })
          .its('status')
          .should('eq', 200);
      },
      cacheAcrossSpecs: true,
    }
  );
}
```
Tradeoff: The `localStorage` sentinel is only checked at the time the `validate()` callback runs — if Cypress restores a session whose token expired mid-spec (e.g., a long-running test), the sentinel may still appear fresh while the actual server-side token has been revoked. Set the TTL conservatively (well under the real token lifetime) to reduce this risk.

---

**Pattern 574: `cy.clock()` Before `cy.visit()` for Full Timer Control** [official]
Always install `cy.clock()` before `cy.visit()` to ensure that timers registered during framework initialisation (React `useEffect`, Vue `onMounted`, Angular `ngOnInit`) use the fake clock. Timers created before `cy.clock()` run on the real clock and are invisible to `cy.tick()`.

```typescript
it('auto-logs out after 15-minute idle timeout', () => {
  cy.clock(); // install BEFORE visit so useEffect's setInterval uses fake clock

  cy.visit('/dashboard');
  loginAsUser('alice@example.com', 'password123');

  // Fast-forward 14 minutes — session should still be active
  cy.tick(14 * 60 * 1000);
  cy.get('[data-cy="session-banner"]').should('not.exist');

  // Fast-forward 1 more minute — idle timeout fires
  cy.tick(60 * 1000);
  cy.get('[data-cy="session-banner"]')
    .should('be.visible')
    .and('contain.text', 'Your session has expired');

  cy.url().should('include', '/login');
});
```
Tradeoff: `cy.clock()` freezes `Date.now()` at the time it is called unless you pass an initial timestamp. If the app uses `Date.now()` to compute relative times displayed to the user, pass `cy.clock(Date.now())` to start the fake clock at the real current time, preventing stale "last updated" labels from confusing assertions.

---

**Pattern 575: Component Testing Spy-Based Event Emission Verification** [official]
Use `cy.spy()` wrapped in an alias to assert that component output events (React `onFoo` callbacks, Vue `emits`, Angular `EventEmitter`) are called with the correct arguments. This avoids inspecting internal component state and validates the public API contract.

```typescript
// React example — stepper component emits onChange with new count
import { mount } from 'cypress/react';
import { Stepper } from '../../src/components/Stepper';

it('emits onChange with incremented count on each click', () => {
  const onChangeSpy = cy.spy().as('onChange');

  mount(<Stepper initialCount={0} onChange={onChangeSpy} />);

  cy.get('[data-cy="increment"]').click();
  cy.get('@onChange').should('have.been.calledOnceWith', 1);

  cy.get('[data-cy="increment"]').click();
  cy.get('@onChange').should('have.been.calledWith', 2);

  cy.get('[data-cy="decrement"]').click();
  cy.get('@onChange').should('have.been.calledWith', 1);

  // Verify call count and argument history
  cy.get('@onChange').should('have.been.calledThrice');
  cy.get('@onChange').its('args').should('deep.equal', [[1], [2], [1]]);
});
```
Tradeoff: `cy.spy()` wraps the function synchronously at mount time. If the component stores the prop reference internally and later re-reads it (common in class components or memoised hooks), the spy must be passed as the same reference on re-renders. Avoid recreating the spy inside `beforeEach` if the component is mounted once in a shared `before()` — the alias would be overwritten.

---

**Pattern 576: `cy.fixture()` Lazy Loading with `import()` Syntax Alternative** [community]
Instead of `cy.fixture()`, use ES dynamic `import()` for JSON fixtures in TypeScript specs. Dynamic imports are resolved at bundle time, giving you full IntelliSense and type safety on the fixture shape, whereas `cy.fixture()` yields `any`. Wrap in `cy.wrap()` to re-enter the Cypress command queue.

```typescript
// cypress/fixtures/user.fixture.ts
export const adminUser = {
  id: 'usr_001',
  email: 'admin@example.com',
  role: 'admin' as const,
  permissions: ['read', 'write', 'delete'],
};

// In spec file
import { adminUser } from '../fixtures/user.fixture';

it('pre-populates the edit form with user data', () => {
  // Fully typed — no cy.fixture() call needed
  cy.intercept('GET', `/api/users/${adminUser.id}`, { body: adminUser }).as('getUser');

  cy.visit(`/users/${adminUser.id}/edit`);
  cy.wait('@getUser');

  cy.get('[data-cy="email-input"]').should('have.value', adminUser.email);
  cy.get('[data-cy="role-select"]').should('have.value', adminUser.role);
  adminUser.permissions.forEach((perm) => {
    cy.get(`[data-cy="permission-${perm}"]`).should('be.checked');
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: Dynamic `import()` for fixtures couples the spec to the TypeScript build pipeline — fixtures must be `.ts` files inside the Cypress root, and Cypress's Vite/webpack config must resolve them. `cy.fixture()` supports any format (JSON, images, binary) and does not require TypeScript. Use `cy.fixture()` for binary or non-JSON fixtures; use `import()` for typed JSON/object fixtures.

---

**Pattern 577: `Cypress._.throttle()` and `Cypress._.debounce()` for Rapid Input Simulation** [community]
Cypress bundles Lodash as `Cypress._`. Use `Cypress._.throttle()` and `Cypress._.debounce()` in test helper functions to accurately simulate user input patterns that trigger debounced search fields or throttled scroll handlers — without adding `cy.wait(ms)` anti-patterns.

```typescript
// cypress/support/commands.ts
Cypress.Commands.add('typeInSearchBox', (selector: string, text: string) => {
  // Simulate typing each character with a 50ms inter-key delay to trigger debounce
  cy.get(selector).focus();
  [...text].forEach((char, i) => {
    cy.get(selector).type(char, { delay: 50 });
    if (i < text.length - 1) {
      // Verify debounced request has NOT fired mid-type
      cy.get('[data-cy="search-spinner"]').should('not.be.visible');
    }
  });
});

it('fires exactly one search request for a typed query', () => {
  cy.intercept('GET', '/api/search*').as('search');

  cy.visit('/search');
  cy.typeInSearchBox('[data-cy="search-input"]', 'cypress');

  // After typing stops, debounce fires the request
  cy.wait('@search')
    .its('request.url')
    .should('include', 'query=cypress');

  // Only one request should have been made despite 7 keystrokes
  cy.get('@search.all').should('have.length', 1);
});
```
Tradeoff: The `delay` option in `cy.type()` adds real clock time per character. For a 20-character query with 50 ms delay, that is 1 second added to the test. If the app's debounce window is 300 ms and the inter-key delay is 50 ms, the debounce resets on every keystroke — matching real user behavior. If the debounce is longer than the inter-key delay, increase `delay` to match.

---

**Pattern 578: `cy.request()` Typed API Seeding Helper with `afterEach` Idempotent Cleanup** [official]
Seed test data via `cy.request()` in `before()` and clean it up in `afterEach()` using an idempotent DELETE — `failOnStatusCode: false` ensures the cleanup does not fail if the resource was already deleted by the test itself.

```typescript
// cypress/support/api-seed.ts
interface SeedResult {
  userId: string;
  postId: string;
}

export function seedUserWithPost(overrides?: Partial<SeedResult>): Cypress.Chainable<SeedResult> {
  return cy
    .request<{ id: string }>('POST', '/api/test/users', {
      email: `test-${Date.now()}@example.com`,
      role: 'editor',
    })
    .then(({ body: user }) =>
      cy
        .request<{ id: string }>('POST', `/api/test/users/${user.id}/posts`, {
          title: 'Seed post',
          published: false,
        })
        .then(({ body: post }) => ({
          userId: user.id,
          postId: post.id,
          ...overrides,
        }))
    );
}

// In spec
describe('post editing', () => {
  let seed: SeedResult;

  before(() => { seedUserWithPost().then((s) => { seed = s; }); });
  afterEach(() => {
    cy.request({ method: 'DELETE', url: `/api/test/posts/${seed.postId}`, failOnStatusCode: false });
    cy.request({ method: 'DELETE', url: `/api/test/users/${seed.userId}`, failOnStatusCode: false });
  });

  it('displays the post editor for unpublished posts', () => {
    cy.visit(`/posts/${seed.postId}/edit`);
    cy.get('[data-cy="post-title"]').should('have.value', 'Seed post');
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: API seeding creates real server state, making tests slower and dependent on a running backend. It is the right choice for critical paths (billing, data integrity) where stubbing would not catch integration bugs. For fast unit-style tests of UI behavior, prefer `cy.intercept()` stubs.

---

**Pattern 579: `cy.task()` Typed Task Map with Null Return Requirement** [official]
Define a strictly typed task map in `cypress.config.ts` and reference it in tests via a typed wrapper command. Every task handler must return a non-`undefined` value — return `null` explicitly to signal "no meaningful return value" and avoid Cypress throwing an uncaught error.

```typescript
// cypress.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from 'cypress';
import { resetDatabase, getEmailFromInbox } from './cypress/tasks';

export interface TaskMap {
  resetDb: { input: void; output: null };
  getLatestEmail: { input: { to: string }; output: { subject: string; body: string } | null };
}

export default defineConfig({
  e2e: {
    setupNodeEvents(on) {
      on('task', {
        resetDb: async () => {
          await resetDatabase();
          return null; // MUST return null, not undefined
        },
        getLatestEmail: async ({ to }) => {
          return await getEmailFromInbox(to) ?? null;
        },
      });
    },
  },
});

// cypress/support/commands.ts
Cypress.Commands.add('resetDb', () => cy.task('resetDb'));
Cypress.Commands.add('getLatestEmail', (to: string) =>
  cy.task('getLatestEmail', { to })
);
```
Tradeoff: The `null` return requirement is a Cypress-specific convention — returning `undefined` causes Cypress to throw `"cy.task('resetDb') failed with: Task must explicitly return a value"`. This surprises developers familiar with Node.js where `undefined` and `null` are often interchangeable. Lint for this with an ESLint rule: `no-undefined-return` scoped to `cypress/tasks/`.

---

**Pattern 580: `cy.get('@alias.all')` Count Assertion with Prior `cy.wait()` Guard** [official]
When asserting total request counts via `cy.get('@alias.all').should('have.length', N)`, always precede it with `cy.wait('@alias')` (repeated if N > 1) to block until the expected requests have arrived. `cy.get('@alias.all')` is a synchronous alias lookup that resolves immediately with whatever has arrived so far — without a prior `cy.wait()`, it returns an empty array even if requests are in flight.

```typescript
it('tracks exactly three API calls on initial dashboard load', () => {
  cy.intercept('GET', '/api/widgets*').as('widgets');
  cy.intercept('GET', '/api/announcements*').as('announcements');
  cy.intercept('GET', '/api/user/activity*').as('activity');

  cy.visit('/dashboard');

  // Guard: wait for each expected request before counting
  cy.wait('@widgets');
  cy.wait('@announcements');
  cy.wait('@activity');

  // Now safe to assert the total collection length
  cy.get('@widgets.all').should('have.length', 1);
  cy.get('@announcements.all').should('have.length', 1);
  cy.get('@activity.all').should('have.length', 1);

  // Verify no unexpected additional requests were made
  cy.get('[data-cy="dashboard-loaded"]').should('be.visible');
});
```
Tradeoff: `cy.wait('@alias')` blocks until the first matching request and response complete. If the app makes N identical requests, call `cy.wait('@alias')` N times or use `cy.wait(['@alias', '@alias', '@alias'])` (array form). Calling `cy.wait('@alias')` once then `cy.get('@alias.all').should('have.length', 3)` will fail if the second and third requests arrive after the `wait` resolves.

---

**Pattern 581: Component Testing with `createTestingPinia` for Vuex/Pinia State Isolation** [official]
In Vue component tests, use `createTestingPinia()` from `@pinia/testing` to mount components with a sandboxed store. Each test gets a fresh store instance with stubbed actions by default, preventing state bleed across tests.

```typescript
import { mount } from 'cypress/vue';
import { createTestingPinia } from '@pinia/testing';
import UserDashboard from '../../src/components/UserDashboard.vue';
import { useUserStore } from '../../src/stores/user';

it('displays user name and subscription tier from store', () => {
  mount(UserDashboard, {
    global: {
      plugins: [
        createTestingPinia({
          initialState: {
            user: {
              name: 'Alice Johnson',
              tier: 'premium',
              notificationCount: 5,
            },
          },
          stubActions: false, // allow real actions for this test
        }),
      ],
    },
  });

  cy.get('[data-cy="user-name"]').should('contain.text', 'Alice Johnson');
  cy.get('[data-cy="tier-badge"]').should('contain.text', 'Premium');
  cy.get('[data-cy="notification-badge"]').should('contain.text', '5');

  // Trigger a store action and verify UI updates
  cy.get('[data-cy="mark-all-read"]').click();
  cy.get('[data-cy="notification-badge"]').should('not.exist');
});
```
Tradeoff: `stubActions: true` (the default) replaces all store actions with stubs — ideal for unit-style component tests but bypasses actual state mutation logic. If your component's behavior depends on a computed property that is derived from state mutated by an action, set `stubActions: false` and seed `initialState` to the pre-action state, then trigger the action to verify the derived UI.

---

**Pattern 582: `cy.origin()` Structured Data Passing with `args` to Avoid Closure Serialization** [official]
Pass data into `cy.origin()` callbacks via the `args` option rather than closing over variables from the outer scope. Closure variables are not serialized into the cross-origin iframe context — only `args` are, via the structured clone algorithm.

```typescript
it('completes OAuth login via third-party identity provider', () => {
  const oauthConfig = {
    email: Cypress.env('OAUTH_TEST_EMAIL'),
    password: Cypress.env('OAUTH_TEST_PASSWORD'),
    provider: 'github' as const,
  };

  cy.visit('/login');
  cy.get('[data-cy="login-with-github"]').click();

  cy.origin(
    'https://github.com',
    { args: oauthConfig }, // CORRECT: pass via args, not closure
    ({ email, password }) => {
      cy.get('#login_field').type(email);
      cy.get('#password').type(password);
      cy.get('[type="submit"]').click();
    }
  );

  // Back on the original origin after OAuth redirect
  cy.url().should('include', '/dashboard');
  cy.get('[data-cy="oauth-provider-badge"]').should('contain.text', 'GitHub');
});
```
Tradeoff: The structured clone algorithm used by `args` does not support functions, class instances, `Map`, `Set`, `RegExp`, or `undefined`. If you need to pass complex types, serialize them to plain JSON in the outer scope and deserialize inside the callback. For functions (e.g., custom matchers), extract them to a shared module and use `Cypress.require()` with `experimentalOriginDependencies` enabled.

---

### Community Gotchas

**Gotcha G361: `cy.intercept()` routes match in reverse registration order — a broad catch-all registered first is matched last, so the catch-all never fires when a narrow handler below it matches**
A developer registers `cy.intercept('GET', '/api/**')` to log all API calls, then `cy.intercept('GET', '/api/users')` to stub the users endpoint. The stub fires as expected, but the logging intercept never triggers for `/api/users` requests. WHY: Cypress evaluates non-middleware intercepts in reverse registration order (last registered = first evaluated). The narrower `/api/users` handler is registered later, so it matches first and Cypress stops looking for additional non-middleware handlers. Fix: either promote the catch-all to middleware with `{ middleware: true }` so it always runs first (and passes through to later handlers), or register the catch-all after the specific handlers so it evaluates first in the reverse order.

**Gotcha G362: `cy.clock()` does not affect `performance.now()` — animations driven by `requestAnimationFrame` callbacks that use `performance.now()` as their timestamp source continue to run on real time even after `cy.tick()` advances the fake clock**
A developer tests a CSS progress bar that advances via a JavaScript animation loop using `performance.now()` for easing calculations. They call `cy.clock()` and `cy.tick(2000)`, expecting the bar to show 2-second progress. The bar stays at 0% because the rAF callback reads `performance.now()` which is still the real monotonic clock. WHY: `cy.clock()` replaces `Date`, `setTimeout`, `setInterval`, and `clearTimeout`/`clearInterval`, but does NOT replace `performance.now()` or `requestAnimationFrame`. Fix: for animation testing, use `cy.stub(window, 'requestAnimationFrame')` to control rAF manually, or mock `performance.now` via `cy.window().then((win) => cy.stub(win.performance, 'now').returns(fakeTime))` before `cy.visit()`.

**Gotcha G363: `cypress.d.ts` declaration merging breaks silently when the file contains a top-level `import` or `export` — the file becomes a module and `declare namespace Cypress` stops augmenting the global namespace, causing all custom command types to disappear from IntelliSense without any TypeScript error**
A developer adds `import type { MyPayload } from '../src/types'` to `cypress.d.ts` to type a custom command parameter. After the import, `cy.myCommand()` stops appearing in editor autocomplete even though the runtime behavior is unchanged. TypeScript reports no errors. WHY: TypeScript files with top-level `import`/`export` are ES modules with local scope. `declare namespace Cypress { interface Chainable { ... } }` inside a module is a local declaration, not a global augmentation. Fix: keep `cypress.d.ts` as a pure ambient declaration file (no `import`/`export`) and use `/// <reference types="../../src/types" />` directives, or use `declare global { namespace Cypress { interface Chainable { myCommand(): Chainable<void>; } } }` wrapping to explicitly target the global scope from within a module.

**Gotcha G364: `.then()` in the middle of a Cypress command chain breaks retry-ability for all subsequent assertions — once `.then()` is called, Cypress treats everything after it as a one-time synchronous callback, meaning `.should()` assertions that follow will not retry if the DOM has not yet settled**
A developer writes `cy.get('[data-cy="count"]').then(($el) => $el.text()).should('eq', '5')`. The count updates asynchronously after a button click, but the test intermittently passes (when the DOM updates fast) and fails (when it updates slowly). The `.should('eq', '5')` on the string returned from `.then()` does retry the assertion, but does not re-execute the `.then($el => $el.text())` call — so it retries the same stale text value. WHY: `.then()` executes once and yields its return value to the next command. Subsequent `.should()` assertions retry the assertion predicate only, not the chain leading up to it. Fix: use `.should(($el) => { expect($el.text()).to.eq('5') })` so the entire property extraction and assertion retries as a unit.

**Gotcha G365: `cy.get('@alias.all')` resolves immediately with an empty array if called before any matching intercept has fired — unlike `cy.wait('@alias')`, it does not block waiting for requests, so `.should('have.length', N)` on it passes instantly with 0 even though N requests are in flight**
A developer writes `cy.intercept('GET', '/api/events').as('events'); cy.visit('/dashboard'); cy.get('@events.all').should('have.length', 3)`. The dashboard fires three event requests after a 200 ms delay. `cy.get('@events.all')` resolves at the moment it is evaluated — the alias store is empty at that point, yielding `[]`. The `.should('have.length', 3)` retries the assertion but `cy.get('@events.all')` re-evaluates each retry and keeps returning `[]` because the underlying query is synchronous. WHY: `cy.get('@events.all')` reads the alias store synchronously at query time — it is not a network listener. Fix: always precede `cy.get('@alias.all')` with the appropriate number of `cy.wait('@events')` calls to block until all expected requests have arrived, then assert the count.
