## Cycle 58 — 2026-05-14

### Patterns

**Pattern 613** — `cy.intercept()` Request Body Mutation via `req.body`
```typescript
// Intercept a POST and rewrite the request body before it reaches the server.
// Useful for injecting tracking IDs or normalising test payloads without
// touching application source code.
cy.intercept('POST', '/api/orders', (req) => {
  // Mutate req.body — Cypress serialises the modified value automatically
  req.body = {
    ...req.body,
    testRunId: Cypress.env('TEST_RUN_ID') ?? 'local',
    source: 'e2e',
  };
  // Do NOT call req.reply() — let it continue to the real server
}).as('createOrder');

cy.visit('/checkout');
cy.get('[data-cy="place-order"]').click();
cy.wait('@createOrder').then(({ request }) => {
  expect(request.body).to.have.property('testRunId');
  expect(request.body).to.have.property('source', 'e2e');
});
```
Tradeoff: Mutating `req.body` only works when the content type is JSON or URL-encoded. For multipart/form-data or binary uploads the body is a `Uint8Array` and must be reconstructed manually. Also, mutating the body changes what the real server receives — use this only in environments where idempotent seeding is safe, or combine with a `req.reply()` stub to avoid hitting the real server.

---

**Pattern 614** — Aliased `cy.intercept()` Array Wait for Parallel Requests
```typescript
// Wait for multiple independent requests that fire in parallel after a
// single user action (e.g. a dashboard load that fetches stats, user info,
// and recent items simultaneously).
cy.intercept('GET', '/api/stats').as('stats');
cy.intercept('GET', '/api/user').as('user');
cy.intercept('GET', '/api/recent').as('recent');

cy.visit('/dashboard');

// Pass an array of aliases — cy.wait() resolves only after ALL three respond
cy.wait(['@stats', '@user', '@recent']).then((interceptions) => {
  const [statsInt, userInt, recentInt] = interceptions;
  expect(statsInt.response?.statusCode).to.eq(200);
  expect(userInt.response?.body).to.have.property('id');
  expect(recentInt.response?.body).to.be.an('array');
});

// Now the dashboard is guaranteed to be fully populated
cy.get('[data-cy="stats-widget"]').should('be.visible');
cy.get('[data-cy="welcome-msg"]').should('contain', 'Alice');
```
Tradeoff: `cy.wait(arrayOfAliases)` resolves when each alias has been matched at least once. If any single request fires more than once (pagination, polling), only the first match is consumed. Use `.times` on the intercept and index into the returned array if you need to assert on a specific occurrence. Also note that the order of the returned interceptions array matches the order of the aliases array, not request arrival order.

---

**Pattern 615** — `cy.fixture()` with TypeScript Generics for Type-Safe Test Data
```typescript
// cypress/fixtures/product.json
// { "id": "p1", "name": "Widget", "price": 9.99, "stock": 100 }

// cypress/support/types.ts
export interface Product {
  id: string;
  name: string;
  price: number;
  stock: number;
}

// In a spec — cy.fixture() returns Cypress.Chainable<unknown> by default.
// Provide a generic to get a typed subject throughout the chain.
cy.fixture<Product>('product').then((product) => {
  // TypeScript now knows `product` is Product — autocompletion works
  cy.intercept('GET', `/api/products/${product.id}`, { body: product }).as('getProduct');
  cy.visit(`/products/${product.id}`);
  cy.wait('@getProduct');
  cy.get('[data-cy="product-name"]').should('have.text', product.name);
  cy.get('[data-cy="product-price"]').should('contain', product.price.toFixed(2));
});

// Alternatively, alias for reuse across tests
beforeEach(() => {
  cy.fixture<Product>('product').as('product');
});

it('shows product details', function () {
  // Access via `this` inside function() — NOT arrow function
  const product = this.product as Product;
  cy.get('[data-cy="product-name"]').should('have.text', product.name);
});
```
Tradeoff: The `this.fixture` alias pattern requires `function()` syntax (not arrow functions) because `this` is bound by Mocha's context. Teams using arrow functions everywhere must switch to `cy.fixture().then()` instead. Also, fixtures are loaded fresh each test — mutations in `.then()` are not persisted between tests.

---

**Pattern 616** — `cy.intercept()` `statusCode` + `headers` Response Override
```typescript
// Force specific HTTP error states to test error-boundary UI, retry logic,
// and user-facing error messages without needing the server to fail.

// Test a 429 rate-limit banner
cy.intercept('POST', '/api/search', {
  statusCode: 429,
  headers: { 'Retry-After': '30' },
  body: { error: 'rate_limit_exceeded', retryAfter: 30 },
}).as('rateLimited');

cy.visit('/search');
cy.get('[data-cy="search-input"]').type('cypress');
cy.get('[data-cy="search-submit"]').click();

cy.wait('@rateLimited');
cy.get('[data-cy="rate-limit-banner"]')
  .should('be.visible')
  .and('contain', '30 seconds');

// Test a 503 with retry — verify the app retries after a configured delay
let callCount = 0;
cy.intercept('GET', '/api/status', (req) => {
  callCount++;
  if (callCount === 1) {
    req.reply({ statusCode: 503, body: { error: 'unavailable' } });
  } else {
    req.reply({ statusCode: 200, body: { status: 'ok' } });
  }
}).as('statusCheck');
```
Tradeoff: Using a closure variable like `callCount` is fragile in parallelised CI because each spec runs in its own browser process — the closure is not shared. For stateful stubbing across multiple requests, prefer `cy.intercept()` with the `times` option paired with a second unconditional intercept to simulate the recovery state cleanly without shared mutable state.

---

**Pattern 617** — Custom Cypress Command with TypeScript Declaration Merging
```typescript
// cypress/support/commands.ts
Cypress.Commands.add(
  'fillForm',
  (fields: Record<string, string>) => {
    Object.entries(fields).forEach(([name, value]) => {
      cy.get(`[data-cy="${name}"]`).clear().type(value);
    });
  }
);

Cypress.Commands.add(
  'assertToast',
  (message: string, variant: 'success' | 'error' | 'info' = 'success') => {
    cy.get(`[data-cy="toast"][data-variant="${variant}"]`, { timeout: 8_000 })
      .should('be.visible')
      .and('contain.text', message);
  }
);

// cypress/support/index.d.ts  (or add to cypress.d.ts)
declare global {
  namespace Cypress {
    interface Chainable {
      fillForm(fields: Record<string, string>): Chainable<void>;
      assertToast(message: string, variant?: 'success' | 'error' | 'info'): Chainable<void>;
    }
  }
}

// Usage in a spec
cy.fillForm({ username: 'alice', email: 'alice@example.com' });
cy.get('[data-cy="submit"]').click();
cy.assertToast('Profile updated', 'success');
```
Tradeoff: Declaration merging in `cypress/support/index.d.ts` is picked up by TypeScript only when `tsconfig.json` includes the `cypress` directory or `types: ["cypress"]` is listed in `compilerOptions.types`. Projects that scope their tsconfig strictly must add an explicit `include` path or use a project reference to avoid "Property 'fillForm' does not exist on type Chainable" errors at compile time.

---

**Pattern 618** — `cy.spy()` on Window Methods for Analytics Verification
```typescript
// Verify that the application fires the correct analytics event without
// needing a real analytics endpoint — spy on the window method directly.
cy.visit('/products/p1', {
  onBeforeLoad(win) {
    // Spy on analytics before the page script runs so we capture all calls
    cy.spy(win, 'gtag').as('gtag');
    cy.spy(win, 'dataLayer' in win
      ? 'dataLayer'
      : 'gtag'               // fallback if dataLayer not initialised yet
    );
  },
});

cy.get('[data-cy="add-to-cart"]').click();

// Assert the specific gtag event was fired with correct parameters
cy.get('@gtag').should('have.been.calledWithMatch',
  'event',
  'add_to_cart',
  Cypress.sinon.match({
    currency: 'USD',
    value: Cypress.sinon.match.number,
    items: Cypress.sinon.match.array,
  })
);

// Assert call count — not just that it was called at all
cy.get('@gtag').its('callCount').should('be.gte', 1);
```
Tradeoff: `cy.spy()` wraps the existing method — it calls through to the real implementation. If the real `gtag` makes a network call, those calls still fire during tests. Use `cy.stub()` instead of `cy.spy()` when you want to suppress the actual analytics call while still asserting the arguments. Also note that `cy.spy()` / `cy.stub()` are synchronous but their sinon assertions are wrapped in a Cypress-aware adapter that enables retry-ability via `.should()`.

---

**Pattern 619** — `cy.stub()` for Third-Party SDK Side Effects
```typescript
// Stub window.Stripe to prevent real Stripe SDK initialisation during CT
// and assert the correct publishable key is used.

cy.stub(win, 'Stripe').as('stripeInit').returns({
  elements: cy.stub().returns({
    create: cy.stub().returns({
      mount: cy.stub(),
      on: cy.stub(),
    }),
  }),
  confirmCardPayment: cy.stub().resolves({ paymentIntent: { status: 'succeeded' } }),
});

cy.visit('/checkout');

// Assert Stripe was initialised with the correct public key
cy.get('@stripeInit').should(
  'have.been.calledWith',
  Cypress.env('STRIPE_PK')
);

// Assert the card element was mounted into the expected container
cy.get('@stripeInit').invoke('returnValues.0.elements')
  .its('create')
  .should('have.been.calledWith', 'card', Cypress.sinon.match.object);
```
Tradeoff: Deeply nested stub chains (stub returning stubs returning stubs) become brittle when the SDK's internal API changes — a patch release can rename an internal method and silently break the stub tree. Pin the SDK version in `package.json` with an exact version (`"stripe": "3.47.0"` not `"^3.47.0"`) when using this pattern. Alternatively, wrap the SDK in a thin service module and stub the service instead of the SDK directly.

---

**Pattern 620** — `cy.origin()` Cookie Pass-through for SSO Redirect Flows
```typescript
// For SSO flows where the IdP sets a cookie on its own domain and then
// redirects back to the app, cy.origin() lets you assert on the IdP
// domain before the redirect and inject the cookie for the app domain.

const SSO_DOMAIN = Cypress.env('SSO_DOMAIN') as string; // e.g. 'sso.example.com'

cy.visit('/login');
cy.get('[data-cy="sso-login"]').click();

cy.origin(SSO_DOMAIN, { args: { user: 'alice@example.com', pass: Cypress.env('SSO_PASS') } },
  ({ user, pass }) => {
    cy.get('#username').type(user);
    cy.get('#password').type(pass);
    cy.get('#submit').click();
    // Assert the IdP set its session cookie before redirect
    cy.getCookie('idp_session').should('exist');
  }
);

// Back in the app origin after redirect
cy.url().should('include', '/dashboard');
cy.getCookie('app_session').should('exist');

// Wrap in cy.session() for caching across tests
export function loginViaSso(user: string): void {
  cy.session(['sso', user], () => {
    // ... the above flow
  }, { cacheAcrossSpecs: true });
}
```
Tradeoff: `cy.origin()` serialises `args` via the structured clone algorithm — functions, class instances, and symbols are silently dropped. Always use plain objects/primitives in `args`. Also, `cy.intercept()` routes defined outside the `cy.origin()` block do not apply inside it — register any stubs needed on the IdP domain inside the `cy.origin()` callback.

---

**Pattern 621** — `cy.clock()` Pre-Visit Date Freezing for Time-Sensitive UI
```typescript
// Freeze time BEFORE cy.visit() so that all module-level timers,
// React useEffect intervals, and Date constructors use the frozen clock.

const FROZEN_DATE = new Date('2026-03-01T09:00:00.000Z');

cy.clock(FROZEN_DATE);          // freeze before visit — critical ordering

cy.visit('/dashboard');

// Test a "days until renewal" counter that calculates from new Date()
// Without clock, this would vary day-to-day and fail on certain dates
cy.get('[data-cy="renewal-countdown"]').should('have.text', '30 days');

// Advance time by 24 hours to test the counter decrements
cy.tick(24 * 60 * 60 * 1000);
cy.get('[data-cy="renewal-countdown"]').should('have.text', '29 days');

// Advance past the renewal date to test the "expired" state
cy.tick(30 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000);
cy.get('[data-cy="renewal-banner"]').should('be.visible').and('contain', 'expired');

cy.clock().invoke('restore'); // restore real clock at end of test
```
Tradeoff: `cy.clock()` freezes `Date`, `setTimeout`, `setInterval`, and `clearTimeout`/`clearInterval`. It does NOT freeze `performance.now()`, `requestAnimationFrame`, or `queueMicrotask`. Animation libraries and React's `useTransition` that rely on `performance.now()` for scheduling will still use real time. Combine with `cy.stub()` on `performance.now` if animations under test use it for timing.

---

**Pattern 622** — `Commands.addQuery()` for Retry-able Shadow DOM Piercing
```typescript
// cy.get() with {includeShadowDom: true} retries, but when you need
// to pierce multiple nested shadow roots, addQuery() gives full
// retry-able control.

Cypress.Commands.addQuery(
  'shadowFind',
  function shadowFind(selector: string) {
    // The outer function sets up the query — runs once
    const getFn = this.get('body');          // seed query
    return (subject: JQuery<HTMLElement>) => {
      // Inner function is retried until assertion passes or timeout
      const host = subject.find(selector)[0];
      if (!host) return subject.find(selector); // return empty jQuery for retry
      const shadow = host.shadowRoot;
      if (!shadow) return subject.find(selector);
      return Cypress.$(shadow);
    };
  }
);

// Type augmentation
declare global {
  namespace Cypress {
    interface Chainable {
      shadowFind(selector: string): Chainable<JQuery<HTMLElement>>;
    }
  }
}

// Usage — retries until the shadow root element is present
cy.get('my-custom-element').shadowFind('[data-cy="inner-btn"]')
  .should('be.visible')
  .click();
```
Tradeoff: `Commands.addQuery()` requires the double-function pattern — the outer setup function runs once, the inner subject transformer is retried. If you accidentally place side effects (like `cy.log()`) in the inner function, they execute on every retry iteration, flooding the command log. Place all logging and setup in the outer function.

---

**Pattern 623** — Declarative `cy.intercept()` Fixture Routing Table
```typescript
// Instead of registering individual intercepts per test, define a routing
// table in beforeEach that maps URL patterns to fixture files, keeping
// specs clean and fixtures easy to audit.

type RouteEntry = { method?: string; url: string; fixture: string; alias: string };

const API_ROUTES: RouteEntry[] = [
  { url: '/api/user',       fixture: 'user.json',       alias: 'getUser'    },
  { url: '/api/products',   fixture: 'products.json',   alias: 'getProducts'},
  { url: '/api/cart',       fixture: 'cart.json',       alias: 'getCart'    },
  { url: '/api/categories', fixture: 'categories.json', alias: 'getCategories'},
];

function stubApiRoutes(overrides: Partial<Record<string, unknown>> = {}) {
  API_ROUTES.forEach(({ method = 'GET', url, fixture, alias }) => {
    if (overrides[alias]) {
      cy.intercept(method, url, overrides[alias]).as(alias);
    } else {
      cy.intercept(method, url, { fixture }).as(alias);
    }
  });
}

beforeEach(() => stubApiRoutes());

it('shows cart item count from fixture', () => {
  cy.visit('/shop');
  cy.wait('@getCart');
  cy.get('[data-cy="cart-count"]').should('have.text', '3');
});

it('handles empty products gracefully', () => {
  stubApiRoutes({ getProducts: { body: { items: [], total: 0 } } });
  cy.visit('/shop');
  cy.get('[data-cy="empty-state"]').should('be.visible');
});
```
Tradeoff: Routing tables centralise fixture management but create implicit coupling — a test that passes because the fixture has `3` cart items will silently break if someone edits `cart.json` for a different test's needs. Use a shared fixture only for "happy path" defaults; create dedicated test-scoped fixtures for edge cases. The `overrides` pattern mitigates this for one-off divergences.

---

**Pattern 624** — `cy.task()` for Database Seed and Teardown
```typescript
// cypress/plugins/db-tasks.ts  (registered in defineConfig)
import { Pool } from 'pg';

const pool = new Pool({ connectionString: process.env.TEST_DATABASE_URL });

export const dbTasks = {
  async seedUser(user: { email: string; role: string }): Promise<{ id: string }> {
    const { rows } = await pool.query(
      `INSERT INTO users (email, role, created_at)
       VALUES ($1, $2, NOW())
       ON CONFLICT (email) DO UPDATE SET role = EXCLUDED.role
       RETURNING id`,
      [user.email, user.role]
    );
    return { id: rows[0].id };
  },
  async clearUsers(): Promise<null> {    // MUST return null, not undefined
    await pool.query(`DELETE FROM users WHERE email LIKE '%@test.example.com'`);
    return null;
  },
};

// cypress.config.ts
import { dbTasks } from './cypress/plugins/db-tasks';
export default defineConfig({
  e2e: {
    setupNodeEvents(on) {
      on('task', dbTasks);
    },
  },
});

// In a spec
beforeEach(() => {
  cy.task<{ id: string }>('seedUser', { email: 'bob@test.example.com', role: 'admin' })
    .then(({ id }) => cy.wrap(id).as('userId'));
});
afterEach(() => cy.task('clearUsers'));
```
Tradeoff: `cy.task()` runs in the Node.js plugin process, not the browser. The task must return a JSON-serialisable value or `null` — returning `undefined` causes Cypress to throw "cy.task('clearUsers') timed out". Database connections in plugin tasks persist for the entire Cypress process lifetime; use a connection pool rather than creating new connections per task to avoid exhausting the DB connection limit in large test suites.

---

**Pattern 625** — `cy.request()` JWT Injection for Fast API Authentication
```typescript
// Bypass the UI login flow entirely for tests that only need an
// authenticated API state — fetch a JWT via cy.request() and inject it
// into localStorage/cookies before visiting the app.

function apiLogin(email: string, password: string): Cypress.Chainable<string> {
  return cy.request<{ token: string }>({
    method: 'POST',
    url: `${Cypress.env('API_BASE_URL')}/auth/login`,
    body: { email, password },
    failOnStatusCode: true,
  }).its('body.token');
}

Cypress.Commands.add('loginByApi', (email: string, password: string) => {
  cy.session(['api-login', email], () => {
    apiLogin(email, password).then((token) => {
      // Inject into localStorage so the app's auth module picks it up
      window.localStorage.setItem('auth_token', token);
      // Or set a cookie if the app expects one
      cy.setCookie('auth_token', token, {
        httpOnly: false,
        secure: Cypress.env('IS_SECURE') === 'true',
      });
    });
  }, {
    validate() {
      cy.window().its('localStorage').invoke('getItem', 'auth_token').should('exist');
    },
  });
});

// Usage
beforeEach(() => cy.loginByApi('alice@example.com', Cypress.env('ALICE_PASSWORD')));
```
Tradeoff: JWT injection bypasses SSO, MFA, and CSRF protection — it's valid only when testing application features that require auth, not the auth flow itself. The token expiry must match `cy.session()` cache lifetime; if the API issues short-lived tokens (< 15 min), add server-side clock override or use a long-lived test token issued specifically for the CI environment.

---

**Pattern 626** — `cy.intercept()` Network Latency Simulation
```typescript
// Simulate slow networks to test loading states, skeleton screens, and
// timeout error UI without a real slow connection.

cy.intercept('GET', '/api/feed', (req) => {
  req.on('response', (res) => {
    // Delay the response by 3 seconds while it's in-flight
    res.setDelay(3_000);
  });
}).as('slowFeed');

cy.visit('/home');

// Assert loading skeleton is shown immediately
cy.get('[data-cy="feed-skeleton"]').should('be.visible');

// Wait for the delayed response to arrive
cy.wait('@slowFeed');

// Assert skeleton is replaced by real content
cy.get('[data-cy="feed-skeleton"]').should('not.exist');
cy.get('[data-cy="feed-item"]').should('have.length.gte', 1);

// Simulate timeout: throttle beyond the app's configured request timeout
cy.intercept('GET', '/api/feed', (req) => {
  req.on('response', (res) => {
    res.setDelay(11_000); // exceeds 10 s app timeout
  });
}).as('timedOutFeed');

cy.get('[data-cy="timeout-error"]').should('be.visible');
```
Tradeoff: `res.setDelay()` is applied after the server responds — the request still hits the real server (or stub). The delay counts against Cypress's `responseTimeout` (default 30 s). Setting a delay beyond `responseTimeout` causes Cypress itself to time out the wait, not the application. Configure `responseTimeout` in `cypress.config.ts` to be higher than the maximum simulated delay when testing timeout-error UI.

---

**Pattern 627** — Component Testing with `cy.mount()` and Slot/Children Assertions
```typescript
// cypress/component/Card.cy.tsx
import { Card } from '../../src/components/Card';
import { CardHeader, CardBody, CardFooter } from '../../src/components/Card';

it('renders header, body, and footer slots', () => {
  cy.mount(
    <Card>
      <CardHeader>My Title</CardHeader>
      <CardBody>Content here</CardBody>
      <CardFooter>
        <button data-cy="action">Save</button>
      </CardFooter>
    </Card>
  );

  cy.get('[data-cy="card-header"]').should('have.text', 'My Title');
  cy.get('[data-cy="card-body"]').should('contain.text', 'Content here');
  cy.get('[data-cy="action"]').should('be.visible').click();
});

it('applies variant class when variant prop is passed', () => {
  cy.mount(<Card variant="danger"><CardBody>Error</CardBody></Card>);
  cy.get('[data-cy="card"]').should('have.class', 'card--danger');
});

// Test with Tailwind class assertions — use have.css for computed values
it('renders compact variant with reduced padding', () => {
  cy.mount(<Card compact><CardBody>Dense</CardBody></Card>);
  cy.get('[data-cy="card"]')
    .should('have.class', 'p-2')  // Tailwind class present
    .and('have.css', 'padding', '8px'); // computed value verification
});
```
Tradeoff: Component tests run in an isolated DOM — global CSS, router context, and theme providers are absent unless explicitly mounted. Always wrap components that depend on context (theme, i18n, router) in their respective providers inside `cy.mount()`. Asserting on Tailwind utility class names is fragile — prefer asserting on computed CSS values (`have.css`) which are implementation-independent.

---

### Community Gotchas

**G376** — `cy.intercept()` wildcard patterns match query strings unexpectedly — `'/api/users*'` matches `/api/users-admin` as well as `/api/users?page=2`
Why this matters: Developers who write `cy.intercept('GET', '/api/users*')` expecting to match `/api/users` and `/api/users?page=2` also inadvertently match `/api/users-admin`, `/api/users-export`, and any other path with `users` as a prefix. This causes unrelated endpoints to be stubbed silently, producing test results that appear correct locally but fail against a real API.
Fix: Use a minimatch-style pattern with a question mark for the query string boundary (`'/api/users?*'`) or switch to a `RegExp` route matcher (`/\/api\/users(\?.*)?$/`) which gives precise control over what the pattern matches. When the URL has no query string, match the exact path string rather than a wildcard suffix.

---

**G377** — `cy.wait('@alias')` on a POST that triggers a page navigation hangs indefinitely — the intercept alias is consumed by Cypress but the navigation happens before the response is fully read
Why this matters: When clicking a "Submit" button causes the server to respond with a `302 redirect` and the browser immediately navigates away, Cypress registers the request match for the alias but the response arrives at a different navigation point. The `cy.wait('@alias')` call can hang until the default 5 s timeout because the response object is attached to the pre-navigation request context.
Fix: Before calling `cy.wait('@alias')` after a form submission that redirects, add `cy.url().should('include', '/expected-path')` first to confirm the navigation completed. Alternatively, intercept the redirected GET request with its own alias and wait on that instead. This ensures Cypress's network layer has a stable page context when it finalises the alias.

---

**G378** — Cypress `baseUrl` is not automatically applied inside `cy.origin()` blocks — `cy.visit('/path')` inside `cy.origin()` throws "baseUrl not set" because the origin context has its own isolated Cypress instance
Why this matters: Developers who set `baseUrl` in `cypress.config.ts` expect `cy.visit('/dashboard')` to work everywhere. Inside a `cy.origin('https://sso.example.com', ...)` callback, the cy instance is scoped to that origin — `cy.visit('/path')` will attempt to resolve against the origin domain, not the app's `baseUrl`. If the path does not exist on the SSO domain, the visit throws or navigates to the wrong URL.
Fix: Always pass fully qualified URLs inside `cy.origin()` blocks: `cy.visit('https://sso.example.com/authorize')`. Pass the full URL via the `args` object if it needs to be dynamic: `cy.origin(domain, { args: { redirectUrl: `${domain}/authorize` } }, ({ redirectUrl }) => { cy.visit(redirectUrl); })`.

---

**G379** — Calling `cy.get()` inside `cy.should(callback)` creates a nested Cypress chain that throws "Cypress detected you returned a promise" — the callback must be synchronous
Why this matters: A developer tries to assert on a sibling element inside a `.should()` callback by writing `cy.get('[data-cy="status"]').should(($el) => { cy.get('[data-cy="label"]').should('exist'); })`. The inner `cy.get()` enqueues a new command on the Cypress queue asynchronously, which Cypress detects as an illegal promise-like return inside a synchronous callback.
Fix: Inside `.should(callback)` assertions, use only synchronous jQuery methods on `$el` and native `expect()` assertions. To assert on a related element simultaneously, chain with `.and()` using a different query or restructure the test to use two separate `cy.get()` chains outside the callback. If you need to check multiple elements atomically, use `cy.get()` chains independently — Cypress processes them in declared order.

---

**G380** — `cy.stub()` on a module export that is called at import time (e.g., a module-level `setInterval`) cannot be intercepted because the call has already executed before the stub is registered
Why this matters: Some application modules run initialization code at import time — for example, `const poller = setInterval(fetchStatus, 5000)`. By the time `cy.stub(win, 'setInterval')` is called in a test's `beforeEach`, the module has already been evaluated and the real `setInterval` was invoked. The stub has no effect on that existing timer.
Fix: Use `cy.clock()` before `cy.visit()` to replace `setInterval` at the browser level before any application scripts execute. For Component Testing, use `cy.clock()` before `cy.mount()`. If the goal is to prevent a specific module's polling, refactor the module to accept an injectable clock dependency (dependency injection pattern) that can be replaced in tests without needing `cy.stub()` on the window object.

## Cycle 59 — 2026-05-14

### Patterns

**Pattern 561** — `cy.intercept()` Request Body Mutation via `req.body` for Downstream Contract Testing

When testing how an application responds to mutated server data mid-flight, use the `req.body` setter inside a `cy.intercept()` handler to replace the request payload before it reaches the server. This validates that the client correctly handles unexpected server-side transformations without modifying the actual server.

```typescript
// cypress/e2e/checkout.cy.ts
it('shows validation error when server strips required fields', () => {
  cy.intercept('POST', '/api/orders', (req) => {
    // Mutate request body to simulate a server-side field strip
    const body = req.body as Record<string, unknown>;
    delete body['shippingAddress'];
    req.body = body;
  }).as('createOrder');

  cy.visit('/checkout');
  cy.get('[data-cy="shipping-name"]').type('Jane Doe');
  cy.get('[data-cy="shipping-street"]').type('123 Main St');
  cy.get('[data-cy="place-order"]').click();

  cy.wait('@createOrder').then(({ request }) => {
    expect(request.body).not.to.have.property('shippingAddress');
  });

  // App should show a graceful fallback error when required field missing
  cy.get('[data-cy="order-error"]')
    .should('be.visible')
    .and('contain.text', 'Missing shipping information');
});
```
Tradeoff: Mutating `req.body` only works for JSON and form-encoded bodies — binary or multipart payloads require the raw buffer approach (`req.body` as `Buffer`). The mutation happens before the request is sent, so the real server never sees the original body; combine with `req.continue()` when you still want a real server response after mutation.

---

**Pattern 562** — `cy.wait([alias1, alias2])` Array Form for Parallel Request Assertion

When a single user action triggers multiple concurrent XHR/fetch requests, use the array form of `cy.wait()` to block until all aliases are satisfied. This avoids flaky sequential waits and provides typed access to each interception object for independent assertions.

```typescript
// cypress/e2e/dashboard.cy.ts
it('loads dashboard data from multiple endpoints simultaneously', () => {
  cy.intercept('GET', '/api/user/profile').as('userProfile');
  cy.intercept('GET', '/api/notifications*').as('notifications');
  cy.intercept('GET', '/api/activity-feed*').as('activityFeed');

  cy.visit('/dashboard');

  cy.wait(['@userProfile', '@notifications', '@activityFeed']).then(
    ([profileInterception, notifInterception, feedInterception]) => {
      expect(profileInterception.response?.statusCode).to.eq(200);
      expect(notifInterception.response?.body).to.have.property('items');
      expect(feedInterception.response?.body).to.have.property('events');
    }
  );

  cy.get('[data-cy="profile-name"]').should('be.visible');
  cy.get('[data-cy="notification-badge"]').should('exist');
  cy.get('[data-cy="activity-list"]').should('have.length.greaterThan', 0);
});
```
Tradeoff: The array form resolves only after ALL listed aliases fire — if any one request is conditionally made (e.g., notifications only fetched when unread count > 0), the wait will time out. Use individual `cy.wait('@alias')` with conditional guards when not all requests are guaranteed.

---

**Pattern 563** — `cy.fixture()` with TypeScript Generic for Type-Safe Test Data

Annotate `cy.fixture()` calls with a TypeScript generic to propagate the fixture type through the chain. This eliminates `unknown` types in test bodies and provides autocomplete for fixture properties during development.

```typescript
// cypress/fixtures/user.json  →  { "id": 1, "email": "test@example.com", "role": "admin" }

// cypress/support/types.ts
export interface UserFixture {
  id: number;
  email: string;
  role: 'admin' | 'editor' | 'viewer';
}

// cypress/e2e/user-profile.cy.ts
import type { UserFixture } from '../support/types';

it('displays admin badge for admin users', () => {
  cy.fixture<UserFixture>('user').then((user) => {
    // `user` is typed as UserFixture — autocomplete + type safety
    cy.intercept('GET', '/api/me', { body: user }).as('getMe');

    cy.visit('/profile');
    cy.wait('@getMe');

    if (user.role === 'admin') {
      cy.get('[data-cy="admin-badge"]').should('be.visible');
    }
    cy.get('[data-cy="user-email"]').should('contain.text', user.email);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: The generic annotation is only a compile-time cast — Cypress does not validate that the fixture file matches the declared type at runtime. Add a Zod schema parse inside the `.then()` callback (`UserFixtureSchema.parse(user)`) if runtime validation is required in CI.

---

**Pattern 564** — `cy.spy()` on `window` Methods for Third-Party Analytics Verification

Spy on `window.analytics.track` (or any window-level analytics SDK method) before visiting the page so that every call made by the application is intercepted and inspectable. This tests the analytics contract without any network overhead.

```typescript
// cypress/e2e/analytics.cy.ts
it('fires a "page_view" event when the dashboard loads', () => {
  cy.visit('/dashboard', {
    onBeforeLoad(win) {
      // Stub the analytics object so it exists even if SDK is blocked by ad-blocker
      win.analytics = { track: cy.stub().as('analyticsTrack') } as unknown as SegmentAnalytics;
    },
  });

  cy.get('[data-cy="dashboard-loaded"]').should('be.visible');

  cy.get('@analyticsTrack')
    .should('have.been.calledWith', 'page_view', Cypress.sinon.match({
      page: 'dashboard',
      userId: Cypress.sinon.match.string,
    }));
});

it('fires "add_to_cart" event on product click', () => {
  cy.visit('/products', {
    onBeforeLoad(win) {
      win.analytics = { track: cy.stub().as('analyticsTrack') } as unknown as SegmentAnalytics;
    },
  });

  cy.get('[data-cy="product-card"]').first().find('[data-cy="add-to-cart"]').click();

  cy.get('@analyticsTrack')
    .should('have.been.calledOnce')
    .and('have.been.calledWithMatch', 'add_to_cart');
});
```
Tradeoff: The stub replaces the real SDK — actual network calls to the analytics endpoint are never made. This is intentional for unit-level event testing, but add a separate smoke test that asserts `window.analytics` is loaded from the real CDN in a staging environment to validate that the SDK itself initializes correctly.

---

**Pattern 565** — `cy.stub()` for Third-Party Payment SDK Side-Effect Suppression

When testing checkout flows, stub `window.Stripe` (or any payment SDK) to prevent real API calls, eliminate flakiness from SDK network dependencies, and control the card tokenization response deterministically.

```typescript
// cypress/support/stubs/stripe.ts
export function stubStripe(tokenId = 'tok_test_visa'): void {
  cy.visit('/checkout', {
    onBeforeLoad(win) {
      const mockToken = { id: tokenId, card: { last4: '4242', brand: 'Visa' } };

      const mockStripeInstance = {
        elements: cy.stub().returns({
          create: cy.stub().returns({
            mount: cy.stub(),
            on: cy.stub(),
            unmount: cy.stub(),
          }),
        }),
        createToken: cy.stub().as('createToken').resolves({ token: mockToken }),
        confirmCardPayment: cy.stub().as('confirmPayment').resolves({ paymentIntent: { status: 'succeeded' } }),
      };

      (win as Window & { Stripe?: unknown }).Stripe = cy.stub().returns(mockStripeInstance);
    },
  });
}

// cypress/e2e/checkout.cy.ts
it('completes checkout with a valid card token', () => {
  stubStripe('tok_test_visa');
  cy.get('[data-cy="pay-now"]').click();
  cy.get('@confirmPayment').should('have.been.calledOnce');
  cy.get('[data-cy="order-confirmation"]').should('be.visible');
});
```
Tradeoff: Stubbing the payment SDK means the integration contract with Stripe is only tested in end-to-end staging runs. Keep a separate `cypress/e2e/staging/` suite (excluded from unit CI) that uses Stripe test cards against the real SDK to catch API version mismatches.

---

**Pattern 566** — `cy.origin()` Cookie Pass-Through for Subdomain SSO Redirect Flows

When an application SSO login flow redirects through a separate subdomain (e.g., `auth.example.com`) before returning to the app, use `cy.origin()` to perform actions on the auth subdomain and pass the resulting session cookie back to the main app domain.

```typescript
// cypress/support/auth.ts
export function loginViaSso(username: string, password: string): void {
  const authDomain = 'https://auth.example.com';
  const appDomain = Cypress.config('baseUrl') as string;

  cy.visit(`${appDomain}/login`);
  // App redirects to SSO — now in auth domain context
  cy.origin(authDomain, { args: { username, password } }, ({ username, password }) => {
    cy.get('[data-cy="sso-username"]').type(username);
    cy.get('[data-cy="sso-password"]').type(password);
    cy.get('[data-cy="sso-submit"]').click();
    // Auth domain sets session cookie and redirects back to app
    cy.url().should('include', 'callback');
  });

  // Back on app domain — session cookie should be present
  cy.getCookie('session_token').should('exist');
  cy.url().should('include', '/dashboard');
}

// Usage in test
it('logs in via SSO and lands on dashboard', () => {
  loginViaSso('user@example.com', 'password123');
  cy.get('[data-cy="welcome-message"]').should('be.visible');
});
```
Tradeoff: `cy.origin()` callbacks are serialized and evaluated in a separate JavaScript context — closures that reference outer-scope variables will silently receive `undefined`. Always use the `args` parameter to pass data into the callback, and only pass JSON-serializable values (no class instances, no functions).

---

**Pattern 567** — `cy.clock()` Pre-Visit Date Freezing for Time-Sensitive UI States

Call `cy.clock()` with a specific timestamp BEFORE `cy.visit()` so that every `new Date()`, `Date.now()`, `setTimeout`, and `setInterval` call made during page initialization uses the frozen time. This prevents test flakiness caused by day-boundary conditions or expiry logic.

```typescript
// cypress/e2e/subscription.cy.ts
it('shows "Trial expires today" banner when trial end date is today', () => {
  // Freeze time to a specific date before any page scripts run
  const frozenDate = new Date('2026-06-01T10:00:00Z').getTime();
  cy.clock(frozenDate, ['Date', 'setTimeout', 'setInterval']);

  cy.intercept('GET', '/api/subscription', {
    body: {
      plan: 'trial',
      trialEndsAt: '2026-06-01T23:59:59Z',  // same day as frozen time
    },
  }).as('getSubscription');

  cy.visit('/account');
  cy.wait('@getSubscription');

  cy.get('[data-cy="trial-banner"]')
    .should('be.visible')
    .and('contain.text', 'Trial expires today');
});

it('shows "X days remaining" when trial has future end date', () => {
  const frozenDate = new Date('2026-05-25T10:00:00Z').getTime();
  cy.clock(frozenDate);

  cy.intercept('GET', '/api/subscription', {
    body: { plan: 'trial', trialEndsAt: '2026-06-01T23:59:59Z' },
  }).as('getSubscription');

  cy.visit('/account');
  cy.wait('@getSubscription');

  cy.get('[data-cy="trial-banner"]').should('contain.text', '7 days remaining');
});
```
Tradeoff: `cy.clock()` with `['Date']` only freezes `Date` — it does not stop real wall-clock time for network timeouts or Cypress's own command timeouts. Passing `['setTimeout', 'setInterval']` as well freezes those, but then `cy.tick(ms)` is required to advance animations or debounced logic. Avoid freezing `performance.now()` — Cypress internally relies on it for timeout tracking and freezing it can cause spurious test failures.

**Pattern 568** — `Commands.addQuery()` Typed Retry-Able Shadow DOM Piercing Query

Implement a custom retry-able query that traverses a shadow DOM tree using `Cypress.Commands.addQuery()`. Unlike `cy.get()`, this query re-evaluates its traversal on every retry tick, making it safe to use against components that attach shadow roots asynchronously.

```typescript
// cypress/support/commands.ts
declare global {
  namespace Cypress {
    interface Chainable {
      shadowGet(cssSelector: string): Chainable<JQuery>;
    }
  }
}

Cypress.Commands.addQuery('shadowGet', function shadowGet(selector: string) {
  // The outer function runs once; the inner function is retried
  return (subject: JQuery | Document) => {
    const root = subject instanceof Document ? subject.body : subject[0];

    // Traverse shadow roots depth-first to find the element
    function queryShadow(node: Element | ShadowRoot): Element | null {
      const found = (node as Element).querySelector?.(selector);
      if (found) return found;
      const children = node.querySelectorAll('*');
      for (const child of Array.from(children)) {
        if (child.shadowRoot) {
          const deep = queryShadow(child.shadowRoot);
          if (deep) return deep;
        }
      }
      return null;
    }

    const el = queryShadow(root as Element);
    // Return empty jQuery if not found — retry-ability handles the wait
    return el ? Cypress.$(el) : Cypress.$();
  };
});

// Usage
it('interacts with a web component button inside shadow DOM', () => {
  cy.visit('/web-components-demo');
  cy.get('my-widget').shadowGet('[data-cy="widget-submit"]').click();
  cy.get('[data-cy="result"]').should('contain.text', 'Submitted');
});
```
Tradeoff: The double-function pattern (`addQuery` outer/inner) is mandatory — Cypress calls the inner function on every retry tick. If you collapse it into a single function, the query executes only once and does not retry. Shadow DOM traversal is O(n) over all elements — for deeply nested or very large shadow trees, consider caching the host element reference.

**Pattern 569** — Declarative `cy.intercept()` Fixture Routing Table for Multi-Endpoint Stubs

Define all network stubs as a declarative routing table at the top of a test file or in a `beforeEach`. This eliminates scattered `cy.intercept()` calls, makes it easy to see all mocked endpoints at a glance, and allows individual tests to override a specific route without repeating the others.

```typescript
// cypress/support/intercept-table.ts
type RouteEntry = {
  method: string;
  url: string;
  fixture?: string;
  body?: unknown;
  statusCode?: number;
  alias: string;
};

export function applyInterceptTable(routes: RouteEntry[]): void {
  routes.forEach(({ method, url, fixture, body, statusCode = 200, alias }) => {
    const response = fixture ? { fixture } : { body, statusCode };
    cy.intercept(method as Cypress.HttpMethod, url, response).as(alias);
  });
}

// cypress/e2e/product-catalog.cy.ts
import { applyInterceptTable } from '../support/intercept-table';

const ROUTES: Parameters<typeof applyInterceptTable>[0] = [
  { method: 'GET', url: '/api/categories',      fixture: 'categories.json',    alias: 'getCategories' },
  { method: 'GET', url: '/api/products*',        fixture: 'products.json',      alias: 'getProducts'   },
  { method: 'GET', url: '/api/user/cart',        fixture: 'cart-empty.json',    alias: 'getCart'       },
  { method: 'POST', url: '/api/user/cart/items', body: { success: true },        alias: 'addToCart'     },
];

beforeEach(() => {
  applyInterceptTable(ROUTES);
  cy.visit('/products');
});

it('displays all product categories in the sidebar', () => {
  cy.wait('@getCategories');
  cy.get('[data-cy="category-list"]').should('have.length.greaterThan', 0);
});

it('adds a product to the cart and updates badge', () => {
  cy.get('[data-cy="product-card"]').first().find('[data-cy="add-to-cart"]').click();
  cy.wait('@addToCart');
  cy.get('[data-cy="cart-badge"]').should('contain.text', '1');
});
```
Tradeoff: A shared routing table applied in `beforeEach` means every test in the file gets all stubs, even those that do not exercise every endpoint. This is acceptable for most cases, but if a test needs to assert that a specific endpoint is NOT called, move that intercept into the individual test body and define it without a default fixture.

**Pattern 570** — `cy.task()` Typed Registry Pattern with `null` Return Enforcement

Define all Cypress tasks in a strongly typed registry object and enforce that every task returns `null` (not `undefined`) when it has no meaningful return value. Returning `undefined` causes Cypress to throw a cryptic "task must not return undefined" error at runtime.

```typescript
// cypress/plugins/tasks.ts
import { db } from '../../src/lib/db';

interface TaskMap {
  'db:seedUser': (args: { email: string; role: string }) => Promise<null>;
  'db:clearUsers': () => Promise<null>;
  'db:getUserCount': () => Promise<number>;
}

export const tasks: TaskMap = {
  async 'db:seedUser'({ email, role }) {
    await db.user.upsert({
      where: { email },
      update: { role },
      create: { email, role },
    });
    return null;  // explicit null, never undefined
  },

  async 'db:clearUsers'() {
    await db.user.deleteMany({});
    return null;
  },

  async 'db:getUserCount'() {
    return await db.user.count();
  },
};

// cypress.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from 'cypress';
import { tasks } from './cypress/plugins/tasks';

export default defineConfig({
  e2e: {
    setupNodeEvents(on) {
      on('task', tasks);
    },
  },
});

// Usage in tests
it('shows empty state when no users exist', () => {
  cy.task('db:clearUsers');
  cy.visit('/admin/users');
  cy.get('[data-cy="empty-state"]').should('be.visible');
});
```
Tradeoff: Tasks run in the Node.js process (not the browser) — they can access databases, file systems, and environment variables freely, but cannot use `window` or DOM APIs. Keep tasks stateless and idempotent so they can safely run in parallel CI workers without conflicts.

**Pattern 571** — `cy.request()` Typed API Seeding Helper with Idempotent `afterEach` Teardown

Use `cy.request()` with a TypeScript generic to build strongly typed API seed helpers. Pair each seed call with an idempotent `afterEach` teardown to ensure test isolation even when a test fails mid-execution.

```typescript
// cypress/support/api-helpers.ts
export interface CreatedProduct {
  id: string;
  name: string;
  price: number;
}

export function createProduct(overrides: Partial<CreatedProduct> = {}): Cypress.Chainable<CreatedProduct> {
  return cy.request<CreatedProduct>({
    method: 'POST',
    url: '/api/admin/products',
    body: {
      name: `Test Product ${Date.now()}`,
      price: 29.99,
      category: 'test',
      ...overrides,
    },
    headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${Cypress.env('ADMIN_TOKEN')}` },
  }).its('body');
}

// cypress/e2e/product-edit.cy.ts
import { createProduct, type CreatedProduct } from '../support/api-helpers';

describe('Product editing', () => {
  let product: CreatedProduct;

  beforeEach(() => {
    createProduct({ name: 'Widget Pro' }).then((p) => { product = p; });
  });

  afterEach(() => {
    // Idempotent teardown — 404 is acceptable (already deleted or test failed before creation)
    if (product?.id) {
      cy.request({
        method: 'DELETE',
        url: `/api/admin/products/${product.id}`,
        headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${Cypress.env('ADMIN_TOKEN')}` },
        failOnStatusCode: false,
      });
    }
  });

  it('updates product name and reflects change in the listing', () => {
    cy.visit(`/admin/products/${product.id}/edit`);
    cy.get('[data-cy="product-name"]').clear().type('Widget Pro Deluxe');
    cy.get('[data-cy="save"]').click();
    cy.get('[data-cy="product-name-display"]').should('contain.text', 'Widget Pro Deluxe');
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `cy.request()` bypasses the browser — cookies set by `cy.session()` are not automatically included. Pass the auth token explicitly via `headers` or `auth` options. For full browser-based seeding with cookie auth, use `cy.visit()` + UI actions instead.

**Pattern 572** — `cy.intercept()` Response Delay Simulation with `res.setDelay()` for Loading State Verification

Use `res.setDelay(ms)` inside a `cy.intercept()` response handler to introduce artificial latency and verify that the application renders loading skeletons, spinners, and progress indicators correctly before the data arrives.

```typescript
// cypress/e2e/loading-states.cy.ts
it('shows skeleton loader during slow API response', () => {
  cy.intercept('GET', '/api/products*', (req) => {
    req.continue((res) => {
      res.setDelay(1500);  // delay response by 1.5 seconds
    });
  }).as('slowProducts');

  cy.visit('/products');

  // Immediately assert loading state is visible before response arrives
  cy.get('[data-cy="product-skeleton"]').should('be.visible');
  cy.get('[data-cy="product-list"]').should('not.exist');

  // After response arrives, assert real content replaces skeleton
  cy.wait('@slowProducts');
  cy.get('[data-cy="product-skeleton"]').should('not.exist');
  cy.get('[data-cy="product-list"]').should('be.visible');
});

it('shows error toast when API responds with 500', () => {
  cy.intercept('GET', '/api/products*', (req) => {
    req.continue((res) => {
      res.statusCode = 500;
      res.body = { error: 'Internal Server Error' };
    });
  }).as('failedProducts');

  cy.visit('/products');
  cy.wait('@failedProducts');

  cy.get('[data-cy="error-toast"]')
    .should('be.visible')
    .and('contain.text', 'Failed to load products');
});
```
Tradeoff: `res.setDelay(ms)` adds real wall-clock delay to the test run — use the minimum delay needed to observe the loading state reliably (typically 500–1500ms). Avoid using `res.setDelay()` in `beforeEach` blocks that run before unrelated tests, as it will slow the entire suite.

**Pattern 573** — Component Testing with React Context and Redux Provider Mounting Helper

When React components depend on multiple context providers (React Context, Redux store, React Router), create a typed `mountWithProviders()` helper that wraps `cy.mount()` with all required providers. This eliminates repetitive boilerplate across component test files.

```typescript
// cypress/support/mount-helpers.tsx
import React from 'react';
import { Provider } from 'react-redux';
import { MemoryRouter } from 'react-router-dom';
import { QueryClient, QueryClientProvider } from '@tanstack/react-query';
import { createTestStore, type AppStore } from '../../src/store';
import type { RootState } from '../../src/store/types';

interface MountOptions {
  preloadedState?: Partial<RootState>;
  initialPath?: string;
}

export function mountWithProviders(
  component: React.ReactNode,
  { preloadedState = {}, initialPath = '/' }: MountOptions = {}
): { store: AppStore } {
  const store = createTestStore(preloadedState);
  const queryClient = new QueryClient({
    defaultOptions: { queries: { retry: false } },
  });

  cy.mount(
    <Provider store={store}>
      <QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>
        <MemoryRouter initialEntries={[initialPath]}>
          {component}
        </MemoryRouter>
      </QueryClientProvider>
    </Provider>
  );

  return { store };
}

// cypress/component/ProductCard.cy.tsx
import { mountWithProviders } from '../support/mount-helpers';
import { ProductCard } from '../../src/components/ProductCard';

it('dispatches ADD_TO_CART action on button click', () => {
  const { store } = mountWithProviders(
    <ProductCard id="prod-1" name="Widget" price={19.99} />,
    { preloadedState: { cart: { items: [] } } }
  );

  cy.get('[data-cy="add-to-cart"]').click();

  const state = store.getState();
  expect(state.cart.items).to.have.length(1);
  expect(state.cart.items[0]).to.deep.include({ id: 'prod-1' });
});
```
Tradeoff: The `QueryClient` instance is created fresh per test (with `retry: false`), which prevents stale cache data leaking between tests. However, server-side state mutations from `cy.intercept()` are not automatically reflected in the QueryClient cache — call `queryClient.invalidateQueries()` inside the component or trigger a refetch via UI interaction.

**Pattern 574** — `@cypress/grep` Tag-Based CI Tier Filtering with `grepFilterSpecs`

Use `@cypress/grep` to tag tests with severity levels (`@smoke`, `@regression`, `@critical`) and configure separate CI pipelines to run only the relevant tier. The `grepFilterSpecs: true` option skips spec files entirely if no tests match the grep tag, dramatically reducing CI startup overhead.

```typescript
// cypress.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from 'cypress';
import { addMatchImageSnapshotPlugin } from '@sinonjs/fake-timers';

export default defineConfig({
  e2e: {
    setupNodeEvents(on, config) {
      require('@cypress/grep/src/plugin')(config);
      return config;
    },
    env: {
      grepFilterSpecs: true,   // skip whole spec files with no matching tags
      grepOmitFiltered: true,  // omit filtered tests from the output
    },
  },
});

// cypress/support/e2e.ts
import registerCypressGrep from '@cypress/grep';
registerCypressGrep();

// Tests tagged by severity
it('user can log in @smoke @critical', () => {
  cy.visit('/login');
  cy.get('[data-cy="email"]').type('user@example.com');
  cy.get('[data-cy="password"]').type('password');
  cy.get('[data-cy="submit"]').click();
  cy.url().should('include', '/dashboard');
});

it('product search filters by category @regression', () => {
  cy.visit('/products');
  cy.get('[data-cy="category-filter"]').select('Electronics');
  cy.get('[data-cy="product-card"]').should('have.length.greaterThan', 0);
});
```

```yaml
# .github/workflows/ci.yml (excerpt)
jobs:
  smoke:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: npx cypress run --env grep=@smoke,grepFilterSpecs=true
  regression:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: smoke
    steps:
      - run: npx cypress run --env grep=@regression
```
Tradeoff: `grepFilterSpecs: true` works by statically scanning spec file text for the tag string — it cannot detect tags generated dynamically at runtime (e.g., tags stored in a variable or built via template literals). Always write tags as plain string literals in the `it()` description.

**Pattern 575** — `cy.intercept()` GraphQL Per-Operation Aliasing via `req.body.operationName`

For GraphQL APIs where all mutations and queries hit a single `/graphql` endpoint, use the `req.body.operationName` field inside a `cy.intercept()` handler to conditionally set aliases. This gives individual test assertions precise control over specific operations without needing separate endpoint URLs.

```typescript
// cypress/support/graphql.ts
export function interceptGql(operationName: string, alias: string): void {
  cy.intercept('POST', '/graphql', (req) => {
    const body = req.body as { operationName?: string };
    if (body.operationName === operationName) {
      req.alias = alias;
    }
  });
}

// cypress/e2e/user-settings.cy.ts
import { interceptGql } from '../support/graphql';

beforeEach(() => {
  interceptGql('GetUserProfile', 'getUserProfile');
  interceptGql('UpdateUserEmail', 'updateEmail');
  interceptGql('UpdateUserPassword', 'updatePassword');
  cy.visit('/settings');
});

it('updates email and shows success message', () => {
  cy.wait('@getUserProfile');
  cy.get('[data-cy="email-input"]').clear().type('new@example.com');
  cy.get('[data-cy="save-email"]').click();

  cy.wait('@updateEmail').then(({ request, response }) => {
    expect(request.body.variables.email).to.eq('new@example.com');
    expect(response?.body.data.updateUserEmail.success).to.be.true;
  });

  cy.get('[data-cy="success-toast"]').should('be.visible');
});

it('shows validation error on weak password', () => {
  cy.wait('@getUserProfile');
  cy.get('[data-cy="password-input"]').type('123');
  cy.get('[data-cy="save-password"]').click();

  cy.wait('@updatePassword').then(({ response }) => {
    expect(response?.body.errors?.[0]?.message).to.include('too short');
  });

  cy.get('[data-cy="password-error"]').should('contain.text', 'Password too short');
});
```
Tradeoff: Multiple `cy.intercept('POST', '/graphql')` handlers registered for different operations all match the same URL — Cypress applies them in reverse registration order (last registered wins for route matching, but all handlers with `req.alias` conditional logic still execute). Ensure handlers only set `req.alias` when `operationName` matches to avoid aliasing the wrong request.

### Community Gotchas

**G381** — `cy.get()` inside a `.should(callback)` enqueues a new Cypress command on the global queue causing "Cypress detected you returned a promise" — the callback must be purely synchronous
Why this matters: Developers write `.should(($el) => { cy.get('[data-cy="sibling"]').should('exist'); })` expecting Cypress to evaluate the inner `cy.get()` as part of the retry-able assertion. Instead, the inner `cy.get()` enqueues itself on the global command queue asynchronously from within a synchronous assertion callback. Cypress detects the pending command and throws an error. This is a common refactor mistake when converting `.then()` chains to `.should()` for retry-ability.
Fix: Inside `.should(callback)`, use only synchronous jQuery methods (`$el.find()`, `$el.text()`) and native `expect()` assertions from Chai. To assert on a related element, declare two separate `cy.get()` chains outside the callback. For compound assertions on a single element, chain multiple `.and()` assertions rather than introducing new `cy.get()` calls.

---

**G382** — `cy.intercept()` handlers registered inside a `cy.then()` callback do not apply to requests triggered by actions in the same chain because `cy.then()` resolves after the preceding command, making the intercept arrive too late
Why this matters: A developer writes `cy.get('[data-cy="submit"]').then(() => { cy.intercept('POST', '/api/form').as('formPost'); }).click()`. The `.then()` callback runs and registers the intercept, but the `.click()` action has already been queued to run before the intercept is registered. The `POST /api/form` request fires without the alias being set, causing `cy.wait('@formPost')` to time out.
Fix: Always register `cy.intercept()` calls at the top level of the test body (or in `beforeEach`) before the action that triggers the request. Intercept registration is synchronous from Cypress's perspective — it does not need to await a preceding command.

---

**G383** — `cy.session()` `validate()` is called before `setup()` on the very first warmup in a test run — if `validate()` throws before the session exists, the error message says "session not found" which misleads developers into thinking the cache key is wrong
Why this matters: On a cold CI runner with no cached session, Cypress calls `validate()` first to check if the session is already valid. Since no session exists yet, `validate()` fails (or throws). Cypress then correctly falls through to `setup()` to create the session. But if `validate()` has a bug (e.g., `cy.request('/api/me').its('status').should('eq', 200)` on a server that returns 403 for unauthenticated users), the error message from the failed validate — "CypressError: cy.session() errored during validate" — is printed even though setup was about to run anyway. Developers see this and incorrectly assume the cache key format is wrong.
Fix: Wrap the `validate()` body in a `try/catch` or use `failOnStatusCode: false` in the request, then assert on the status code explicitly: `cy.request({ url: '/api/me', failOnStatusCode: false }).its('status').should('eq', 200)`. This produces a clear assertion failure rather than an uncaught error.

---

**G384** — Aliases created with `.as()` inside `cy.each()` callbacks share the same name and the last iteration's value overwrites all previous ones — only the final element's alias is accessible after the loop
Why this matters: A developer iterates over a list of product cards and aliases each one: `cy.get('[data-cy="product"]').each(($el, i) => { cy.wrap($el).as(`product${i}`) })`. This looks correct, but Cypress's alias registry uses a flat string key — each `as('product0')`, `as('product1')` etc. works in isolation only within the current `cy.wrap()` chain scope during the iteration. Referencing `@product0` after the loop sometimes returns the wrong element because the iteration's inner scope has already completed.
Fix: Collect the elements into a typed array using `.then()` after `cy.get()` and iterate in plain JavaScript: `cy.get('[data-cy="product"]').then(($els) => { Array.from($els).forEach((el, i) => { /* use Cypress.$(el) */ }) })`. Or use `cy.each()` for self-contained assertions that do not require cross-iteration aliasing.

---

**G385** — `cy.stub()` on a module export that is called during module evaluation (e.g., at the top level of a module, outside any function) cannot be intercepted because the module has already executed by the time `beforeEach` runs
Why this matters: An application module exports a `startPolling()` function that immediately invokes `setInterval` at the module's top level when the module is first imported: `const interval = setInterval(fetchStatus, 5000)`. Calling `cy.stub(win, 'setInterval')` in `beforeEach` has no effect because the module was evaluated (and `setInterval` was called with the real implementation) when the app bundle was parsed — before any test code runs.
Fix: Use `cy.clock()` with `['setInterval']` called before `cy.visit()` (or before `cy.mount()` in Component Testing). `cy.clock()` replaces `setInterval` at the browser API level before the application scripts execute, so module-level interval registrations are intercepted. Alternatively, refactor the module to lazily initialize polling via an exported `init()` function that tests can call (or skip) explicitly.

## Cycle 60 — 2026-05-14

### Patterns

**Pattern 643** — `cy.intercept()` middleware header injection for global auth tokens
```typescript
// support/commands.ts
before(() => {
  cy.task<string>('getAccessToken').then((token) => {
    cy.intercept({ url: '/api/**', middleware: true }, (req) => {
      req.headers['authorization'] = `Bearer ${token}`;
      req.headers['x-request-id'] = crypto.randomUUID();
    }).as('apiMiddleware');
  });
});

it('authenticated endpoint returns user data', () => {
  cy.intercept('GET', '/api/users/me').as('getMe');
  cy.visit('/profile');
  cy.wait('@getMe').its('request.headers.authorization').should('match', /^Bearer /);
  cy.get('[data-cy="username"]').should('be.visible');
});
```
Tradeoff: Middleware intercepts run before all other handlers for the same URL pattern (they execute first due to `middleware: true`), which means they run even when subsequent handlers stub responses — useful for auditing all outbound headers but requires the middleware to call `req.continue()` or let the chain fall through, otherwise it may silently block requests that are fully stubbed.

---

**Pattern 644** — `cy.intercept()` `times` for one-shot error injection
```typescript
it('shows retry UI after transient 503', () => {
  // Fail exactly once, then let the real request succeed
  cy.intercept('GET', '/api/dashboard', { statusCode: 503, times: 1 }).as('failOnce');
  cy.intercept('GET', '/api/dashboard').as('succeed');

  cy.visit('/dashboard');
  cy.wait('@failOnce');
  cy.get('[data-cy="retry-button"]').should('be.visible').click();
  cy.wait('@succeed');
  cy.get('[data-cy="dashboard-content"]').should('be.visible');
});
```
Tradeoff: `times: 1` consumes the stub on the first match and then removes it, letting later requests pass through to the network or the next matching handler — this is far simpler than manually removing aliases, but requires that stub registration order mirrors expected request order; if the app fires two requests concurrently before the first resolves, the second may bypass the stub and hit the real server.

---

**Pattern 645** — `cy.session()` multi-user factory with role-keyed cache
```typescript
// support/auth.ts
type Role = 'admin' | 'editor' | 'viewer';

function loginAs(role: Role): void {
  cy.session(
    ['user', role],
    () => {
      cy.request('POST', '/api/auth/login', {
        email: `${role}@example.com`,
        password: Cypress.env(`${role.toUpperCase()}_PASSWORD`),
      }).then(({ body }) => {
        window.localStorage.setItem('auth_token', body.token);
      });
    },
    {
      validate() {
        cy.request({
          url: '/api/auth/me',
          failOnStatusCode: false,
        }).its('status').should('eq', 200);
      },
      cacheAcrossSpecs: true,
    }
  );
}

Cypress.Commands.add('loginAs', loginAs);
```
Tradeoff: Using `cacheAcrossSpecs: true` with role-keyed IDs means all three sessions persist for the entire CI run, eliminating repeated login sequences across spec files; the cost is that if a role's password rotates mid-run the cached session will fail `validate`, triggering re-setup only for that role rather than the whole suite — a desirable property for multi-role suites.

---

**Pattern 646** — `Commands.addQuery()` retry-able `findByRole` wrapper with ARIA semantics
```typescript
// support/queries.ts
Cypress.Commands.addQuery('findByRole', function findByRole(
  role: string,
  options: { name?: string | RegExp } = {}
) {
  const getFn = cy.now('get', `[role="${role}"]`) as (subject: unknown) => JQuery;
  return (subject: unknown) => {
    const elements = getFn(subject);
    if (!options.name) return elements;
    return elements.filter((_, el) => {
      const label = el.getAttribute('aria-label') ?? el.textContent ?? '';
      return typeof options.name === 'string'
        ? label.includes(options.name)
        : (options.name as RegExp).test(label);
    });
  };
});

// Usage — retry-able: re-evaluates until an element matches
cy.findByRole('button', { name: /submit/i }).should('not.be.disabled').click();
```
Tradeoff: `Commands.addQuery()` requires the double-function pattern (the outer function returns an inner function that does the DOM work) and the inner function must be synchronous — wrapping `cy.get()` internally via `cy.now()` is the correct approach; using `cy.get()` directly inside the inner function enqueues a new command and causes Cypress to throw "Cannot call cy.get() from inside a query".

---

**Pattern 647** — `cy.intercept()` `req.on('before:response')` for non-blocking response header audit
```typescript
it('response contains security headers', () => {
  const capturedHeaders: Record<string, string> = {};

  cy.intercept('GET', '/api/**', (req) => {
    req.on('before:response', (res) => {
      capturedHeaders['x-content-type-options'] = res.headers['x-content-type-options'] as string;
      capturedHeaders['x-frame-options'] = res.headers['x-frame-options'] as string;
      // Do NOT call res.send() — just observe; the response continues automatically
    });
  }).as('apiCall');

  cy.visit('/dashboard');
  cy.wait('@apiCall').then(() => {
    expect(capturedHeaders['x-content-type-options']).to.eq('nosniff');
    expect(capturedHeaders['x-frame-options']).to.eq('DENY');
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `req.on('before:response', cb)` fires after the real server responds but before the browser receives the data, allowing read-only header inspection without the overhead of `req.continue((res) => { … })` which holds the entire response in Node memory for modification — use `before:response` for audit-only scenarios and `req.continue()` only when mutation is needed.

---

**Pattern 648** — `cy.clock()` pre-visit with `cy.tick()` for JWT expiry re-authentication flow
```typescript
it('refreshes token 60 s before expiry and stays logged in', () => {
  const now = Date.now();
  cy.clock(now, ['Date', 'setTimeout', 'setInterval', 'clearInterval']);

  cy.intercept('POST', '/api/auth/refresh').as('refresh');
  cy.loginAs('editor'); // cy.session() sets localStorage token with 15-min expiry
  cy.visit('/dashboard');

  // Advance to 14 min 1 s — app's proactive-refresh window fires at T-60s
  cy.tick(14 * 60 * 1000 + 1000);
  cy.wait('@refresh').its('response.statusCode').should('eq', 200);

  // Advance past original expiry — should still be authenticated
  cy.tick(60 * 1000);
  cy.get('[data-cy="user-menu"]').should('be.visible');
});
```
Tradeoff: Passing `['Date', 'setTimeout', 'setInterval', 'clearInterval']` to `cy.clock()` before `cy.visit()` ensures the application's module-level timers are intercepted from the first script evaluation; omitting the array defaults to controlling all clock APIs including `performance.now()`, which can break third-party analytics SDKs that compute elapsed time using `performance.now()` — be explicit about which APIs to fake.

---

**Pattern 649** — `cy.task()` typed task registry with Node-side database seeding
```typescript
// cypress.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from 'cypress';
import { seedUser, deleteUser } from './test-support/db';

interface TaskMap {
  seedUser: (opts: { role: string; email: string }) => Promise<{ id: string }>;
  deleteUser: (id: string) => Promise<null>;
}

export default defineConfig({
  e2e: {
    setupNodeEvents(on) {
      on('task', {
        seedUser: ({ role, email }) => seedUser({ role, email }),
        deleteUser: (id) => deleteUser(id).then(() => null),
      } satisfies TaskMap);
    },
  },
});

// In test
it('admin can deactivate an editor', () => {
  cy.task<{ id: string }>('seedUser', { role: 'editor', email: 'ed@example.com' })
    .then(({ id }) => {
      cy.wrap(id).as('editorId');
    });
  cy.loginAs('admin');
  cy.visit('/admin/users');
  cy.get<string>('@editorId').then((id) => {
    cy.get(`[data-cy="user-row-${id}"] [data-cy="deactivate"]`).click();
  });
  cy.get('[data-cy="success-banner"]').should('contain.text', 'User deactivated');
});

afterEach(() => {
  cy.get<string>('@editorId').then((id) => cy.task('deleteUser', id));
});
```
Tradeoff: Using `satisfies TaskMap` in `setupNodeEvents` gives compile-time task name validation without widening the type to `Record<string, unknown>`, catching typos in task names at build time; the cost is that all task return types must ultimately resolve to a JSON-serializable value since Cypress serializes task results over the CDP bridge — class instances with methods are silently stripped down to plain objects.

---

**Pattern 650** — `Commands.overwrite('type')` masking for sensitive field logging
```typescript
// support/commands.ts
Cypress.Commands.overwrite(
  'type',
  (
    originalFn: (
      subject: JQuery,
      text: string,
      options?: Partial<Cypress.TypeOptions>
    ) => Cypress.Chainable,
    subject: JQuery,
    text: string,
    options: Partial<Cypress.TypeOptions> = {}
  ) => {
    if ((options as { sensitive?: boolean }).sensitive) {
      options.log = false;
      Cypress.log({
        $el: subject,
        name: 'type',
        message: '*'.repeat(text.length),
        consoleProps: () => ({ 'Masked input': '(hidden)' }),
      });
    }
    return originalFn(subject, text, options);
  }
);

// Usage
cy.get('[data-cy="password"]').type(Cypress.env('USER_PASSWORD'), { sensitive: true } as Cypress.TypeOptions);
```
Tradeoff: Overwriting `type` with a `sensitive` flag prevents passwords from appearing in Cypress screenshots, videos, and Cloud test replays — critical for compliance; the downside is that `Cypress.TypeOptions` does not include `sensitive` so TypeScript requires a `declare global` augmentation in a `.d.ts` file to avoid type errors on the option, and the cast `as Cypress.TypeOptions` must be used at each callsite until the augmentation is in place.

---

**Pattern 651** — `cy.origin()` with `args` for cross-domain OAuth PKCE flow
```typescript
it('completes OAuth PKCE login from identity provider', () => {
  const clientId = Cypress.env('OAUTH_CLIENT_ID') as string;
  const redirectUri = 'http://localhost:3000/auth/callback';

  cy.visit('/login');
  cy.get('[data-cy="sso-button"]').click();

  cy.origin(
    'https://sso.example.com',
    { args: { clientId, redirectUri } },
    ({ clientId, redirectUri }) => {
      cy.get('[data-cy="email"]').type('user@example.com');
      cy.get('[data-cy="password"]').type('TestPass1!');
      cy.get('[data-cy="authorize"]').click();

      cy.url().should('include', redirectUri).and('include', 'code=');
    }
  );

  // Back on primary origin after redirect
  cy.get('[data-cy="app-shell"]').should('be.visible');
});
```
Tradeoff: All values passed in `args` must be JSON-serializable because Cypress serializes them via the structured-clone algorithm to cross the cross-origin iframe boundary — functions, class instances with methods, `Map`, `Set`, `RegExp`, and `undefined` values are silently dropped or throw; only plain objects, arrays, strings, numbers, booleans, and `null` survive the transfer reliably.

---

**Pattern 652** — Declarative fixture routing table with `cy.intercept()` and a typed config object
```typescript
// support/fixtures.ts
interface RouteStub {
  method: string;
  url: string;
  fixture: string;
  alias: string;
}

const API_STUBS: RouteStub[] = [
  { method: 'GET', url: '/api/products',   fixture: 'products.json',   alias: 'getProducts'   },
  { method: 'GET', url: '/api/categories', fixture: 'categories.json', alias: 'getCategories' },
  { method: 'GET', url: '/api/promotions', fixture: 'promotions.json', alias: 'getPromotions' },
];

export function stubCatalogApis(): void {
  API_STUBS.forEach(({ method, url, fixture, alias }) => {
    cy.intercept(method, url, { fixture }).as(alias);
  });
}

// In test
beforeEach(() => { stubCatalogApis(); });

it('renders catalogue page with all data sections', () => {
  cy.visit('/catalogue');
  cy.wait(['@getProducts', '@getCategories', '@getPromotions']);
  cy.get('[data-cy="product-grid"]').should('be.visible');
  cy.get('[data-cy="category-filter"]').children().should('have.length.gt', 0);
});
```
Tradeoff: Centralising route stubs in a typed array makes it trivial to add or remove stubs without scanning test bodies, and the `cy.wait([…])` array form asserts all stubs resolved in parallel — the tradeoff is that large routing tables can mask missing stubs for endpoints added later in the application; pair with a `cy.intercept('GET', '/api/**')` catch-all that asserts `req.url` is in the declared table to surface unregistered endpoints.

---

**Pattern 653** — React component testing with Redux store and `cy.spy()` on dispatched actions
```typescript
// ProductCard.cy.tsx
import { mount } from 'cypress/react';
import { Provider } from 'react-redux';
import { configureStore } from '@reduxjs/toolkit';
import cartReducer, { addToCart } from '../../store/cartSlice';
import ProductCard from './ProductCard';

it('dispatches addToCart action when button clicked', () => {
  const store = configureStore({ reducer: { cart: cartReducer } });
  const dispatchSpy = cy.spy(store, 'dispatch').as('dispatch');

  mount(
    <Provider store={store}>
      <ProductCard id="42" name="Widget" price={9.99} />
    </Provider>
  );

  cy.get('[data-cy="add-to-cart"]').click();

  cy.get('@dispatch').should('have.been.calledOnce');
  cy.get('@dispatch')
    .its('firstCall.args.0')
    .should('deep.equal', addToCart({ id: '42', qty: 1 }));
});
```
Tradeoff: Spying on `store.dispatch` directly gives action-level assertion granularity without mocking the entire Redux slice, but it requires the test to import the exact action creator to construct the expected value — if the action creator signature changes, the test breaks loudly (a feature, not a bug) and the import serves as a living contract between the test and the store.

---

**Pattern 654** — `cy.request()` chained with `cy.intercept()` for dual API + UI contract assertion
```typescript
it('API response shape matches UI rendering', () => {
  cy.intercept('GET', '/api/invoice/123').as('getInvoice');

  // First assert the API contract directly
  cy.request<InvoiceDto>('GET', '/api/invoice/123').then(({ body }) => {
    expect(body).to.have.keys(['id', 'amount', 'currency', 'lineItems', 'status']);
    expect(body.lineItems).to.be.an('array').and.have.length.gt(0);
  });

  // Then assert the UI renders the same data
  cy.visit('/invoices/123');
  cy.wait('@getInvoice').then(({ response }) => {
    const invoice = response!.body as InvoiceDto;
    cy.get('[data-cy="invoice-amount"]').should(
      'contain.text',
      `${invoice.currency} ${invoice.amount.toFixed(2)}`
    );
    cy.get('[data-cy="line-item"]').should('have.length', invoice.lineItems.length);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: Running `cy.request()` independently of the page visit confirms the API contract without relying on the browser's network stack, making failures unambiguously backend-related; the UI assertion in the `cy.wait('@getInvoice')` callback then confirms the rendering layer — the dual assertion pattern doubles the network call but provides a clear separation between data-contract failures and rendering failures that a single end-to-end assertion cannot distinguish.

---

**Pattern 655** — `res.setThrottle()` for progressive loading state assertions
```typescript
it('shows skeleton placeholders during slow network load', () => {
  cy.intercept('GET', '/api/feed', (req) => {
    req.continue((res) => {
      res.setThrottle(50); // 50 kbps — simulates slow 3G
    });
  }).as('slowFeed');

  cy.visit('/home');

  // Assert skeleton is visible before response arrives
  cy.get('[data-cy="feed-skeleton"]').should('be.visible');

  // Wait for throttled response to complete
  cy.wait('@slowFeed');
  cy.get('[data-cy="feed-skeleton"]').should('not.exist');
  cy.get('[data-cy="feed-item"]').should('have.length.gte', 5);
});
```
Tradeoff: `res.setThrottle(kbps)` throttles the response transfer rate at the Cypress proxy layer, accurately simulating network conditions without a browser DevTools profile, making it reliable in CI headless mode; the cost is that the throttle applies to the entire response body regardless of content-encoding, so for large compressed API payloads the decompressed byte count determines throttle duration — add an explicit `cy.wait()` timeout override to prevent flakiness on payloads larger than the default 30 s timeout allows.

---

**Pattern 656** — `cy.fixture<T>()` TypeScript generic for type-safe test data access
```typescript
// cypress/fixtures/user-admin.ts — type declaration lives next to fixture
export interface UserFixture {
  id: string;
  email: string;
  role: 'admin' | 'editor' | 'viewer';
  permissions: string[];
}

// In test
it('admin sees all permission toggles', () => {
  cy.fixture<UserFixture>('user-admin').then((user) => {
    expect(user.role).to.eq('admin'); // type-safe: role is a union
    cy.intercept('GET', '/api/users/me', { body: user }).as('getMe');
    cy.visit('/settings/permissions');
    cy.wait('@getMe');
    user.permissions.forEach((perm) => {
      cy.get(`[data-cy="perm-${perm}"]`).should('have.attr', 'aria-checked', 'true');
    });
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: Typing `cy.fixture<T>()` with the fixture's interface provides IntelliSense and compile-time checks on fixture property access, catching stale fixture references when the DTO shape changes; the fixture JSON file itself is not validated at compile time — only the TypeScript cast is checked — so a mismatch between the `.json` file structure and the declared interface will compile cleanly but throw at runtime; add a Zod schema parse inside the `then()` callback for runtime validation in critical flows.

---

**Pattern 657** — `cy.wrap(null).should()` retry-able analytics event collection
```typescript
it('dashboard fires all required analytics events on load', () => {
  const events: string[] = [];

  cy.intercept('POST', '/analytics/event', (req) => {
    events.push((req.body as { name: string }).name);
    req.continue();
  });

  cy.visit('/dashboard');
  cy.get('[data-cy="dashboard-kpi"]').should('be.visible');

  // Assert all expected events were collected (order-independent, retry-able)
  cy.wrap(null).should(() => {
    expect(events).to.include.members([
      'page_view',
      'dashboard_loaded',
      'kpi_rendered',
    ]);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: Using `cy.wrap(null).should(() => { … })` makes the assertion retry-able — Cypress will keep re-evaluating the callback until the `events` array contains all required members or the command timeout is reached; a plain `expect(events).to.include.members([…])` after the `cy.get()` executes only once and fails immediately if events are still in-flight, producing a race condition that passes locally but fails under CI load.
