**Pattern 699** — `cy.intercept()` `req.continue` callback for asserting Content-Security-Policy response header
```typescript
cy.intercept(
  {
    method: 'GET',
    url: '/',
  },
  (req) => {
    req.continue((res) => {
      // Assert that the server sends a CSP header on the HTML document response
      const csp = res.headers['content-security-policy'] as string | undefined;
      expect(csp, 'CSP header must be present on HTML document').to.be.a('string');
      expect(csp).to.include("default-src 'self'");
      expect(csp).to.include("script-src 'self'");
      expect(csp).not.to.include("'unsafe-inline'");
    });
  }
).as('htmlDoc');

cy.visit('/');
cy.wait('@htmlDoc');
cy.log('CSP header validated on HTML document response');
```
Tradeoff: Asserting response headers inside a `req.continue` callback is the only way to inspect headers that Cypress cannot surface via `cy.location()` or DOM assertions, catching misconfigured reverse-proxy header stripping invisible to the application itself — but `res.headers` keys are always lowercase strings in Cypress regardless of how the server sends them (HTTP/2 mandates lowercase; Cypress normalises HTTP/1.1 headers as well), so comparing against `Content-Security-Policy` with capital letters always produces a falsy result and the assertion silently passes as `undefined.to.be.a('string')` throws instead of catching the missing header; always use all-lowercase header names.

**Pattern 700** — `cy.request()` typed response helper with automatic base URL resolution and auth token injection
```typescript
interface ApiResponse<T> {
  status: number;
  body: T;
  headers: Record<string, string>;
}

const apiRequest = <T>(
  method: 'GET' | 'POST' | 'PUT' | 'DELETE' | 'PATCH',
  path: string,
  body?: unknown
): Cypress.Chainable<ApiResponse<T>> => {
  const token = Cypress.env('API_TOKEN') as string | undefined;

  return cy.request<T>({
    method,
    url: `${Cypress.config('baseUrl')}${path}`,
    body,
    headers: token ? { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` } : {},
    failOnStatusCode: false,
  });
};

// Usage in a spec
it('returns 409 Conflict when creating a duplicate user', () => {
  apiRequest<{ error: string }>('POST', '/api/users', {
    email: 'existing@example.com',
    name: 'Alice',
  }).then((res) => {
    expect(res.status).to.eq(409);
    expect(res.body.error).to.include('already exists');
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: Centralising auth header injection in a typed `apiRequest` wrapper ensures every `cy.request()` call sends the correct token without copy-paste, and the generic type parameter lets TypeScript infer response body shape at the callsite catching field-name typos at compile time — but `Cypress.env('API_TOKEN')` reads from the in-memory env at call time, so if a test refreshes the token mid-spec via a `cy.session()` login the caller must ensure the updated token is written back to `Cypress.env()` before the next `apiRequest()` invocation; unlike browser-based commands, `cy.request()` runs outside the browser context so reading the updated token from `window.localStorage` inside the helper is not possible.

**Pattern 701** — Component test `mountWithMSW()` using Mock Service Worker for isolated fetch interception
```typescript
import { mount } from 'cypress/react18';
import { http, HttpResponse } from 'msw';
import { setupWorker } from 'msw/browser';
import UserProfile from '../../src/components/UserProfile';

// Start MSW worker once per suite; reset handlers per test to avoid bleed
let worker: ReturnType<typeof setupWorker>;

before(() => {
  worker = setupWorker();
  worker.start({ onUnhandledRequest: 'bypass' });
});

afterEach(() => worker.resetHandlers());
after(() => worker.stop());

it('renders user name and avatar from API', () => {
  worker.use(
    http.get('/api/users/42', () =>
      HttpResponse.json({ id: 42, name: 'Bob', avatarUrl: '/avatars/bob.png' })
    )
  );

  mount(<UserProfile userId={42} />);

  cy.get('[data-cy="user-name"]').should('contain.text', 'Bob');
  cy.get('[data-cy="user-avatar"]').should('have.attr', 'src', '/avatars/bob.png');
});
```
Tradeoff: Using MSW's `worker.use()` per test gives you fetch-level interception without needing `cy.intercept()` (which is unavailable in component testing mode) and lets you reuse the same handler definitions from unit tests and Storybook stories — but MSW runs as a Service Worker inside the Cypress-controlled browser frame and Service Workers are scope-limited to the registered path; if the component test runner serves assets from a non-root path, the SW may not intercept requests without explicit `scope` configuration in `worker.start()`, and calling `worker.resetHandlers()` in `afterEach` is mandatory to prevent handler bleed across component tests.

### Community Gotchas

**G401** — `cy.intercept()` `req.reply()` inside a conditional branch silently lets non-matching requests pass through to the real server, causing live network calls in CI where the real endpoint is unreachable
Why this matters: A team writes `cy.intercept('POST', '/api/checkout', (req) => { if (req.body.cart.length > 0) { req.reply({ statusCode: 200, body: { orderId: 'test-123' } }); } })` expecting to stub all checkout requests. For an edge-case test where an empty cart triggers a validation error, the `if` condition is false so `req.reply()` is never called. Cypress's default when a handler does not call `req.reply()` or `req.continue()` is to forward the request to the real server. In CI, the real `/api/checkout` is unavailable, causing a network error that surfaces as a cryptic `Error: connect ECONNREFUSED` failure rather than a clear assertion failure, making the root cause hard to diagnose.
Fix: Always include a final `else` branch or a default `req.reply()` / `req.continue()` at the end of every conditional intercept handler to ensure every code path explicitly disposes of the request. For exhaustive stubbing in CI, add a catch-all `cy.intercept('*', (req) => { throw new Error(\`Unexpected request: ${req.url}\`) })` after all specific intercepts to surface unhandled requests immediately.

---

**G402** — `cy.session()` `cacheAcrossSpecs: true` silently reuses a stale session from a previous test run when `cypress run` is invoked without clearing the session storage directory on persistent CI agents
Why this matters: A team enables `cacheAcrossSpecs: true` to speed up their suite. On a fresh CI runner the session is created correctly. On a reused runner (common with self-hosted GitHub Actions runners or Buildkite elastic CI), the Cypress session cache directory persists from a prior run. If the application rotated signing keys or the test user's password changed since the last run, the restored cookies fail silently — the `validate` function only fires if a session file exists, but if the prior run cached a session before the key rotation, `validate` may not detect the stale token because the `/api/me` endpoint returns 200 with a redirect payload rather than a strict 401.
Fix: In CI pipelines, add a pre-run step that deletes the Cypress session cache directory before each `cypress run` invocation. Alternatively, scope `cacheAcrossSpecs` to local developer runs only by reading `Cypress.env('CI')` and setting the option to `!Cypress.env('CI')` so persistent agents always create fresh sessions.

---

**G403** — `cy.origin()` callbacks that import shared utility functions via `Cypress.require()` throw `Module not found` errors in Webpack-bundled Cypress setups because `experimentalOriginDependencies` must be explicitly enabled and the module path resolves relative to the support file, not the spec file
Why this matters: A developer wants to share a `formatLoginUrl()` helper between the main test scope and a `cy.origin()` callback. They write `cy.origin('auth.example.com', () => { const { formatLoginUrl } = Cypress.require('./support/url-helpers'); })` after reading the Cypress docs. The test throws `Error: Cypress.require() is only supported within a cy.origin() callback` (if the flag is off) or `Module not found: ./support/url-helpers` (if the flag is on but the path resolution fails). The root cause is that `Cypress.require()` resolves modules relative to the Cypress `supportFile`, not relative to the spec file, and the `experimentalOriginDependencies` flag must be `true` in `cypress.config.ts`.
Fix: Add `experimentalOriginDependencies: true` to the `e2e` block in `cypress.config.ts`. Place shared helpers in a path reachable from the `supportFile` (e.g., `cypress/support/helpers/`) and use a path relative to `supportFile` in `Cypress.require()`. Verify the resolved path using `Cypress.resolve('./helpers/url-helpers')` in the Cypress console before committing.

---

**G404** — Component tests that use `cy.mount()` without a fixed-height container produce false-positive visibility assertions when the component renders at zero height due to the test harness `div` having no explicit height
Why this matters: A team writes `cy.mount(<Tooltip content="Help text" />); cy.get('[data-cy="tooltip-bubble"]').should('be.visible')`. The assertion passes, but in the real application the tooltip is invisible because the test harness `div` has `height: 0` and `overflow: hidden`. Cypress's `be.visible` check verifies the element is not `display: none`, `visibility: hidden`, or `opacity: 0` and is within the viewport — it does not verify the element is within a container with non-zero computed height. The component is technically "visible" in the Cypress DOM even though it is visually clipped.
Fix: Wrap mounted components in an explicit container with defined height when testing absolutely positioned overlay elements: `cy.mount(<div style={{ height: '400px', position: 'relative' }}><Tooltip content="Help text" /></div>)`. For teams that frequently test overlay components, define a `mountWithLayout()` custom command that wraps every mounted component in a 100vh container to match production rendering context.

---

**G405** — `cy.clock()` does not intercept `queueMicrotask()` or Promise microtasks, so components that schedule state updates via `Promise.resolve().then()` instead of `setTimeout` will update their DOM outside `cy.tick()` control, causing assertions to pass or fail before `cy.tick()` is called
Why this matters: A developer tests a component that shows a loading spinner for exactly 500ms by scheduling `setLoading(false)` inside `Promise.resolve().then(() => setTimeout(() => setLoading(false), 500))`. They call `cy.tick(400)` expecting the spinner to still be visible, then `cy.tick(150)` expecting it to be gone. The spinner disappears immediately after `cy.mount()` because `Promise.resolve().then()` schedules a microtask that resolves in the real event loop before `cy.tick(400)` is evaluated — `cy.clock()` only intercepts macrotask-based timer APIs (`setTimeout`, `setInterval`, `Date`) and has no effect on the microtask queue.
Fix: Refactor components that need deterministic delay behavior to use only `setTimeout`-based scheduling rather than `Promise.resolve().then()` chains, which Cypress can control via `cy.tick()`. If the component code cannot be changed, test the loading state synchronously immediately after mount (before any microtasks drain) using an inline `.should('be.visible')`, rather than relying on `cy.tick()` to hold the component in a loading state.

## Cycle 64 — 2026-05-14

### Patterns

**Pattern 702** — `cy.intercept()` middleware chain for global auth-header injection
```typescript
// cypress/support/e2e.ts
beforeEach(() => {
  cy.intercept({ url: '/api/**', middleware: true }, (req) => {
    req.headers['Authorization'] = `Bearer ${Cypress.env('ACCESS_TOKEN')}`;
    req.headers['X-Test-Run-Id'] = Cypress.currentTest.titlePath.join(' > ');
    req.continue();
  }).as('authMiddleware');
});

// Individual tests can still override specific routes
it('fetches protected resource', () => {
  cy.intercept('GET', '/api/users', { fixture: 'users.json' }).as('getUsers');
  cy.visit('/users');
  cy.wait('@getUsers');
  cy.get('[data-cy="user-list"]').should('have.length.gt', 0);
});
```
Tradeoff: Middleware intercepts (`middleware: true`) fire before specific-route intercepts in the same chain, letting you inject headers globally without duplicating them in every test — but `Cypress.env('ACCESS_TOKEN')` must be populated before `beforeEach` runs (e.g., via a `cy.session()` login that writes the token to `Cypress.env`), and if the middleware handler calls `req.continue()` unconditionally it will forward even requests that a later specific intercept intends to stub, requiring that specific stubs also call `req.reply()` explicitly to terminate the chain early.

**Pattern 703** — `cy.intercept()` response array cycling for paginated list tests
```typescript
const pages = [
  { items: ['a', 'b', 'c'], nextCursor: 'cursor-1' },
  { items: ['d', 'e', 'f'], nextCursor: 'cursor-2' },
  { items: ['g'],           nextCursor: null },
];

it('loads all pages via infinite scroll', () => {
  let callIndex = 0;

  cy.intercept('GET', '/api/items*', (req) => {
    const page = pages[callIndex] ?? pages[pages.length - 1];
    callIndex++;
    req.reply({ statusCode: 200, body: page });
  }).as('getItems');

  cy.visit('/items');
  cy.wait('@getItems');
  cy.scrollTo('bottom');
  cy.wait('@getItems');
  cy.scrollTo('bottom');
  cy.wait('@getItems');
  cy.get('[data-cy="item"]').should('have.length', 7);
});
```
Tradeoff: A closure counter is the simplest way to return different responses per call without StatefulMock libraries — the approach is fully synchronous and requires no extra dependencies — but the `callIndex` variable leaks across retried test runs if Cypress retries the test on failure without reloading the spec, because the closure is closed over a module-level variable; wrapping tests with `beforeEach(() => { callIndex = 0; })` is mandatory to guarantee deterministic sequencing on retries.

**Pattern 704** — `cy.intercept()` `req.on('response')` for latency SLO assertions
```typescript
it('API 95th-percentile latency stays under 300 ms in mocked network', () => {
  const latencies: number[] = [];

  cy.intercept('GET', '/api/**', (req) => {
    const start = Date.now();
    req.on('response', () => {
      latencies.push(Date.now() - start);
    });
    req.continue();
  }).as('apiCalls');

  cy.visit('/dashboard');
  // trigger several API calls via UI interactions
  cy.get('[data-cy="refresh"]').click();
  cy.get('[data-cy="filter-by-date"]').click();
  cy.get('[data-cy="export-btn"]').click();

  cy.wrap(null).then(() => {
    const sorted = [...latencies].sort((a, b) => a - b);
    const p95 = sorted[Math.floor(sorted.length * 0.95)];
    expect(p95, '95th-percentile latency').to.be.lessThan(300);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `req.on('response')` fires synchronously in the Cypress intercept layer and `Date.now()` measures wall-clock time for the full round-trip including Cypress's own proxy overhead — this means measured latencies include ~5–20 ms of internal Cypress serialization noise; the technique is useful for catching regressions larger than ~50 ms but is not suitable for sub-millisecond SLO verification, and the assertion must be wrapped in `cy.wrap(null).then()` to defer evaluation until all requests have resolved.

**Pattern 705** — `cy.session()` multi-role factory with per-role `cacheAcrossSpecs`
```typescript
// cypress/support/auth.ts
type Role = 'admin' | 'editor' | 'viewer';

export function loginAs(role: Role) {
  cy.session(
    ['user-session', role],
    () => {
      cy.request('POST', '/api/auth/login', {
        username: Cypress.env(`${role.toUpperCase()}_USER`),
        password: Cypress.env(`${role.toUpperCase()}_PASS`),
      }).then(({ body }) => {
        window.localStorage.setItem('auth_token', body.token);
      });
    },
    {
      validate() {
        cy.request({
          method: 'GET',
          url: '/api/me',
          headers: {
            Authorization: `Bearer ${window.localStorage.getItem('auth_token')}`,
          },
          failOnStatusCode: true,
        });
      },
      cacheAcrossSpecs: !Cypress.env('CI'),
    }
  );
}
```
Tradeoff: Passing an array `['user-session', role]` as the session id creates a distinct cache entry per role so admin and viewer tokens never collide — but `window.localStorage` is not accessible inside the `session` setup callback on the first call (before a page has been loaded) unless you call `cy.window()` first; prefer returning the token via `cy.setCookie()` or calling `cy.visit('/')` before writing to storage, and disable `cacheAcrossSpecs` in CI via `!Cypress.env('CI')` to avoid stale-token failures on reused agents.

---

**Pattern 706** — `cy.session()` sentinel `validate` with lightweight `cy.request()`
```typescript
// cypress/support/commands.ts
Cypress.Commands.add('loginWithSession', (email: string) => {
  cy.session(
    email,
    () => {
      cy.visit('/login');
      cy.get('[data-cy="email"]').type(email);
      cy.get('[data-cy="password"]').type(Cypress.env('DEFAULT_PASS'));
      cy.get('[data-cy="submit"]').click();
      cy.url().should('include', '/dashboard');
    },
    {
      validate() {
        // Fast sentinel: single authenticated API call is cheaper than a full page load
        cy.request({
          method: 'GET',
          url: '/api/auth/ping',
          followRedirect: false,
          failOnStatusCode: true,
        }).its('status').should('eq', 200);
      },
      cacheAcrossSpecs: true,
    }
  );
  cy.visit('/dashboard');
});
```
Tradeoff: Using `cy.request()` inside `validate` instead of `cy.visit()` makes session validation ~10x faster because it avoids full page rendering — but the sentinel endpoint (`/api/auth/ping`) must return a non-200 status when the session has expired rather than redirecting to `/login` with a 302; without `followRedirect: false`, Cypress follows the 302 and sees a 200 on the login page, causing `validate` to pass for an expired session and the cached invalid session to be served for the entire spec.

**Pattern 707** — `cy.origin()` sequential SSO hop across identity provider and app
```typescript
it('logs in via third-party SSO and lands on dashboard', () => {
  cy.visit('/login');
  cy.get('[data-cy="sso-btn"]').click();

  // First hop: identity provider login form
  cy.origin('https://idp.example.com', () => {
    cy.get('#username').type('testuser@example.com');
    cy.get('#password').type('S3cr3t!');
    cy.get('[type="submit"]').click();
    // Wait for MFA page or redirect
    cy.url().should('include', '/oauth/authorize');
    cy.get('[data-cy="approve-btn"]').click();
  });

  // Control returns to app origin after redirect
  cy.url().should('include', '/dashboard');
  cy.get('[data-cy="welcome-msg"]').should('contain', 'testuser');
});
```
Tradeoff: `cy.origin()` handles the cross-origin redirect automatically as long as the callback scope is entered before the browser navigates away from the primary origin — but you cannot pass functions, class instances, or Cypress chain references through `args`; only structured-clone-serializable values (plain objects, strings, numbers) are supported, so passing a login helper class reference fails silently and must be replaced with raw credential strings passed via `{ args }`.

---

**Pattern 708** — `cy.origin()` with `args` for parameterized OAuth credential injection
```typescript
it('authenticates two different users in sequence', () => {
  const users = [
    { email: 'alice@example.com', password: Cypress.env('ALICE_PASS') },
    { email: 'bob@example.com',   password: Cypress.env('BOB_PASS')   },
  ];

  for (const user of users) {
    cy.visit('/login');
    cy.get('[data-cy="sso-login"]').click();

    cy.origin(
      'https://auth.example.com',
      { args: { email: user.email, password: user.password } },
      ({ email, password }) => {
        cy.get('#email').type(email);
        cy.get('#password').type(password);
        cy.get('[type="submit"]').click();
      }
    );

    cy.url().should('include', '/home');
    cy.get('[data-cy="avatar"]').should('exist');
    cy.clearCookies();
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: Passing credentials via `args` is the only supported mechanism to inject test-specific data into a `cy.origin()` callback — but `args` values are serialized with the structured clone algorithm, meaning Dates become plain objects and class instances lose their prototype chain; always validate that your `args` payload is JSON-round-trip-safe before relying on it in the callback, and never include raw passwords in `args` logged by Cypress screenshots by obscuring them with `Cypress.env()` lookup at the point of use.

**Pattern 709** — Custom `Cypress.Commands.addQuery()` retry-able table row finder
```typescript
// cypress/support/commands.ts
Cypress.Commands.addQuery(
  'findTableRow',
  function findTableRow(columnHeader: string, cellText: string) {
    return (subject: JQuery<HTMLElement>) => {
      const table = subject[0];
      const headers = Array.from(table.querySelectorAll('th')).map(
        (th) => th.textContent?.trim() ?? ''
      );
      const colIndex = headers.indexOf(columnHeader);
      if (colIndex === -1) throw new Error(`Column "${columnHeader}" not found`);

      const rows = Array.from(table.querySelectorAll('tbody tr'));
      const match = rows.find((row) => {
        const cells = row.querySelectorAll('td');
        return cells[colIndex]?.textContent?.trim() === cellText;
      });

      if (!match) throw new Error(`Row with "${columnHeader}" = "${cellText}" not found`);
      return Cypress.$(match);
    };
  }
);

// Usage
cy.get('[data-cy="orders-table"]')
  .findTableRow('Status', 'Shipped')
  .find('[data-cy="track-btn"]')
  .click();
```
Tradeoff: `Commands.addQuery()` registers a synchronous query that integrates with Cypress's built-in retry logic — the function is re-invoked on each DOM poll until it stops throwing, so the table row will be found even if data loads asynchronously after `cy.get()` resolves — but because the query is synchronous it must not contain any Cypress commands internally; using `cy.get()` or `cy.wrap()` inside the query body causes the "Cypress detected that you invoked one or more cy commands" error, so all DOM traversal must use raw `querySelector` / `querySelectorAll`.

---

**Pattern 710** — `Cypress.Commands.overwrite()` for `cy.type()` with automatic clear and PII masking
```typescript
// cypress/support/commands.ts
Cypress.Commands.overwrite<'type', 'dom'>(
  'type',
  function (originalFn, element, text, options) {
    // Always clear the field first to prevent value concatenation on retry
    const clearOptions = { ...options, log: false };
    cy.wrap(element, { log: false }).clear(clearOptions);

    // Mask PII fields in Cypress command log
    const isSensitive =
      typeof text === 'string' &&
      (element[0]?.getAttribute('type') === 'password' ||
       element[0]?.getAttribute('data-sensitive') === 'true');

    const logText = isSensitive ? '••••••••' : text;

    Cypress.log({
      name: 'type',
      message: logText,
      consoleProps: () => ({ Element: element[0], TypedValue: logText }),
    });

    return originalFn(element, text, { ...options, log: false });
  }
);
```
Tradeoff: Overwriting `cy.type()` with an automatic `clear()` prevents the most common source of flaky form tests — residual values from a previous retry filling in on top of existing text — but wrapping `element` in `cy.wrap()` inside a command overwrite creates a nested Cypress chain that can interfere with timeout propagation; if the parent `cy.type()` has a `timeout` option, the inner `cy.wrap().clear()` inherits the global `defaultCommandTimeout`, not the overriding value, so time-critical form tests with custom timeouts must pass `timeout` explicitly to the `clear()` call.

---

**Pattern 711** — `cy.clock()` seeded to a fixed timestamp before `cy.visit()` for date-dependent UI
```typescript
it('displays "Renewal Due" banner when subscription expires in 7 days', () => {
  // Seed clock BEFORE cy.visit() so app JS sees the frozen date at boot
  const sevenDaysFromNow = new Date('2026-05-21T00:00:00Z').getTime();
  const subscriptionExpiry = new Date('2026-05-28T00:00:00Z').getTime();

  cy.clock(sevenDaysFromNow, ['Date']);
  cy.intercept('GET', '/api/account', {
    body: { subscriptionExpiry, plan: 'pro' },
  }).as('getAccount');

  cy.visit('/account');
  cy.wait('@getAccount');
  cy.get('[data-cy="renewal-banner"]')
    .should('be.visible')
    .and('contain', '7 days');

  // Advance clock to just after expiry
  cy.tick(7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000 + 1);
  cy.get('[data-cy="renewal-banner"]').should('contain', 'Expired');
});
```
Tradeoff: Calling `cy.clock()` before `cy.visit()` ensures the frozen `Date` is active when the app's JavaScript modules first execute, preventing initialization code that calls `new Date()` at module load time from capturing the real wall-clock time — but stubbing only `['Date']` (not `setTimeout` / `setInterval`) avoids accidentally freezing polling timers that the app needs to run normally; if the renewal-check logic uses a `setInterval` internally rather than computing the diff on each render, you must include `'setInterval'` in the stubbed list and call `cy.tick()` to trigger the interval callback.

---

**Pattern 712** — `cy.clock()` + `cy.tick()` for debounce fire-once verification
```typescript
it('fires search API exactly once after 400 ms debounce', () => {
  let callCount = 0;

  cy.clock();
  cy.intercept('GET', '/api/search*', (req) => {
    callCount++;
    req.reply({ body: { results: [] } });
  }).as('search');

  cy.visit('/search');
  cy.get('[data-cy="search-input"]').type('react', { delay: 0 });

  // Advance to just before debounce fires — no call expected
  cy.tick(399);
  cy.wrap(null).then(() => expect(callCount).to.equal(0));

  // Cross the debounce threshold
  cy.tick(1);
  cy.wait('@search');
  cy.wrap(null).then(() => expect(callCount).to.equal(1));

  // Type again mid-debounce — should reset and fire once more
  cy.get('[data-cy="search-input"]').type(' hooks', { delay: 0 });
  cy.tick(400);
  cy.wait('@search');
  cy.wrap(null).then(() => expect(callCount).to.equal(2));
});
```
Tradeoff: `cy.clock()` + `cy.tick()` gives deterministic sub-millisecond control over debounce timing without `cy.wait(500)` sleep calls, cutting debounce test suite time from ~seconds to ~milliseconds per test — but `{ delay: 0 }` in `cy.type()` is mandatory when the clock is frozen; the default `type` delay uses real `setTimeout` to space keystrokes, and with the clock frozen those synthetic keystrokes never fire, causing the `cy.type()` command to hang indefinitely.

---

**Pattern 713** — `cy.clock().invoke('setSystemTime')` for long-duration token expiry without CPU spin
```typescript
it('shows re-authentication modal when JWT expires after 1 hour', () => {
  const now = Date.UTC(2026, 4, 14, 8, 0, 0); // 08:00 UTC

  cy.clock(now);
  cy.intercept('GET', '/api/me', { statusCode: 200, body: { userId: 'u1' } }).as('ping');
  cy.visit('/app');

  // Jump system time forward 1 hour without firing every intervening timer
  cy.clock().invoke('setSystemTime', now + 60 * 60 * 1000);

  // App polls /api/me every 5 min — advance by one polling interval to trigger the check
  cy.tick(5 * 60 * 1000);

  // After setSystemTime the app's JWT expiry check sees "now" as T+1h
  cy.intercept('GET', '/api/me', { statusCode: 401 }).as('pingExpired');
  cy.tick(5 * 60 * 1000);
  cy.wait('@pingExpired');
  cy.get('[data-cy="reauth-modal"]').should('be.visible');
});
```
Tradeoff: `clock.setSystemTime()` moves the `Date` forward without firing all intervening timers, which avoids the CPU and timeout overhead of calling `cy.tick(3600000)` when thousands of `setTimeout` callbacks are scheduled in the app — but `setSystemTime` only updates `Date`; it does not advance the timer queue, so any logic that relies on `setTimeout` callbacks at intermediate intervals between `now` and `now + 1h` will not fire; you must still call `cy.tick()` after `setSystemTime` to advance the timer queue to trigger polling-based checks.

**Pattern 714** — Component test `mountWithRouter()` for route-aware React components
```typescript
// cypress/support/component.tsx
import { mount } from 'cypress/react18';
import { MemoryRouter, Route, Routes } from 'react-router-dom';

Cypress.Commands.add(
  'mountWithRouter',
  (component: React.ReactNode, initialEntry = '/') => {
    return mount(
      <MemoryRouter initialEntries={[initialEntry]}>
        <Routes>
          <Route path="*" element={component} />
        </Routes>
      </MemoryRouter>
    );
  }
);

// Usage
it('redirects unauthenticated user to /login', () => {
  cy.mountWithRouter(<ProtectedRoute><Dashboard /></ProtectedRoute>, '/dashboard');
  // Assert on rendered content, NOT cy.url() — MemoryRouter does not update the iframe URL
  cy.get('[data-cy="login-form"]').should('exist');
});

it('renders breadcrumb based on current path', () => {
  cy.mountWithRouter(<Breadcrumb />, '/products/42/reviews');
  cy.get('[data-cy="breadcrumb"]').should('contain', 'Products').and('contain', 'Reviews');
});
```
Tradeoff: Wrapping mounted components in a `MemoryRouter` with a configurable `initialEntry` lets you test route-dependent rendering without a running dev server — but `cy.url()` inside component tests reads the Cypress test runner's iframe URL, not the `MemoryRouter` internal location; assertions like `cy.url().should('include', '/login')` will always fail because the iframe URL never changes; assert on rendered DOM content instead, or render the `useLocation().pathname` value into a `data-cy="current-path"` element via a helper component for path-state assertions.

**Pattern 715** — Component test `cy.spy()` on Vue 3 `emit` for event contract verification
```typescript
// ConfirmDialog.cy.ts  (Vue 3 + Cypress Component Testing)
import ConfirmDialog from './ConfirmDialog.vue';
import { mount } from 'cypress/vue';

it('emits confirm with payload when OK clicked and cancel when dismissed', () => {
  const onConfirm = cy.spy().as('confirmSpy');
  const onCancel  = cy.spy().as('cancelSpy');

  mount(ConfirmDialog, {
    props: {
      title:   'Delete record?',
      payload: { id: 42 },
      onConfirm,
      onCancel,
    },
  });

  cy.get('[data-cy="dialog-title"]').should('contain', 'Delete record?');

  cy.get('[data-cy="ok-btn"]').click();
  cy.get('@confirmSpy')
    .should('have.been.calledOnce')
    .and('have.been.calledWith', { id: 42 });
  cy.get('@cancelSpy').should('not.have.been.called');

  mount(ConfirmDialog, { props: { title: 'Delete record?', payload: { id: 42 }, onConfirm, onCancel } });
  cy.get('[data-cy="cancel-btn"]').click();
  cy.get('@cancelSpy').should('have.been.calledOnce');
});
```
Tradeoff: Passing `cy.spy()` as a Vue prop listener lets you assert on the emitted event payload with Sinon's `.calledWith()` matcher without mounting a parent wrapper component — but this pattern works only when the component uses `defineEmits` and the parent binds the handler as a prop (`onConfirm`); if the component dispatches events through a shared event bus (e.g., mitt) or provide/inject, the prop spy receives no calls and you must intercept at the event bus level instead.

**Pattern 716** — Component test `mountWithQueryClient()` for React Query data-fetching components
```typescript
// cypress/support/component.tsx
import { mount } from 'cypress/react18';
import { QueryClient, QueryClientProvider } from '@tanstack/react-query';

Cypress.Commands.add(
  'mountWithQueryClient',
  (component: React.ReactNode, queryClientOptions = {}) => {
    const queryClient = new QueryClient({
      defaultOptions: {
        queries: { retry: false, gcTime: Infinity },
        ...queryClientOptions,
      },
    });
    return mount(
      <QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>
        {component}
      </QueryClientProvider>
    );
  }
);

// Usage
it('shows loading skeleton then renders user list', () => {
  cy.intercept('GET', '/api/users', (req) => {
    req.on('response', (res) => { res.setDelay(200); });
    req.continue();
  }).as('getUsers');

  cy.mountWithQueryClient(<UserList />);
  cy.get('[data-cy="skeleton"]').should('be.visible');
  cy.wait('@getUsers');
  cy.get('[data-cy="user-item"]').should('have.length.gt', 0);
});
```
Tradeoff: Creating a fresh `QueryClient` per test with `retry: false` prevents React Query's automatic retry logic from masking failed network stubs and avoids cache bleed across component tests — but setting `gcTime: Infinity` prevents garbage collection of query results between re-renders within a single test, which is useful for testing cache-hit renders; if two `it` blocks share the same `QueryClientProvider` instance via a spec-level `before()` mount, stale query data from the first test will be served from cache in the second, so always construct a new `QueryClient` inside each individual `cy.mountWithQueryClient()` call.

---

### Community Gotchas

**G406** — `cy.intercept()` handler that throws inside `req.on('response')` silently swallows the error instead of failing the test
Why this matters: A developer adds a Chai assertion inside `req.on('response', (res) => { expect(res.statusCode).to.equal(200); })` to fail the test on unexpected error responses. The `expect` call throws an `AssertionError`, but because it executes inside an event listener callback that Cypress cannot attach to its command chain, the error is caught by Cypress's internal network layer and logged only as a browser console warning — the test continues and passes even though the assertion failed. This is identical to the problem of throwing inside a `.then()` handler on a native Promise that lacks a `.catch()`.
Fix: Do not place Chai assertions directly inside `req.on('response')` event listeners. Instead, accumulate response data into a test-scoped array and assert against it in a `cy.wrap(null).then()` after all requests have resolved, or use `req.continue((res) => { if (res.statusCode !== 200) { throw new Error(`Unexpected status: ${res.statusCode}`); } })` which executes in the Cypress command chain context where errors are properly propagated.

---

**G407** — `cy.session()` `setup` callback that contains `cy.visit()` causes the second test to start on a blank page because `cy.visit()` does not re-run when the session is restored from cache
Why this matters: With `testIsolation: true` (the default in Cypress 12+), Cypress clears cookies, localStorage, and the page between every test. When `cy.session()` is called in `beforeEach` and a cached session exists, the `setup` callback is skipped — so any `cy.visit()` inside `setup` never fires for the second and subsequent tests. The test starts on a blank page and `cy.get()` calls immediately fail with "element not found" errors that look like a broken selector, obscuring the real root cause of missing navigation.
Fix: Always place `cy.visit('/your-start-page')` immediately after `cy.session()` in `beforeEach`, never inside the `setup` callback. The `setup` callback should contain only authentication actions (posting credentials, setting cookies/tokens). The navigation that starts the actual test must live outside `setup` so it runs regardless of whether the session was freshly created or restored from cache.

---

**G408** — `cy.clock()` called after `cy.visit()` does not stub `Date` for initialization code that already ran at page load, causing timestamp-dependent state to be captured with the real wall-clock time
Why this matters: A developer writes a test for a "last seen online" feature that formats the timestamp as "just now" if the difference is under 60 seconds. They call `cy.visit('/profile')` first, then `cy.clock(fixedTimestamp)` afterward. The app's component calls `new Date()` inside its `created()` hook to capture the load time, which runs during `cy.visit()` before the clock is stubbed. The `cy.clock()` call then freezes `Date` for subsequent renders, but the initial timestamp has already been captured as the real system time — so the "just now" calculation uses a delta between real-now and frozen-now, producing an unexpected large offset that causes the assertion to fail intermittently depending on test execution speed.
Fix: Always call `cy.clock(timestamp)` before `cy.visit()`. This ensures the stub is active before any application JavaScript executes, including module-level code, framework lifecycle hooks, and service worker registration. If you need to test behavior at different points in time within the same page session, use `cy.clock().invoke('setSystemTime', newTimestamp)` after the initial visit rather than calling `cy.clock()` again.

---

**G409** — `cy.origin()` callback that `cy.wait()`s on an alias defined in the primary origin throws a cross-origin alias error because aliases are scoped to the origin context where they were created
Why this matters: A developer defines `cy.intercept('POST', '/api/token').as('tokenExchange')` in the primary test scope, then inside `cy.origin('https://idp.example.com', () => { cy.wait('@tokenExchange'); })` expects to wait for the token exchange during the OAuth redirect. Cypress throws `Error: cy.wait() could not find a registered alias for: @tokenExchange` because `cy.origin()` runs in an isolated execution context with its own alias registry — aliases defined outside the callback are invisible inside it, and vice versa.
Fix: Move the `cy.intercept().as()` call inside the `cy.origin()` callback if the intercepted request originates from the cross-origin page, or wait for the alias outside the `cy.origin()` block if the request is made after the redirect returns to the primary origin. For requests that span the origin boundary (e.g., a fetch from `idp.example.com` to `api.example.com`), register the intercept on the primary origin after `cy.origin()` returns and call `cy.wait()` in the primary scope.

---

**G410** — Component tests using `cy.stub()` to replace a named ES module export fail silently because static `import` bindings are live read-only references that cannot be reassigned via object property mutation
Why this matters: A developer imports `import { fetchUser } from '../api/users'` in a React component and stubs it in a component test with `cy.stub(usersModule, 'fetchUser').returns(Promise.resolve({ id: 1 }))`. The stub appears to be set up correctly, but the component still calls the real `fetchUser` because the component's static `import` binding holds a reference to the original function pointer established at module parse time — reassigning the property on the module namespace object does not update the binding inside the component's closure. The test neither throws nor warns; it simply exercises the real implementation.
Fix: Refactor the module to use a default-exported object or a service class so that the component holds a reference to the container, not the function directly: `import api from '../api/users'; api.fetchUser()`. Stubbing `api.fetchUser` then works because the component reads through the mutable object reference at call time. Alternatively, use a dependency injection pattern (pass `fetchUser` as a prop or via React context) so that component tests can pass a stub directly without module-level mutation.

## Cycle 66 — 2026-05-14

### Patterns

**Pattern 717** — `cy.intercept()` Middleware Route for Global Authorization Header Injection
```javascript
// cypress/support/commands.js
Cypress.Commands.add('injectAuthHeaders', (token) => {
  cy.intercept(
    { url: '/api/**', middleware: true },
    (req) => {
      req.headers['Authorization'] = `Bearer ${token}`;
      req.headers['X-Request-ID'] = `test-${Date.now()}`;
    }
  ).as('authMiddleware');
});

// cypress/e2e/dashboard.cy.js
beforeEach(() => {
  cy.session('admin', () => {
    cy.request('POST', '/api/auth/login', {
      username: 'admin', password: Cypress.env('ADMIN_PASSWORD'),
    }).then((res) => {
      window.localStorage.setItem('token', res.body.token);
    });
  });
  cy.injectAuthHeaders(window.localStorage.getItem('token'));
  cy.visit('/dashboard');
});

it('fetches user list with auth header', () => {
  cy.get('[data-cy="user-list"]').should('be.visible');
});
```
Tradeoff: Using `{ middleware: true }` ensures this handler fires before all other matching routes, making it the correct place for cross-cutting concerns like auth headers — but because middleware routes execute for every matched request regardless of test, a middleware intercept registered in a `beforeEach` that is not cleared between specs will persist and inject headers into unrelated spec files when `cacheAcrossSpecs` is in use, causing test pollution that only manifests in full `cypress run` mode and not in headed `cypress open` single-spec mode.

---

**Pattern 718** — Disabling Browser Cache via `cy.intercept()` Response Header Mutation to Ensure Intercepts Always Fire
```javascript
// cypress/support/e2e.js — applied globally to prevent cache-serving bypassing intercepts
beforeEach(() => {
  cy.intercept({ url: '**', middleware: true }, (req) => {
    req.on('response', (res) => {
      // Strip all caching directives so subsequent navigations always hit the network
      res.headers['cache-control'] = 'no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate';
      res.headers['pragma'] = 'no-cache';
      delete res.headers['etag'];
      delete res.headers['last-modified'];
    });
  });
});

// Now a per-test intercept is guaranteed to run even for assets the browser previously cached
it('verifies the updated banner text after a content deployment', () => {
  cy.intercept('GET', '/api/config', { fixture: 'config-v2.json' }).as('config');
  cy.visit('/');
  cy.wait('@config');
  cy.get('[data-cy="banner"]').should('contain.text', 'Version 2.0 Released');
});
```
Tradeoff: Globally mutating cache headers guarantees every `cy.intercept()` stub fires on every request, eliminating the entire class of "my intercept didn't match because the browser served from cache" failures — but it increases total network traffic during the Cypress run because static assets (fonts, scripts, images) that would normally be served from the HTTP cache are re-fetched on every `cy.visit()`, adding 100–400 ms per test for asset-heavy applications.

---

**Pattern 719** — Conditional `req.reply()` vs `req.continue()` Based on Request Body Content for Chaos Testing
```javascript
// Simulate a server that rejects requests containing a specific product ID
cy.intercept('POST', '/api/orders', (req) => {
  const body = req.body;

  if (body && body.productId === 'DISCONTINUED-001') {
    // Short-circuit: reply immediately with an error, never hit the real server
    req.reply({
      statusCode: 422,
      body: {
        error: 'PRODUCT_DISCONTINUED',
        message: 'This product is no longer available for purchase.',
      },
      headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    });
  } else {
    // For all other products, let the request pass through to the real server
    req.continue();
  }
}).as('orderSubmit');

it('shows discontinuation error for removed product', () => {
  cy.get('[data-cy="product-select"]').select('DISCONTINUED-001');
  cy.get('[data-cy="submit-order"]').click();
  cy.wait('@orderSubmit');
  cy.get('[data-cy="error-banner"]').should('contain.text', 'no longer available');
});
```
Tradeoff: Mixing `req.reply()` and `req.continue()` within a single handler lets you inject targeted failure scenarios without a separate test-only server endpoint — but request body inspection requires the body to be fully buffered before the handler runs; for multipart or streaming POST requests, `req.body` may be `undefined` or partially populated, and calling `req.reply()` after `req.continue()` has already been invoked throws an `Error: Cannot call reply() after the response has been started` that surfaces as a misleading Cypress internal error rather than a test assertion failure.

---

**Pattern 720** — `cy.session()` Multi-Method Login Factory Using Array IDs to Prevent Collision
```javascript
// cypress/support/auth-commands.js
function loginByForm(username, password) {
  cy.session(['loginByForm', username], () => {
    cy.visit('/login');
    cy.get('[data-cy="username"]').type(username);
    cy.get('[data-cy="password"]').type(password, { log: false });
    cy.get('[data-cy="login-btn"]').click();
    cy.url().should('include', '/dashboard');
  }, {
    validate() {
      cy.request({ url: '/api/me', failOnStatusCode: false })
        .its('status').should('eq', 200);
    },
    cacheAcrossSpecs: true,
  });
}

function loginByApi(username, password) {
  cy.session(['loginByApi', username], () => {
    cy.request('POST', '/api/auth/login', { username, password })
      .then((res) => {
        window.localStorage.setItem('authToken', res.body.token);
        document.cookie = `session=${res.body.sessionId}; path=/`;
      });
  }, {
    validate() {
      cy.request({ url: '/api/me', failOnStatusCode: false })
        .its('status').should('eq', 200);
    },
    cacheAcrossSpecs: true,
  });
}

Cypress.Commands.add('loginByForm', loginByForm);
Cypress.Commands.add('loginByApi', loginByApi);
```
Tradeoff: Prefixing the session ID array with the login method name (`['loginByForm', username]` vs `['loginByApi', username]`) ensures the two strategies produce independent cache entries even for the same username — but using `cacheAcrossSpecs: true` for both strategies simultaneously means a CI run that re-orders spec files may restore a `loginByApi` session for a spec that expects a `loginByForm` session state (e.g., different cookie structure), causing subtle authentication state mismatches that only appear in parallel Cypress Cloud runs where spec distribution is non-deterministic.

---

**Pattern 721** — `cy.session()` `validate` Callback Using `cy.request()` Token Liveness Check
```javascript
// cypress/support/commands.js
Cypress.Commands.add('loginAsEditor', (email) => {
  cy.session(
    ['editor', email],
    () => {
      // Programmatic login — faster than UI form
      cy.request('POST', '/api/auth/token', {
        email,
        password: Cypress.env('EDITOR_PASSWORD'),
        grant_type: 'password',
      }).then((res) => {
        window.localStorage.setItem('access_token', res.body.access_token);
        window.localStorage.setItem('refresh_token', res.body.refresh_token);
        window.localStorage.setItem('token_expiry',
          String(Date.now() + res.body.expires_in * 1000));
      });
    },
    {
      validate() {
        // Lightweight liveness check: a 401 will throw, triggering session re-setup
        cy.request({
          method: 'GET',
          url: '/api/auth/validate',
          headers: {
            Authorization: `Bearer ${window.localStorage.getItem('access_token')}`,
          },
          failOnStatusCode: true,
        });
      },
      cacheAcrossSpecs: true,
    }
  );
});
```
Tradeoff: Using `failOnStatusCode: true` inside `validate` means a 401 response automatically throws, which triggers `cy.session()` to re-run `setup` and obtain fresh credentials without any manual retry logic — but the `validate` callback executes in the browser context, so `window.localStorage.getItem()` returns `null` when the session is being validated in a spec that has a different origin than the one that created it, causing the `Authorization` header to be sent as `Bearer null` and producing a spurious 401 that forces needless re-authentication on every cross-origin spec.

---

**Pattern 722** — `Cypress.session.clearAllSavedSessions()` in `before()` for Forced Re-Authentication During Debug Runs
```javascript
// cypress/e2e/auth-debug.cy.js
describe('Authentication edge cases (debug mode)', () => {
  before(() => {
    // Force all cached sessions to be re-created for this spec during debugging.
    // Remove this call before merging to avoid unnecessary re-auth in CI.
    if (Cypress.env('FORCE_REAUTH')) {
      Cypress.session.clearAllSavedSessions();
    }
  });

  beforeEach(() => {
    cy.loginByApi('testuser@example.com', Cypress.env('TEST_PASSWORD'));
    cy.visit('/settings/security');
  });

  it('shows active session list after fresh login', () => {
    cy.get('[data-cy="session-list"]').should('have.length.gte', 1);
    cy.get('[data-cy="session-item"]').first()
      .should('contain.text', 'Current session');
  });

  it('allows revoking all other sessions', () => {
    cy.get('[data-cy="revoke-all-btn"]').click();
    cy.get('[data-cy="confirmation-dialog"]').should('be.visible');
    cy.get('[data-cy="confirm-revoke"]').click();
    cy.get('[data-cy="session-list"]').should('have.length', 1);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: Gating `clearAllSavedSessions()` behind a `FORCE_REAUTH` env variable lets developers flush stale session caches locally without committing a permanent re-auth overhead to CI — but `clearAllSavedSessions()` clears the in-memory session store for the entire Cypress run, not just the current spec, so calling it in a `before()` hook of any spec that runs before a spec with `cacheAcrossSpecs: true` sessions will force all subsequent specs to re-authenticate, negating the performance benefit of cross-spec caching for the remainder of the run.

**Pattern 723** — `cy.origin()` with `args` for Parameterized Cross-Origin Login Form Interaction
```javascript
// cypress/support/commands.js
Cypress.Commands.add('loginViaIdP', ({ idpUrl, username, password }) => {
  // Navigate to the app, which redirects to the IdP login page
  cy.visit('/app/protected-resource');

  cy.origin(
    idpUrl,
    { args: { username, password } },
    ({ username, password }) => {
      // All variables must come through args — this callback is NOT a closure
      cy.get('[data-testid="username-field"]').type(username);
      cy.get('[data-testid="password-field"]').type(password, { log: false });
      cy.get('[data-testid="sign-in-button"]').click();

      // Wait for the IdP to redirect back to our app origin
      cy.url().should('not.include', Cypress.env('IDP_URL'));
    }
  );

  // After cy.origin() returns, we are back on the primary origin
  cy.url().should('include', '/app/protected-resource');
  cy.get('[data-cy="page-title"]').should('be.visible');
});
```
Tradeoff: Passing credentials via the `args` option is the only supported way to inject runtime values into a `cy.origin()` callback because the callback is serialized and executed in an isolated context rather than as a closure — but `args` uses the structured clone algorithm, so any non-serializable value (functions, class instances, DOM nodes, Cypress chainables) passed via `args` will throw a `DataCloneError` at serialization time that surfaces as an opaque `cy.origin() failed` error, making it critical to ensure all `args` values are plain JSON-compatible objects before passing them.

---

**Pattern 724** — `cy.origin()` Combined with `cy.session()` for Cached SSO Login Across Specs
```javascript
// cypress/support/commands.js
Cypress.Commands.add('loginViaSso', (username) => {
  cy.session(
    ['sso', username],
    () => {
      cy.visit('/');
      // App redirects to third-party SSO provider
      cy.origin(
        Cypress.env('SSO_PROVIDER_ORIGIN'),
        { args: { username, password: Cypress.env('SSO_PASSWORD') } },
        ({ username, password }) => {
          cy.get('#email').type(username);
          cy.get('#password').type(password, { log: false });
          cy.get('[type="submit"]').click();
          // IdP redirects back; wait until we have left the IdP origin
          cy.url().should('not.include', Cypress.env('SSO_PROVIDER_ORIGIN'));
        }
      );
      // Confirm final redirect landed on protected app page
      cy.url().should('include', '/home');
    },
    {
      validate() {
        cy.request({ url: '/api/session', failOnStatusCode: false })
          .its('status').should('eq', 200);
      },
      cacheAcrossSpecs: true,
    }
  );
  cy.visit('/home');
});
```
Tradeoff: Wrapping `cy.origin()` inside `cy.session()` means the full SSO redirect dance (which may involve 3–5 network hops and 1–2 seconds of real time) is performed only once per Cypress run and the resulting cookies are replayed for all subsequent specs — but `cy.intercept()` and `cy.session()` are explicitly prohibited inside a `cy.origin()` callback, so any intercept needed to stub IdP analytics or error-tracking calls that fire during the login page must be registered before the `cy.origin()` call in the primary origin context, where it will be silently ignored for cross-origin requests.

**Pattern 725** — `cy.task()` Database Seeding with Async Promise and Per-Task Timeout Override
```javascript
// cypress.config.js
const { defineConfig } = require('cypress');
const { seedDatabase, resetDatabase } = require('./test-helpers/db');

module.exports = defineConfig({
  e2e: {
    setupNodeEvents(on) {
      on('task', {
        'db:seed': async ({ scenario }) => {
          await resetDatabase();
          const result = await seedDatabase(scenario);
          // MUST return a value — returning undefined causes Cypress to fail the test
          return { rowsInserted: result.count, scenario };
        },
        'db:reset': async () => {
          await resetDatabase();
          return null; // Explicit null when there is no meaningful return value
        },
      });
    },
  },
});

// cypress/e2e/product-catalog.cy.js
describe('Product catalog', () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    // Override default taskTimeout for slow seed operations
    cy.task('db:seed', { scenario: 'full-catalog' }, { timeout: 30000 })
      .then(({ rowsInserted, scenario }) => {
        cy.log(`Seeded ${rowsInserted} rows for scenario: ${scenario}`);
      });
    cy.visit('/catalog');
  });

  it('displays all seeded products', () => {
    cy.get('[data-cy="product-card"]').should('have.length', 50);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: Returning a structured object from `cy.task()` (rather than `null`) lets the test log seeding metadata for debugging flaky tests — but every value passed to and returned from `cy.task()` must be JSON-serializable; returning a Knex `QueryBuilder` object, a Sequelize model instance, or a database connection handle instead of a plain object will cause `cy.task()` to throw a serialization error that manifests as a timeout failure with no clear indication of the root cause.

---

**Pattern 726** — `cy.task()` `readFileMaybe` for Conditional Fixture Loading Without Crashing on Missing Files
```javascript
// cypress.config.js
const fs = require('fs');
const path = require('path');

module.exports = defineConfig({
  e2e: {
    setupNodeEvents(on) {
      on('task', {
        'fs:readFileMaybe': (filePath) => {
          const resolved = path.resolve(filePath);
          if (fs.existsSync(resolved)) {
            return fs.readFileSync(resolved, 'utf8');
          }
          return null; // null signals "not found" without throwing
        },
        'fs:countFiles': (folderPath) => {
          return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
            fs.readdir(path.resolve(folderPath), (err, files) => {
              if (err) return reject(err);
              resolve(files.filter((f) => !f.startsWith('.')).length);
            });
          });
        },
      });
    },
  },
});

// cypress/e2e/export.cy.js
it('export creates a CSV file in the downloads folder', () => {
  const downloadPath = 'cypress/downloads/report.csv';

  // Ensure the file does not exist before the test action
  cy.task('fs:readFileMaybe', downloadPath).should('be.null');

  cy.get('[data-cy="export-btn"]').click();
  cy.get('[data-cy="export-success-toast"]').should('be.visible');

  // Poll until the file appears (cy.task retries on null via cypress-wait-until or manual retry)
  cy.task('fs:readFileMaybe', downloadPath).should('not.be.null');
  cy.task('fs:countFiles', 'cypress/downloads').should('eq', 1);
});
```
Tradeoff: Returning `null` instead of throwing when a file is missing allows the test to make a positive assertion (`should('be.null')`) before an action and a negative assertion (`should('not.be.null')`) after, cleanly encoding the before/after state without try/catch — but `cy.task()` does not automatically retry on `null` the way `cy.get()` retries on empty DOM; to poll for a file that is created asynchronously (e.g., a background export job), you must use a manual retry wrapper like `cypress-wait-until` or a recursive `cy.task()` call, otherwise the assertion will fail immediately on the first invocation before the file is written.

---

**Pattern 727** — `cy.clock(null, ['setTimeout', 'clearTimeout'])` Selective Timer Override Without Affecting `Date`
```javascript
// When you only need to control timers but your app uses Date for display logic,
// selectively override only the timer functions to avoid breaking date formatting.

it('auto-dismisses the notification after 5 seconds without waiting in real time', () => {
  // Stub only timer functions; leave Date.now() and new Date() running at real speed
  // so that timestamp display logic in the notification component is unaffected
  cy.clock(null, ['setTimeout', 'clearTimeout', 'setInterval', 'clearInterval']);

  cy.visit('/notifications');
  cy.get('[data-cy="trigger-notification"]').click();
  cy.get('[data-cy="notification-banner"]').should('be.visible');

  // Advance fake timers by 5 000 ms to trigger the auto-dismiss callback
  cy.tick(5000);

  cy.get('[data-cy="notification-banner"]').should('not.exist');

  // Date-based timestamp in the notification history is still accurate
  // because Date was NOT stubbed
  cy.get('[data-cy="notification-history"]')
    .first()
    .invoke('text')
    .should('match', /\d{1,2}:\d{2} (AM|PM)/);
});
```
Tradeoff: Passing an explicit array of function names to `cy.clock()` lets you freeze only the subset of global time APIs that your test scenario requires, preventing unintended interference with `Date`-dependent UI — but if `setTimeout` and `setInterval` are stubbed selectively without also stubbing `Date`, code that derives a deadline by calling `Date.now() + delayMs` and then passes that deadline to `clearTimeout` will compute a real-wall-clock deadline while the timer fires at fake-clock time, causing the `clearTimeout` call to use a future epoch timestamp as a timer ID (which is a no-op) and leaving the timer running indefinitely after `cy.clock().invoke('restore')`.

---

**Pattern 728** — `cy.clock().invoke('restore')` Mid-Test for Hybrid Real/Fake Timer Assertions
```javascript
// Some tests need fake timers for setup, then real timers for final verification
// (e.g., an animated progress bar that uses requestAnimationFrame after the timer fires)

it('shows progress animation after delayed start, then completes in real time', () => {
  cy.clock();
  cy.visit('/upload');

  cy.get('[data-cy="upload-input"]').selectFile('cypress/fixtures/sample.pdf');
  cy.get('[data-cy="start-upload"]').click();

  // The upload progress bar has a 2-second artificial delay before starting animation
  cy.get('[data-cy="progress-bar"]').should('not.be.visible');
  cy.tick(2000); // Skip the delay synchronously
  cy.get('[data-cy="progress-bar"]').should('be.visible');

  // Restore real timers so requestAnimationFrame-driven animation runs at real speed
  cy.clock().invoke('restore');

  // Now the progress bar completes using real animation frames
  cy.get('[data-cy="progress-bar"][data-progress="100"]', { timeout: 10000 })
    .should('exist');
  cy.get('[data-cy="upload-complete"]').should('be.visible');
});
```
Tradeoff: Calling `cy.clock().invoke('restore')` mid-test restores all native timer functions to their real implementations, allowing you to combine synchronous timer-skipping for artificial delays with real-time waiting for animation-dependent UI — but Cypress does not re-yield the clock subject after `invoke('restore')`, so any subsequent `cy.tick()` calls in the same test will throw `TypeError: cy.tick() can only be called if cy.clock() is active`, which is easy to trigger accidentally when tests are refactored and `cy.tick()` calls are reordered relative to the `restore()` call.

**Pattern 729** — `cy.request()` Recursive Polling Helper for Long-Running Background Jobs
```javascript
// cypress/support/commands.js
Cypress.Commands.add('waitForJobCompletion', (jobId, options = {}) => {
  const {
    maxAttempts = 20,
    interval = 1000,
    attempt = 1,
  } = options;

  cy.request({
    method: 'GET',
    url: `/api/jobs/${jobId}`,
    failOnStatusCode: true,
  }).then((res) => {
    const { status, result } = res.body;

    if (status === 'completed') {
      return cy.wrap(result); // Yield the job result to the next chain step
    }

    if (status === 'failed') {
      throw new Error(`Job ${jobId} failed: ${res.body.error}`);
    }

    if (attempt >= maxAttempts) {
      throw new Error(`Job ${jobId} did not complete after ${maxAttempts} attempts`);
    }

    // Wait the interval, then recurse with incremented attempt count
    cy.wait(interval);
    cy.waitForJobCompletion(jobId, { ...options, attempt: attempt + 1 });
  });
});

// Usage
it('processes the bulk import job and shows row count', () => {
  cy.request('POST', '/api/import', { file: 'large-dataset.csv' })
    .its('body.jobId').then((jobId) => {
      cy.waitForJobCompletion(jobId, { maxAttempts: 30, interval: 2000 });
    });
  cy.visit('/import/history');
  cy.get('[data-cy="import-row-count"]').should('contain.text', '10000');
});
```
Tradeoff: Recursive `cy.request()` polling encapsulates retry logic in a reusable command and surfaces job failures as named test errors rather than timeouts — but `cy.request()` bypasses `cy.intercept()` stubs entirely because it executes in Node rather than the browser, so a test that stubs `/api/jobs/:id` with `cy.intercept()` to simulate a completing job will find that the stub is never invoked by `waitForJobCompletion`, and the command silently hits the real server endpoint; if the real server returns a different schema, the `status` property check will silently evaluate as `undefined` and the poll will exhaust `maxAttempts` with a misleading timeout error.

---

**Pattern 730** — Component Test `cy.spy()` on React Prop Callback to Verify Event Contract
```javascript
// src/components/QuantitySelector.cy.jsx
import React from 'react';
import { mount } from 'cypress/react';
import QuantitySelector from './QuantitySelector';

describe('QuantitySelector', () => {
  it('calls onQuantityChange with the correct new value when increment is clicked', () => {
    const onChangeSpy = cy.spy().as('onQuantityChange');

    mount(
      <QuantitySelector
        initialValue={1}
        min={1}
        max={10}
        onQuantityChange={onChangeSpy}
      />
    );

    cy.get('[data-cy="increment-btn"]').click();

    // Verify the callback was called exactly once with the expected incremented value
    cy.get('@onQuantityChange')
      .should('have.been.calledOnce')
      .and('have.been.calledWith', 2);

    cy.get('[data-cy="increment-btn"]').click();
    cy.get('@onQuantityChange')
      .should('have.been.calledTwice')
      .and('have.been.calledWith', 3);
  });

  it('does not call onQuantityChange when increment is clicked at max value', () => {
    const onChangeSpy = cy.spy().as('onQuantityChange');
    mount(
      <QuantitySelector initialValue={10} min={1} max={10} onQuantityChange={onChangeSpy} />
    );
    cy.get('[data-cy="increment-btn"]').click();
    cy.get('@onQuantityChange').should('not.have.been.called');
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: Using `cy.spy()` directly on a prop callback lets you assert on call count and arguments without importing a separate mocking library, keeping component tests self-contained — but `cy.spy()` wraps the function reference passed at mount time and does not intercept calls made to a re-constructed function if the parent re-renders the component with a new callback identity (e.g., an inline arrow function created on each render); in that case, the spy captures zero calls because React replaced the prop with a new function instance that was never wrapped by the spy, and the test silently passes without verifying anything.

**Pattern 731** — `Cypress.Commands.add()` with `prevSubject: 'element'` for Chainable Within-Table Row Assertion Helper
```javascript
// cypress/support/commands.js

/**
 * Custom child command that chains off a table row element and asserts
 * the value of a specific named cell within that row.
 *
 * Usage: cy.get('[data-cy="order-row"]').first().shouldHaveCellValue('status', 'Shipped')
 */
Cypress.Commands.add(
  'shouldHaveCellValue',
  { prevSubject: 'element' },
  (rowSubject, columnName, expectedValue) => {
    // The subject is the <tr> element; find the cell by its data attribute
    cy.wrap(rowSubject)
      .find(`[data-cy="cell-${columnName}"]`)
      .should('exist')
      .invoke('text')
      .invoke('trim')
      .should('eq', String(expectedValue));

    // Return the original row subject so the chain can continue
    return cy.wrap(rowSubject);
  }
);

// Usage in tests
it('shows correct order details in the order table', () => {
  cy.visit('/orders');
  cy.get('[data-cy="order-row"]').eq(0)
    .shouldHaveCellValue('status', 'Shipped')
    .shouldHaveCellValue('total', '$149.99')
    .shouldHaveCellValue('destination', 'New York, NY');
});
```
Tradeoff: Returning `cy.wrap(rowSubject)` from a `prevSubject: 'element'` command allows the command to be chained multiple times on the same row, producing readable multi-assertion chains — but the `{ prevSubject: 'element' }` constraint means the command is type-checked at runtime by Cypress and will throw `CypressError: Oops, the subject must be a DOM element but you passed: [object Object]` if it is accidentally called after a command that yields a non-DOM value (e.g., after `.invoke('text')` which yields a string); this validation error is more helpful than a generic `find()` failure but can confuse developers who are not aware of Cypress's subject type enforcement for child commands.

### Community Gotchas

**G411** — `cy.task()` Handler That Returns `undefined` Instead of `null` Fails the Test with a Misleading Timeout Error
Why this matters: A developer writes a `cy.task()` handler for a fire-and-forget side effect (e.g., writing a log entry to a file) and forgets to add a return value. The handler function implicitly returns `undefined`. Cypress requires all task handlers to return a non-`undefined` value and throws `Error: The task 'writeLog' returned undefined. Tasks must return a value or a Promise that resolves to a value.` — but this error surfaces in the Cypress runner as a command timeout on the `cy.task()` call rather than an explicit error message in the Command Log, leading developers to increase `taskTimeout` in `cypress.config.js` rather than investigating the handler's return value.
Fix: Always return an explicit value from every `cy.task()` handler. For side-effect-only tasks with no meaningful return, return `null` explicitly: `return null;`. For async handlers, return a Promise that resolves to `null`: `return Promise.resolve(null)`. Add an ESLint rule (`consistent-return`) to the `cypress/plugins/` and `cypress.config.js` files to catch implicit `undefined` returns at lint time before they reach CI.

---

**G412** — `cy.origin()` Callback Silently Ignores Outer-Scope Variables Because It Is Not a Closure
Why this matters: A developer writes `const credentials = { user: 'alice', pass: 'secret' }` in the test body and then writes `cy.origin('https://auth.example.com', () => { cy.get('#user').type(credentials.user); })` expecting the callback to close over `credentials`. In Chrome-family browsers Cypress executes the callback in a separate JavaScript context for the cross-origin page, and the callback is serialized to a string via `Function.prototype.toString()` before being deserialized in the remote context. The `credentials` variable does not exist in the remote context, so `credentials.user` throws `ReferenceError: credentials is not defined` — but this error appears in the test runner as `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'user')` with a stack trace pointing to the callback internals, obscuring the root cause.
Fix: Pass all data needed inside `cy.origin()` through the `args` option: `cy.origin('https://auth.example.com', { args: { user: credentials.user, pass: credentials.pass } }, ({ user, pass }) => { cy.get('#user').type(user); })`. The `args` value is serialized using the structured clone algorithm and deserialized in the remote context, making it available as a function parameter. Only JSON-compatible plain objects, arrays, strings, numbers, booleans, and `null` can be passed; functions, class instances, and DOM elements will throw `DataCloneError`.

---

**G413** — `cy.clock()` Does Not Stub Time Inside Iframes, Causing Timer-Dependent Iframe Content to Run at Real Speed
Why this matters: An application embeds a third-party payment widget or a chat widget inside an `<iframe>`. A developer calls `cy.clock()` to freeze time and then `cy.tick(30000)` to simulate a 30-second session timeout that should trigger a "session expired" warning inside the iframe. The iframe runs its own JavaScript execution context with its own copies of `setTimeout` and `Date`, which are not replaced by Cypress's clock stub — only the top-level `window` is patched. The iframe's timer fires after 30 real seconds, not after `cy.tick(30000)`, causing the test to assert on the warning immediately after `cy.tick()` but find no element because the iframe has not yet triggered its timeout handler.
Fix: If the iframe content is same-origin and under your control, communicate the simulated time to it via `postMessage` or a shared `localStorage` key that the iframe polls. If the iframe is cross-origin (e.g., a third-party widget), do not attempt to control its internal timers with `cy.clock()`; instead, stub the API call that the iframe makes to check session validity using `cy.intercept()` from the primary origin context, and simulate expiry by returning a 401 from the stub rather than relying on timer advancement.

---

**G414** — `cy.request()` Always Bypasses `cy.intercept()` Stubs, Sending Requests Directly to the Real Network
Why this matters: A developer intercepts `GET /api/users` with a fixture stub for E2E tests, then writes a `beforeEach` that calls `cy.request('GET', '/api/users')` to verify the endpoint is reachable before each test. The `cy.request()` bypasses the stub and hits the real server because it executes in the Node.js process, not in the browser's network stack where intercepts operate. In a CI environment without a running backend, the `cy.request()` in `beforeEach` times out, and because it runs before any test body, the failure message reads `cy.request() failed on GET /api/users: connect ECONNREFUSED` — making it appear that the network is misconfigured rather than that an unnecessary liveness check was added to a test that was designed to run against stubs.
Fix: Use `cy.request()` only for operations that genuinely need to bypass stubs — specifically for programmatic test setup against a real server (seeding, token generation) or for direct API contract assertions. Never use `cy.request()` as a liveness check before tests that are designed to run against `cy.intercept()` stubs; the stub registration itself confirms the intent to mock the endpoint, and adding `cy.request()` as a preflight check contradicts that intent and makes the test environment-dependent.

---

**G415** — `cy.session()` `cacheAcrossSpecs` with an Unstable `validate` Callback Forces All Downstream Specs to Re-Authenticate
Why this matters: A team sets `cacheAcrossSpecs: true` to avoid logging in for every spec file in a 40-spec suite. The `validate` callback visits a protected route with `cy.visit('/dashboard')` and asserts `cy.url().should('include', '/dashboard')`. An intermittent feature flag causes `/dashboard` to redirect some users to `/onboarding` during a rollout, which makes the `validate` assertion fail non-deterministically. When `validate` fails on a cached session, Cypress re-runs the full `setup` callback to obtain a fresh session. If this occurs mid-suite in a `cacheAcrossSpecs` scenario, all 30 remaining specs each trigger their own `validate` failure and re-authentication, turning a 5-minute suite into a 15-minute suite with no indication in the test output that the root cause is a flaky feature flag rather than an authentication regression.
Fix: Write `validate` callbacks to make the lightest possible non-UI request: prefer `cy.request({ url: '/api/me', failOnStatusCode: false }).its('status').should('eq', 200)` over `cy.visit()` + URL assertion. A lightweight API check is unaffected by UI-level feature flags and routing changes. For extra resilience, wrap the `validate` request URL in an environment variable so it can be swapped without touching test code when the auth health-check endpoint changes between environments.
