## Cycle 65 — 2026-05-14

### Patterns

**Pattern 717** — `cy.intercept()` browser-cache bypass middleware for cache-controlled resources
```typescript
// cypress/support/e2e.ts
beforeEach(() => {
  cy.intercept('**/*', { middleware: true }, (req) => {
    req.on('before:response', (res) => {
      res.headers['cache-control'] = 'no-store';
      res.headers['pragma'] = 'no-cache';
      res.headers['expires'] = '0';
    });
  });
});

// In a spec — intercept now fires even for previously-cached responses
it('always intercepts GET /api/config even after hot reload', () => {
  cy.intercept('GET', '/api/config').as('config');
  cy.visit('/settings');
  cy.wait('@config').its('response.statusCode').should('eq', 200);
});
```
Tradeoff: Adding a global `middleware: true` intercept that strips cache headers guarantees every network request flows through Cypress's interception layer — eliminating the silent miss where a browser-cached response is served before the test's `cy.intercept()` has a chance to fire — but it also disables HTTP caching for the entire test run, which doubles or triples network round-trips for asset-heavy SPAs during development mode and can expose latency-sensitive timing assertions to false failures if the app uses service-worker pre-caching that itself relies on `Cache-Control` headers.

---

**Pattern 718** — `cy.intercept()` per-request GraphQL alias via `req.alias` assignment inside route handler
```typescript
// cypress/support/commands.ts
Cypress.Commands.add('interceptGql', (operationName: string) => {
  cy.intercept('POST', '/graphql', (req) => {
    const body = req.body as { operationName?: string };
    if (body.operationName === operationName) {
      req.alias = `gql_${operationName}`;
    }
  });
});

// In a spec
it('loads dashboard after CreateProject mutation resolves', () => {
  cy.interceptGql('CreateProject');
  cy.interceptGql('ListProjects');

  cy.visit('/projects/new');
  cy.get('[data-cy="project-name"]').type('Alpha');
  cy.get('[data-cy="submit"]').click();

  cy.wait('@gql_CreateProject')
    .its('response.body.data.createProject.id')
    .should('be.a', 'string');

  cy.wait('@gql_ListProjects');
  cy.get('[data-cy="project-row"]').should('contain.text', 'Alpha');
});
```
Tradeoff: Assigning `req.alias` inside a conditional route handler lets a single `/graphql` intercept fan out into per-operation aliases without registering O(n) separate `cy.intercept()` calls — keeping the network registration list short and avoiding handler-ordering confusion — but because all GraphQL requests share one physical intercept registration, the `cy.wait('@gql_ListProjects')` call will time out if any intermediate mutation also POSTs to `/graphql` without matching an expected operation name, since Cypress's alias queue only dequeues the oldest unmatched request.

---

**Pattern 719** — `cy.intercept()` `req.continue()` with response callback for latency SLO assertion without mocking
```typescript
interface TimedRouteAlias {
  alias: string;
  maxMs: number;
}

function interceptWithLatency({ alias, maxMs }: TimedRouteAlias, url: string) {
  cy.intercept('GET', url, (req) => {
    const start = Date.now();
    req.continue((res) => {
      const elapsed = Date.now() - start;
      expect(elapsed, `${alias} must respond within ${maxMs}ms`).to.be.lessThan(maxMs);
      res.send();
    });
  }).as(alias);
}

it('search endpoint responds within 300 ms under normal load', () => {
  interceptWithLatency({ alias: 'search', maxMs: 300 }, '/api/search*');
  cy.visit('/');
  cy.get('[data-cy="search-input"]').type('cypress');
  cy.wait('@search');
});
```
Tradeoff: Measuring `Date.now()` inside `req.continue()` captures real server round-trip time using the actual backend — providing SLO coverage without a synthetic stub — but the assertion executes inside a network callback where Cypress propagation of thrown errors is not guaranteed on all browser/Cypress version combinations; if the latency SLO fires, the error may surface as an uncaught exception rather than a labelled command failure, making CI log triage harder than a standard `cy.wait('@search').then()` approach.

---

**Pattern 720** — `cy.intercept()` `req.destroy()` for testing app-level network error recovery UI
```typescript
it('shows retry banner when the API is unreachable', () => {
  let callCount = 0;

  cy.intercept('GET', '/api/feed', (req) => {
    callCount += 1;
    if (callCount === 1) {
      // Simulate total network failure on first attempt
      req.destroy();
    } else {
      // Allow subsequent retry attempts to reach the real server
      req.continue();
    }
  }).as('feed');

  cy.visit('/home');
  cy.get('[data-cy="error-banner"]').should('be.visible');
  cy.get('[data-cy="retry-button"]').click();

  cy.wait('@feed').its('response.statusCode').should('eq', 200);
  cy.get('[data-cy="error-banner"]').should('not.exist');
  cy.get('[data-cy="feed-item"]').should('have.length.gt', 0);
});
```
Tradeoff: `req.destroy()` triggers an actual `ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED`-class failure in the browser's Fetch/XHR pipeline, which exercises the app's true error-handling path including any retry logic — unlike stubbing a `{ statusCode: 503 }` response which still constitutes a successful HTTP exchange — but `req.destroy()` does not guarantee which specific browser network error code is emitted, so error message assertions (e.g., `cy.contains('Network Error')`) may be brittle if the app branches on error type rather than error category.

---

**Pattern 721** — `cy.session()` multi-role factory with stable composite ID and lightweight `validate` sentinel
```typescript
type Role = 'admin' | 'editor' | 'viewer';

function loginAs(role: Role, username: string, password: string) {
  cy.session(
    [`${role}`, username],   // composite ID — role + username prevents cross-role cache collision
    () => {
      cy.request('POST', '/api/auth/login', { username, password })
        .its('body.token')
        .then((token: string) => {
          window.localStorage.setItem('auth_token', token);
        });
    },
    {
      validate() {
        cy.request({
          method: 'GET',
          url: '/api/auth/me',
          headers: {
            Authorization: `Bearer ${window.localStorage.getItem('auth_token') ?? ''}`,
          },
          failOnStatusCode: false,
        }).its('status').should('eq', 200);
      },
      cacheAcrossSpecs: true,
    }
  );
}

beforeEach(() => loginAs('admin', Cypress.env('ADMIN_USER'), Cypress.env('ADMIN_PASS')));
```
Tradeoff: Building the session ID from `[role, username]` as a tuple guarantees that two different users with the same role never share a cached session — preventing the subtle bug where `loginAs('admin', 'alice')` followed later by `loginAs('admin', 'bob')` reuses Alice's token for Bob — but `cacheAcrossSpecs: true` means a token revoked server-side mid-run will cause the `validate` sentinel to fail and trigger a fresh `setup`, adding one extra login round-trip for every subsequent spec that needs that role.

---

**Pattern 722** — `cy.session()` with `idleTimeout` simulation using a localStorage expiry sentinel
```typescript
const SESSION_EXPIRY_KEY = 'session_expires_at';
const SESSION_TTL_MS = 30 * 60 * 1000; // 30 minutes

function loginWithExpiry(username: string, password: string) {
  cy.session(
    ['expiry-aware', username],
    () => {
      cy.request('POST', '/api/auth/login', { username, password }).then((res) => {
        window.localStorage.setItem('auth_token', res.body.token);
        window.localStorage.setItem(
          SESSION_EXPIRY_KEY,
          String(Date.now() + SESSION_TTL_MS)
        );
      });
    },
    {
      validate() {
        const expiresAt = Number(window.localStorage.getItem(SESSION_EXPIRY_KEY));
        expect(Date.now()).to.be.lessThan(expiresAt);
      },
    }
  );
}

it('redirects to login after idle timeout', () => {
  loginWithExpiry(Cypress.env('USER'), Cypress.env('PASS'));
  cy.visit('/dashboard');
  cy.clock(Date.now() + SESSION_TTL_MS + 1000); // advance clock past expiry
  cy.get('[data-cy="trigger-check"]').click();   // action that triggers client-side expiry check
  cy.url().should('include', '/login');
});
```
Tradeoff: Storing a `session_expires_at` sentinel in localStorage and checking it inside `validate()` lets Cypress automatically invalidate and recreate sessions that have drifted past their TTL across spec files — avoiding stale-token 401 failures in later specs — but this approach only works when the app also reads that same key at runtime; if the server-side session timeout differs from the localStorage sentinel value (e.g., the server uses a sliding window that extends on each request), the sentinel will expire the session prematurely on the test side even though the real token remains valid.

---

**Pattern 723** — `cy.origin()` with `args` for structured parameterized OAuth credential injection
```typescript
interface OAuthArgs {
  username: string;
  password: string;
  clientId: string;
}

it('completes OAuth authorization code flow with PKCE', () => {
  cy.visit('/connect');
  cy.get('[data-cy="connect-idp"]').click();

  const oauthArgs: OAuthArgs = {
    username: Cypress.env('IDP_USER'),
    password: Cypress.env('IDP_PASS'),
    clientId: Cypress.env('CLIENT_ID'),
  };

  cy.origin(
    'https://idp.example.com',
    { args: oauthArgs },
    ({ username, password, clientId }) => {
      cy.url().should('include', `client_id=${clientId}`);
      cy.get('#username').type(username);
      cy.get('#password').type(password);
      cy.get('[type="submit"]').click();
      cy.get('[data-cy="allow-button"]').click();
    }
  );

  // Back in primary origin after redirect
  cy.url().should('include', '/connect/callback');
  cy.get('[data-cy="connection-status"]').should('have.text', 'Connected');
});
```
Tradeoff: Passing all dynamic values through `args` as a plain serializable object satisfies Cypress's structured-clone boundary requirement — ensuring credentials and IDs cross the origin context correctly — but because `args` values are deep-cloned at the point of the `cy.origin()` call, any mutation of `oauthArgs` after that line (e.g., by a `cy.then()` callback that updates a shared fixture) will not be reflected inside the origin callback, making test flows that need to dynamically derive credentials from a prior response require splitting the logic into a `cy.then()` that constructs a new `args` object before the `cy.origin()` call.

---

**Pattern 724** — `cy.origin()` return value extraction using `.invoke('text')` for serializable string bridging
```typescript
it('asserts that the IdP confirmation page shows the correct application name', () => {
  cy.visit('/authorize');

  const appName = cy
    .origin('https://idp.example.com', () => {
      cy.visit('/consent');
      // cy.get() yields a non-serializable jQuery element — must extract text
      return cy.get('[data-cy="app-name-label"]').invoke('text');
    });

  // Yielded string is serializable and chains normally in primary origin
  appName.should('eq', 'My Application');
});

// Separate test: extracting multiple values via a cy.wrap()-based tuple
it('reads form field values from IdP and asserts them in primary origin', () => {
  cy.origin('https://idp.example.com', () => {
    cy.visit('/profile');
    return cy.get('[data-cy="display-name"]').invoke('text');
  }).then((displayName: string) => {
    expect(displayName.trim()).to.match(/^[A-Z][a-z]+ [A-Z][a-z]+$/);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: Using `.invoke('text')` to extract a primitive string before the cross-origin boundary satisfies the structured-clone serialization requirement — since DOM elements cannot be cloned — but this means you can only assert on the text content of the element, not on its visual properties (color, computed style, visibility), so accessibility or styling assertions that depend on computed CSS must be made inside the `cy.origin()` callback itself before returning the string.

---

**Pattern 725** — `cy.origin()` sequential multi-hop SSO through intermediate redirect domain
```typescript
it('handles three-party SSO: app → gateway → IdP → app', () => {
  cy.visit('/sso/start');

  // Hop 1: SSO gateway (subdomain of company)
  cy.origin('https://sso.corp.example.com', () => {
    cy.url().should('include', '/saml/redirect');
    cy.get('[data-cy="continue"]').click();
  });

  // Hop 2: External identity provider
  const idpArgs = {
    user: Cypress.env('SSO_USER'),
    pass: Cypress.env('SSO_PASS'),
  };
  cy.origin('https://idp.external.com', { args: idpArgs }, ({ user, pass }) => {
    cy.get('#email').type(user);
    cy.get('#password').type(pass);
    cy.get('[type="submit"]').click();
    cy.get('[data-cy="mfa-skip"]').click(); // bypass MFA in test env
  });

  // Back to primary origin after final redirect
  cy.url().should('include', '/dashboard');
  cy.get('[data-cy="user-avatar"]').should('be.visible');
});
```
Tradeoff: Splitting each cross-origin hop into its own sequential top-level `cy.origin()` block satisfies Cypress's prohibition on nested `cy.origin()` calls — which throw immediately — and makes the hop sequence explicit and debuggable in the Cypress command log — but each `cy.origin()` block opens a new iframe execution context and tears it down on completion, meaning any cookies or localStorage values written during Hop 1 that are needed in Hop 2 must be pre-seeded before the first `cy.origin()` or read back from the network response rather than from the browser storage of the intermediate domain.

**Pattern 726** — `Cypress.Commands.addQuery()` typed retry-able table-row finder with `has` attribute guard
```typescript
// cypress/support/commands.ts
declare global {
  namespace Cypress {
    interface Chainable {
      findRowByText(text: string): Chainable<JQuery<HTMLTableRowElement>>;
    }
  }
}

Cypress.Commands.addQuery('findRowByText', (text: string) => {
  // addQuery requires the double-function pattern:
  // outer fn registers; inner fn is called each retry
  return () => {
    const rows = cy.$$('tbody tr');
    const match = rows.filter((_: number, el: HTMLTableRowElement) =>
      Cypress.$(el).text().trim().includes(text)
    );
    if (match.length === 0) {
      throw new Error(`No table row found containing: "${text}"`);
    }
    return match.first();
  };
});

it('finds newly-added row without cy.get() polling delay', () => {
  cy.visit('/admin/users');
  cy.get('[data-cy="add-user"]').click();
  cy.get('[data-cy="username-input"]').type('jane.doe');
  cy.get('[data-cy="save"]').click();
  cy.findRowByText('jane.doe').should('be.visible');
});
```
Tradeoff: `Cypress.Commands.addQuery()` registers the inner function as a retry-able synchronous query — so Cypress keeps re-invoking it until the row appears or the assertion timeout expires — which is fundamentally more correct than `cy.get('tbody tr').contains(text)` for dynamic tables where the DOM is re-rendered after each data fetch, because `.contains()` matches the first element in the current DOM snapshot and does not re-query; however, `addQuery()` requires strict synchronous DOM access via `cy.$$()` and prohibits asynchronous operations inside the inner function, so any row-finding logic that needs to cross an iframe boundary or read from a Web Worker cannot use this API.

**Pattern 727** — `Cypress.Commands.overwrite()` for `cy.type()` with automatic prior-value clear and masked PII logging
```typescript
// cypress/support/commands.ts
Cypress.Commands.overwrite(
  'type',
  (originalFn, element: Cypress.PrevSubject, text: string, options?: Partial<Cypress.TypeOptions>) => {
    const isSensitive = options && (options as { sensitive?: boolean }).sensitive;

    // Always clear before typing to prevent accidental value concatenation
    cy.wrap(element, { log: false }).clear({ log: false });

    if (isSensitive) {
      Cypress.log({
        name: 'type',
        message: '***',
        consoleProps: () => ({ note: 'sensitive value masked' }),
      });
      return originalFn(element, text, { ...options, log: false });
    }

    return originalFn(element, text, { ...options });
  }
);

it('fills password field without exposing value in logs', () => {
  cy.visit('/login');
  cy.get('#email').type('user@example.com');
  cy.get('#password').type(Cypress.env('USER_PASS'), { sensitive: true } as never);
  cy.get('[type="submit"]').click();
});
```
Tradeoff: Overwriting `cy.type()` globally to auto-clear and mask sensitive fields eliminates an entire class of test flakiness caused by pre-filled input values left over from autofill or previous test state — and the `sensitive` option prevents passwords from appearing in the Cypress Cloud screenshot timeline — but the automatic `clear()` call breaks legitimate tests for inputs with `readonly` or `disabled` attributes where clearing is invalid and will throw, requiring those callers to pass `{ noClear: true }` and adding a custom option branch to the overwrite that the TypeScript declaration must also expose.

---

**Pattern 728** — `cy.clock()` seeded before `cy.visit()` for deterministic date-dependent UI rendering
```typescript
const FIXED_NOW = new Date('2026-03-15T10:00:00.000Z').getTime();

beforeEach(() => {
  // Must call cy.clock() BEFORE cy.visit() so that module-level
  // and lifecycle-hook calls to new Date() see the stubbed time
  cy.clock(FIXED_NOW, ['Date', 'setTimeout', 'setInterval']);
});

it('shows "expires in 3 days" badge for a token expiring 2026-03-18', () => {
  cy.visit('/api-keys');
  cy.get('[data-cy="token-row"]')
    .contains('my-api-key')
    .closest('tr')
    .find('[data-cy="expiry-badge"]')
    .should('have.text', 'Expires in 3 days');
});

it('shows "expired" badge after clock advances past expiry', () => {
  cy.visit('/api-keys');
  // Advance 4 days in synthetic time — no real wait required
  cy.tick(4 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000);
  cy.get('[data-cy="expiry-badge"]').should('have.text', 'Expired');
});
```
Tradeoff: Seeding `cy.clock()` before `cy.visit()` ensures the stub is active before any application JavaScript — including module initializers, framework `created()` hooks, and service worker registration — so all `new Date()` calls return the fixed timestamp and time-relative UI is deterministic; however, stubbing `setTimeout` and `setInterval` globally means that third-party libraries loaded by the page (analytics SDKs, polling libraries, heartbeat pings) will also have their timers frozen, which can cause those libraries to throw unhandled errors if they rely on timers completing within a real-time window, requiring a selective stub that passes an array of only the specific globals to freeze rather than using the default all-timers behavior.

**Pattern 729** — `cy.clock()` + `cy.tick()` for testing debounced search input without real-world wait
```typescript
const DEBOUNCE_MS = 400;

it('fires exactly one API call after debounced search input settles', () => {
  cy.clock();

  let apiCallCount = 0;
  cy.intercept('GET', '/api/search*', (req) => {
    apiCallCount += 1;
    req.reply({ body: { results: [] } });
  }).as('search');

  cy.visit('/search');
  cy.get('[data-cy="search-input"]').type('cyp'); // triggers debounce timer on each keystroke
  cy.tick(DEBOUNCE_MS - 1);                       // advance to just before debounce fires
  cy.wrap(null).then(() => expect(apiCallCount).to.eq(0)); // no call yet
  cy.tick(1);                                     // push past debounce threshold
  cy.wait('@search');
  cy.wrap(null).then(() => expect(apiCallCount).to.eq(1)); // exactly one call
});
```
Tradeoff: Using `cy.tick()` to advance synthetic time by the exact debounce duration tests the timing contract of the debounce implementation without any `cy.wait(ms)` real-time delay — making the test run in milliseconds rather than seconds and eliminating the flakiness window around the debounce boundary — but because `cy.clock()` also freezes `setInterval`, any polling-based status update or keepalive that runs during the debounce window will also be suspended, which can cause the app to enter an unexpected state (e.g., connection timeout) if the polling interval is shorter than the debounce period and the app treats a missed poll as a session error.

**Pattern 730** — `cy.clock().invoke('setSystemTime')` for long-duration token expiry simulation without CPU spin
```typescript
it('forces re-authentication when JWT expires after 8 hours', () => {
  const loginTime = new Date('2026-04-01T09:00:00.000Z').getTime();
  cy.clock(loginTime);

  cy.visit('/login');
  cy.get('#email').type('user@example.com');
  cy.get('#password').type(Cypress.env('USER_PASS'));
  cy.get('[type="submit"]').click();
  cy.url().should('include', '/dashboard');

  // Advance clock 8 hours + 1 second — simulates token expiry without cy.tick(28801000)
  // which would need to pump all timers sequentially and could trigger thousands of intervals
  cy.clock().invoke('setSystemTime', loginTime + 8 * 60 * 60 * 1000 + 1000);

  // Trigger the action that checks token validity
  cy.get('[data-cy="fetch-profile"]').click();
  cy.url().should('include', '/login');
  cy.get('[data-cy="session-expired-banner"]').should('be.visible');
});
```
Tradeoff: Calling `cy.clock().invoke('setSystemTime', targetMs)` jumps the synthetic clock to an arbitrary future timestamp in one step — bypassing the need to `cy.tick()` through 28,800,000 ms which would trigger every `setInterval` and `setTimeout` callback registered in that window, potentially producing thousands of Cypress log entries and slowing the test by several seconds — but `setSystemTime` does not fire any pending timers for the skipped interval, so if the app's token expiry check is implemented as a `setInterval` that fires every 60 seconds and compares `Date.now()` to the stored expiry, those interval callbacks will not have run and the expiry state will only be detected when the interval next fires after the time jump, which happens only if you call `cy.tick(60001)` after `setSystemTime` to trigger one polling cycle.

**Pattern 731** — Component test `cy.spy()` on a service method injected via React context for call-contract verification
```typescript
// cypress/component/NotificationService.cy.tsx
import React from 'react';
import { mount } from 'cypress/react18';
import { NotificationContext } from '../../src/context/NotificationContext';
import { SaveButton } from '../../src/components/SaveButton';

it('calls notificationService.success exactly once on successful save', () => {
  const notificationService = {
    success: cy.spy().as('successSpy'),
    error: cy.spy().as('errorSpy'),
  };

  cy.intercept('POST', '/api/save', { statusCode: 200, body: { ok: true } });

  mount(
    <NotificationContext.Provider value={notificationService}>
      <SaveButton resourceId="abc-123" />
    </NotificationContext.Provider>
  );

  cy.get('[data-cy="save-btn"]').click();

  cy.get('@successSpy')
    .should('have.been.calledOnce')
    .and('have.been.calledWithMatch', { message: 'Saved successfully' });

  cy.get('@errorSpy').should('not.have.been.called');
});
```
Tradeoff: Wrapping a plain object's methods with `cy.spy()` and injecting it via React context gives the component test precise call-count and argument-shape assertions without any DOM assertion workarounds — making the service contract the primary test subject — but this approach tightly couples the test to the component's use of `useContext(NotificationContext)` rather than to the observable UI outcome (e.g., a toast appearing), so if the notification system is later refactored to use a global event bus instead of React context, the test will pass incorrectly because the spy no longer intercepts the real notification path.

**Pattern 732** — Component test `mountWithI18n()` for locale-dependent text rendering without full app bootstrap
```typescript
// cypress/support/component.ts
import { mount } from 'cypress/react18';
import i18n from '../../src/i18n';
import { I18nextProvider } from 'react-i18next';

declare global {
  namespace Cypress {
    interface Chainable {
      mountWithI18n(
        component: React.ReactNode,
        locale?: string
      ): Cypress.Chainable;
    }
  }
}

Cypress.Commands.add(
  'mountWithI18n',
  (component: React.ReactNode, locale = 'en') => {
    i18n.changeLanguage(locale);
    return mount(
      <I18nextProvider i18n={i18n}>{component}</I18nextProvider>
    );
  }
);

// In a spec
it('renders French button label when locale is fr', () => {
  cy.mountWithI18n(<SubmitButton />, 'fr');
  cy.get('[data-cy="submit"]').should('have.text', 'Envoyer');
});

it('renders English button label when locale is en', () => {
  cy.mountWithI18n(<SubmitButton />, 'en');
  cy.get('[data-cy="submit"]').should('have.text', 'Submit');
});
```
Tradeoff: Wrapping `mount()` with a locale-aware helper that calls `i18n.changeLanguage()` before mounting tests the real i18next translation pipeline rather than mocking it — catching missing translation key regressions and RTL layout issues that mocks would hide — but calling `i18n.changeLanguage()` mutates the shared `i18n` singleton, so if two component tests run in the same spec with different locales and the second test's `mountWithI18n()` call is preceded by a `cy.get()` assertion that runs before the language has fully changed (i18next's `changeLanguage` is async), the component may momentarily render with the previous locale's strings, causing flaky text assertions.

### Community Gotchas

**G411** — `cy.intercept()` handler registration order: last-registered handler wins, not first, causing unexpected stub override when a `beforeEach` global stub is silently overridden by a test-local stub with a broader URL pattern
Why this matters: A developer registers `cy.intercept('GET', '/api/**', { fixture: 'empty.json' }).as('apiCatchAll')` in `beforeEach` as a safety net, then in a specific test registers `cy.intercept('GET', '/api/users', fixtureData).as('users')`. They expect the more specific `/api/users` handler to take precedence. Instead, Cypress evaluates handlers in reverse order of registration — LIFO — so the `beforeEach` catch-all, registered first, is evaluated last and overrides the test-local stub for `/api/users` requests, returning `empty.json` instead of `fixtureData` and causing the test to fail with empty data.
Fix: Register broad catch-all intercepts after specific ones, or mark catch-all intercepts with `{ middleware: true }` so they run in a separate pass before non-middleware handlers rather than competing with them in LIFO order. Alternatively, restructure the `beforeEach` to only intercept routes the test does not locally override by using `times: 1` on the specific intercept so it is consumed before the catch-all can match.

---

**G412** — `cy.session()` `validate()` that performs a `cy.visit()` causes the browser to navigate away from the test's intended start URL because `validate()` runs inside the `beforeEach` context before any spec-level `cy.visit()` call
Why this matters: A developer adds `cy.visit('/api/auth/me')` inside `validate()` to check the authentication status page. The validate callback passes, but the test then starts on `/api/auth/me` instead of the intended `/dashboard`. The first `cy.get('[data-cy="dashboard-header"]')` call fails with "element not found" because the browser is still on the auth check page. The error message does not mention the session validation or the unexpected navigation, making the root cause very hard to identify.
Fix: Use `cy.request()` for session validation instead of `cy.visit()`. A `cy.request({ url: '/api/auth/me', failOnStatusCode: false }).its('status').should('eq', 200)` call checks the session without navigating the browser, leaving the page state untouched for the test's own `cy.visit()` call that follows `cy.session()` in `beforeEach`.

---

**G413** — `cy.origin()` callback that references a `const` variable from the outer test scope — rather than passing it via `args` — receives `undefined` at runtime because the callback is serialized and executed in an isolated context
Why this matters: A developer writes `const token = 'Bearer abc123'` outside the `cy.origin()` call, then uses it directly inside the callback: `cy.origin('https://idp.example.com', () => { cy.get('#token-input').type(token); })`. In their IDE the closure looks valid. At runtime, Cypress serializes the callback function as a string and re-executes it in the cross-origin iframe context, where the outer scope no longer exists — `token` is `undefined`, `cy.type(undefined)` silently types the string `"undefined"` into the field, and the test either passes incorrectly or fails with a confusing value mismatch error rather than a "variable not found" error.
Fix: Pass all variables needed inside `cy.origin()` through the `args` option: `cy.origin('https://idp.example.com', { args: { token } }, ({ token }) => { cy.get('#token-input').type(token); })`. The `args` object is the only data transmission channel across the origin boundary; any outer-scope variable accessed without `args` will silently resolve to `undefined`.

---

**G414** — `Cypress.Commands.addQuery()` inner function that calls `cy.$$()` with a CSS attribute selector containing pseudo-syntax throws a jQuery/Sizzle selector parse error in certain Cypress versions
Why this matters: A developer writes a custom `findInput` query using `cy.$$('input[type="email"]')` expecting it to work identically to `cy.get('input[type="email"]')`. In Cypress versions that bundle jQuery 3.6.x (which uses the Sizzle CSS selector engine), the selector is parsed correctly. In Cypress versions that upgraded to jQuery 4.x or replaced Sizzle with a native `querySelectorAll` shim, the same selector either throws or returns an empty set because the internal evaluation path changed. The test fails with a cryptic jQuery internal error rather than "element not found".
Fix: Use `cy.$$(document.querySelectorAll('input[type="email"]'))` — wrapping the native `querySelectorAll` result in a jQuery object — inside `addQuery()` inner functions. This bypasses Sizzle entirely and uses the browser's native CSS selector engine, which has consistent behavior across all Cypress versions and supports the full CSS4 attribute selector syntax.

---

**G415** — Component test that calls `cy.intercept()` after `mount()` does not intercept requests triggered by the component's `useEffect` that fires synchronously on mount, because `cy.intercept()` is not yet registered when the initial render effect runs
Why this matters: A React component calls `fetch('/api/data')` inside a `useEffect(() => { ... }, [])` hook that fires immediately after the first render. A developer writes the test as: `mount(<DataComponent />)` followed by `cy.intercept('GET', '/api/data', fixture).as('data')`. The `useEffect` fetch fires during the React render cycle triggered by `mount()`, which executes before Cypress processes the subsequent `cy.intercept()` command — so the real network request goes through unintercepted, hitting the actual backend (or failing with a network error in CI where no backend exists) and the `cy.wait('@data')` call times out.
Fix: Always register `cy.intercept()` calls before calling `mount()`. The correct order is: `cy.intercept('GET', '/api/data', fixture).as('data')` then `mount(<DataComponent />)` then `cy.wait('@data')`. This mirrors the E2E pattern of intercepting before `cy.visit()` and ensures that all network interception rules are active before any component lifecycle code runs.

## Cycle 67 — 2026-05-14

### Patterns

**Pattern 733** — `cy.request()` recursive polling until backend seeding completes before `cy.visit()`
```javascript
// cypress/support/commands.ts
Cypress.Commands.add('waitForSeed', (maxAttempts = 10) => {
  function poll(attempt: number): Cypress.Chainable {
    return cy
      .request({ url: '/api/health/seed', failOnStatusCode: false })
      .then((res) => {
        if (res.status === 200 && res.body.seeded === true) {
          return;
        }
        if (attempt >= maxAttempts) {
          throw new Error(
            `Seed not ready after ${maxAttempts} attempts: ${JSON.stringify(res.body)}`
          );
        }
        cy.wait(500);
        return poll(attempt + 1);
      });
  }
  return poll(1);
});

// In beforeEach
beforeEach(() => {
  cy.task('db:reset');
  cy.waitForSeed();
  cy.visit('/');
});
```
Tradeoff: Polling via `cy.request()` inside a recursive helper gives a deterministic readiness gate without introducing a fixed `cy.wait(ms)` sleep — but each polling iteration consumes a Cypress command queue slot and resets the `defaultCommandTimeout` retry clock to zero, so setting `maxAttempts` too high in a slow CI environment can push total test setup time past the spec timeout; cap `maxAttempts` at a value where `maxAttempts × 500ms` comfortably fits within your `taskTimeout` configuration value.

---

**Pattern 734** — `cy.intercept()` with `req.destroy()` to test network-error recovery UI
```javascript
it('shows retry banner when primary API request is destroyed', () => {
  let callCount = 0;
  cy.intercept('GET', '/api/feed', (req) => {
    callCount += 1;
    if (callCount === 1) {
      req.destroy(); // simulates TCP connection drop, not an HTTP error response
    } else {
      req.reply({ fixture: 'feed.json' });
    }
  }).as('feedRequest');

  cy.visit('/home');
  cy.wait('@feedRequest');
  cy.get('[data-cy="network-error-banner"]').should('be.visible');
  cy.get('[data-cy="retry-button"]').click();
  cy.wait('@feedRequest');
  cy.get('[data-cy="feed-item"]').should('have.length.gt', 0);
  cy.get('[data-cy="network-error-banner"]').should('not.exist');
});
```
Tradeoff: `req.destroy()` simulates a hard TCP-level failure (no response at all) rather than an HTTP 5xx, which is the only way to reach error-handling branches that check for `TypeError: Failed to fetch` rather than non-2xx status codes — but `req.destroy()` is not supported inside `cy.origin()` cross-origin contexts and will throw; for cross-origin fetch failure testing, substitute `req.reply({ statusCode: 503 })` to approximate the failure path instead.

---

**Pattern 735** — `cy.selectFile()` with `{ action: 'drag-drop' }` for drop-zone upload components
```javascript
it('uploads a CSV via drag-and-drop and previews the first row', () => {
  // Build the file object programmatically to avoid fixture path fragility
  cy.fixture('sample-data.csv', 'binary')
    .then(Cypress.Buffer.from)
    .then((buf) => {
      cy.get('[data-cy="drop-zone"]').selectFile(
        {
          contents: buf,
          fileName: 'sample-data.csv',
          mimeType: 'text/csv',
          lastModified: Date.now(),
        },
        { action: 'drag-drop' }
      );
    });

  cy.get('[data-cy="preview-table"] tbody tr')
    .first()
    .find('td')
    .first()
    .should('not.be.empty');

  cy.get('[data-cy="upload-status"]').should('contain.text', 'sample-data.csv');
});
```
Tradeoff: Constructing the file object from `Cypress.Buffer` rather than a fixture path allows runtime control over `fileName` and `mimeType`, enabling tests for MIME-type validation logic without maintaining multiple identically-named fixture files — but `{ action: 'drag-drop' }` dispatches `dragenter`, `dragover`, and `drop` DOM events synthetically, so drop-zone libraries that require `dataTransfer.items` to be populated (e.g., react-dropzone in certain modes) may still reject the file; in those cases, add `{ force: true }` and verify that the library's internal state is updated rather than relying solely on UI assertions.

**Pattern 736** — `cy.press()` keyboard tab-order assertion for accessibility compliance
```javascript
it('tab order through the checkout form matches the visual layout', () => {
  cy.visit('/checkout');

  // Start focus on the first field explicitly
  cy.get('[data-cy="card-number"]').focus();
  cy.get('[data-cy="card-number"]').should('have.focus');

  cy.press(Cypress.Keyboard.Keys.TAB);
  cy.get('[data-cy="expiry-date"]').should('have.focus');

  cy.press(Cypress.Keyboard.Keys.TAB);
  cy.get('[data-cy="cvv"]').should('have.focus');

  cy.press(Cypress.Keyboard.Keys.TAB);
  cy.get('[data-cy="billing-zip"]').should('have.focus');

  cy.press(Cypress.Keyboard.Keys.TAB);
  cy.get('[data-cy="submit-payment"]').should('have.focus');

  // Verify Shift+Tab reverses correctly
  cy.press(Cypress.Keyboard.Keys.SHIFT_TAB);
  cy.get('[data-cy="billing-zip"]').should('have.focus');
});
```
Tradeoff: `cy.press(Cypress.Keyboard.Keys.TAB)` dispatches a real `keydown` event on the focused element, which exercises the browser's native focus management — catching `tabindex` ordering bugs and modal trap failures that `cy.trigger('keydown')` simulated events would not catch — but `cy.press()` returns `null` and cannot be chained, so each assertion must be a separate `cy.get().should('have.focus')` call; `cy.press()` is only available in Cypress 13.6+ and throws in older versions, so gate its use with a `Cypress.version` semver check in shared support files.

---

**Pattern 737** — `cypress-axe` `checkA11y()` with `includedImpacts` filter and `cy.task` violation reporter
```javascript
// cypress/support/a11y.ts
import 'cypress-axe';

function logViolations(violations: any[]) {
  const fmt = violations
    .map(
      ({ id, impact, description, nodes }) =>
        `[${impact.toUpperCase()}] ${id}: ${description} — ${nodes.length} node(s)`
    )
    .join('\n');
  cy.task('log', fmt); // echoes to terminal stdout
}

Cypress.Commands.add('checkCriticalA11y', (context?: string) => {
  cy.checkA11y(
    context,
    {
      runOnly: { type: 'tag', values: ['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa'] },
      includedImpacts: ['critical', 'serious'],
    },
    logViolations,
    false // skipFailures = false: violations hard-fail the test
  );
});

// In a spec
it('login page has no critical WCAG 2.1 AA violations', () => {
  cy.visit('/login');
  cy.injectAxe();
  cy.checkCriticalA11y('[data-cy="login-form"]');
});
```
Tradeoff: Scoping `includedImpacts` to `['critical', 'serious']` prevents minor cosmetic violations from blocking CI while still catching keyboard-inaccessible controls and color-contrast failures — but `moderate` and `minor` violations accumulate silently until a separate audit run; maintain a parallel `skipFailures: true` check that logs all violations to a test artifact so the team has visibility into the full violation inventory without blocking the pipeline.

**Pattern 738** — `cy.task()` for database state seeding and teardown via Node.js ORM
```javascript
// cypress.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from 'cypress';
import { PrismaClient } from '@prisma/client';

const prisma = new PrismaClient();

export default defineConfig({
  e2e: {
    setupNodeEvents(on) {
      on('task', {
        async 'db:seed:user'(attrs: Partial<User>) {
          return prisma.user.create({
            data: {
              email: attrs.email ?? `seed+${Date.now()}@test.local`,
              role: attrs.role ?? 'viewer',
              ...attrs,
            },
          });
        },
        async 'db:clean:users'() {
          await prisma.user.deleteMany({
            where: { email: { contains: '@test.local' } },
          });
          return null; // task must never return undefined
        },
      });
    },
  },
});

// In a spec
beforeEach(() => {
  cy.task<User>('db:seed:user', { role: 'admin' }).as('adminUser');
});
afterEach(() => {
  cy.task('db:clean:users');
});
```
Tradeoff: Running ORM calls directly in `setupNodeEvents` gives exact control over test fixture state and avoids HTTP round-trips to seed endpoints — but the Prisma client instance is shared across all parallel Cypress workers in the same process; in `--parallel` cloud runs where multiple spec workers share the Node.js plugin process, concurrent `db:seed:user` tasks can create race conditions on unique-constraint columns unless each seed call uses a unique discriminator (e.g., the `Date.now()` suffix in the email field).

**Pattern 739** — Per-test retry configuration with `Cypress.currentRetry` guard to skip expensive setup on re-runs
```javascript
// cypress.config.ts — global baseline
export default defineConfig({
  retries: { runMode: 2, openMode: 0 },
});

// In a spec with expensive setup
describe('payment flow', { retries: { runMode: 3, openMode: 1 } }, () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    // Only re-seed on the first attempt; retries reuse the existing DB state
    if (Cypress.currentRetry === 0) {
      cy.task('db:seed:order', { status: 'pending' }).as('order');
    }
    cy.session('paymentUser', () => {
      cy.request('POST', '/api/login', {
        email: 'pay@test.local',
        password: 'secret',
      });
    });
    cy.visit('/orders');
  });

  it('completes checkout and shows confirmation', () => {
    cy.get('[data-cy="checkout-btn"]').click();
    cy.get('[data-cy="confirmation-number"]').should('be.visible');
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: Gating the expensive `db:seed` task with `Cypress.currentRetry === 0` prevents redundant database mutations on retry attempts, which is critical when seed operations create rows that trigger unique-constraint violations on the second run — but if the failure was caused by stale seed data (e.g., a prior test partial-mutated the order), the retry exercises the same broken state rather than starting fresh; only use this pattern for flakiness caused by timing or network instability, not for seed-data-dependent failures.

**Pattern 740** — `cy.intercept()` GraphQL operation aliasing via `req.alias` for fine-grained wait control
```javascript
// cypress/support/graphql.ts
export function aliasGraphQLOperation(req: any) {
  if (req.body?.operationName) {
    req.alias = `gql_${req.body.operationName}`;
  }
}

// In beforeEach — single catch-all intercept produces per-operation aliases
beforeEach(() => {
  cy.intercept('POST', '/graphql', aliasGraphQLOperation);
});

// In a spec
it('shows user profile after GetUser query resolves', () => {
  cy.visit('/profile/42');
  cy.wait('@gql_GetUser')
    .its('response.body.data.user')
    .should((user) => {
      expect(user).to.have.property('id', '42');
      expect(user.name).to.be.a('string');
    });
  cy.get('[data-cy="profile-name"]').should('not.be.empty');
});

it('displays error state when GetUser returns null', () => {
  cy.intercept('POST', '/graphql', (req) => {
    if (req.body?.operationName === 'GetUser') {
      req.reply({ body: { data: { user: null } } });
    }
  });
  cy.visit('/profile/42');
  cy.get('[data-cy="profile-error"]').should('be.visible');
});
```
Tradeoff: Setting `req.alias` inside the handler dynamically converts a single catch-all intercept into per-operation aliases, avoiding the combinatorial explosion of one `cy.intercept` per GraphQL operation — but when two operations fire concurrently (e.g., `GetUser` and `GetPermissions` in a page-level query batch), `cy.wait('@gql_GetUser')` matches only the first request whose `operationName` matches, leaving the second queued response unconsumed; use a generous `{ timeout: 8000 }` and verify the response body rather than assuming a single wait captures all instances.

**Pattern 741** — `cy.within()` scoped table-row assertion to avoid ambiguous multi-row selectors
```javascript
it('updates only the target row status without affecting sibling rows', () => {
  cy.visit('/users');

  // Scope all sub-assertions to the specific row matching the target email
  cy.contains('[data-cy="user-row"]', 'alice@example.com').within(() => {
    cy.get('[data-cy="status-badge"]').should('have.text', 'Active');
    cy.get('[data-cy="deactivate-btn"]').click();
  });

  // Confirm the targeted row changed
  cy.contains('[data-cy="user-row"]', 'alice@example.com').within(() => {
    cy.get('[data-cy="status-badge"]').should('have.text', 'Inactive');
  });

  // Confirm a sibling row is unaffected
  cy.contains('[data-cy="user-row"]', 'bob@example.com').within(() => {
    cy.get('[data-cy="status-badge"]').should('have.text', 'Active');
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: Chaining `.within()` off `cy.contains('[data-cy="user-row"]', email)` creates a precise DOM scope that prevents `cy.get('[data-cy="status-badge"]')` from matching identical elements in other rows — eliminating the "subject is ambiguous" error in tables with many visually identical cells — but `.within()` requires its parent to be a single node; if `cy.contains()` matches multiple rows with the same email (a duplicate-data regression), Cypress 12+ throws "Subject must be a single element" rather than silently matching the first, which is actually desirable as a secondary uniqueness assertion.

**Pattern 742** — Component test `cy.spy()` on a React `useContext` provider value method
```javascript
// NotificationContext.tsx — the context shape
// interface NotificationCtx { notify: (msg: string, type: 'info' | 'error') => void; }

import { NotificationContext } from '../../contexts/NotificationContext';

it('calls notify("error") when the form submit fails', () => {
  const notifySpy = cy.spy().as('notifySpy');

  cy.mount(
    <NotificationContext.Provider value={{ notify: notifySpy }}>
      <ContactForm />
    </NotificationContext.Provider>
  );

  // Stub the network to simulate a 422 validation error
  cy.intercept('POST', '/api/contacts', {
    statusCode: 422,
    body: { error: 'Invalid email' },
  });

  cy.get('[data-cy="email-input"]').type('not-an-email');
  cy.get('[data-cy="submit-btn"]').click();

  cy.get('@notifySpy').should('have.been.calledOnce');
  cy.get('@notifySpy').should('have.been.calledWith', 'Invalid email', 'error');
});
```
Tradeoff: Providing a spy as the `notify` function directly via `NotificationContext.Provider` decouples the component test from the real notification service implementation, making it a pure contract test for how the component calls the context API — but a real integration bug where the app-level `NotificationContext.Provider` wraps the value differently (e.g., with `useMemo`) will not be caught; supplement with an E2E test or a provider integration test to verify the full notification pipeline.

**Pattern 743** — `cy.intercept()` response fixture switching based on request body content for multi-state form flows
```javascript
it('shows different confirmation copy for new vs returning customer', () => {
  cy.intercept('POST', '/api/checkout', (req) => {
    const fixture = req.body.isReturningCustomer
      ? 'checkout-returning.json'
      : 'checkout-new.json';
    req.reply({ fixture });
  }).as('checkout');

  // Test new customer path
  cy.visit('/checkout?customerType=new');
  cy.get('[data-cy="place-order-btn"]').click();
  cy.wait('@checkout').its('request.body.isReturningCustomer').should('eq', false);
  cy.get('[data-cy="confirmation-headline"]')
    .should('contain.text', 'Welcome! Your first order is on its way.');

  // Test returning customer path in the same spec
  cy.visit('/checkout?customerType=returning');
  cy.get('[data-cy="place-order-btn"]').click();
  cy.wait('@checkout').its('request.body.isReturningCustomer').should('eq', true);
  cy.get('[data-cy="confirmation-headline"]')
    .should('contain.text', 'Good to see you again!');
});
```
Tradeoff: Branching the fixture inside the handler allows a single `cy.intercept()` registration to cover multiple request variants without registering separate intercepts per path, reducing boilerplate and avoiding LIFO ordering conflicts — but asserting on `cy.wait('@checkout').its('request.body')` after the response is already served can give false confidence; always assert both the response-driven UI text and the outgoing request body so that a regression where the wrong `customerType` is sent is caught at the request assertion, not only via the UI copy.

**Pattern 744** — `cy.session()` with composite cache key for multi-tenant test suites
```javascript
// cypress/support/auth.ts
type Tenant = 'acme' | 'globex' | 'initech';
type Role = 'admin' | 'editor' | 'viewer';

function loginSession(tenant: Tenant, role: Role) {
  const sessionId = `${tenant}:${role}`;
  cy.session(
    sessionId,
    () => {
      cy.request('POST', `/api/${tenant}/auth/login`, {
        username: Cypress.env(`${tenant}_${role}_user`),
        password: Cypress.env(`${tenant}_${role}_pass`),
      }).then((res) => {
        window.localStorage.setItem(`${tenant}_token`, res.body.token);
      });
    },
    {
      cacheAcrossSpecs: true,
      validate() {
        cy.request({
          url: `/api/${tenant}/auth/me`,
          failOnStatusCode: false,
        })
          .its('status')
          .should('eq', 200);
      },
    }
  );
}

Cypress.Commands.add('loginAs', loginSession);

// In a spec
beforeEach(() => {
  cy.loginAs('acme', 'admin');
  cy.visit('/acme/dashboard');
});
```
Tradeoff: Embedding both `tenant` and `role` in the `sessionId` string ensures each tenant-role combination gets an independent session cache entry, preventing cross-tenant token bleed when tests for `acme:admin` and `globex:viewer` run in the same spec — but `cacheAcrossSpecs: true` means the session persists for the entire `cypress run` process; if a tenant's backend rotates JWTs mid-run (e.g., a scheduled token-invalidation job fires during a long suite), the cached session will fail its `validate()` and trigger a full re-login, causing unexpected latency spikes when many specs hit the re-login path simultaneously.

**Pattern 745** — `cy.screenshot()` with viewport capture and `onAfterScreenshot` metadata logging for visual regression triage
```javascript
// cypress/support/visual.ts
Cypress.Commands.add(
  'captureComponent',
  (selector: string, name: string) => {
    cy.get(selector).screenshot(`components/${name}`, {
      capture: 'viewport',
      disableTimersAndAnimations: true,
      onAfterScreenshot(_$el, props) {
        cy.task('log', `Screenshot: ${props.path} (${props.width}x${props.height})`);
      },
    });
  }
);

// In a spec — pair with Percy or a diff-based snapshot check
it('renders the data table in its empty-state variant', () => {
  cy.intercept('GET', '/api/items', { body: [] }).as('items');
  cy.visit('/items');
  cy.wait('@items');
  cy.get('[data-cy="data-table"]').should('be.visible');
  cy.captureComponent('[data-cy="data-table"]', 'data-table--empty');
  // Percy.snapshot() or cy.matchImageSnapshot() would follow here
});
```
Tradeoff: `capture: 'viewport'` captures the full viewport around the element rather than clipping to the element's bounding box, ensuring box-shadow, tooltip overflow, and dropdown content are visible in the diff — but the screenshot includes surrounding page content that may change independently of the component under test, increasing visual diff noise; for pure component isolation, use Cypress component testing with `cy.mount()` so only the component's rendered pixels appear.

**Pattern 746** — `Cypress.Commands.addQuery()` typed retry-able finder that filters by ARIA role and accessible name
```javascript
// cypress/support/aria.ts
declare global {
  namespace Cypress {
    interface Chainable {
      findByRole(role: string, name: string): Chainable<JQuery<HTMLElement>>;
    }
  }
}

Cypress.Commands.addQuery(
  'findByRole',
  function findByRole(role: string, accessibleName: string) {
    const getFn = cy.now('get', `[role="${role}"]`) as () => JQuery<HTMLElement>;
    return () => {
      const elements = getFn();
      const matched = elements.filter((_index, el) => {
        const labelledById = el.getAttribute('aria-labelledby');
        const label =
          el.getAttribute('aria-label') ||
          (labelledById && document.getElementById(labelledById)?.textContent) ||
          el.textContent;
        return label?.trim() === accessibleName;
      });
      this.set('timeout', Cypress.config('defaultCommandTimeout'));
      return matched;
    };
  }
);

// Usage
it('closes the dialog when the close button is activated', () => {
  cy.visit('/settings');
  cy.get('[data-cy="open-dialog-btn"]').click();
  cy.findByRole('button', 'Close dialog').click();
  cy.get('[role="dialog"]').should('not.exist');
});
```
Tradeoff: Implementing `findByRole` as an `addQuery()` command makes it retry-able like `cy.get()` — retrying the full `[role]` query and name filter on each assertion tick until the element appears or the timeout expires — whereas a custom command built with `Cypress.Commands.add()` would execute once and fail immediately if the element is not yet in the DOM; the tradeoff is that `addQuery()` inner functions cannot call other Cypress commands and must rely on synchronous DOM APIs, which means cross-document `aria-labelledby` lookups for shadow DOM or portal elements will require a simplified fallback.

**Pattern 747** — `cy.request()` JWT token extraction and expired-token 401 assertion without advancing a real clock
```javascript
it('accepts a valid bearer token and rejects a tampered expired token', () => {
  cy.request('POST', '/api/auth/login', {
    email: 'api@test.local',
    password: Cypress.env('API_TEST_PASS'),
  })
    .its('body.token')
    .then((token: string) => {
      // Valid token: expect 200
      cy.request({
        method: 'GET',
        url: '/api/me',
        headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` },
      })
        .its('status')
        .should('eq', 200);

      // Expired token: forge expiry by patching the payload's `exp` field
      const parts = token.split('.');
      const payload = JSON.parse(atob(parts[1]));
      const expiredPayload = btoa(
        JSON.stringify({ ...payload, exp: 1 })
      ).replace(/=/g, '');
      const expiredToken = [parts[0], expiredPayload, parts[2]].join('.');

      cy.request({
        method: 'GET',
        url: '/api/me',
        headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${expiredToken}` },
        failOnStatusCode: false,
      })
        .its('status')
        .should('eq', 401);
    });
});
```
Tradeoff: Using `cy.request()` for both token acquisition and API assertion keeps the test entirely out of the browser DOM and runs 3-5x faster than an equivalent E2E flow — and testing the expired-token 401 path without needing to advance a real clock or mock `Date` — but forging an expired JWT by patching the payload only works when the backend performs standard stateless JWT signature validation; if the backend uses opaque session tokens or validates against a database record, the tampered token will fail with a 401 for the wrong reason (invalid signature rather than expiry), and the test should instead use `cy.task()` to expire the token record directly in the database.

### Community Gotchas

**G416** — `cy.within()` scope escapes to the full document when an inner `cy.get()` receives `{ withinSubject: null }` implicitly, producing false positives when the scoped element is absent
Why this matters: A developer writes `cy.contains('[data-cy="card"]', 'Alice').within(() => { cy.get('[data-cy="edit-btn"]').click(); })`. The card for "Alice" is absent because the fixture returned a different name. In Cypress 11 and earlier, `.within()` on an empty jQuery set would silently widen scope, so `cy.get('[data-cy="edit-btn"]')` would match the first edit button anywhere on the page. The click succeeds, the test passes, and a real rendering regression is masked with no indication of the mismatched scope.
Fix: After entering `.within()`, assert that at least one expected child exists before performing actions: `cy.contains('[data-cy="card"]', 'Alice').within(() => { cy.contains('Alice').should('exist'); cy.get('[data-cy="edit-btn"]').click(); })`. In Cypress 12+, `.within()` on multiple elements throws "Subject must be a single element" immediately, which catches the root cause earlier — upgrade to 12+ if your project is on an older version to benefit from this guard.

---

**G417** — `cy.task()` that returns `undefined` (an implicit `async` function return) fails the test with "Task must not resolve with undefined" even though the database operation succeeded
Why this matters: A developer adds a `db:clean` task that calls `await prisma.user.deleteMany(...)` and returns nothing. The `async` function implicitly returns `Promise<void>`, which resolves to `undefined`. Cypress's task system requires every task to resolve with a non-undefined value as its completion signal — if `undefined` is returned, Cypress throws `Error: The task 'db:clean' returned undefined` and fails the test. The error message gives no hint that a return value is needed, leading developers to incorrectly suspect the Prisma call or database connection failed.
Fix: Always return an explicit non-undefined sentinel from every task, even tasks with no meaningful return data. Use `return null` as the conventional no-op return: `async 'db:clean'() { await prisma.user.deleteMany(...); return null; }`. Add a comment in your project's `setupNodeEvents` block reminding future authors of this requirement, because the error is not obvious from the Cypress error message alone.

---

**G418** — `cy.intercept()` with `{ times: 1 }` registered in `beforeEach` is consumed by the first test and silently stops intercepting for all subsequent tests, causing them to hit the real network
Why this matters: A developer registers `cy.intercept('GET', '/api/config', fixture, { times: 1 }).as('config')` in `beforeEach`, expecting `times: 1` to mean "intercept once per test". However, `{ times: 1 }` is a lifetime counter for the intercept registration, not a per-test counter — once the intercept is matched once in the first test, it is permanently deactivated for the rest of the Cypress run. Every subsequent test hits the real `/api/config` endpoint, producing different data than the fixture and causing intermittent failures that appear unrelated to the intercept.
Fix: Never rely on `{ times: N }` for per-test call counting when the intercept is registered in `beforeEach`. Register the intercept inside each individual `it()` block instead, or use a stateful counter inside the handler: `let count = 0; cy.intercept('GET', '/api/config', (req) => { req.reply(count++ < 1 ? fixture : { passthrough: true }); })` and reset the counter in `beforeEach`.

---

**G419** — `cy.screenshot()` inside a `cy.then()` callback captures intermediate loading states because `.then()` resolves the moment the preceding assertion passes, before animation-frame paint completes
Why this matters: A developer writes `cy.get('[data-cy="chart"]').should('be.visible').then(() => { cy.screenshot('chart-loaded'); })`, expecting the screenshot to show the fully rendered chart. The `be.visible` assertion passes as soon as the DOM node is displayed — but chart libraries that use `requestAnimationFrame` for their canvas or SVG draw complete the paint asynchronously. The screenshot captures the skeleton or blank canvas frame that is visible immediately after the node becomes visible, not the drawn chart content, producing a misleading artifact in CI.
Fix: Assert on a post-render data attribute that the chart library sets after drawing completes: `cy.get('[data-cy="chart"]').should('have.attr', 'data-rendered', 'true').then(() => { cy.screenshot('chart-loaded'); })`. If the library sets no such attribute, add one manually in an `onChartReady` callback. Alternatively, use `cy.wait(0)` inside `.then()` to surrender one event loop tick to the browser's rendering pipeline before the screenshot command is enqueued.

---

**G420** — `cy.session()` with `cacheAcrossSpecs: true` does not invalidate when the `setup` function body changes between runs, restoring a stale cached session despite updated authentication logic
Why this matters: A developer updates the `setup` callback to add a new MFA step. On the next `cypress run`, the session cache on disk still contains the pre-MFA session. Cypress computes the cache key from the `sessionId` string only, not from the `setup` function body — so the old session is restored without re-running `setup`, the MFA token is never entered, and tests requiring MFA-authenticated state fail with a 403. The developer sees only the 403 and spends hours debugging the MFA integration rather than realizing the stale session is being restored from disk.
Fix: Encode a version discriminator into the `sessionId` whenever the `setup` logic changes: `cy.session('login:v3', setupFn, options)` where the version suffix is incremented manually with each `setup` change. Alternatively, derive the version from an environment variable: `cy.session('login:' + Cypress.env('SESSION_VERSION'), setupFn)` and bump `SESSION_VERSION` in `cypress.env.json` whenever the authentication flow changes.

## Cycle 68 — 2026-05-14

### Patterns

**Pattern 748** — `cy.intercept()` middleware cache-control header stripping in `beforeEach` for all API responses
```javascript
// cypress/support/e2e.ts
// Register once globally — strips cache headers from every API response before assertions run
beforeEach(() => {
  cy.intercept({ middleware: true, url: '/api/**' }, (req) => {
    req.continue((res) => {
      // Force the browser to never serve this endpoint from cache
      delete res.headers['cache-control'];
      delete res.headers['etag'];
      delete res.headers['last-modified'];
      delete res.headers['expires'];
      res.headers['cache-control'] = 'no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate';
    });
  });
});

// In a spec — no extra intercept setup needed; all /api/** responses arrive fresh
it('renders updated inventory after server-side change', () => {
  cy.visit('/inventory');
  cy.intercept('GET', '/api/items', { fixture: 'items-v2.json' }).as('items');
  cy.reload();
  cy.wait('@items');
  cy.get('[data-cy="item-list"]').should('have.length', 3);
});
```
Tradeoff: A single `middleware: true` intercept in the global support file eliminates intermittent cache-hit failures without touching individual specs — but it fires a `req.continue()` callback on every `/api/**` response including high-frequency polling endpoints, adding per-response overhead that compounds in suites with long-lived sessions that poll every few seconds; scope the URL pattern to paths that historically caused cache-related flakiness rather than using a broad wildcard.

---

**Pattern 749** — `cy.intercept()` `req.continue()` upstream response body partial merge for server-driven feature-flag injection
```javascript
// Inject a feature-flag field into the real /api/config response without fully mocking it
cy.intercept('GET', '/api/config', (req) => {
  req.continue((res) => {
    if (res.statusCode === 200 && typeof res.body === 'object') {
      // Merge the flag into the real response body; all other config fields remain authentic
      res.body = {
        ...res.body,
        featureFlags: {
          ...res.body.featureFlags,
          newCheckoutFlow: true,  // force-enable the flag under test
          legacyPricing: false,   // force-disable a conflicting flag
        },
      };
      // Explicitly call res.send() after mutation to flush the modified body
      res.send(res.body);
    }
  });
}).as('config');

cy.visit('/shop');
cy.wait('@config');
cy.get('[data-cy="new-checkout-btn"]').should('be.visible');
cy.get('[data-cy="legacy-price-badge"]').should('not.exist');
```
Tradeoff: Partial-merging the real server response instead of fully stubbing it keeps all non-flag config fields authentic, reducing the risk that a stub with hardcoded fields diverges from the real API schema — but calling `res.send(res.body)` after mutation bypasses Cypress's automatic content-type negotiation; if the real server responded with `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8` and Cypress re-encodes the body as UTF-16 internally, the client may receive a garbled JSON payload.

---

**Pattern 750** — `cy.intercept()` `res.setDelay()` for loading-state appearance SLO assertion under simulated latency
```javascript
// Verify the loading skeleton is shown and dismissed within a 3-second SLO
// under 400 ms of simulated API latency
cy.intercept('GET', '/api/dashboard', (req) => {
  req.continue((res) => {
    res.setDelay(400); // simulate 400 ms server response time
  });
}).as('dashboard');

cy.visit('/');

// Loading skeleton must be visible immediately after visit
cy.get('[data-cy="skeleton-card"]').should('be.visible');

// Record when the response completes
const sloStart = Date.now();
cy.wait('@dashboard').then(() => {
  const elapsed = Date.now() - sloStart;
  expect(elapsed, 'dashboard API must respond within SLO').to.be.lt(3000);
});

// Skeleton dismissed and real content visible after data arrives
cy.get('[data-cy="skeleton-card"]').should('not.exist');
cy.get('[data-cy="dashboard-widget"]').should('have.length.gte', 1);
```
Tradeoff: `res.setDelay()` tests the full loading-state lifecycle against a realistic latency budget without a real slow server or external proxy — but `Date.now()` inside `.then()` measures wall-clock time from the Cypress command queue's perspective, which includes command-queue scheduling overhead of 10–50 ms per command on fast CI machines; for strict SLO budgets under 200 ms, use `performance.now()` captured in a `cy.window().then()` callback immediately before and after the wait instead of `Date.now()` in a Cypress `.then()`.

---

**Pattern 751** — `cy.session()` `cacheAcrossSpecs: true` with versioned session ID to force cache invalidation on auth flow changes
```javascript
// cypress/support/commands.ts
// Bump SESSION_V when the setup callback's authentication flow changes
const SESSION_V = 'v4';

Cypress.Commands.add('loginAs', (role: 'admin' | 'editor') => {
  const creds = {
    admin:  { email: 'admin@example.com',  password: Cypress.env('ADMIN_PASS') },
    editor: { email: 'editor@example.com', password: Cypress.env('EDITOR_PASS') },
  };
  const { email, password } = creds[role];

  cy.session(
    [SESSION_V, role, email],  // version prefix prevents stale-session reuse after flow changes
    () => {
      cy.visit('/login');
      cy.get('[data-cy="email"]').type(email);
      cy.get('[data-cy="password"]').type(password);
      cy.get('[data-cy="mfa-token"]').type(Cypress.env('MFA_SECRET'));
      cy.get('[data-cy="submit"]').click();
      cy.url().should('include', '/dashboard');
    },
    {
      cacheAcrossSpecs: true,
      validate: () => {
        cy.request({ url: '/api/me', failOnStatusCode: false })
          .its('status').should('eq', 200);
      },
    }
  );
});
```
Tradeoff: Embedding a version string in the session ID as the first element of the composite array forces Cypress to treat the session as new whenever the prefix is bumped, preventing stale-session reuse after MFA steps or redirect URLs are added to the setup callback — but bumping `SESSION_V` in source code requires a commit and redeploy to CI, which cannot be done at runtime if an on-call engineer needs to force re-authentication from a running pipeline without modifying source files; for that case, add a `Cypress.env('SESSION_V')` override fallback: `[Cypress.env('SESSION_V') ?? SESSION_V, role, email]`.

---

**Pattern 752** — `cy.session()` mid-test role switch with explicit storage assertion to verify clean slate between users
```javascript
describe('admin reviews user-submitted report', () => {
  const session = (role: string, email: string, pass: string) =>
    cy.session([role, email], () => {
      cy.visit('/login');
      cy.get('[data-cy="email"]').type(email);
      cy.get('[data-cy="password"]').type(pass);
      cy.get('[data-cy="submit"]').click();
      cy.url().should('include', '/home');
    });

  it('user submits report and admin approves it', () => {
    // Step 1: user submits a report
    session('user', 'user@example.com', Cypress.env('USER_PASS'));
    cy.visit('/reports/new');
    cy.get('[data-cy="report-title"]').type('Q1 Summary');
    cy.get('[data-cy="submit-report"]').click();
    cy.get('[data-cy="success-toast"]').should('be.visible');

    // Step 2: switch to admin — verify storage was cleared before asserting
    session('admin', 'admin@example.com', Cypress.env('ADMIN_PASS'));
    // cy.session() clears all cookies/storage; confirm no user token leaks
    cy.window().its('localStorage').invoke('getItem', 'userId').should('be.null');
    cy.visit('/admin/reports');
    cy.get('[data-cy="report-row"]').contains('Q1 Summary')
      .closest('[data-cy="report-row"]')
      .find('[data-cy="approve-btn"]')
      .click();
    cy.get('[data-cy="approved-badge"]').should('be.visible');
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: Asserting `localStorage.getItem('userId') === null` after the role switch confirms that `cy.session()`'s storage clear actually ran and no sensitive user-identifying data leaked into the admin session — adding one defensive assertion that costs a single `cy.window()` call — but this assertion will fail in browsers configured with partitioned storage or where the application stores `userId` in a `sessionStorage` key rather than `localStorage`; the guard should be adapted to match the actual storage mechanism used by the application under test.

**Pattern 753** — `cy.origin()` with `Cypress.require()` shared IdP helper under `experimentalOriginDependencies`
```javascript
// cypress/support/idp-helpers.ts (shared helper importable inside cy.origin())
export function fillIdpLoginForm(username: string, password: string): void {
  cy.get('#idp-username').clear().type(username);
  cy.get('#idp-password').clear().type(password);
  cy.get('#idp-submit').click();
}

// cypress/support/commands.ts
Cypress.Commands.add('loginViaSso', (username: string, password: string) => {
  cy.visit('/app');
  cy.origin(
    'https://idp.example.com',
    { args: { username, password } },
    ({ username, password }) => {
      // Cypress.require() needs experimentalOriginDependencies: true in cypress.config.ts
      const { fillIdpLoginForm } = Cypress.require(
        '../../support/idp-helpers'
      ) as typeof import('../../support/idp-helpers');
      fillIdpLoginForm(username, password);
    }
  );
  cy.url().should('include', '/app/home');
});

// cypress/e2e/sso.cy.ts
it('authenticates via SSO and reaches the app home page', () => {
  cy.loginViaSso(Cypress.env('SSO_USER'), Cypress.env('SSO_PASS'));
  cy.get('[data-cy="user-greeting"]').should('contain', Cypress.env('SSO_USER'));
});
```
Tradeoff: `Cypress.require()` inside `cy.origin()` avoids copy-pasting the IdP form-fill logic into every test and every `cy.session()` setup callback — but `Cypress.require()` resolves module paths relative to the support file entry point, not the spec file, so paths that work locally may break after restructuring the support directory; prefer absolute imports relative to the project root (`/cypress/support/idp-helpers`) over relative paths (`../../support/idp-helpers`) to make the import path refactor-safe.

---

**Pattern 754** — `cy.task()` with typed discriminated-union registry for type-safe multi-task Node plugin
```typescript
// cypress/plugins/tasks.ts
import type { Pool } from 'pg';

export type TaskInput =
  | { name: 'seedUser';   args: { email: string; role: string } }
  | { name: 'deleteUser'; args: { id: string } }
  | { name: 'getSecret';  args: { key: string } };

export type TaskOutput<T extends TaskInput['name']> =
  T extends 'seedUser'   ? { id: string } :
  T extends 'deleteUser' ? null :
  T extends 'getSecret'  ? string :
  never;

export function registerTasks(on: Cypress.PluginEvents, pool: Pool): void {
  on('task', {
    async seedUser({ email, role }: { email: string; role: string }): Promise<{ id: string }> {
      const { rows } = await pool.query(
        'INSERT INTO users (email, role) VALUES ($1,$2) RETURNING id::text',
        [email, role]
      );
      return { id: rows[0].id };
    },
    async deleteUser({ id }: { id: string }): Promise<null> {
      await pool.query('DELETE FROM users WHERE id = $1', [id]);
      return null;
    },
    getSecret({ key }: { key: string }): string {
      const v = process.env[key];
      if (!v) throw new Error(`Secret "${key}" is not set`);
      return v;
    },
  });
}

// In a spec — full TypeScript inference on task name and return type
cy.task<{ id: string }>('seedUser', { email: 'bob@test.com', role: 'viewer' })
  .then(({ id }) => cy.wrap(id).as('userId'));
```
Tradeoff: Centralising all task registrations in a typed `registerTasks` function lets TypeScript enforce that every task name, argument shape, and return type is consistent between the plugin file and the spec — catching argument typos at compile time rather than as runtime Cypress task errors — but the discriminated-union approach requires a manual type-level mapping between task names and their I/O types, which must be kept in sync with the implementation; if a developer adds a new task to the `on('task', ...)` object without updating the `TaskInput` union, TypeScript silently allows the task call with `any` types in the spec.

---

**Pattern 755** — `cy.clock()` pre-visit with selective `['Date']` override for date-display testing without disrupting `setTimeout`
```javascript
// Freeze only the Date constructor — leave setTimeout/setInterval on the real clock
// so animation timers, toast auto-dismiss, and debounce handlers behave normally
cy.clock(Date.UTC(2025, 11, 31, 23, 58, 0), ['Date']); // 2025-12-31 23:58 UTC

cy.visit('/dashboard');

// Components reading `new Date()` or `Date.now()` see the frozen date
cy.get('[data-cy="current-date"]').should('contain', 'December 31, 2025');
cy.get('[data-cy="days-remaining"]').should('contain', '0 days remaining in 2025');

// A real debounce (300 ms setTimeout) still fires — refresh button works
cy.get('[data-cy="refresh-btn"]').click();
// No cy.tick() needed; the real clock advances the debounce timer
cy.get('[data-cy="last-updated"]').should('contain', 'Just now');

// After date-specific assertions restore the real clock
cy.clock().then((clock) => clock.restore());
```
Tradeoff: Passing `['Date']` as the functions array to `cy.clock()` scopes the override exclusively to date construction and `Date.now()`, preventing the widespread disruption that a full `cy.clock()` call (which also overrides `setTimeout` and `setInterval`) causes to animation libraries and polling components — but `cy.clock()` only patches the top-level `window.Date` object, so any Web Worker or `<iframe>` that creates `new Date()` still receives the real system time; tests that assert on date-formatted content rendered inside workers or third-party embeds will see inconsistent values.

**Pattern 756** — `.should(callback)` for complex multi-step DOM assertion with retry-ability across sibling elements
```javascript
// Assert that a summary row shows the correct subtotal derived from a list of line items
// The entire callback retries until all conditions pass simultaneously
cy.get('[data-cy="order-summary"]').should(($summary) => {
  // Read all line-item prices from within the same subject to keep the chain retry-able
  const prices = $summary
    .find('[data-cy="line-item-price"]')
    .toArray()
    .map((el) => parseFloat((el as HTMLElement).textContent!.replace(/[^0-9.]/g, '')));

  // Ensure at least one item is rendered before asserting the sum
  expect(prices.length, 'at least one line item is rendered').to.be.gte(1);

  const sum = prices.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0);
  const subtotalText = $summary.find('[data-cy="subtotal"]').text();
  const subtotal = parseFloat(subtotalText.replace(/[^0-9.]/g, ''));

  // Allow ±0.01 floating-point tolerance
  expect(Math.abs(sum - subtotal), 'subtotal matches sum of line items').to.be.lt(0.01);
});
```
Tradeoff: Computing both the individual prices and the subtotal from within the same `.should()` callback means Cypress retries the entire DOM read-and-compare block together, guaranteeing that both the line items and the subtotal are read from the same DOM snapshot in each retry cycle — but calling `$summary.find()` inside a `.should()` callback performs synchronous jQuery DOM queries that are not themselves retry-able; if the subtotal element renders with a brief loading state, the callback will throw a `parseFloat(undefined)` error on early retries rather than waiting for the element to appear.
