**Pattern 757** — `Cypress.Commands.addQuery()` with `querySelectorAll` for CSS4-compatible retry-able ARIA role finder
```typescript
// cypress/support/commands.ts
declare global {
  namespace Cypress {
    interface Chainable {
      findByAriaRole(
        role: string,
        options?: { name?: string; level?: number }
      ): Chainable<JQuery<HTMLElement>>;
    }
  }
}

Cypress.Commands.addQuery(
  'findByAriaRole',
  function findByAriaRole(role, options = {}) {
    return (subject) => {
      // Use native querySelectorAll to avoid Sizzle version incompatibilities
      const root: Element = subject ? subject[0] : document.body;
      const candidates = Array.from(root.querySelectorAll(`[role="${role}"]`));

      let filtered = candidates;

      if ((options as { name?: string }).name) {
        filtered = filtered.filter(
          (el) => el.getAttribute('aria-label') === (options as { name?: string }).name
        );
      }

      if ((options as { level?: number }).level !== undefined) {
        filtered = filtered.filter(
          (el) =>
            el.getAttribute('aria-level') ===
            String((options as { level?: number }).level)
        );
      }

      return Cypress.$(filtered);
    };
  }
);

// In a spec
it('navigates the accessible heading structure', () => {
  cy.visit('/docs');
  cy.findByAriaRole('heading', { level: 1 }).should('have.length', 1);
  cy.findByAriaRole('button', { name: 'Close dialog' }).click();
  cy.findByAriaRole('dialog').should('not.exist');
});
```
Tradeoff: Using `querySelectorAll` inside `addQuery()` makes the finder CSS4-native and avoids Sizzle pseudo-selector parse errors — and the double-function pattern of `addQuery` gives built-in retry-ability without manual polling — but `[role="button"]` matches only elements with an explicit `role` attribute and misses native `<button>` elements, `<input type="submit">`, and anchor tags that have an implicit ARIA button role; for a complete ARIA role finder, supplement the attribute-selector filter with a native `matches` check against semantic HTML tags using a lookup table of implicit ARIA roles.

---

**Pattern 758** — Component test `cy.intercept()` before `mount()` with `cy.wait()` for `useEffect`-driven fetch and error state coverage
```typescript
// cypress/component/ProductList.cy.tsx
import { mount } from 'cypress/react';
import ProductList from '../../src/components/ProductList';

describe('ProductList', () => {
  it('renders products from API response', () => {
    // Register intercept BEFORE mount() — useEffect fetch fires on first render
    cy.intercept('GET', '/api/products', {
      statusCode: 200,
      body: [
        { id: 1, name: 'Widget Alpha', price: 9.99 },
        { id: 2, name: 'Widget Beta',  price: 14.99 },
      ],
    }).as('products');

    mount(<ProductList categoryId={5} />);
    cy.wait('@products');

    cy.get('[data-cy="product-card"]').should('have.length', 2);
    cy.get('[data-cy="product-card"]').first().should('contain.text', 'Widget Alpha');
  });

  it('shows empty-state when API returns an empty array', () => {
    cy.intercept('GET', '/api/products', { statusCode: 200, body: [] }).as('emptyProducts');

    mount(<ProductList categoryId={5} />);
    cy.wait('@emptyProducts');

    cy.get('[data-cy="product-card"]').should('not.exist');
    cy.get('[data-cy="empty-state-message"]').should('be.visible');
  });

  it('shows error banner when API returns 503', () => {
    cy.intercept('GET', '/api/products', { statusCode: 503 }).as('failedProducts');

    mount(<ProductList categoryId={5} />);
    cy.wait('@failedProducts');

    cy.get('[data-cy="error-banner"]').should('contain.text', 'Service temporarily unavailable');
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: Splitting the happy path, empty state, and error state across three separate `it()` blocks — each with its own `cy.intercept()` before `mount()` — produces isolated, readable component specs with a single clear failure mode per test — but mounting the component three times in the same describe block increases the total test execution time compared to a single mount with sequential state changes; for components with expensive setup (e.g., those that load a large vendor bundle), consider using `beforeEach` to share the `mount()` and parameterise the intercept stub instead.

---

**Pattern 759** — `cy.request()` recursive polling helper for async backend seed job completion before `cy.visit()`
```javascript
// cypress/support/commands.ts
Cypress.Commands.add('waitForSeedJob', (jobId: string, maxRetries = 10) => {
  const poll = (attempt: number): Cypress.Chainable => {
    if (attempt > maxRetries) {
      throw new Error(`Seed job ${jobId} did not complete after ${maxRetries} retries`);
    }
    return cy
      .request({
        url: `/api/jobs/${jobId}`,
        failOnStatusCode: false,
        log: false,
      })
      .then((resp) => {
        if (resp.body?.status === 'completed') return cy.wrap(resp.body);
        if (resp.body?.status === 'failed') {
          throw new Error(`Seed job ${jobId} failed: ${resp.body?.error}`);
        }
        // Job still running — wait 500 ms then retry
        return cy.wait(500).then(() => poll(attempt + 1));
      });
  };
  return poll(1);
});

// In a spec
before(() => {
  cy.task<{ jobId: string }>('triggerDataSeed', { scenario: 'checkout' })
    .then(({ jobId }) => cy.waitForSeedJob(jobId));
});

it('completes checkout with seeded product data', () => {
  cy.visit('/checkout');
  cy.get('[data-cy="product-item"]').should('have.length.gte', 1);
});
```
Tradeoff: Recursive `cy.request()` polling inside a Cypress command gives the seed job a configurable retry budget without using `cy.wait()` with a fixed sleep duration — adapting automatically to fast CI environments where jobs finish in 1 second and slow ones where they take 8 seconds — but each recursive call increases the depth of the Cypress promise chain, and deep recursion (more than ~20 levels) can trigger "Maximum call stack size exceeded" errors in Node.js's promise implementation; cap `maxRetries` at 15 and increase `cy.wait(500)` to `cy.wait(2000)` for long-running jobs to avoid stack overflow.

---

**Pattern 760** — `cy.press()` keyboard tab-order assertion for sequential accessibility compliance
```javascript
// Assert that the focus order within a modal dialog matches the expected sequence
// cy.press() was introduced in Cypress 14.x as a semantic keyboard event command
cy.get('[data-cy="open-modal-btn"]').click();
cy.get('[data-cy="modal"]').should('be.visible');

// Focus starts on the first focusable element inside the modal
cy.focused().should('have.attr', 'data-cy', 'modal-title-close');

// Tab through modal controls in expected order
cy.press('Tab');
cy.focused().should('have.attr', 'data-cy', 'modal-email-input');

cy.press('Tab');
cy.focused().should('have.attr', 'data-cy', 'modal-submit-btn');

cy.press('Tab');
cy.focused().should('have.attr', 'data-cy', 'modal-cancel-btn');

// Tab should cycle back to the close button (focus trap)
cy.press('Tab');
cy.focused().should('have.attr', 'data-cy', 'modal-title-close');

// Shift+Tab reverses direction
cy.press('Shift+Tab');
cy.focused().should('have.attr', 'data-cy', 'modal-cancel-btn');
```
Tradeoff: `cy.press()` fires semantic keyboard events through the browser's accessibility tree, testing the actual tab-order implementation rather than simulating synthetic `keydown` events that bypass focus management — catching focus-trap regressions in modals and dialogs that `cy.type('{tab}')` misses — but `cy.press()` is only available from Cypress 14.0 onward; teams on Cypress 13.x must emulate tab-order testing with `cy.get('body').tab()` from the `cypress-real-events` plugin, which fires native browser events using Chrome DevTools Protocol and is not available in Firefox.

---

**Pattern 761** — `Cypress.Commands.overwrite('type')` for automatic prior-value clear and PII-masked log output
```javascript
// cypress/support/commands.ts
// Overwrite cy.type() to: 1) clear the input before typing, 2) mask values in the Command Log
Cypress.Commands.overwrite(
  'type',
  (
    originalFn: Cypress.CommandOriginalFnWithSubject<'type'>,
    subject: JQuery<HTMLElement>,
    text: string,
    options?: Cypress.TypeOptions & { sensitive?: boolean }
  ) => {
    const { sensitive = false, ...typeOptions } = options ?? {};

    if (sensitive) {
      // Suppress the default log entry and write a masked replacement
      Cypress.log({
        name: 'type',
        message: '*'.repeat(String(text).length),
        $el: subject,
        consoleProps: () => ({ note: 'value masked — sensitive field' }),
      });
      // Pass { log: false } to originalFn to avoid a second, unmasked log entry
      return originalFn(subject, text, { ...typeOptions, log: false });
    }

    return originalFn(subject, text, typeOptions);
  }
);

// In a spec — use { sensitive: true } for password/token fields
it('logs in without exposing the password in the Command Log', () => {
  cy.visit('/login');
  cy.get('[data-cy="email"]').type('user@example.com');
  cy.get('[data-cy="password"]').type(Cypress.env('PASSWORD'), { sensitive: true });
  cy.get('[data-cy="submit"]').click();
  cy.url().should('include', '/dashboard');
});
```
Tradeoff: Overwriting `cy.type()` to support `{ sensitive: true }` lets teams retrofit PII masking onto existing tests without replacing every `cy.type()` call with a custom `cy.sensitiveType()` command — keeping the API surface familiar and discoverable — but because the overwrite receives the plain-text value in its signature and must pass it to `originalFn`, the value is still visible to any `beforeEach` or `afterEach` hook that wraps the command chain; secrets captured in `cypress-terminal-report` or third-party plugins that hook into Cypress's command events will see the unmasked value regardless of the log override.

---

**Pattern 762** — Component test `mountWithQueryClient()` factory for React Query v5 with seeded cache for offline rendering assertion
```typescript
// cypress/support/react-query-mount.tsx
import { mount } from 'cypress/react';
import { QueryClient, QueryClientProvider } from '@tanstack/react-query';

interface MountWithQueryClientOptions {
  queryKey: unknown[];
  data: unknown;
  staleTime?: number;
}

export function mountWithQueryClient(
  component: React.ReactElement,
  { queryKey, data, staleTime = Infinity }: MountWithQueryClientOptions
) {
  const queryClient = new QueryClient({
    defaultOptions: { queries: { retry: false, gcTime: 0 } },
  });

  // Seed the cache synchronously so the component renders immediately without fetching
  queryClient.setQueryData(queryKey, data);

  return mount(
    <QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>
      {component}
    </QueryClientProvider>
  );
}

// In a spec
it('renders seeded user profile without a network request', () => {
  cy.intercept('GET', '/api/user/1', cy.spy().as('fetchSpy')); // should NOT be called

  mountWithQueryClient(<UserProfile userId={1} />, {
    queryKey: ['user', 1],
    data: { id: 1, name: 'Ada Lovelace', role: 'admin' },
  });

  cy.get('[data-cy="user-name"]').should('have.text', 'Ada Lovelace');
  // Assert the network was never hit because the cache was pre-seeded
  cy.get('@fetchSpy').should('not.have.been.called');
});
```
Tradeoff: Pre-seeding the React Query cache via `queryClient.setQueryData()` before mounting lets you test the component's rendering logic in complete isolation from the network — verifying that stale-time, loading, and error states render correctly from controlled data without relying on `cy.intercept()` timing — but `gcTime: 0` in the test `QueryClient` causes the cache to be garbage-collected immediately after the query is unmounted; if the component mounts a child that subscribes to the same query key after the parent unmounts, the child will see an empty cache and trigger a real fetch, causing a test-isolation leak.

---

### Community Gotchas

**G421** — `cy.intercept()` with `{ times: 1 }` registered in `beforeEach` is consumed by the first test and silently passes all subsequent matching requests to the real network
Why this matters: A developer registers `cy.intercept('GET', '/api/config', fixture, { times: 1 }).as('config')` in `beforeEach`, expecting `times: 1` to mean "intercept once per individual test". The `times` option is a lifetime counter for the intercept registration itself, not a per-test counter — once the intercept is matched once by the first test, it is permanently deactivated. Every subsequent test's `/api/config` request bypasses the fixture and hits the real server, returning environment-specific data that causes intermittent assertion failures in CI that look like data inconsistencies rather than stub exhaustion.
Fix: Register intercepts with `{ times: 1 }` inside each individual `it()` block instead of in `beforeEach`. If the intercept must live in `beforeEach`, omit `{ times: N }` and use a stateful closure counter inside the handler instead: `let count = 0; cy.intercept('GET', '/api/config', (req) => { req.reply(++count <= 1 ? fixture : { passthrough: true }); })` with `count = 0` reset at the top of each `beforeEach`.

---

**G422** — `cy.clock()` does not patch `Date` inside Web Workers — worker-thread timestamp logic runs on the real system clock regardless of the frozen browser clock
Why this matters: A developer uses `cy.clock(Date.UTC(2025, 0, 1))` to freeze time and asserts that a background sync Web Worker logs a timestamp of `2025-01-01`. The worker's `new Date()` call executes in a separate worker thread context that Cypress never patched, so the worker logs the real current timestamp. The test assertion fails with a date mismatch, and the developer — seeing no error about iframes or workers — assumes the clock override failed entirely and starts adding `cy.wait()` calls to compensate.
Fix: Do not rely on `cy.clock()` for timestamp assertions inside Web Workers. Instead, inject the desired timestamp into the worker via `postMessage`: send `{ type: 'setTestTime', ts: Date.UTC(2025, 0, 1) }` to the worker and have it store the value in a `testTime` variable that overrides `Date.now()` when present. In tests, assert on output that the worker sends back via `postMessage` rather than on a `Date` the worker creates internally.

---

**G423** — `cacheAcrossSpecs: true` session is not invalidated when the `setup()` function body changes, causing stale cached sessions to be restored on CI agents with persistent Cypress session storage
Why this matters: A developer adds an MFA step to the `cy.session()` setup callback and bumps the version in code, but does not change the `sessionId` string. On a persistent CI agent that cached the pre-MFA session in a previous run, Cypress restores the old cookie set from disk. The `validate()` callback passes because the server still accepts the old cookie during its grace period. Tests that reach the MFA-gated dashboard appear to succeed, but subsequent tests that call an MFA-protected API endpoint receive 403 errors, and the root cause — a stale session silently restored from the persistent cache — is invisible in the Cypress Dashboard.
Fix: Include a semantic version discriminator in the `sessionId` that is incremented every time the `setup()` callback's authentication flow changes: `cy.session(['login', 'v5', email], setupFn, options)`. Alternatively, configure CI to clear the Cypress session cache directory (`~/.cache/Cypress/sessions/` or the path set by `Cypress.config('sessionDir')`) at the start of each pipeline run using a pre-test shell step.

---

**G424** — Using `.then()` between two query commands breaks the retry-ability of the entire chain, causing `.should()` at the end to assert only once against the first resolved value
Why this matters: A developer writes `cy.get('[data-cy="total"]').invoke('text').then((t) => parseFloat(t.replace(/\$/g, ''))).should('be.gt', 0)`. They expect Cypress to retry the chain until a positive number appears. The `.then()` callback executes once when `invoke('text')` resolves — if the element renders `$0.00` on the first render because data is still loading, `parseFloat('0.00')` returns `0`, the `.should('be.gt', 0)` assertion fires once and fails without retrying, and the test fails even though the correct value would appear 200 ms later.
Fix: Replace the `.then(transform).should(assert)` pattern with a single `.should(callback)` that performs both the transform and the assertion inside the retried block: `cy.get('[data-cy="total"]').should(($el) => { expect(parseFloat($el.text().replace(/\$/g, ''))).to.be.gt(0); })`. The `.should(callback)` form causes Cypress to re-query and re-execute the entire callback on every retry cycle until it passes or times out.

---

**G425** — `Cypress.Commands.overwrite('visit')` that calls `cy.visit()` internally instead of calling `originalFn` causes infinite recursion and a stack overflow
Why this matters: A developer wants to add a `cy.wait(100)` after every page navigation and writes: `Cypress.Commands.overwrite('visit', (_originalFn, url, opts) => { cy.visit(url, opts); cy.wait(100); })`. The overwrite ignores `_originalFn` and calls `cy.visit()` directly, which triggers the overwrite again, which calls `cy.visit()` again — infinite recursion. Cypress's command queue fills up and the runner crashes with "Maximum call stack size exceeded" without identifying the overwrite as the source. The developer assumes it is a Cypress version bug and files a false issue.
Fix: Always call `originalFn(subject, ...args)` inside `Cypress.Commands.overwrite()` — never call the command by name from within its own overwrite. The correct implementation is: `Cypress.Commands.overwrite('visit', (originalFn, url, opts) => { return originalFn(url, opts).then(() => cy.wait(100)); })`. The `originalFn` reference is Cypress's pre-overwrite implementation and does not re-trigger the overwrite.

## Cycle 69 — 2026-05-14

### Patterns

**Pattern 763** — `cy.intercept()` `req.on('before:response')` for response header injection without body replacement
```typescript
// Inject custom headers into real backend responses to test header-consumer UI
// without replacing the body and introducing fixture drift.

cy.intercept('GET', '/api/**', (req) => {
  req.on('before:response', (res) => {
    res.headers['x-feature-flag']        = 'dark-mode-v2';
    res.headers['x-rate-limit-remaining'] = '3';
  });
}).as('apiWithHeaders');

cy.visit('/dashboard');
cy.wait('@apiWithHeaders').then(({ response }) => {
  expect(response?.headers['x-feature-flag']).to.eq('dark-mode-v2');
});
cy.get('[data-cy="rate-limit-banner"]').should('be.visible');
```
Tradeoff: Using `req.on('before:response')` preserves the real response body while injecting arbitrary headers, catching missing-header regressions that fixture-based stubs would mask — but the handler fires asynchronously through the Cypress proxy and adds ~5–15 ms per intercepted response; in suites that wait on hundreds of XHR aliases, the accumulated overhead can push `cy.wait()` assertions past the default 5-second timeout when the backend is already near its latency budget.

---

**Pattern 764** — `cy.intercept()` `res.setThrottle()` for slow-network skeleton-loader and progressive-disclosure testing
```typescript
// Simulate a 56 Kbps connection to verify loading-state UI that only appears
// under constrained bandwidth.

cy.intercept('GET', '/api/feed', (req) => {
  req.continue((res) => {
    res.setThrottle(56);  // kilobits per second
    res.setDelay(800);    // additional fixed latency ms
  });
}).as('slowFeed');

cy.visit('/home');
cy.get('[data-cy="skeleton-card"]').should('be.visible');
cy.wait('@slowFeed');
cy.get('[data-cy="feed-item"]').should('have.length.greaterThan', 0);
cy.get('[data-cy="skeleton-card"]').should('not.exist');
```
Tradeoff: `res.setThrottle()` accurately simulates byte-level delivery rate through Cypress's proxy, making it the most realistic way to test loading states — but a 200 KB JSON body at 56 Kbps takes ~28 seconds to deliver in real time, making these tests unsuitable for standard CI pipelines unless quarantined into a dedicated slow-network suite with an extended `responseTimeout`.

**Pattern 765** — `cy.intercept()` regex route matcher with per-request alias assigned from URL capture group
```typescript
// Dynamically alias each request by extracting an ID from the URL so
// individual fetches can be waited on by ID rather than position.

cy.intercept(/\/api\/orders\/(\d+)/, (req) => {
  const match = req.url.match(/\/api\/orders\/(\d+)/);
  if (match) {
    req.alias = `order-${match[1]}`;
  }
  req.continue();
});

cy.visit('/orders');
cy.get('[data-cy="order-101-link"]').click();
cy.wait('@order-101').its('response.statusCode').should('eq', 200);

cy.get('[data-cy="back-btn"]').click();
cy.get('[data-cy="order-202-link"]').click();
cy.wait('@order-202').its('response.statusCode').should('eq', 200);
```
Tradeoff: Dynamic `req.alias` assignment keeps setup O(1) regardless of how many distinct IDs are tested — but the regex handler also fires for browser-prefetch requests triggered by hover events, so `cy.wait('@order-101')` may resolve against a prefetch rather than the click-driven fetch, producing a false-pass when the click fetch returns a different status code.

**Pattern 766** — `cy.session()` `cacheAcrossSpecs` with environment-hash composite ID for automatic cache invalidation
```typescript
// Cache the login session across all spec files and automatically invalidate
// the cache when the target environment changes between local dev and CI.

function loginWithCachedSession(user: { name: string; password: string }) {
  const envHash = btoa(JSON.stringify({
    baseUrl: Cypress.config('baseUrl'),
    apiEnv:  Cypress.env('API_ENV') ?? 'local',
  }));
  cy.session(
    [user.name, envHash],
    () => {
      cy.visit('/login');
      cy.get('[data-cy="username"]').type(user.name);
      cy.get('[data-cy="password"]').type(user.password, { log: false });
      cy.get('[data-cy="login-btn"]').click();
      cy.url().should('include', '/dashboard');
    },
    {
      cacheAcrossSpecs: true,
      validate: () =>
        cy.request({ url: '/api/me', failOnStatusCode: false })
          .its('status').should('eq', 200),
    }
  );
}
```
Tradeoff: The environment hash ensures a local-run cache is never reused against staging, preventing silent auth failures — but `btoa(JSON.stringify(...))` evaluates inside `beforeEach` at `cy.session()` call time; if any `Cypress.env()` value is lazily resolved via a `before:run` plugin hook, it may still be `undefined` when `btoa` runs, producing a hash of `undefined` values and silently defeating the invalidation logic.

**Pattern 767** — `cy.session()` mid-test user switching for two-actor workflow validation
```typescript
// Admin creates a resource and viewer reads it — deterministic role switching
// without manual cookie clearing between actors.

function loginAs(role: 'admin' | 'viewer') {
  cy.session(role, () => {
    cy.request('POST', '/api/test-auth', { role }).then((res) => {
      cy.setCookie('session_token', res.body.token);
    });
  });
}

it('admin creates item visible to viewer', () => {
  loginAs('admin');
  cy.visit('/admin/items/new');
  cy.get('[data-cy="item-name"]').type('Shared Widget');
  cy.get('[data-cy="save-btn"]').click();
  cy.url().should('match', /\/admin\/items\/\d+/);
  cy.location('pathname').invoke('split', '/').its(3).as('itemId');

  loginAs('viewer'); // cy.session() clears admin cookies automatically
  cy.get('@itemId').then((id) => cy.visit(`/items/${id}`));
  cy.get('[data-cy="item-title"]').should('have.text', 'Shared Widget');
});
```
Tradeoff: `cy.session()` makes role switching deterministic by clearing all storage before restoring a cached session — but the `@itemId` alias created under the admin session may be garbage-collected by Mocha under memory pressure in long spec files when `cy.session()` replaces the page, causing `cy.get('@itemId')` to yield `null`.

**Pattern 768** — `cy.origin()` `Cypress.require()` to import a CJS helper module in the cross-origin VM
```typescript
// Load a shared helper file inside cy.origin() using Cypress.require()
// so the same form-filling logic is available across origin boundaries.

// support/origin-helpers.js  (must be CommonJS)
module.exports = {
  fillLoginForm(username, password) {
    cy.get('#username').type(username);
    cy.get('#password').type(password, { log: false });
    cy.get('[type="submit"]').click();
  },
};

it('completes SSO via identity provider', () => {
  cy.visit('/app');
  cy.get('[data-cy="sso-login"]').click();
  cy.origin(
    'https://idp.example.com',
    { args: { user: 'test@corp.com', pass: Cypress.env('IDP_PASS') } },
    ({ user, pass }) => {
      const { fillLoginForm } = Cypress.require('./support/origin-helpers');
      fillLoginForm(user, pass);
      cy.url().should('include', '/app/dashboard');
    }
  );
});
```
Tradeoff: `Cypress.require()` enables sharing helper logic across origin boundaries without duplication — but the module must use CommonJS `module.exports` syntax; a module using top-level ESM `import` throws `SyntaxError: Cannot use import statement in a module` inside the Cypress bundler's cross-origin VM, with an error pointing to bundler internals rather than the offending `import` line.

**Pattern 769** — `cy.origin()` persistent JS execution context for multi-step cross-origin form flows
```typescript
// JS context persists across successive cy.origin() calls to the same origin;
// use this to pass state between steps without the args serialization channel.

it('completes two-step cross-origin checkout', () => {
  cy.visit('/cart');
  cy.get('[data-cy="checkout-btn"]').click();

  cy.origin('https://payments.example.com', () => {
    (window as any).__orderRef = 'ORD-2026-001';
    cy.get('#ship-addr').type('123 Main St');
    cy.get('[data-cy="continue"]').click();
  });

  cy.origin('https://payments.example.com', () => {
    const ref = (window as any).__orderRef; // still 'ORD-2026-001'
    cy.get('#confirm-ref').invoke('text').should('eq', ref);
    cy.get('[data-cy="pay-btn"]').click();
  });

  cy.url().should('include', '/confirmation');
});
```
Tradeoff: The persistent origin context avoids `args` serialization and supports non-serializable values like `RegExp` — but if the application performs a full-page redirect back to the primary origin between the two `cy.origin()` calls, the context is destroyed and `window.__orderRef` is `undefined` in step 2, silently corrupting the assertion.

**Pattern 770** — `cy.clock()` with `['Date']` selector to freeze only the Date constructor, leaving timers native
```typescript
// Freeze only Date so date-display components render deterministically while
// setTimeout/setInterval run normally without requiring cy.tick() calls.

describe('invoice due-date rendering', () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    cy.clock(new Date('2026-03-15T09:00:00Z'), ['Date']);
    cy.visit('/invoices/123');
  });

  it('shows "Due in 7 days" for a 2026-03-22 invoice', () => {
    cy.get('[data-cy="due-date-label"]').should('have.text', 'Due in 7 days');
  });

  it('shows "Overdue" for a 2026-03-10 invoice', () => {
    cy.get('[data-cy="due-date-label-overdue"]').should('have.text', 'Overdue');
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: Passing `['Date']` to `cy.clock()` allows real timer-based polling to run without `cy.tick()` — but if the application uses `performance.now()` for high-resolution relative timestamps, those calls remain uncontrolled and may produce non-deterministic results on CPU-loaded CI machines.

**Pattern 771** — `cy.clock()` incremental `cy.tick()` loop to assert every intermediate countdown display value
```typescript
// Test all intermediate countdown states by advancing the clock one second
// at a time, without any real-time waiting.

it('counts down from 5 to 0 and shows done banner', () => {
  cy.clock();
  cy.visit('/countdown?start=5');
  cy.get('[data-cy="timer"]').should('have.text', '5');

  for (let remaining = 4; remaining >= 0; remaining--) {
    cy.tick(1000);
    cy.get('[data-cy="timer"]').should('have.text', String(remaining));
  }

  cy.get('[data-cy="done-banner"]').should('be.visible');
  cy.tick(1000); // confirm timer does not go negative
  cy.get('[data-cy="timer"]').should('have.text', '0');
});
```
Tradeoff: The `for` loop with `cy.tick(1000)` makes a 5-second countdown test run in milliseconds — but if the component batches DOM updates with `requestAnimationFrame` (also overridden by `cy.clock()`), omitting a subsequent `cy.tick(16)` to advance one rAF frame may leave the DOM one update behind, causing the text assertion to read the pre-tick value.

**Pattern 772** — `cy.task()` runtime credential retrieval from HashiCorp Vault for SOC-2-compliant secret hygiene
```typescript
// Retrieve secrets at test runtime so credentials never appear in source files
// or CI logs — satisfying SOC 2 / ISO 27001 secret-hygiene requirements.

// cypress.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from 'cypress';
import { getSecret } from './scripts/vault-client';

export default defineConfig({
  e2e: {
    setupNodeEvents(on) {
      on('task', {
        async getVaultSecret({ path, key }: { path: string; key: string }) {
          const value = await getSecret(path, key);
          return value ?? null; // must return null, not undefined
        },
      });
    },
  },
});

// In spec:
it('logs in with vault-sourced credentials', () => {
  cy.task<string>('getVaultSecret', {
    path: 'secret/qa/staging',
    key: 'admin_password',
  }).then((password) => {
    cy.visit('/login');
    cy.get('#password').type(password, { log: false });
    cy.get('[type="submit"]').click();
    cy.url().should('include', '/dashboard');
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: Vault-sourced secrets eliminate credential exposure in source and CI logs — but if the vault client uses AWS IMDS (169.254.169.254) and the Docker-based CI runner lacks an IAM task-role, the request fails silently and the task returns `null`, causing `cy.type(null)` to fail with "value must be a string" rather than the informative "vault unreachable".

**Pattern 773** — `cy.task()` async database seed returning a teardown token for surgical per-test cleanup
```typescript
// Seed exactly the rows a test needs and receive a teardown token so afterEach
// deletes only those rows, enabling safe parallel worker execution.

// In cypress.config.ts setupNodeEvents:
on('task', {
  async seedProduct(p: { name: string; price: number }) {
    const productId = await db.products.create(p);
    return { productId };
  },
  async deleteProduct({ productId }: { productId: number }) {
    await db.products.delete(productId);
    return null;
  },
});

// In spec:
describe('Product detail page', () => {
  let productId: number;

  beforeEach(() => {
    cy.task<{ productId: number }>('seedProduct', {
      name: 'Widget Pro',
      price: 29.99,
    }).then(({ productId: id }) => { productId = id; });
  });

  afterEach(() => {
    cy.task('deleteProduct', { productId });
  });

  it('shows seeded product price', () => {
    cy.visit(`/products/${productId}`);
    cy.get('[data-cy="price"]').should('have.text', '$29.99');
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: Teardown tokens enable row-level cleanup without truncating tables, making parallel workers safe — but if the `beforeEach` task times out, the `.then()` callback never runs, `productId` stays `undefined`, and `cy.task('deleteProduct', { productId: undefined })` silently deletes nothing, leaving orphan rows that accumulate across flaky re-runs.

**Pattern 774** — `Cypress.Commands.addAll()` bulk registration of typed CRUD helpers as parent commands
```typescript
// Register a full set of resource helpers in one object literal for clean
// colocation and TypeScript declaration merging.

Cypress.Commands.addAll({
  createWidget(payload: { name: string; qty: number }) {
    return cy.request('POST', '/api/widgets', payload).its('body');
  },
  getWidget(id: number) {
    return cy.request('GET', `/api/widgets/${id}`).its('body');
  },
  updateWidget(id: number, patch: Partial<{ name: string; qty: number }>) {
    return cy.request('PATCH', `/api/widgets/${id}`, patch).its('body');
  },
  deleteWidget(id: number) {
    return cy.request('DELETE', `/api/widgets/${id}`).its('status');
  },
});

declare namespace Cypress {
  interface Chainable {
    createWidget(payload: { name: string; qty: number }): Chainable<unknown>;
    getWidget(id: number): Chainable<unknown>;
    updateWidget(id: number, patch: Partial<{ name: string; qty: number }>): Chainable<unknown>;
    deleteWidget(id: number): Chainable<number>;
  }
}
```
Tradeoff: `addAll()` colocates related commands cleanly — but all commands registered via `addAll()` are parent commands (no `prevSubject` support), so any helper that logically chains from a previous subject must be registered separately with `Cypress.Commands.add(..., { prevSubject: true }, ...)`, fragmenting related command registrations across two call sites.

**Pattern 775** — `Cypress.Commands.overwrite()` wrapping `cy.get()` to capture a debug screenshot on element-not-found timeout
```typescript
// Auto-screenshot on every cy.get() timeout for zero-effort debug artifacts
// without modifying individual tests.

Cypress.Commands.overwrite(
  'get',
  (
    originalFn,
    selector: string,
    options?: Cypress.Loggable & Cypress.Timeoutable,
  ) => {
    return originalFn(selector, options).then(
      (subject) => subject,
      (err: Error) => {
        if (err.message.includes('Timed out retrying')) {
          const safe = selector.replace(/[^a-z0-9]/gi, '_').slice(0, 60);
          cy.screenshot(`debug__${safe}__${Date.now()}`, { overwrite: true });
        }
        throw err;
      }
    );
  }
);
```
Tradeoff: Overwriting `cy.get()` provides a screenshot for every selector failure without touching individual tests — but `cy.screenshot()` is itself an async Cypress command enqueued after the failure; Cypress may already be tearing down the runner state by the time it executes, causing the screenshot to capture a blank or partially destroyed page rather than the live DOM state at the moment of failure.

**Pattern 776** — Component test `cy.spy()` on a `useImperativeHandle` ref method to verify parent-to-child call contracts
```typescript
// Test that a parent correctly calls an imperative method on a forwardRef child
// without needing to observe child internal state changes.

import { forwardRef, useImperativeHandle } from 'react';
import { mount } from 'cypress/react';

const Drawer = forwardRef((_, ref) => {
  useImperativeHandle(ref, () => ({ open: () => {}, close: () => {} }));
  return <aside data-cy="drawer" />;
});

it('parent calls drawer.open() when menu button is clicked', () => {
  const drawerRef: React.RefObject<any> = { current: null };
  const openSpy = cy.spy().as('openSpy');

  mount(
    <div>
      <Drawer ref={(el) => { if (el) { el.open = openSpy; drawerRef.current = el; } }} />
      <button data-cy="menu" onClick={() => drawerRef.current?.open()}>Menu</button>
    </div>
  );

  cy.get('[data-cy="menu"]').click();
  cy.get('@openSpy').should('have.been.calledOnce');
});
```
Tradeoff: Patching the ref callback keeps the test focused on the call contract rather than drawer visibility — but if the parent calls `drawerRef.current.open()` in a `useEffect` on mount, `useEffect` fires before React assigns the patched ref and the spy is not yet installed, causing the call to be missed and the assertion to false-fail.

**Pattern 777** — Component test `cy.mount()` + `cy.clock()` for `setTimeout`-driven CSS class transitions
```typescript
// Deterministically test a component's "loading" → "loaded" CSS class swap
// that is driven by a setTimeout animation delay.

import { mount } from 'cypress/react';
import { SlideInPanel } from '../../src/components/SlideInPanel';

it('transitions from loading to loaded class after 400ms', () => {
  cy.clock();
  mount(<SlideInPanel title="Settings" />);

  cy.get('[data-cy="panel"]')
    .should('have.class', 'loading')
    .and('not.have.class', 'loaded');

  cy.tick(400); // advance past the setTimeout threshold

  cy.get('[data-cy="panel"]')
    .should('have.class', 'loaded')
    .and('not.have.class', 'loading');
});
```
Tradeoff: `cy.clock()` + `cy.tick()` makes `setTimeout`-driven transitions fully deterministic and eliminates CI flakiness — but `cy.clock()` also overrides `requestAnimationFrame`; components that schedule the class swap via `rAF` (common in Framer Motion wrappers) require an additional `cy.tick(16)` to advance one animation frame, requiring test authors to know whether the component uses `setTimeout` or `rAF` internally — an implementation detail the test should ideally not need to know.

### Community Gotchas

**G426** — `res.send()` called twice inside the same `req.continue()` handler surfaces as `ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT` in the Cypress proxy rather than a test assertion failure
Why this matters: A developer adds a `res.send({ body: newBody })` to replace the response body in a `req.continue()` handler, then later adds a second `res.send()` inside a conditional branch in the same function. The first call finalizes the response at the proxy level; the second triggers Node's `ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT` error, which surfaces as an uncaught exception in the Cypress runner command log rather than as a failed assertion. The error cites internal Cypress proxy source files, making the stack trace nearly impossible to trace back to the developer's intercept handler without proxy source maps.
Fix: Treat `res.send()` as a terminal operation — ensure only one code path leads to it. Use a single `const body = condition ? bodyA : bodyB` assignment, then one `res.send({ body })` call. Alternatively, mutate `res.body` directly via `Object.assign(res, { body: newBody })` without calling `res.send()` at all; Cypress forwards the mutated response automatically when the handler returns.

---

**G427** — `cy.session()` `cacheAcrossSpecs: true` produces intermittent 401 errors when parallel CI workers on the same machine race to write the on-disk session cache
Why this matters: When Cypress Cloud runs specs across parallel workers on the same machine, two workers may simultaneously detect an expired session, both execute the setup function, and both try to write the cache file at the same instant. The last write wins, but the first worker has already resumed testing with a session token the second worker's setup just invalidated server-side. All subsequent authenticated requests from the first worker return 401s with no trace of the cache-write race in the error output, making the root cause extremely difficult to identify.
Fix: Append `Cypress.env('WORKER_ID') ?? '0'` to the session ID when `cacheAcrossSpecs` is enabled, giving each worker its own cache file and eliminating the race at the cost of one extra login per worker. Alternatively, disable `cacheAcrossSpecs` for parallel CI runs entirely and reserve it for serial local dev runs.

---

**G428** — `Cypress.require()` inside `cy.origin()` throws `SyntaxError` when the target module uses top-level ESM `import`
Why this matters: A shared helper `support/auth-helpers.ts` uses `import type { User } from '../types'` at the top level. Calling `Cypress.require('./support/auth-helpers')` inside a `cy.origin()` callback causes the Cypress bundler to throw `SyntaxError: Cannot use import statement in a module` inside the cross-origin VM, which does not support native ESM. The error message references bundler output rather than the developer's source file, and the test fails before any assertions run — indistinguishable from a path-resolution error at a glance.
Fix: All files intended for `Cypress.require()` must use CommonJS: replace `import X from 'Y'` with `const X = require('Y')` and `export function foo` with `module.exports = { foo }`. For TypeScript, add a `tsconfig.cypress-origin.json` with `"module": "commonjs"` scoped to `support/` files used in `cy.origin()` callbacks.

---

**G429** — `cy.task()` returning a class instance silently strips prototype methods via JSON serialization
Why this matters: A task returns `new AuthSession(token, userId)`. The return value crosses a JSON channel from Node to the browser context: `JSON.stringify` captures only enumerable own-properties and `JSON.parse` reconstructs a plain object — not a class instance. Calling `session.isValid()` (a prototype method) throws `TypeError: session.isValid is not a function`. If the class stores all data in private fields, the round-trip produces `{}` and every property access returns `undefined`, with no error to indicate why.
Fix: Return only plain serializable objects from `cy.task()` handlers: `{ token: s.token, userId: s.userId }`. Reconstruct class instances in the `.then()` callback: `cy.task('getAuth').then((d) => new AuthSession(d.token, d.userId))`. Add a comment at every `cy.task()` handler definition reminding authors that class instances are silently coerced to plain objects across the JSON channel.

---

**G430** — `cy.clock()` called after `cy.visit()` does not freeze `Date.now()` already captured in module-scope closures evaluated during initial page load
Why this matters: An application module writes `const BOOT_TIME = Date.now()` at the top level when the script is first parsed, then computes uptime as `Date.now() - BOOT_TIME` on user actions. Calling `cy.clock(fixedTime)` after `cy.visit()` successfully replaces the global `Date.now` function — but `BOOT_TIME` was captured in a closure before the override, using the real epoch time. The computed uptime mixes the fake `Date.now()` return with the real `BOOT_TIME`, producing a large negative number and making uptime assertions fail unpredictably.
Fix: Always call `cy.clock(fixedTime)` before `cy.visit()`. When the clock is established before page load, the browser's `Date` is replaced before any application module is evaluated, so module-level `Date.now()` calls also use the fake clock. If a test must visit before manipulating time, refactor the application to compute `BOOT_TIME` lazily inside a function rather than at module scope.

**Pattern 778** — `cy.intercept()` browser-cache bypass via `Cache-Control` header removal
```typescript
// Ensure responses are never served from browser cache during tests.
// Cache hits bypass cy.intercept() entirely — the request never reaches the network layer.

// Global cache-buster in cypress/support/e2e.ts:
beforeEach(() => {
  cy.intercept({ url: '**', middleware: true }, (req) => {
    // Strip caching directives so every request goes to the server
    req.headers['cache-control'] = 'no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate';
    req.headers['pragma'] = 'no-cache';
    req.on('before:response', (res) => {
      // Prevent the browser from caching the response for subsequent tests
      res.headers['cache-control'] = 'no-store';
      delete res.headers['etag'];
      delete res.headers['last-modified'];
    });
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: Stripping cache headers from every request ensures all stubs and spies fire reliably — but it also disables performance-related caching metrics that some teams want to assert on (e.g., verifying that a CDN returns a cached response). Create a separate fixture that re-enables caching headers only in tests that explicitly verify cache behavior.

**Pattern 779** — `cy.prompt()` multi-call atomicity guard: wrapping long flows in named sub-prompts
```typescript
// cy.prompt() has a 50-step cap per call. Splitting long workflows across multiple calls
// loses atomicity — a failure in call 2 leaves state from call 1 in place.
// Use a named wrapper command that communicates intent and logs the multi-call boundary.

Cypress.Commands.add('safePrompt', (description: string, steps: string): Cypress.Chainable => {
  // Guard: enforce Chromium-only restriction before cloud round-trip
  if (!['chrome', 'electron', 'edge'].includes(Cypress.browser.name)) {
    cy.log(`safePrompt skipped — browser: ${Cypress.browser.name} (Chromium required)`);
    return cy.wrap(null);
  }
  return cy.prompt(description, steps);
});

// Multi-actor scenario split safely across two prompts with explicit state validation
it('transfers funds between accounts', () => {
  // Step 1: sender flow (≤50 steps)
  cy.safePrompt(
    'Log in as sender and initiate transfer',
    `
    - Login as "alice@example.com" with password "{{senderPass}}"
    - Navigate to Transfers
    - Enter amount 100
    - Select recipient "bob@example.com"
    - Click Send
    - Assert confirmation dialog is visible
    `,
  );

  // Validate state before second prompt — prevents cascade failure masking
  cy.get('[data-cy="confirmation-dialog"]').should('be.visible');

  // Step 2: receiver validation (≤50 steps)
  cy.safePrompt(
    'Verify recipient received funds',
    `
    - Logout
    - Login as "bob@example.com" with password "{{receiverPass}}"
    - Navigate to Balance
    - Assert balance shows 100
    `,
  );
});
```
Tradeoff: Adding explicit state assertions between `cy.prompt()` calls makes failure attribution clear — but doubles the number of AI round-trips and may exhaust the 600-prompt/hour quota faster on large suites. Consider exporting the generated Cypress code after the first successful run and committing it directly to avoid re-paying the AI cost on every CI run.

**Pattern 780** — `cy.origin()` spec-bridge iframe leak detection + 15.15.0 migration check
```typescript
// Before Cypress 15.15.0, cy.origin() could fail when a previous test left
// spec-bridge iframes in the DOM. This was fixed in 15.15.0, but teams running
// older pinned versions need to manually clear orphaned iframes.

// Support file: cypress/support/e2e.ts
afterEach(() => {
  // Remove lingering spec-bridge iframes if running Cypress < 15.15.0
  cy.window().then((win) => {
    const frames = win.document.querySelectorAll('iframe[id^="spec-bridge"]');
    frames.forEach((frame) => frame.remove());
  });
});

// In CI: verify Cypress version to skip workaround on patched builds
const CYPRESS_VERSION = Cypress.version;
const [major, minor, patch] = CYPRESS_VERSION.split('.').map(Number);
const needsSpecBridgeFix = major === 15 && minor <= 14;

Cypress.Commands.add('safeOrigin', (
  origin: string,
  fn: Parameters<typeof cy.origin>[1],
) => {
  if (needsSpecBridgeFix) {
    cy.window().then((win) => {
      win.document.querySelectorAll('iframe[id^="spec-bridge"]')
        .forEach((el) => el.remove());
    });
  }
  cy.origin(origin, fn);
});
```
Tradeoff: The spec-bridge iframe fix in 15.15.0 is transparent after upgrade — but teams pinned to `15.14.x` for stability (e.g., awaiting Angular CT monorepo fix verification) must apply the manual iframe cleanup or face intermittent `cy.origin()` failures that reproduce only when two cross-origin tests run in sequence within the same spec file.

**Pattern 781** — `cy.intercept()` with `req.alias` dynamic routing based on request body content
```typescript
// Route the same URL to different fixtures depending on what's in the request body.
// Useful for GraphQL endpoints where URL is always "/graphql" but operation name varies.

cy.intercept('POST', '/graphql', (req) => {
  const { operationName } = req.body;

  // Map operation name to fixture — avoids dozens of separate cy.intercept() calls
  const fixtureMap: Record<string, string> = {
    GetUser:       'graphql/get-user.json',
    ListProducts:  'graphql/list-products.json',
    CreateOrder:   'graphql/create-order.json',
  };

  const fixture = fixtureMap[operationName];
  if (fixture) {
    req.alias = `gql_${operationName}`;  // dynamic alias from operation name
    req.reply({ fixture });
  } else {
    // Unknown operation: pass through to real server and log
    cy.log(`[graphql] unmatched operation: ${operationName}`);
    req.continue();
  }
});

// Wait on specific operation by alias
cy.visit('/user-profile');
cy.wait('@gql_GetUser').its('request.body.operationName').should('eq', 'GetUser');
cy.wait('@gql_ListProducts');
cy.get('[data-cy="product-count"]').should('contain', '3');
```
Tradeoff: The `fixtureMap` + `req.alias` pattern keeps a single `cy.intercept()` call for all GraphQL operations and makes operation-specific `cy.wait()` readable — but `req.alias` assigned inside a route handler is not visible to `cy.wait()` until the alias is matched at least once; calling `cy.wait('@gql_CreateOrder')` before any CreateOrder request fires causes an indefinite hang rather than a clear "alias not found" error.

**Pattern 782** — `cy.exec()` `exitCode` migration guard for teams upgrading from Cypress 14
```typescript
// Cypress 15 renamed cy.exec() result.code → result.exitCode.
// Teams running mixed CI environments (some with Cy 14, some with Cy 15) need a guard.

// shared helper: cypress/support/commands.ts
const CY_MAJOR = parseInt(Cypress.version.split('.')[0], 10);

Cypress.Commands.add(
  'execWithExitCode',
  (command: string, options?: Cypress.ExecOptions): Cypress.Chainable<number> => {
    return cy.exec(command, { ...options, failOnNonZeroExit: false }).then((result) => {
      // Use exitCode (Cy 15+) with fallback to code (Cy 14)
      const code = CY_MAJOR >= 15
        ? (result as any).exitCode
        : (result as any).code;
      return code as number;
    });
  }
);

// Usage — works on both Cy 14 and Cy 15:
it('database seed succeeds', () => {
  cy.execWithExitCode('npm run db:seed').should('eq', 0);
});

// After full Cy 15 rollout, replace with direct:
// cy.exec('npm run db:seed').its('exitCode').should('eq', 0)
```
Tradeoff: The version guard lets teams upgrade Cypress incrementally across environments without breaking CI — but it adds a custom command that must be maintained and eventually removed; set a deprecation comment or lint rule referencing the target Cypress version for cleanup.

**Pattern 783** — Command Log memory reclaim: `numTestsKeptInMemory` tuning for long interactive sessions
```typescript
// Cypress 15.14.0 introduced automatic command log clearing once tests age out of
// numTestsKeptInMemory. Tune this for very long runs to prevent browser OOM.

// cypress.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from 'cypress';

export default defineConfig({
  e2e: {
    // Default is 50. Reduce for suites with >200 tests in open mode to prevent
    // Chromium renderer OOM after several hundred test runs.
    numTestsKeptInMemory: 20,

    setupNodeEvents(on, config) {
      // Log current setting for CI diagnostics
      on('before:run', () => {
        console.log(
          `[cypress] numTestsKeptInMemory: ${config.numTestsKeptInMemory}`,
        );
      });
      return config;
    },
  },
});
```
Tradeoff: Reducing `numTestsKeptInMemory` reclaims RAM during long interactive sessions (especially after 15.14.0's automatic clearing) — but time-travel debugging only covers the most recent N test runs; developers lose access to the command log for tests that have aged out, making retrospective debugging after a test suite completes harder.

**Pattern 784** — CSS selector resilience: escaping regex metacharacters in `data-*` attribute values
```typescript
// Cypress 15.15.0 fixed a crash where element attribute values containing regex
// metacharacters (e.g., data-cy="items[0].name") caused the CSS selector engine
// to throw. Even after the fix, construct safe selectors defensively.

// Helper: escape attribute values for use in CSS attribute selectors
function cyAttr(attr: string, value: string): string {
  // CSS attribute selectors need brackets and quotes escaped
  // e.g., [data-cy="items[0].name"] → invalid CSS without escaping
  const escapedValue = CSS.escape ? value : value.replace(/[^\w-]/g, (c) => `\\${c}`);
  return `[${attr}="${escapedValue}"]`;
}

// Usage:
const dynamicKey = 'items[0].name';  // array notation from form libraries
cy.get(cyAttr('data-cy', dynamicKey)).should('be.visible');
// equivalent to: cy.get('[data-cy="items\\[0\\]\\.name"]')

// Alternative: use cy.contains() for partial text match when selector is complex
cy.contains('[data-cy^="items"]', 'Product Name').should('be.visible');

// Alternative: use data-testid with safe slugs instead of dot-bracket notation
// <input data-cy="items-0-name" />  ← generated from template: key.replace(/[.\[\]]/g, '-')
```
Tradeoff: Defensive escaping guards against both the pre-15.15.0 crash and the post-fix subtle mismatch between developer intent and CSS selector semantics — but it adds cognitive overhead. The preferred fix is to use safe slug keys in `data-cy` attributes at render time rather than escaping dynamic values in tests.

### Community Gotchas

**G431** — `cy.prompt()` non-English prompts fail silently without error context  
Why this matters: A team writing prompts in Japanese or German discovers that natural-language steps in non-English are "optimized for English" only at runtime — `cy.prompt()` executes with no generated steps and no assertion failure, making the test pass vacuously. The Command Log shows zero sub-steps for the prompt call, which developers interpret as "the prompt ran instantly" rather than "the prompt produced nothing."  
Fix: Always write `cy.prompt()` steps in English, even in localized codebases. Add a lint rule or pre-commit hook that flags any `cy.prompt()` call whose step string contains non-ASCII characters and requires a comment explaining the exception.

---

**G432** — `cy.prompt()` multi-call self-healing cascades: a healed selector in call 1 silently breaks call 2's cached steps  
Why this matters: In a multi-call `cy.prompt()` flow, the first call heals a selector (e.g., `[data-cy="login-btn"]` → `[data-cy="signin-button"]`). The cached steps for the second call still reference the old selector via a placeholder that was captured before healing. When call 2 executes from cache, it uses the healed selector — but if the component is later reverted, call 1 heals again and call 2 silently reverts too. The test passes or fails non-deterministically depending on which cached version was last written.  
Fix: After a self-healing event, export the generated code (`cypress/prompts/*.cy.ts`) to version control immediately. Treat self-healed selectors as "unstable" and add a manual assertion comment: `// HEALED: verify this selector reflects current DOM`.

---

**G433** — `cy.exec()` `exitCode` vs `code` — the wrong property returns `undefined` without throwing  
Why this matters: A Cypress 15 upgrade leaves a test calling `cy.exec('cmd').its('code')`. The `code` property no longer exists; `its('code')` yields `undefined`. The subsequent `.should('eq', 0)` assertion passes because Chai treats `undefined == 0` as false, but Cypress's retry-ability causes `.its('code')` to retry until timeout, then ultimately throw a timeout error — not a property-not-found error. The message "Timed out retrying after 4000ms: expected undefined to equal 0" is confusing because it implies the command ran slowly, not that the property was renamed.  
Fix: Search the codebase for `.its('code')` in Cypress tests and replace with `.its('exitCode')` (Cypress 15+). Add a `cy.exec().its('exitCode')` to ESLint's `cypress/no-unnecessary-waiting` equivalent rule set via a custom ESLint rule that flags `.its('code')` on exec results.

---

**G434** — `numTestsKeptInMemory: 0` causes `cy.go('back')` to lose time-travel screenshot context for the previous test  
Why this matters: A developer sets `numTestsKeptInMemory: 0` to aggressively reclaim memory. Time-travel debugging for the immediately preceding test now shows a "screenshot not available" message in the Command Log timeline even when the test just finished. This breaks the standard Cypress debugging workflow of clicking a command log step to see the DOM state at that moment.  
Fix: Use `numTestsKeptInMemory: 1` as the minimum — preserving only the most recently completed test's context is sufficient for most post-failure debugging while reclaiming memory from all older tests. Reserve `numTestsKeptInMemory: 0` only for pure CI run-only mode where the Cypress runner UI is never opened.

---

**G435** — `cy.intercept()` browser cache bypass requires `no-store` on responses, not just `no-cache` on requests  
Why this matters: A test sets `cache-control: no-cache` on the outgoing request via `middleware: true` intercept. The browser still serves subsequent requests from disk cache because `no-cache` only tells the browser to revalidate with the server — it does not prevent storing. If the server returns `ETag` or `Last-Modified` headers and the test runs multiple times in the same browser session, the browser sends a conditional GET, the server responds `304 Not Modified`, and the intercept stub is never reached for the second+ test run. The stub fires on the first run but fails silently on reruns.  
Fix: In the `before:response` handler, also set `res.headers['cache-control'] = 'no-store'` and delete `etag` and `last-modified` headers. Use `no-store` (prevents storage) rather than `no-cache` (allows storage but requires revalidation) to fully disable browser caching during test runs.

**Pattern 785** — `allowCypressEnv: false` enforcement + `Cypress.env()` → `cy.env()` migration command

```typescript
// cypress.config.ts — block the deprecated synchronous Cypress.env() in all tests
import { defineConfig } from 'cypress';

export default defineConfig({
  e2e: {
    // Introduced in Cypress 15.10. When false, calling Cypress.env() in test
    // code returns undefined silently (does NOT throw). Use this to surface
    // calls during a migration: set to false, grep CI output for unexpected
    // undefined env values, then flip tests to cy.env() one by one.
    allowCypressEnv: false,

    // Preferred: expose non-sensitive config values via Cypress.expose()
    expose: {
      APP_VERSION: '2.4.1',
      FEATURE_FLAGS_URL: 'https://flags.example.com',
    },
  },
});

// ── Migration: typed cy.env() helper ─────────────────────────────────────────
// cypress/support/env.ts
// Always request all variables for a test in a single cy.env() call to avoid
// deep .then() nesting (see gotcha G436 for why you can't call cy.env()
// inside cy.intercept() handlers).

export type EnvKeys = 'API_TOKEN' | 'ADMIN_PASS' | 'TEST_EMAIL' | 'STAGING_URL';

export function withEnv<K extends EnvKeys>(
  keys: K[],
  fn: (vars: Record<K, string>) => void,
): void {
  cy.env(keys).then((vars) => fn(vars as Record<K, string>));
}

// Usage in specs:
import { withEnv } from '../support/env';

it('seeds data with API token', () => {
  withEnv(['API_TOKEN', 'STAGING_URL'], ({ API_TOKEN, STAGING_URL }) => {
    cy.request({
      url: `${STAGING_URL}/api/seed`,
      headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${API_TOKEN}` },
      method: 'POST',
      body: { scenario: 'checkout' },
    }).its('status').should('eq', 201);
  });
});

// ── Backward-compat shim for gradual migration ────────────────────────────────
// If you have hundreds of Cypress.env() calls and need time to migrate,
// add this shim in cypress/support/e2e.ts to log (not break) legacy calls:
// This only works when allowCypressEnv is still true.
const _origEnv = Cypress.env.bind(Cypress);
(Cypress as any).env = (...args: unknown[]) => {
  if (typeof args[0] === 'string' && args.length === 1) {
    console.warn(`[migration] Cypress.env("${args[0]}") — migrate to cy.env()`);
  }
  return _origEnv(...args as [string]);
};
```
Tradeoff: `allowCypressEnv: false` is the correct enforcement posture for new projects but is too disruptive for existing suites with hundreds of `Cypress.env()` calls. Use the shim approach (logging + warning) during the migration window, then flip `allowCypressEnv: false` once all calls are replaced. Verify via `npx grep -r "Cypress\.env(" cypress/` to confirm zero remaining calls before enforcing.

**Pattern 786** — `--posix-exit-codes` flag for CI exit code normalization + exit-112 network guard

```yaml
# .github/workflows/e2e.yml — normalize Cypress exit codes for all CI consumers
# Without --posix-exit-codes, Cypress exits with the NUMBER of failed tests
# (e.g., 3 failures → exit code 3). Most CI systems treat any non-zero exit as
# failure, but scripts that check for specific exit codes (like bash pipelines
# and status matchers) can misinterpret exit code 3 as "permission denied"
# or "quota exceeded" depending on the consumer.
#
# With --posix-exit-codes:
#   0 = all tests passed
#   1 = one or more tests failed
# 112 = Cypress Cloud could not determine the next spec (network error during
#       Smart Orchestration). This is NOT a test failure — treat it as a
#       infra-retry signal.

jobs:
  cypress:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    container:
      image: cypress/browsers:22.15.0
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: cypress-io/github-action@v7
        with:
          record: true
          parallel: true
          ci-build-id: "${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}"
          browser: chrome
          # Pass as extra CLI args:
          command: npx cypress run --posix-exit-codes --record --parallel
        env:
          CYPRESS_RECORD_KEY: ${{ secrets.CYPRESS_RECORD_KEY }}
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        # Capture exit code for the network-guard step:
        id: cypress_run
        continue-on-error: true

      - name: Guard against exit-112 Cloud orchestration failure
        if: steps.cypress_run.outcome == 'failure'
        run: |
          EXIT_CODE=${{ steps.cypress_run.outputs.exit-code || '1' }}
          if [ "$EXIT_CODE" = "112" ]; then
            echo "::warning::Cypress exited with 112 (Cloud orchestration network error). Retrying..."
            exit 1  # Still fail the job, but log as infra issue, not test failure
          fi
          echo "Cypress exited with code $EXIT_CODE (test failure)"
          exit $EXIT_CODE
```

```typescript
// cypress/support/e2e.ts — annotate test intent for posix-exit-codes runs
// When --posix-exit-codes is active, the only way to distinguish "1 test failed"
// from "100 tests failed" is via the Cypress Cloud dashboard or the after:run hook.
// Log a summary in after:run to compensate for the information lost in exit-code compression.

// cypress.config.ts setupNodeEvents:
on('after:run', (results) => {
  if ('totalFailed' in results && results.totalFailed > 0) {
    // Write a summary artifact for CI to upload
    const fs = require('fs');
    fs.writeFileSync(
      'cypress-summary.json',
      JSON.stringify({
        totalTests: results.totalTests,
        totalFailed: results.totalFailed,
        totalPassed: results.totalPassed,
        runUrl: results.runUrl,
      }, null, 2),
    );
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: `--posix-exit-codes` is essential for CI pipelines that pass Cypress as a step in a larger orchestration script — exit code 0 or 1 is universally understood. The trade-off is losing the count of failures in the exit code, which was a convenient quick-look metric for scripts that did `if [ $? -gt 5 ]; then page_oncall; fi`. Migrate such checks to `cypress-summary.json` + `after:run` or to Cypress Cloud's webhook/Slack notification.

**Pattern 787** — Angular 21 zoneless component testing with `angular-zoneless` mount function

```typescript
// Requires: Angular 21+, @angular/core >=18 with zoneless experimental provider
// Angular 21 removes Zone.js as a required dependency. Cypress 15.8.0 added
// the `angular-zoneless` mount helper for testing zoneless Angular components.

// cypress/support/component.ts
import { mountAngularZoneless } from 'cypress/angular-zoneless';
// Register the angular-zoneless mount command
Cypress.Commands.add('mountZoneless', mountAngularZoneless);

declare global {
  namespace Cypress {
    interface Chainable {
      mountZoneless: typeof mountAngularZoneless;
    }
  }
}

// ── Example: testing a zoneless signal-based component ─────────────────────
// src/app/counter/counter.component.ts
// @Component({ standalone: true, ... })
// export class CounterComponent {
//   count = signal(0);
//   increment() { this.count.update(c => c + 1); }
// }

// counter.cy.ts
import { CounterComponent } from './counter.component';
import { provideExperimentalZonelessChangeDetection } from '@angular/core';

describe('CounterComponent (zoneless)', () => {
  it('increments signal-based count', () => {
    // Must provide the zoneless CD provider — without it the component renders
    // but change detection never runs, so assertions on updated state will flake.
    cy.mountZoneless(CounterComponent, {
      providers: [provideExperimentalZonelessChangeDetection()],
    });

    cy.get('[data-cy="count"]').should('have.text', '0');
    cy.get('[data-cy="increment"]').click();
    // Zoneless CD triggers synchronously in response to signal updates —
    // no detectChanges() call needed (unlike Zone.js-based tests).
    cy.get('[data-cy="count"]').should('have.text', '1');
  });

  it('cleans up signal subscriptions after unmount', () => {
    const fixture = cy.mountZoneless(CounterComponent, {
      providers: [provideExperimentalZonelessChangeDetection()],
    });
    cy.get('[data-cy="increment"]').click().click();
    // Cypress auto-destroys the component after the test — confirm no memory
    // leak by asserting signal count does not persist to the next test.
    cy.wrap(null).then(() => {
      // After unmount, the component instance is destroyed — reading count
      // from a stored reference would throw (good: confirms cleanup).
    });
  });
});

// ── Legacy Zone.js test still works alongside zoneless ─────────────────────
// Standard cy.mount() continues to work for Zone.js components.
// Use cy.mountZoneless() only for components that explicitly opt out of Zone.js.
// Do NOT mix zone and zoneless components in the same module hierarchy —
// Angular warns about this combination at runtime.
```
Tradeoff: Zoneless Angular components provide faster change detection and simpler reasoning about when the DOM updates (signals trigger CD synchronously), but the migration path from Zone.js is non-trivial for large apps. In Cypress CT, the primary benefit is eliminating `fixture.detectChanges()` boilerplate and the flakiness it introduces. Use `provideExperimentalZonelessChangeDetection()` only in test providers — never in the app's production providers unless you have fully migrated.

**Pattern 788** — `experimentalFastVisibility` opt-in + caveat matrix for production use

```typescript
// cypress.config.ts — opt in to the faster visibility detection algorithm
// Introduced in Cypress 15.8.0. Uses point-sampling (checking element corners +
// center via elementFromPoint) rather than the legacy recursive getBoundingClientRect
// traversal. Significantly faster on complex DOM (shadow DOM components, deeply
// nested flexbox layouts).
import { defineConfig } from 'cypress';

export default defineConfig({
  e2e: {
    experimentalFastVisibility: true,
    // Known caveats (see matrix below before enabling in production):
    // 1. Shadow DOM elements: NOT yet supported — visibility check falls through
    //    to the legacy algorithm for shadow-host elements, but can miss nested
    //    shadow-tree elements. Do not use with Web Components suites.
    // 2. Off-viewport elements: elements positioned outside the current viewport
    //    (e.g., off-screen drawers, sticky footers below fold) may be incorrectly
    //    identified as visible because point-sampling uses client coordinates.
    // 3. CSS transform: elements with CSS `transform: translateX(-9999px)` are
    //    off-screen but still have in-viewport bounding boxes — the point-sampling
    //    may sample a covered region and report the element as visible.
  },
  component: {
    // Disable experimentalFastVisibility for CT suites that use Web Components
    // (Angular Material, Stencil, Lit) — wait for shadow DOM support.
    experimentalFastVisibility: false,
    devServer: { framework: 'react', bundler: 'vite' },
    specPattern: 'src/**/*.cy.{ts,tsx}',
  },
});

// ── Caveat matrix ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// | Scenario                          | Safe to enable? | Notes                     |
// |-----------------------------------|-----------------|---------------------------|
// | Standard HTML, no shadow DOM      | ✅ Yes          | 2-5x faster               |
// | React/Vue SPA, no Web Components  | ✅ Yes          | Full benefit               |
// | Angular with Angular Material     | ⚠️ Partial       | Material uses shadow DOM  |
// | Lit/Stencil/WASM Web Components   | ❌ No           | Shadow DOM not supported  |
// | Off-screen carousel/drawer tests  | ⚠️ Partial       | Off-viewport false visible|
// | CSS transform-based animations    | ⚠️ Partial       | Off-screen not detected   |

// ── Guard: disable per-test for known shadow DOM interactions ─────────────────
// There is no per-test override API — only per-spec/config-level.
// Workaround: create a separate cypress.config.ct-webcomponents.ts that disables
// the flag and run Web Component specs with:
//   npx cypress run --config-file cypress.config.ct-webcomponents.ts
```
Tradeoff: Enable `experimentalFastVisibility` for all suites that do not use Web Components — the performance gain (2-5x faster `.should('be.visible')` on complex layouts) is significant and the caveats are narrow. For suites that test shadow-DOM components, wait for the flag to graduate from experimental status with shadow DOM support, expected in a future 15.x release.

**Pattern 789** — Firefox transient-launch retry guard (Cypress 15.15.0 fix)

```typescript
// Cypress 15.15.0 fixed a bug where Firefox transient launch failures (race
// condition in the geckodriver startup probe) caused Cypress to immediately
// exit rather than retry the launch. This fix is built-in and requires no
// configuration — but teams that implemented workarounds (custom launch scripts,
// sleep delays) should remove them as they now conflict with Cypress's own retry.

// ── Before (workaround — remove after upgrading to 15.15.0) ─────────────────
// cypress.config.ts (OLD — remove this)
// on('before:browser:launch', (browser, launchOptions) => {
//   if (browser.name === 'firefox') {
//     // Artificial delay to work around transient Firefox launch failures
//     return new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(() => resolve(launchOptions), 2000));
//   }
// });

// ── After (15.15.0+, no workaround needed) ───────────────────────────────────
// Cypress now internally retries the Firefox browser launch up to 3 times
// with exponential backoff before declaring a launch failure. The retry is
// transparent to setupNodeEvents hooks.

// ── Detecting whether your run is affected by the old bug ────────────────────
// Pre-15.15.0 symptoms:
//   Error: "Browser Firefox exited early (exit code 1)" followed by immediate
//   suite failure with 0 tests run.
// Post-15.15.0: The same transient failure is retried automatically; you'll
//   see a "Retrying Firefox launch (attempt 2/3)" log line in the Cypress output.

// ── GitHub Actions: pin to 15.15.0+ for Firefox jobs ─────────────────────────
// .github/workflows/e2e-firefox.yml
// jobs:
//   e2e-firefox:
//     runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
//     container:
//       image: cypress/browsers:22.15.0  # includes Firefox 135
//     steps:
//       - uses: actions/checkout@v4
//       - uses: cypress-io/github-action@v7
//         with:
//           browser: firefox
//           # No artificial sleep or retry wrapper needed — 15.15.0 handles it

// ── Type-safe browser guard for Firefox-only tests ──────────────────────────
// Some test patterns (real clipboard, CDP emulation) are Chromium-only.
// Use a test-level browser guard to prevent false failures on Firefox runs:
function onlyInBrowser(name: string, fn: () => void): void {
  if (Cypress.browser.name === name) {
    fn();
  }
}

it('copies to clipboard (Chromium only)', function () {
  if (Cypress.browser.name !== 'chrome') {
    this.skip(); // skip gracefully — skip() must be called synchronously
  }
  cy.get('[data-cy="copy-btn"]').click();
  cy.window().then((win) => win.navigator.clipboard.readText())
    .should('eq', 'Expected clipboard text');
});
```
Tradeoff: The built-in Firefox launch retry eliminates 80% of "Firefox failed to launch" CI flakiness in multi-browser pipelines. The remaining 20% (geckodriver version mismatch, missing libdbus on stripped CI images) still requires investigation. After upgrading to 15.15.0, remove any custom sleep/retry scripts that were added as workarounds — they introduce double-retry delays (your script + Cypress's internal retry) that can push Firefox startup to 30+ seconds before failing.

**Pattern 790** — Cypress Cloud MCP server setup for AI assistant real-time test data access

```json
// .mcp/config.json (or ~/.cursor/mcp.json for Cursor, .claude/mcp.json for Claude Code)
// Connects AI coding assistants to Cypress Cloud's real-time run data.
// The Cypress Cloud MCP server exposes tools that let AI assistants:
//   - Query the last N test runs, their pass rates, and flakiness metrics
//   - Read specific test failure messages and screenshots without opening the browser
//   - Understand which tests need fixing before suggesting code changes
//   - Generate targeted fix suggestions based on actual failure context

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "cypress-cloud": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["@cypress/mcp-server"],
      "env": {
        "CYPRESS_CLOUD_API_KEY": "${CYPRESS_CLOUD_API_KEY}",
        "CYPRESS_PROJECT_ID": "your-project-id"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

```typescript
// What the Cypress Cloud MCP server exposes to AI assistants:
// (These are the tool names an AI can invoke after connecting to the MCP server)
//
// get_latest_run         — Returns the most recent run summary (pass/fail/flaky counts)
// get_failing_tests      — Returns current failing tests with error messages and stack traces
// get_flaky_tests        — Returns tests flagged as flaky in the last N runs
// get_test_replay_url    — Returns a URL to the Cypress Cloud replay for a specific test run
// get_spec_timings       — Returns per-spec duration data for CI optimization
// get_run_artifacts      — Returns screenshot/video artifact URLs for a failing test

// Example: before asking an AI to fix a failing test, the AI can retrieve the
// exact error message from Cypress Cloud rather than requiring the developer to
// copy-paste it from CI logs.

// ── CI: set CYPRESS_CLOUD_API_KEY securely ──────────────────────────────────
// Never hardcode the API key. In GitHub Actions:
// env:
//   CYPRESS_CLOUD_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.CYPRESS_CLOUD_API_KEY }}
//
// Generate the key at: https://cloud.cypress.io/organizations/YOUR_ORG/integrations/api-keys

// ── Local development: add to .env.local (gitignored) ───────────────────────
// CYPRESS_CLOUD_API_KEY=your_key_here
// CYPRESS_PROJECT_ID=your_project_id

// ── TypeScript type shim for MCP-sourced test context ───────────────────────
// If you build automation scripts that call the MCP server programmatically:
interface CypressCloudRunSummary {
  runId: string;
  runUrl: string;
  totalTests: number;
  totalFailed: number;
  totalFlaky: number;
  startedAt: string;
  completedAt: string | null;
  branch: string;
  commitSha: string;
}

interface CypressCloudFailingTest {
  specFile: string;
  testTitle: string[];
  errorMessage: string;
  errorStack: string;
  screenshotUrl: string | null;
  replayUrl: string | null;
  attempts: number;
}
```
Tradeoff: The Cypress Cloud MCP server is a significant productivity multiplier when using AI coding assistants — instead of the developer copy-pasting failure context from CI, the AI reads it directly and suggests fixes grounded in the actual failure. The requirement is a Cypress Cloud account (free tier includes limited MCP calls). Self-hosted Cypress runners without Cloud recording cannot use the MCP server. For teams on self-hosted infrastructure, the `after:run` hook with a custom webhook to your internal dashboard is the equivalent pattern without Cloud dependency.
